What does Exploria Resorts have to offer?  Serving the vacation ownership and hospitality industry for over 25 years, Exploria Resorts offers full-time employees competitive benefits including Health insurance with HSA and FSA options, Dental Insurance, Vision Insurance, Life/AD&D insurance, Short – Long- Term Disability coverage, 401(k), PTO, Paid Holidays, Employee Referral Program, Employee and Family Discounts, growth opportunities, and more!

Sales Proposal Coordinator

Full Time

Pay Rate: $18.00/ Hour

Location: Exploria Resorts Corporate Office 127 Town Center Blvd. Clermont, FL 34714

(This is not a remote position) 

Shift: 9 AM - 5 PM 

Job Summary:

The Sales Proposal Coordinator will report directly to the Director of Sales Administration. Their primary responsibility will be preparing purchase proposals for the Orlando Sales department for timeshare transactions, ensuring accuracy and complying with company policies and guidelines.

Responsibilities and Duties:

  • Knowledge of current financing terms and guidelines
  • Understand price sheet structure, down payment requirements, and maintenance fee structure
  • Prepare purchase proposals for current owners’ timeshare transactions
  • Review legal documents, i.e., Purchase Proposals for accuracy
  • Ensure current proposal templates are being utilized
  • Communicate any discrepancies with the appropriate management personnel
  • Assist management with various administrative duties as needed such as data entry on excel spreadsheets, scanning, copying, and other admin related duties
  • Communicate discrepancies or compliance issues to management’s attention
  • Must be willing and able to work weekends and holidays and adapt to business needs as they may be adjusted.
  • Must understand the importance of PCI and PII compliance when overseeing sensitive information related to consumers and consumer privacy.

Qualifications

Qualifications and Skills:

  • Previous administrative or sales support preferred
  • High school diploma
  • Ability to work in a high-pressure, fast-paced environment.
  • Detail-oriented and organized.
  • Must possess strong computer skills with high accuracy and must maintain 35+wpm minimum typing speed.
  • Proficient in MS Office
  • Perform various projects requested upon Supervisors and Managers
  • Ability to follow instructions.
  • Must be available to work weekends and holidays and have a flexible schedule should the business needs change.

Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time, 24/7 operation, includes weekends
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Physical: Lifting up to 25 lbs
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off

About this job

Develop and deliver technical training programs for bus and heavy vehicle maintenance personnel at LYNX, a major Central Florida transit system. Combines hands-on expertise with training delivery, curriculum development, and program evaluation to build skilled maintenance teams.

Good fit if you have diesel or heavy vehicle maintenance experience, training delivery experience, and a Florida Class B CDL with airbrakes and passenger endorsement or ability to obtain one.

Full job description

Are you a skilled diesel or heavy vehicle maintenance professional with a passion for teaching and developing others? LYNX is seeking a Maintenance Training Instructor to lead, develop, and deliver engaging technical training programs that empower our maintenance team to keep Central Forida moving safely and efficiently. 

In this impactful role, you'll combine your hands-on maintenance expertise with your ability to train, mentor, and inspire technicians at all levels.  From developing training materials and conducting hands-on instructions to evaluating program effectiveness and supporting regulatory compliance, you'll play a key role in building a highly skilled workforce that supports one of the region's largest public transportation systems. 

This position is considered safety-sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.

Hours of Operation:

Monday-Friday 6am-2:30pm but can work any 8-hour shifts that are needed and we are open 7 days a week depending on training needs, some shifts might be overnight. We are a 24/7 operation; however, we will provide advanced notice 

Day in the Life:

This position develops, coordinates, implements, conducts and evaluates training programs for maintenance personnel in the proper service, repair and maintenance of buses, support vehicles, and shop equipment.
This position is considered safety‐sensitive and subject to the provisions of the Substance Abuse Program Policy for Safety Sensitive Positions.
Essential Functions: This list is intended to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification and is not designed to be interpreted as an exhaustive listing of all tasks required of employees assigned to the job. All employees will be expected to perform other duties as assigned. All jobs require regular and reliable attendance.

In conjunction with the above, the Maintenance Training Instructor will:


• Consults with Maintenance department leadership for input in developing maintenance training programs.
• Delivers effective training programs by applying strong presentation, training and facilitation skills, and delivering feedback to learners; develops action plans and measures the impact to the organization.
• Prepares, plans, organizes and conducts maintenance training needs assessments and analyses, lesson plans, course curricula, visual and mechanical aides, written materials and hands‐on instruction that complies with internal procedures and external mandates or regulations.
• Participates as a resource to maintenance management on safety, technical proficiency and productivity issues, and works with the safety division to develop and implement programs compliant with state and national regulations, to promote the safety and well‐being of Authority employees.
• Coordinates, evaluates and monitors internal and external vendor training programs.
• Monitors and evaluates the effectiveness of training programs by measuring changes in skill levels and improvements demonstrated by maintenance personnel and modifies programs accordingly to improve effectiveness to the quality vehicle maintenance training programs.
• Ensures that all training materials are updated as needed, for new equipment, new procedures, technical information, etc.

Required Qualifications:

• Associate’s degree from a regionally or nationally accredited institution in automotive or diesel technology or related field, plus four years of experience working in heavy vehicle maintenance to include two years of experience conducting training programs; or combination of related experience, education and training.
• Additional directly related experience beyond the minimum requirement may substitute for the required education on a year-for-year basis.
• Must possess and maintain a Florida Class “B” CDL with airbrakes and passenger endorsement, or be able to obtain one within 6 months, have an acceptable driving record, and the ability to pass a DOT physical examination and drug screen.

Desired Qualifications:

• Experience as a presenter/facilitator of leadership and technical training, or previous training experience in a transportation or technical field.
• Bilingual (English/Spanish) helpful.


Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):

• Knowledge of training theory, methods of presentation, theories of learning,     appropriate modes of presentation and other related training issues for adult‐     learners.
• In‐depth knowledge of all heavy vehicle and facilities systems pertinent to the    Authority’s vehicles to include, but not limited to, mechanical systems, fuel   systems, hydraulic systems, pneumatic systems, HVAC, brake systems,   multiplexed systems, electrical/electronic systems, etc.
• Knowledge of tool usage, problem diagnostics and test processes.
• Knowledge of industrial safety rules, regulations, including, but not limited to   US Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations, CFR Title 49 and Florida   Administrative Code 14‐90, hazardous materials handling and storage   regulations as applied to bus maintenance.
• Knowledge of the principles of preventive maintenance and keeps abreast of   new technologies and methodologies in the vehicle maintenance field.
• Ability to develop clear, concise and effective curricula, schedules, course   materials, audio/visual aids, administrative and technical procedures.
• Ability to work from and understand verbal instruction, blueprints, schematics,   diagrams, vendor manuals and manufacturer’s specifications.
• Knowledge of software to include Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and   PowerPoint), audio/visual equipment, maintenance reporting system, web‐   based vendor/OEM troubleshooting trees, computer based diagnostic tools   and other various test/troubleshooting tools.
• Ability to learn and implement provisions of the Authority’s bargaining   agreement with ATU Local 1596 and ATU Local 1749.
• Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
• Ability to work in a diverse environment.
• Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to   establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in   the course of work using principles of excellent customer service.

Work Environment and Special Considerations:

• Will work flexible hours to include nights and weekends.
• Works in office and classroom environments and in environments with   exposure to varying weather conditions; physical, electrical, mechanical and   chemical hazards; must be able to sit and stand for extended periods of time.
• This position requires close visual acuity to perform an activity such as   viewing a computer terminal and extensive reading.
• This position requires the ability to verbally express or exchange ideas by   means of spoken word.
• Must be able to lift up to 25lbs and bend, stoop, reach, push/pull, kneel, crouch, crawl.

Support Personnel Workforce Member:

LYNX provides the community with much needed public transportation, and it is important for the Agency to resume its services as quickly and as safely as possible in the event of any natural, technological, or human-caused emergency or disaster. This position is considered support personnel of LYNX’s emergency preparation and response efforts during an emergency or disaster and as such, shall be expected to return to their normal work schedule as soon as possible or when otherwise notified after the emergency has occurred.

Why Work at LYNX?

    • 100% employer match up to 3% of employee contributions into the 457 plan

  • Employee assistance and wellness programs

About this job

LYNX seeks a detail-oriented data analyst to review, validate, and analyze paratransit and ADA mobility services data. The role develops reports and dashboards to ensure compliance with agency standards, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements while collaborating with internal teams and service providers.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree, three years of data analysis experience, and hands-on experience with Trapeze or mobility services data systems.

Full job description

Position Description

LYNX is seeking a Transit Data & Compliance Analyst -Paratransit/ADA also known internally as a Mobility Data & Compliance Specialist who is a detail-oriented data professional with experience in data analysis or quality assurance and hands-on experience working with mobility services data systems supporting paratransit, ADA eligibility, or on-demand transportation, such as Trapeze, PASS, or Trapeze Certification. 

Working under the direction of the Mobility Supervisor, this position reviews, validates, reconciles, and analyzes operational, eligibility and contractor reporting, and developing reports and dashboards that support operational oversight and compliance with agency standards, contractual obligations, and regulatory requirements.

This role collaborates with internal teams and contracted service providers to resolve data quality issues, improve reporting processes, and maintain accurate, complete, and audit-ready information.  Success requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to clearly communicate findings and recommendations. 

Onsite Position

Lynx

2500 Lynx Lane

Orlando, FL 32804

Shift
Monday - Friday

8:00am to 5:00pm EST

Pay Range

$23.78 to $30.00 per hour, based on qualifications and relevant experience. 

Essential Functions

This list is intended to indicate the general nature and level of work performed by employees within this classification and is not designed to be interpreted as an exhaustive listing of all tasks required of employees assigned to the job.  All employees will be expected to perform other duties as assigned. All jobs require regular and reliable attendance.

  • Collaborates with internal Mobility teams and contracted Mobility service providers to apply data quality standards, resolve discrepancies, and support accurate operational and eligibility reporting.
  • Monitors contractor data submissions and service performance metrics for compliance with Mobility Services contracts, ADA, and FTA expectations.
  • Validates data from Trapeze PASS, Trapeze Certification, scheduling/dispatch systems, and contractor platforms; prepares quality assurance and discrepancy reports for the Mobility Supervisor.
  • Develops and maintains data quality reports to track performance indicators, identify trends, and address deficiencies.
  • Supports development of dashboards, performance visualizations, and trend analyses used for operational oversight and forecasting.
  • Prepares reports and executes SQL/Crystal/Trapeze queries to support compliance monitoring, contractor oversight, ADA standards, and data integrity requirements. Supports documentation and review of contractor training records, FAC 1490 requirements, ADA-related data standards, and contractual reporting obligations.
  • Conducts spot checks of contractor trip data, contractor performance indicators, eligibility timelines, and quality assurance metrics.
  • Provides guidance to staff and contractors regarding data integrity, reporting protocols, and Mobility data workflows.
  • Provides operational support for Mobility Services data systems, including issue tracking, data validation, and coordination with Mobility operational staff.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree from a regionally or nationally accredited institution in Business Administration, Information Management, or related field.
  • Three years of experience in data analysis/quality assurance or a related field.
  • Must possess and maintain a valid Florida driver's license and safe driving record.
  • Experience working with Mobility Services data systems (paratransit, ADA eligibility, on‑demand, or Trapeze PASS/CERT).

Desired Qualifications:

  • Five years of data analysis experience in mobility services.
  • Experience supporting contractor compliance reporting or ADA/FTA performance metrics.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSA)

  • Proficiency in using Microsoft Office applications, including Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Access, and Outlook.
  • Knowledge of database structures, data Queries, and reporting principles.
  • Knowledge of ADA, FTA, and NTD reporting requirements.
  • Knowledge of Trapeze PASS, Trapeze Certification, dispatch/scheduling systems, and contractor data platforms.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to collect, organize, interpret, and present data with accuracy and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.
  • Ability to problem-solve and determine root causes of data anomalies.
  • Ability to prepare clear and concise reports, dashboards, and visualizations.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent customer service.

Job.JobTitle: Senior Diesel Technican a (Master Diesel Technican)
Job.JobDescription:
Join the team that keeps Central Florida moving!

LYNX is seeking a skilled and motivated Sr. Diesel Technician (Master Diesel Technician also known at LYNX as a Technician A - Diesel & CNG to perform diagnostics, repairs, inspections, and preventative maintenance on our fleet of transit vehicles and support equipment. This position offers the opportunity to work with advanced vehicle systems including diesel engines, electrical systems, HVA, brakes, steering, suspension, and hybrid technologies in a safety focused environment.

The ideal candidate is mechanically inclined, enjoys problem-solving, and takes pride in delivering quality repairs that ensure safe and reliable transportation for our community.

As a member of a bargaining unit, this position follows a seniority-based system for bidding on shifts and days off.

Hourly Pay Rate: $32.62 - $38.38 depending on qualifications

Shifts: Must be willing and able to work any and all shifts below as LYNX is a 24/7 operation and this will include weekends and holidays:

  • 6am to 2:30pm
  • 2pm to 10:30pm ($2.00 additional dollars and hour for pay differential)
  • 10:00pm to 6:30am ($3.00 additional dollars and hour for pay differential)
  •  

Technician "A" Essential Job Functions:

  • Carries out ordinary mechanical, hydraulic or structural maintenance repairs and adjustments.
  • Determines the source of trouble; repairs or replaces defective parts or makes changes as instructed.
  • Works from written or verbal instructions, blueprints, schematics, diagrams, vendor manuals and manufacturer’s specifications to accomplish work.
  • Applies diagnostic and analytical tools in problem solving.
  • Is competent in the use of testing equipment such as compression testers, engine/transmission readers, multimeters, AMP meters, logic probes and exhaust gas analyzers.
  • Executes fields repairs on road failures and tows buses if necessary.
  • Provides assistance to lower grade mechanics when instructed.
  • Diagnoses, tunes and repairs engines; replaces all major components including cylinder heads and other major engine components.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all electronic engine and transmission controls and sensors and wiring harness.
  • Diagnoses and repairs transmissions; replaces all internal sensors/solenoids and all major components.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces battery electric and hybrid bus components such as; controls, drive motors, inverters and battery packs.
  • Replaces engine/transmission assemblies and accessories.
  • Diagnoses and repairs air systems and components and relines brakes.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all steering and suspension components.
  • Diagnoses and repairs all wiring harnesses.  Replaces components in electrical subsystems.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all components of wheelchair lifts.  Executes A and C inspections.
  • Diagnoses, repairs and replaces all A/C components.
  • Performs other duties as may be required or assigned.

Required Qualifications:

  • High School diploma or GED plus four years’ experience in transit or heavy vehicle maintenance plus two years of technical school; or an equivalent combination of education, training and experience.
  • Must possess and maintain a current Florida CDL permit/license, Class “B” with Passenger endorsement and Airbrakes.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety precautions of the trade.
  • Ability to work with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to bend, stoop, walk, stretch, kneel, and lift 50 lbs.
  • Ability to work as part of a team.
  • Ability to work nights, weekends and holidays.
  • Ability to pass DOT physical and drug screen.
  • Ability to work in open bays, inside buses and outside in varying weather conditions.
  • Ability to work with commercial cleaners and toxic materials.
  • Ability to effectively communicate in English, both orally and in writing.
  • Ability to read electrical schematics.
  • Ability to provide own tools.
  • Employees must be able to communicate in English on the work site.
  • Ability to exhibit a professional, courteous demeanor.
  • Ability to work in a diverse environment.
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to establish and maintain positive working relationships with those encountered in the course of work using principles of excellent service.

 

Work Environment and Special Considerations:

  • Employees in this position must comply with all requirements of the Federal Transit Administration (FTA) regarding the testing of safety sensitive employees.  This position is considered safety-sensitive under FTA drug and alcohol regulations (49 CFR Part 655).

General Description

The Public Works Business Analyst I is responsible for conducting financial, compliance, and operational analysis of the projects and programs of the Public Works Department for the City of Casselberry, including management of associated grants. The position is also responsible for providing clerical and administrative support for the Public Works Department. The Public Works Business Analyst I performs work independently within established policies and procedures.

Examples of Essential Functions

  1. Provides financial, compliance and operational administrative support for the Public Works Department. (60%)
    1. Develops and monitors performance metrics, data collection systems, and data reporting requirements related to the financial components for Public Works projects.
    2. In cooperation with division heads, prepares preliminary Public Works Department budget for the individual divisions and conducts analysis of prior year budgets to make recommendations for upcoming budget year based on expense history to ensure an accurate budget submittal.
    3. In cooperation with division heads, prepares preliminary Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) budget for the individual divisions and ensures accurate budget submittal.
    4. Monitors and maintains the departmental expenditures, CIP expenses, budget amendments, and requests for fund transfers.
    5. Reconciles current expenditures to contract quotes to ensure accurate invoicing and payment processing.
    6. Performs analysis to determine cost effectiveness of projects.
    7. Performs quality assurance/quality control checks of data accuracy, analyzes aggregated and individualized data sets, and prepares written reports.
    8. Collaborates with the Finance Department to ensure compliance with all financial policies as related to job responsibilities; serves as a liaison between Public Works Department staff and the Finance Department.
    9. Prepares purchase orders and requisitions, processes invoices for payments and reconciles expenses related to capital accounts for assigned divisions.
    10. Assists with developing grant strategy and grant applications as needed; manages awarded grants as assigned with respect to compliance, reporting, and reimbursement requirements.
    11. Assists project managers with setup of budgets and account breakdown for projects to facilitate proper accounting and compliance with grants, policies, rules, and regulations.
  2. Provides clerical and administrative support for the Public Works Department. (35%)
    1. Acts as the department coordinator for the P-card program. Audits P-card reconciliation and reports submittals from applicable Public Works employees for department approval prior to submissions to the Finance Department.
    2. Prepares and/or reviews materials on behalf of the Public Works Department for City Commission agendas, including preparation of agenda items related to solid waste contracted services CPI changes, rate changes, and contract amendments as assigned in cooperation with the Public Works Maintenance Manager, as well as agenda items for various other contracts and purchases as assigned.
    3. Maintains effective communication with the public by responding timely to questions and concerns.
    4. May perform payroll for various divisions as assigned.
    5. Sets up and registers staff for required training.
    6. Fills out travel authorizations and performs associated check requests for staff within assigned divisions.
  3. Additional Duties and Responsibilities (5%)
    1. Encourages and displays a daily teamwork driven mentality based on the unified divisional goals set forth by the Public Works Director or designee. 
    2. Performs all duties and responsibilities in a manner consistent with the core values of the City and Department policies.
    3. Follows and has working knowledge of safety practices and procedures.
    4. Adheres to laws, regulations, and policies of the City and the assigned department.
    5. Follows instructions provided by supervisor, Department Director, or their designee.
    6. Completes the identified, required, or assigned training in a timely fashion and applies acquired knowledge and/or skills.
    7. Participates in department meetings, staff meetings and other related activities.
    8. Provides cross divisional training opportunities to other City employees when requested.
    9. Maintains, preserves, retains, and disposes of public records according to FS Chapter 119.
    10. Coordinates work related activities with other departments to solve job related issues.
  4. Emergency Management Role 
    1. Participates as a member of the City staff as required to take action in the event of an emergency.
    2. Acts in the assigned role to support the City in disaster preparation and/or disaster recovery efforts as described in the City of Casselberry Emergency Management Plan or as assigned by supervisor or designee. 

(These essential and additional job functions are not to be construed as a complete statement of all duties performed. Employees will be required to perform other job related marginal duties as assigned.)

Typical Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. 

  • Education and Training: An Associate Degree (A.A./A.S.) or higher degree in Public Administration, Finance or related field is required. A comparable combination of education and experience may be considered. 
    Experience: A minimum of three (3) years experience in finance, accounting, or administration within a municipal service or related field is required. 
    Certificates, Licenses and/or Registrations Required: Must possess and maintain a valid Florida Driver’s license. A Motor Vehicle Record (MVR) check will be made to determine acceptance of past driving record. 
    Security Clearance: Florida Department of Law Enforcement background clearance.
    Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of local, state and federal regulations affecting work.
  • Knowledge of departmental rules, policies and procedures.
  • Knowledge of business management practices.
  • Ability to apply knowledge of accounting standards and budgeting practices.
  • Ability to research, analyze and reconcile financial data.
  • Knowledge of business arithmetic.
  • Ability to accurately perform difficult arithmetic computations.
  • Ability to create and maintain advanced formulas and spreadsheets.
  • Knowledge (advanced level) of Central Square/NaviLine or similar enterprise software.
  • Ability (intermediate to advanced level) to utilize Microsoft Office Suite, e.g. Outlook, Word and Excel.
  • Ability to deal with stressful conditions in a calm and professional manner.
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relationships with other employees and the public.

General Description

The Utility Engineer I/II is responsible for the design, review and oversight of the projects associated with water, wastewater, and reclaimed utility systems infrastructure improvement, operation, and preventative maintenance of the Utilities Department for the City of Casselberry. The Utility Engineer I/II exercises considerable discretion for independent decisions based on technical and/or professional knowledge.

The pay range listed is the minimum and maximum starting pay range for both Utility Engineer I and II. Pay offered will be dependent upon the level of position offered. The pay range for both positions is below:

Utility Engineer I: $79,290.00 - $99,112.00/Annually
Utility Engineer II: $90,626.00 - $113,277.00/Annually

Please see the typical qualifications section for the minimum requirements for each position

Examples of Essential Functions

  1. Provides design, review and oversight of projects associated with the improvement, operation, and preventative maintenance of water, wastewater, and reclaimed systems. (95%)
  1. Partners with the various Utilities Staff in the development, planning, and project design details to ensure complete engineering plans for assigned rehabilitation, infrastructure design and/or preventative maintenance projects.
  2. Manages water & wastewater projects with oversight from the Senior Utility Engineer. Monitors project progress and performance, including submittal review, budget tracking, and pay application review. 
  3. Facilitates communication and coordinates with various key project personnel, including contractors, consultants, engineers, residents and department staff. 
  4. Conducts and participates in technical research related to water, wastewater, and reclaimed water for the purpose of ensuring safety and regulatory compliance.
  5. Reviews design projects that may include but is not limited to: pipe layout (gravity and pressure); grading; manholes, inlets, outfalls, valves, and other structures and fittings; hydraulic and hydrologic modeling; retention facilities; water and wastewater plant upgrades; and selection and specification of optimal pipe rehabilitation methods. 
  6. Coordinates construction activities for water & wastewater projects with assistance from the Utility Projects Supervisor.
  7. Assists with Septic-to-Sewer identification, project planning, and execution. 
  8. Prepares documents necessary for permitting of projects and submits to appropriate agencies for approval.
  9. Reviews building and engineering permits and provides comments for development reviews.
  10. Audits project areas and developments to determine the need for utility easements.
  11. Assists with the review and verification of as-built data.
  12. Conducts analysis of water production, water reclamation, distribution, and collection data.
  13. Assists in the selection of consultants and/or contractors for the plan design and/or work performed with direct oversight of the respective project, including budget management and goal/objective attainment.
  14. Prepares, submits, and participates in regulatory audits and reports to ensure ongoing compliance, such as Water Audit and Sanitary Survey.
  15. Assists the Senior Utility Engineer in the development of the five (5) year Capital Improvement Programs for assigned divisions, which includes equipment, vehicles, and project initiatives.
  16. Creates, reviews, and updates Utility documents and such as the Utility Standards Manual, Emergency Response Plan, and various Utility Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs). 
  17. Employs value engineering principles and evaluates alternatives on a feasibility, sustainability, and lifecycle cost-benefit basis.
  18. Compiles and analyzes cost estimates for utility related projects.
  19. Assists with asset management, development review, public education, public presentations, public events, grant preparation, file management, and GIS/data integration.
  20. Attends, participates and develops and or presents presentations in the various applicable City and Statewide boards/committees, as required.
  21. Maintains effective public relations with the general public.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Law Enforcement (Police / Deputy), Government / Public Safety
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $64,890 to $97,335 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Casselberry, FL
  • Education: High school diploma or GED

About this job

Perform police duties including patrol, emergency response, traffic regulation, and crime prevention in Casselberry. Enforce state laws and city ordinances while maintaining public peace and safety.

Good fit if you have completed a Florida Law Enforcement Officer Academy and hold current certification

Full job description

General Description

Under general direction, to perform police duties, such as; foot patrol, motorized patrol within the City of Casselberry; to prevent crime; to detect and arrest the perpetrators of crimes; to regulate traffic; to provide public assistance; to perform all additional functions for the rank as prescribed by relevant laws, city ordinances, departmental rules and regulations, orders and directives of the Police Department; to perform special duties and/or assignments as directed by the Chief of Police in his discretion; to enforce the laws of the State of Florida and the ordinances of the City of Casselberry.

IMPORTANT !! - YOU MUST READ THE SUPPLEMENTAL INFORMATION TO DETERMINE YOUR APPLICATION ELIGIBILITY:  

Examples of Essential Functions

- Patrols assigned zone in a police vehicle.
- Responds to emergency and non-emergency calls for police assistance as directed within the City of Casselberry.
- Arrests violators of state laws and city ordinances, as required.
- Directs and regulates traffic within the City.
- Investigates traffic accidents.
- Maintains the public peace.
- Provides general assistance to the public such as: to injured and ill persons, and in public and domestic disturbances.
- Inspects and protects business and residential properties in the nighttime.
- Completes and submits detailed written reports on approved forms on all activities.
- Appears in courts of law to present testimony and evidence in arrest cases.
- Follows safe working practices and has a working knowledge of safety practices and
procedures.
- In the event of a hurricane, major storm, natural or man-made disaster, which may threaten the area, the employee will be expected to work.  

Typical Qualifications


  • Be at least 19 years of age for law enforcement and correctional probation.
  • Be at least 18 years of age for corrections.
  • Be a citizen of the United States.
  • Have earned a high school graduate or equivalent (GED).
  • Have not been convicted of any felony or of any misdemeanor involving perjury or a false statement.
  • Any person who, after July 1, 1981, pleads guilty or nolo contendere to, or is found guilty of any felony or of a misdemeanor involving perjury or a false statement, shall not be eligible for employment or appointment as an officer, not-withstanding suspension of sentence or withholding of adjudication.
  • Have never received a dishonorable discharge from any of the Armed Forces of the United State.
  • Have good moral character.
  • Have successfully completed the Florida Basic Recruit Training Program for the respective discipline or completed the Equivalency of Training process. 
  • Have achieved a passing score on the State Officer Certification Examination.
  • Have been fingerprinted by the employing agency with prints processed by the FDLE and the FBI.
  • Have successfully passed a background investigation, to include drug testing.
  • Have passed a physical examination by a licensed physician, physician assistant, or certified advanced registered nurse practitioner.
 
  • - Qualify in a physical fitness test.
  • - Qualify in an oral review board.
  • - Qualify in a CVSA interview/examination.
  • - Qualify in a physical examination and medical testing administered by the City of Casselberry approved agent prior to employment.
  • - Qualify in a drug screen test.
  • - Qualify in a psychological fitness test administered by the City of Casselberry approved agent prior to employment.

Supplemental Information

APPLICATION ELIGIBILITY:
THIS IS NOT A SPONSORED/PAID POLICE ACADEMY POSITION. In order to be considered for this position, the applicant must have successfully complete a Florida Law Enforcement Officer Academy, be CURRENTLY attending a Florida Law Enforcement Officer Academy or CURRENTLY attending a Florida Cross-Over Law Enforcement Academy and is in good standing or has had their out-of-state Law Enforcement certification transferred over to a Florida Law Enforcement certification.

APPLICATION PROCESS:
- Applicants MUST complete the On-line Application and the Supplement Questions. If you do not have access to a computer with Internet, there is one available at your local library.
- The Recruitment Section will review your On-line Application and the Supplemental Questions. If you do not meet the minimum standards, you will be notified. If you do meet the minimum standards, you will be notified and an Application Packet will be E-mailed to you.
- The Application Packet must be completed either in Adobe and printed or printed and typed. Handwritten documents WILL NOT be accepted. The Application Packet must be complete with all required documents attached, signed, notarized (where applicable) and returned to the Casselberry Police Department by the designated date.
- The Recruitment Section will review your Application Packet. If you do not meet the minimum standards, you will be notified. If you do meet the minimum standards, you will be notified and invited to participate in the oral board interview, submit a writing sample, and take the Physical Abilities Test.
- The oral board interview and writing sample will be conducted in the Casselberry Police Department multi-purpose room at a predetermined date. Applicants that successfully pass the oral board interview and writing sample will be permitted to complete the PAT (Physical Abilities Test).
- The PAT will follow the oral board interview and writing sample. The PAT will be at Secret Lake Park (Maps and directions will be provided). Applicants will be notified immediately of their test time. (The parameters of the PAT are available from the Casselberry Police Department)
- The Recruitment  Section will compile all applicants' files and select the applicants that are going to be sent for a background review, held for further consideration or removed from the process. All applicants will be notified of their status.
- The background process will be handled by the Support Services Corporal and the Casselberry Investigations Section. This process will include, but is not limited to a voice stress examination; a fingerprint comparison; a neighborhood check and a review of the history concerning your employment, driving, credit, criminal history and drug usage. Dates and times associated with this process is at the discretion of the background investigators.  Applicants with acceptable backgrounds will advance to the Chief's Interview.
- The Chief's Interview will be conducted at the discretion of the Chief of Police. The Chief's Administrative Services Coordinator will contact the applicant to schedule the interview. The Chief of Police will select applicants that are going to be recommended for Conditional Employment Offers, held for further consideration or removed from the process. All applicants will be notified of their status by E-mail or phone call.
- Applicants that are given a Conditional Employment Offer will be advanced to the final step.
- The final step consists of a medical physical, drug screen and physiological review of the applicant. Applicants that fail any part of this step will be removed from  employment consideration. Applicants that pass all parts of this step will be authorized for a full-time position with the Casselberry Police Department. The Support Services Sergeant will coordinate the starting date with the new officer and the City of Casselberry Human Resources department.

APPLICATIONS MUST BE SUBMITTED ONLINE AT: http://www.casselberry.org

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Collections Specialist, Customer Service / Call Center
Job.JobDescription:
General Description

The purpose of this position is manage, oversee, and lead the billing department and collections department functions and activities. This position will provide strategic operational direction and guidance to the billing and collections operations, supervise the Billing Supervisor and Collections Supervisor positions, manage resources required to effectively execute strategic and division goals and objectives. This is accomplished by accurately evaluating the Billing Supervisor and Collections Supervisor positions, ensuring optimal performance and process execution.  Other duties included, but not limited to, project management, leadership role in system upgrades or implementation, budgeting, monitoring vendor contracts, and assignments associated with departmental projects. This position reports to the Director of Customer Service. 

Essential Functions

  1. Responsible for managing the delivery of effective collection functions through the supervision of the Collections Supervisor. This includes ensuring the proper handling of both residential and commercial accounts. Adherence to all processes such as write offs, bankruptcy, notices, late fees, deposit quotes, tampering, disconnects, reconnects, and nonpayment accounts. 
  1. Responsible for managing the delivery of accurate and timely billing functions through the supervision of the Billing Supervisor. This includes ensuring all cycle billing, final billing, manual billing, sub-metering, consolidated billing, hydrant meter billing, and sewer deducts have accurately met all departmental deadlines.
  1. Oversees the process of the Customer Information System (CIS) and is responsible for the accuracy of all bill calculations and adjustments related to complex billing errors. 
  1. Responsible for reporting and documenting errors that occur within the Customer Information System (CIS) as well as testing the resolution of errors reported back from the vendor.
  1. Manages performance of staff by developing goals, coaching for improvement; the administration of disciplinary action as needed. 
  1. Resolves any issues by reporting what may impact the efficient operation of the team or division to the Director of Customer Service. 
  1. Assists in the development of new processes and projects associated with technology enhancements prior to introducing it to the division. In addition, provide insight and recommendations for operational improvements within the department for efficiencies as well as provide strong leadership motivational qualities to team members.  
  1. Assists in testing and documenting results with new projects as they come on board. 
  1. Assists with the both capital and operational departmental budgets. 
  1. Assists with vendor contracts.
  1. Responsible for employee hiring and onboarding as well as creation, modification and implementation of team training programs in partnership with the departmental team trainer.

Minimum Qualifications

  1. A Bachelor degree or minimum of 5 years relevant work experience.

About this job

Support reliable operation of water and wastewater treatment facilities through preventive and corrective maintenance of pumps, motors, valves, and related equipment. Position involves diagnosing equipment issues, monitoring performance trends, and implementing maintenance strategies to maximize asset reliability.

Good fit if you have mechanical experience with treatment facility equipment and knowledge of predictive maintenance techniques like vibration analysis and condition monitoring.

Full job description

General Description


Salary:
  Plant Mechanic I: $22.34 - $27.91 Hourly
 Plant Mechanic II: $25.60 - $34.08 Hourly
 Senior Plant Mechanic: $27.36 - $36.45 Hourly
 Master Plant Mechanic: $32.77 - $46.82 Hourly
The purpose of this position is to support the reliable and efficient operation of Water and/or Wastewater Treatment Facilities through predictive, preventive, and corrective maintenance of plant systems and equipment. This position is responsible for monitoring equipment condition, identifying early indicators of mechanical failure, and implementing maintenance strategies that maximize asset reliability and minimize unplanned downtime. Duties include diagnosing, troubleshooting, repairing, and replacing a variety of pumps, motors, valves, and other mechanical equipment; analyzing equipment performance trends; and recommending repairs, upgrades, and maintenance schedules to extend asset life and improve operational performance. 
The ideal candidate is passionate about equipment reliability and proactive maintenance. They possess a strong mechanical aptitude and experience maintaining critical treatment facility equipment, including pumps, motors, valves, gearboxes, and related systems. They are skilled in predictive maintenance techniques such as vibration analysis, lubrication management, condition monitoring, precision alignment, and equipment performance trending. The candidate can effectively diagnose mechanical issues, identify early indicators of failure, and implement maintenance strategies that improve asset reliability, reduce downtime, and extend equipment life. They communicate effectively across operations and maintenance teams, maintain accurate records within the CMMS, and are committed to safety, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

Essential Functions

Plant Mechanic I:

  1. Repairs and replaces various equipment by utilizing truck cranes, hand tools, and electrical meters; locking out tag out; removing debris from impeller and volutes; monitoring motor oil, power cords, bells; assessing conditions; and performing monthly PM's.
  2. Troubleshoots for errors by monitoring meg and ohm motors; checking electrical voltages, components, wiring, and connections; checking floats and transducers; and utilizing Schematic diagrams.
  3. Maintains generators and performs administrative work by conducting preventative maintenance; installing by pass and generators; hooking up power cables; assisting on vac trucks; checking e-mails and SCADA readings; creating work orders; attending monthly safety meetings; and overseeing pagers, phones, and radios.
  4. Manages confined spaces by utilizing gas monitors, oxygen tanks, tripods, etc.; calibrating gas monitors; repairing and changing rails; disposing of debris; changing pipes; and repairing brackets and check valves.
  5. Maintains trucks by inspecting vehicles, lights, gauges, tires, tools, oils, belts, etc.; and inspecting cranes.
  6. All other duties as assigned.

Plant Mechanic II:

  1. Repairs and replaces various equipment by utilizing truck cranes, hand tools, and electrical meters; locking out tag out; removing debris from impellor and volutes; monitoring motor oil, power cords, bells; assessing conditions; and performing monthly PM's.
  2. Troubleshoots for errors by back-flushing check valves; monitoring meg and ohm motors; checking electrical voltages, components, wiring, and connections; checking floats and transducers; and utilizing Schematic diagrams.
  3. Performs administrative work by checking e-mails; overseeing SCADA readings; creating work orders; attending monthly safety meetings and training events; managing credit card statements; supervising pagers and radios; analyzing spill reports and root causes; and creating stand-by and weekend report timesheets.
  4. Performs inspections by checking exit lights and fire extinguishers; overseeing equipment, trucks, and crane; checking confine space trailer equipment; and inspections warehouse and MCC alarm systems.
  5. All other duties as assigned.

Senior Plant Mechanic: 

  1. Understand the principles and processes involved in water and wastewater treatment, including filtration, sedimentation, disinfection, and chemical treatment.
  2. Familiarity with Toho Water standards and specifications, ensuring all equipment meets criteria.
  3. Ability to identify the need for and to submit GIS red lines for system updates.
  4. Ability to analyze data from monitoring equipment and make adjustments to optimize plant performance and efficiency.
  5. Demonstrate proficiency in welding and fabrication techniques to repair or members are informed and compliant with safety regulations.
  6. Proficiency in using computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS) and other software tools for scheduling maintenance, managing inventory, and documenting work activities.
  7. Demonstrate expertise in performing precision shaft alignment to ensure accurate alignment between motors, pumps, gearboxes, and other machinery components to reduce vibration, prevent premature wear, and extend equipment life in accordance with manufacturer specifications and industry standards.
  8. Identify need for confined space entry. Demonstrate understanding of procedures and oversee a team in performing confined space entry, ensuring adherence to safety protocols and regulations.
  9. Demonstrate an understanding of plumbing principles and the ability to work with pipes, fitting, and fixtures to ensure proper installation and functionality.
  10. Demonstrate proficiency in completing pre-hurricane preparation (72 hours prior) and level III hurricane response (36 hours prior) checklists, including placement of generators/bypass pumps for optimal response.
  11. Ability to effectively communicate with team members, supervisors and other stakeholders to coordinate tasks, report findings, and collaborate on projects.
  12. Identify training needs, develop and deliver a training presentation to the department.
  13. Demonstrate skill in handling escalated situations with customers/contractors effectively, maintaining professionalism and resolving issues promptly.

Master Plant Mechanic: 

  1. Demonstrate ability to effectively lead and coordinate a crew, delegating tasks and ensuring efficient workflow.
  2. Demonstrate proficiency in assigning work orders and generating preventative maintenance tasks within INFOR or CityWorks system.
  3. Demonstrate understanding or incident reporting protocols and procedures. Ability to accurately complete supervisor incident reports.
  4. Demonstrate understanding of payroll processes and procedures within ADP. Ability to effectively validate timesheets for payroll purposes.
  5. Proficient in interpreting and comprehending construction and engineering drawings. Demonstrate ability to accurately interpret plan designs for maintenance and repair tasks.
  6. Familiarity with equipment procurement processes and capital budgeting principles.
  7. Demonstrate knowledge of standby protocols and procedures and ability to effectively manage standby operations.
  8. Experience in implementing preventative maintenance programs to ensure optimal performance and longevity of equipment. Proficiency in planning and scheduling maintenance activities.
  9. Demonstrate an understanding of performance management policies and procedures. Participate in employee performance review process to evaluate employee performance. Provide assistance with processes related to documentation of employee conduct.
  10. Understanding of relevant regulations and guidelines governing treatment operations, including environmental standards and reporting requirements.
  11. Ability to evaluate entire system’s performance and understand how mechanical components interact with electrical and control systems.
  12. Demonstrated competency in time management and resources allocation for repair projects.
  13. Commitment to staying updated on advancements in water treatment technology, industry best practices, and relevant certifications or training opportunities.

Minimum Qualifications

Plant Mechanic I:

  1. A minimum of a high school diploma or GED issued from an approved GED Administrator.
  2. Minimum of one-year work experience with a focus on pump, motors, and/or controls.
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License.
  5. A CDL Class A with Hazmat License is preferred but not required. Must be able to obtain State of Florida Class A Driver's License within first six months of employment.

Master Plant Mechanic:

  2. Minimum of ten years’ relevant work experience working in either a utility or Industrial setting with a focus on motors, pumps, piping and control.

The Business Process Specialist is responsible for analyzing, documenting, modeling, and improving business processes across the organization to enhance operational efficiency, service quality, and organizational effectiveness. This role works closely with the Business Transformation Manager to facilitate process discovery workshops, develop process models using BPMN standards, identify improvement opportunities, and support the implementation of process changes.

The Business Process Specialist will work closely with the business stakeholders to document and improve processes across the entire enterprise. He/ she will serve as a bridge between business units and technology teams, ensuring that business requirements, process documentation, and improvement initiatives are effectively aligned with organizational objectives. While the primary focus of the role is process management and continuous improvement, the position also supports technology-related initiatives by collaborating with IT teams, reviewing system impacts, and helping translate business needs into functional requirements as and when necessary.

The ideal candidate is passionate about understanding how work gets done and helping teams improve it. They are comfortable leading process modeling workshops, documenting workflows using BPMN standards, applying Lean Six Sigma techniques, and partnering with both business and technology teams to deliver sustainable process improvements. They can effectively facilitate conversations, challenge assumptions, and translate ideas into actionable process improvements.

Essential Functions

Business Process Management

  • Facilitate process discovery, process mapping, and process improvement workshops with stakeholders across the organization.
  • Document current-state and future-state business processes using BPMN (Business Process Model and Notation) standards.
  • Maintain and govern process documentation repositories to ensure consistency, accuracy, and accessibility.
  • Analyze workflows, procedures, and business operations to identify inefficiencies, bottlenecks, risks, and improvement opportunities.
  • Develop process maps, swim lane diagrams, value stream maps, and supporting documentation.
  • Assist business units in defining process performance measures and key performance indicators (KPIs).
  • Support the development and maintenance of process governance standards, methodologies, and best practices.

Continuous Improvement

  • Apply Lean, Six Sigma, and other continuous improvement methodologies to improve business performance.
  • Conduct root cause analyses and facilitate problem-solving sessions.
  • Recommend process improvements that reduce waste, improve customer experience, enhance compliance, and increase operational effectiveness.
  • Support implementation and change management activities associated with process improvement initiatives.
  • Monitor and measure the effectiveness of implemented process changes.

Business and Technology Collaboration

  • Collaborate with business and IT stakeholders to understand process and system dependencies.
  • Analyze how applications and technology solutions support business processes and identify alignment opportunities.
  • Participate in software implementation, workflow automation, and digital transformation initiatives as needed.
  • Support user acceptance testing (UAT), process validation, and solution adoption activities.

Stakeholder Engagement

  • Build collaborative relationships with leaders, subject matter experts, and frontline employees.
  • Facilitate workshops, interviews, and cross-functional working sessions to elicit process knowledge and improvement opportunities.
  • Present findings, recommendations, and process models to stakeholders at various organizational levels.
  • Provide guidance and coaching on process management methodologies and standards (if needed)

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Bachelor’s degree in relevant field
  2. 1-3 years process mapping/analysis
  3. Awareness of flowcharts and swimlane diagrams
  4. Awareness of basic Lean and Six Sigma concepts
  5. Facilitate SME interviews to document process models
  6. Able to harvest requirements in documented process
  7. Process maps, SOPs, workflows
  8. Analyze workflows and KPIs

The purpose of this position is to operate and maintain the wastewater treatment plant and the drinking water for the public. This is accomplished by collecting daily meter readings; calibrating lab meters; checking plant equipment; adjusting the SCADA computer; checking charts for trends; performing oil changes and greasing; repairing equipment; collecting daily plant samples; recording dissolved oxygen readings; inspecting chlorine cylinders; communicating problems; creating and fulfilling work orders; completing plant and system checks; verifying equipment operation; evaluating trends; and verifying chemical residuals. Other duties include performing UV maintenance and repair; training employees; troubleshooting for plant malfunctions; creating monthly operation reports; managing monthly water charts and plumage reports; developing a majority of the forms the Water Plants uses; replying to e-mails; performing janitorial work; overseeing fire flow tests; and supervising contractors.

Essential Functions

Trainee:

  1. Performs all operational procedures by checking clarifier blankets; obtaining samples; checking equipment; performing inspections on SCADA communications; cleaning channels or splitter boxes; checking water plants and other facilities; performing preventive maintenance; and administering plant tours.
  2. Communicates with customers and community by sending daily emails; creating reports and facility updates; recording all calibrations of meters or analyzers; inputting data in OPS PAC; developing work orders; directing team meetings; and communicating with bio-solids staff, vendors, and visitors.
  3. Performs all housekeeping duties by hosing down areas with debris; addressing safety concerns; checking for proper drainage; painting; disposing of trash; assisting with landscaping or beautification projects; and ensuring the facility is maintained.
  4. Collects samples for analysis by using gloves and caution in sampling areas; managing sampling containers carefully; avoiding contamination; fulfilling chain of custody forms; and obtaining all information for chain of custody forms.
Operator I (C License):
 1.  Performs daily water plant checks by checking all equipment; monitoring hour meters and flow meters; checking chemical residuals; changing chemical analyzers; maintaining chemical inventory; transferring and inspecting chemicals; calibrating test kits; and adjusting feed rates.
 2.   Maintains the plant by completing maintenance work orders; greasing plant equipment; managing rust/corrosion control; and performing housekeeping practices and general cleaning.
 3.  Manages plant repairs by scheduling work orders for internal repair; ensuring all plant equipment in repaired; and assisting mechanics and electricians when necessary.
 4.   All other duties as assigned.

Operator II (B License):
 1.  Performs preventive maintenance by shutting off power; locking out equipment; greasing moving equipment; changing oils in gearboxes; guaranteeing all maintenance activities are safe; and painting equipment.
 2. Controls processes by checking process basins; using odor sensory perception and results from laboratory tests; reviewing the performance of the process; and overseeing the SCADA system.
 3. Performs housekeeping duties by cleaning for spider webs; removing all dirt and debris; maintaining materials and equipment; and ensuring the facility is aesthetically pleasing.
 4. Gives plant tours by evaluating the process and equipment in the treatment process; obtaining daily readings from meters and gauges; maintaining records; and ensuring all equipment functions properly.
 5. Maintains facility logbooks by recording duties and projects; maintaining a record of compliance issues; and maintaining entries of process issues and the integrity of the logbook.
 6. Obtains samples for analysis by using gloves and caution when approaching sampling areas; handling sampling containers carefully; closing sample containers promptly; filling out chain of custody forms; and collecting information for chain of custody form.

The purpose of this position is to operate and maintain the water treatment plant and the drinking water for the public. General Description

The Director of Treatment Facility Engineering is a senior leadership position within Toho’s Engineering group, responsible for leading the planning, design, and delivery of critical treatment facility infrastructure that supports the organization’s operational, regulatory and strategic objectives. This position provides leadership and direction for a portfolio of complex capital improvement projects while fostering technical excellence, organizational capability, and continuous improvement across the program area. 

The Director is responsible for the engineering and design of water treatment facilities, wastewater treatment facilities, reclaimed water systems, supplemental water supply development, storage and pumping infrastructure, and other critical utility assets. The Director also serves as a key stakeholder and partner in long-range planning and capital project development and provides technical leadership throughout construction, commissioning, and operational startup. This role serves as a trusted advisor to the Chief Engineering and Construction Officer, helping translate strategic priorities into actionable programs, projects and engineering solutions.

Key Focus Areas

Deliver Complex Treatment Facility Projects 

Lead the engineering and design of large-scale and technically complex treatment facility projects while also serving as a key stakeholder and advisor in adjoining portions of the project lifecycle including planning, construction, commissioning, and startup.  Ensure projects are delivered safely, efficiently, and in alignment with organizational objectives, regulatory requirements, operational needs, budget expectations, and long-term infrastructure strategies. 

Advance Strategic Planning and Risk Mitigation 

Support the development and execution of the organization’s infrastructure vision by identifying emerging needs and create sustainable strategies that position Toho for future growth and service demands.   Proactively evaluate project risks, resource requirements, schedule impacts and operational considerations to ensure successful project delivery. 

Develop Future Engineering Leaders 

Build and strengthen organizational capability by mentoring engineers, project managers, and emerging leaders.  Foster a culture of accountability, innovation, collaboration and continuous learning while supporting employee development, succession planning, and technical excellence across the Engineering Group. 

Success in this role requires technical leadership and development of trusted partnerships across the organization, collaborating with Operations, Engineering, consultants, contractors, regulatory agencies, and community stakeholders to advance strategic infrastructure investments, manage risk, and deliver sustainable, long-term value.

Essential Functions

  1. Provides technical leadership for the planning, design, and delivery of water treatment, wastewater treatment, reclaimed water, pumping, storage, supplemental water supply, and other treatment-related infrastructure projects.
  2. Collaborates with Operations, Planning, Engineering, Construction, the Program Management Office (PMO), consultants, contractors, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders to develop and deliver effective infrastructure solutions that support organizational objectives.
  3. Leads the planning, development, justification, and execution of the capital improvement program within the assigned program area, ensuring alignment with long-term infrastructure, operational, regulatory, and financial strategies.
  4. Provides technical leadership and support throughout the project lifecycle, including project development, preliminary engineering, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and operational startup.
  5. Directs engineering consultants, contractors, and technical service providers, including procurement, contract negotiations, technical oversight, performance management, and resolution of complex project challenges.
  6. Reviews and approves engineering reports, calculations, drawings, specifications, schedules, bid documents, construction deliverables, and other technical documentation to ensure quality, consistency, and operational reliability.
  7. Interprets and manages regulatory requirements associated with assigned facilities and projects and proactively identifies compliance risks and opportunities.
  8. Develops and maintains engineering standards, technical specifications, design criteria, and related procedures to promote consistency, quality, operational effectiveness, and long-term asset performance.
  9. Coaches, mentors, and develops engineers, project managers, and emerging leaders while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and technical excellence.
  10. Serves as a trusted technical advisor to executive leadership, operational teams, Board members, member governments, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
  11. Develops capital budgets, project forecasts, technical reports, presentations, Board agenda items, and other materials necessary to support project execution and decision-making.
  12. May serve as Engineer of Record and sign and seal engineering documents associated with internal projects.
  13. Maintains awareness of emerging technologies, industry trends, regulatory developments, and best practices to advance organizational performance and infrastructure outcomes.
  14. Supports and promotes workplace safety in accordance with Toho policies and procedures.
  15. May represent the Chief Engineering and Construction Officer in internal and external meetings as delegated.
  16. Performs all other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Bachelor's degree from an ABET accredited university in Civil, Chemical, Mechanical, Environmental Engineering, or related discipline.
  2. Minimum of eight years relevant experience.
  3. Florida Professional Engineer License or the ability to obtain within 12 months.
  4. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  5. Must possess (or have the ability to obtain within 90 days) and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver's License 

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS & ABILITIES:

  1. Extensive knowledge of the planning, design, construction, commissioning, operation, and optimization of water treatment, wastewater treatment, reclaimed water, pumping, storage, and alternative water supply facilities.
  2. Demonstrated ability to build trusted partnerships and effectively collaborate with Operations, Planning, Engineering, Construction, consultants, contractors, regulatory agencies, and other stakeholders.
  3. Demonstrated ability to lead large, complex, and technically challenging capital programs and infrastructure projects.
  4. Strong understanding of applicable engineering principles, regulatory requirements, industry standards, and utility best practices.
  5. Exceptional leadership, coaching, mentoring, and team development skills.
  6. Strong strategic thinking, risk management, analytical, and problem-solving abilities.
  7. Excellent verbal, written, and presentation communication skills, including the ability to communicate complex technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  8. Strong project and program management skills, including management of scope, schedule, budget, quality, and organizational resources.
  9. Ability to collect, analyze, interpret, and apply technical, operational, regulatory, and financial information to support decision-making.
  10. Ability to prioritize competing demands, manage resources effectively, and deliver results in a fast-paced environment.
  11. Skilled in negotiation, conflict resolution, and consensus building.
  12. Demonstrated commitment to customer service, continuous improvement, accountability, and safety.

The purpose of this position is to provide support on critical applications and department operations.  This is accomplished by performing technical work for the operation, performance, and maintenance of the Toho Water Authority Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) system. This system monitors and controls water, wastewater, lifts-stations, and reuse-distribution facilities. Under supervision and direction of the SCADA Manager, perform tasks related to the planning, asset management, programming, network configuration, testing, calibration, commissioning, and preventive maintenance of SCADA and related electrical control systems. Lead internal SCADA projects. Perform design and implementation of control and communication systems.

Essential Functions

  1. Manage SCADA system equipment, components, and assets.
  2. Take the lead in troubleshooting SCADA network communication problems.
  3. Maintain, analyze, and improve network system performance.
  4. Improve existing methodologies to ensure proper network system operation and security.
  5. Set-up Ethernet networks, computers and other HMI (Human Machine Interface) equipment for communication with field equipment using established industrial protocols.
  6. Program, install, and test switches, routers, modems and other network equipment.
  7. Test and run diagnostics to verify connectivity of equipment.
  8. Deploy system patches and firmware updates.
  9. Program PLCs for both control and process information gathering and reporting.
  10. Perform any other needed programming, updates, or diagnostics of the SCADA system.
  11. Develop, and update, equipment databases, software licenses, device applications and configurations.
  12. Develop and implement methods for backing up all systems including PLCs to maintain a current library of all custom applications, and ensure all data is retrievable.
  13. Maintain technical library, accurate records, documentation, work reports. Modify existing documents and drawings and incorporate red line markups as needed.
  14. Advise SCADA Manager of needed technology upgrades and assist in planning for upgrades. Collect historical information. Provide input and cost information for budgets.
  15. Develop specifications for vendors for repairs, upgrades, and new installation work.
  16. Manage equipment and software inventory, including spares, and order replacement equipment and software as needed. Maintain warranty information.
  17. Train technicians & operations staff in operation and maintenance of SCADA and PLCs.
  18. Confer with contractors, operators, mechanics, project engineers and supervisors about SCADA issues.
  19. Respond to and resolve internal customer complaints and issues.
  20. Provide documentation as required by others.
  21. Follow procurement rules to order parts.
  22. Understand and practice safe work procedures such as the NFPA 70E, and OSHA
  23. Gives plant data and backups by tagging databases to reports and iHistorian server; creating reports; updating Human Machine Interface screens; backing up Department of Environmental Protection documents; and backing up GE Intelligent Platform.
  24. Performs administrative duties by attending various meetings; training employees; completing work orders; maintaining vehicles; and answering e-mails. Condition facility assessments, meet with vendors.
  25. All other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

  1. Associate's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or Electronics or 4 years related field experience.
  2. 6 years’ experience in SCADA control systems development and maintenance in lieu of the education requirement.
  3. Any combination of education and experience which demonstrates the candidate’s ability to perform successfully in this position will be considered.
  4. Must possess and maintain a valid State of Florida Class E Driver’s License.
DESIRABLE QUALIFICATIONS: 
  1. ISA – CCST Certification
  2. SANS GIAC Certification
  3. ISA – 62443 Certifications
  4. ISA – CAP Certification

About this job

Grant Coordinator for Orange County Sheriff's Office manages law enforcement grants including researching opportunities, preparing applications, and producing financial and program reports. Starting salary is $54,620.80 to $56,264.00 annually based on experience.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree in public administration or related field plus two years of grant management experience, or four years of direct grant experience.

Full job description

JOB SUMMARY

Starting Salary: ($26.26 hourly) $54,620.80/yr or ($27.05 hourly) $56,264.00/yr. with 3+ years of experience



MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS & ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS

Performs professional grant coordinating functions while implementing and managing law enforcement grants. The primary duties include researching grant opportunities, preparing grant applications, maintaining and managing grant documentation, producing programmatic and financial grant reports, evaluating/analyzing programs, grant performance measurement, and special projects. Work is performed under general supervision and is reviewed while in progress and upon completion. #oj

Minimum Requirements
  • At least 18 years of age.
  • Must be able to comprehend and communicate fluently in verbal and written English.
  • U.S. Citizen or possess a current permanent resident card.
  • Clean criminal history; any arrest history will be individually evaluated.
  • No illegal drug usage within the past year. Other drug usage will be evaluated on a case by case basis.
  • Bachelor’s (B.A. or B.S.) degree from four-year college or university in Public Administration, Business Administration or related field AND a minimum of two (2) years of experience in grant management, budget analysis or other related grant experience. Additional years of experience may substitute for up to two (2) years of education. 
  • If this posting indicates a degree is required, the following experience will apply in lieu of any degree as follows:

    • Four (4) years of direct experience for a Bachelor's Degree

  • Must have a valid Florida driver’s license. Must attend and successfully complete the agency sponsored Law Enforcement Vehicle Operations (LEVO) Training if assignment includes driving agency vehicle. Use of agency vehicle would require appropriate driving history and passing agency biennial driver’s physical exam.
  • Identifies grant opportunities via web research, listserves, networking and other methods.
  • Consults with personnel affected by proposed applications to develop goals and objectives. Coordinates procedures, required compliance, and mandated guidelines necessary to obtain grant funding.  
  • Prepares grant applications for submittal to local agencies, the State, and Federal Government.
  • Prepares grant documents for the Sheriff, Board of County Commissioners, and the granting agency.
  • Manages and maintains master files on grants for auditing and compliance requirements.
  • Coordinates evaluation and monitoring of the grant funded programs, which includes collection and analysis of data. Prepares periodic financial and program reports to comply with grant requirements. Assists grant monitors and auditors as necessary. 
  • Serves as liaison for grant administration with the Orange County Sheriff’s Office, local agencies, and State and Federal Government.  Attends meetings and presents materials to various boards, committees, and grant program managers.
  • Coordinates, prepares, and submits grant-related budget adjustments, monthly claims, and other monthly, quarterly and/or annual reports to the grantor.   
  • Performs other special projects as assigned.
  • Ability to read, analyze, and interpret general business periodicals, professional journals, technical procedures, or governmental regulations.  
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, employees, government officials, foundation board members and/or the general public. 
  • Must have knowledge of grant application process and writing of applications. 
  • Must have advanced writing skills to include creative writing and grammatical proficiency. 
  • Ability to prepare clear and concise written reports/correspondences. 
  • Knowledge of various law enforcement related grant programs available from local agencies, the State, and Federal Government. Knowledge of management research principle techniques, methods, systems analysis, and performance measures. 
  • Knowledge of county administration and organization, functions, budgets, and operations. 
  • Must have proficient computer skills to include MS Word, MS Excel, and basic computer applications.  
  • Ability to interpret and ensure compliance with applicable policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.  
  • Ability to conduct research and compile technical data for the preparation of grant proposals. 
  • Ability to track and monitor various projects and programs. 
  • Ability to assign and review the work of others.  
  • Ability to plan, prioritize, and coordinate multiple projects.  
  • Ability to establish and maintain effective working relations with employees, both sworn and civilian.  
  • Ability to work independently.  Ability to apply basic mathematical concepts, such as computing interest, proportions, percentages, and discounts.

  • PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

    • Experience in a governmental agency preferred. 
    • Experience with 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Chapter I & II, Part 200, et al., also preferred.


PROCESSING & TRAINING

ADDITIONAL PROCESSING:

PHYSICAL DEMANDS & WORK ENVIRONMENT


PHYSICAL DEMANDS
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, talk, and hear. The employee is frequently required to stand, walk, and use hands to handle or feel. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision.

WORK ENVIRONMENT
