About Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride:

In November 2013, Orlando City Soccer Club was awarded a Major League Soccer (MLS) franchise, becoming the league’s 21st franchise. The team began play in March 2015, with 62,510 fans packing the then-Orlando Citrus Bowl for the Club’s MLS debut.

The Lions have reached the postseason in five-consecutive seasons (2020-24), qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup (formerly Concacaf Champions League) in both 2023 and 2024, and reached their first final in 2020 during the MLS is Back Tournament. In 2022, Orlando City won its first championship of its MLS era, lifting the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup trophy, which also marked the first championship by any professional team in the City Beautiful. Prior to its time in MLS, Orlando City boasted a decorated history in the United Soccer League, winning the league’s championship in both the 2011 and 2013 seasons.

In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win.

The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. Former Orlando City defender Seb Hines serves as the team’s head coach, not only the first Black head coach in the league, but also the first to win both the Championship and the NWSL Shield, and the 2024 NWSL Coach of the Year.

In 2017, both teams moved into its privately-owned, soccer-specific venue – Inter&Co Stadium – located in the heart of downtown Orlando.

In July 2021, the Club – which includes Orlando City SC, the Orlando Pride, Orlando City B (MLS NEXT Pro) and Inter&Co Stadium – was purchased by the Wilf Family, who also own the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League.

TITLE: Part-Time Stadium Security Guard
DEPARTMENT: Stadium Operations
REPORTS TO: Security Manager
FLSA: Part Time; Non-Exempt

What Sets You Apart

We are looking for an honest, attentive, and perceptive individual to join our Security team. In this role, you will help secure Inter.Co Stadium and protect the Club’s property, guests, teammates, and players. You will help maintain a safe and secure environment while serving as a visible security presence and deterrent to unauthorized or irregular activity.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Patrol Inter.Co Stadium property to monitor and prevent intrusion, damage, hazards, and security breaches.
  • Lock and unlock doors and conduct facility walkthroughs as needed.
  • Provide a visible presence that promotes and enforces safety and security.
  • Monitor activity throughout the facility via closed-circuit television (CCTV).
  • Respond appropriately to emergencies, including but not limited to fire and burglar alarms.
  • Monitor access to the venue on event and non-event days.
  • Assist with event-day security coverage.
  • Identify and address unauthorized persons and violations of security procedures.
  • Contact appropriate authorities regarding unlawful or irregular activity when necessary.
  • Use radios and other communication devices in a clear, concise, and professional manner.
  • Document and report malfunctions, misconduct, incidents, and operational or safety concerns.
  • Interview victims and witnesses and prepare incident reports as necessary.
  • Maintain a professional appearance and demeanor.
  • Implement prescribed emergency procedures when necessary.
  • Assist with the development and implementation of public safety plans for day-to-day operations and special events.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

It’s never just a job at Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride. It’s a way of life. We live and breathe soccer and entertainment. We believe each role is as unique as the person who does it. To join our team, you will also possess these qualifications:

  • High school diploma, G.E.D., or equivalent required.
  • College coursework in Criminal Justice, Private Investigations, Homeland Security, Emergency Management, Emergency Medical Services, or another security-related field is preferred. Relevant military experience is also preferred.
  • Six (6) months to one (1) year of security experience, preferably in a similar environment.
  • Bilingual in Spanish or Portuguese is preferred.
  • Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to establish rapport and build positive working relationships.
  • Basic computer skills, including Microsoft Office.
  • Ability to successfully complete required background screening and employment verification.
  • Valid Florida driver’s license required.
  • Valid Florida Class “D” Security Officer License required.
  • Appropriate credentials as mandated by state, county, or local law.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

Physical Demands

  • Must be able to lift and/or move up to 50 pounds.
  • Must be able to walk, run, kneel, climb stairs, and react quickly to unpredictable situations.
  • Must be able to work both indoors and outdoors, including exposure to varying weather conditions.
  • Must be able to sit or stand for prolonged periods, including while monitoring surveillance equipment.

The physical demands described herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the core functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing duties, the employee may be regularly required to stand or sit for extended periods, walk long distances, use hands to handle, hold or feel objects, tools, or controls, reach with arms, and talk or hear. Vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. The employee is required to hear conversations in noisy environments. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. TITLE:  Sports Turf Specialist, Stadium
DEPARTMENT:  Stadium Operations

What Sets You Apart

Are you a self-motivated individual with physical stamina? Do you love the outdoors and maintaining aesthetically pleasing outdoor space? If so, our Sports Turf Specialist role could be for you. You will be responsible for mowing, fertilization, edging, irrigation troubleshooting and repair, top dressing, aerating, painting, sodding, and record keeping for the Inter.co Stadium. You will get a chance to use a variety of practical skills which are valuable and essential to the overall Club.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities:

  • Assist with all operations of field maintenance at Inter.co Stadium to include painting, mowing, irrigation, aerification, chemical application and any special projects as needed
  • Proactively identify turf grass diseases, weeds, pests, and work with Director of Turf & Grounds and Grounds Supervisor to take corrective action as needed
  • Assist in equipment and irrigation repair and maintenance
  • Work MLS games, NWSL games and third party events based on business needs
  • Create and maintain good working relationships with all MLS and NWSL coaches and soccer operations staff
  • Participate in procuring equipment and supplies as needed for the facility
  • Provide coverage at the training facilities as needed
  • Other duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • It’s never just a job at Orlando City SC and Orlando Pride.  It’s a way of life. We live and breathe soccer and entertainment. We believe each role is as unique as the person who does it. To join our team, you will also possess these qualifications:

About Orlando City SC & Orlando Pride:

In November 2013, Orlando City Soccer Club was awarded a Major League Soccer (MLS) franchise, becoming the league’s 21st franchise. The team began play in March 2015, with 62,510 fans packing the then-Orlando Citrus Bowl for the Club’s MLS debut.

The Lions have reached the postseason in five-consecutive seasons (2020-24), qualified for the Concacaf Champions Cup (formerly Concacaf Champions League) in both 2023 and 2024, and reached their first final in 2020 during the MLS is Back Tournament. In 2022, Orlando City won its first championship of its MLS era, lifting the Lamar Hunt U.S. Open Cup trophy, which also marked the first championship by any professional team in the City Beautiful. Prior to its time in MLS, Orlando City boasted a decorated history in the United Soccer League, winning the league’s championship in both the 2011 and 2013 seasons.

In October 2015, the Orlando Pride was announced as the 10th team in the National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL), bringing professional women’s soccer to the state of Florida for the first time. The team began play in April 2016, setting a then-league single-game attendance record in its first-ever home game, with 23,403 fans witnessing the Club’s first win.

The Pride feature a star-studded roster of domestic and international talent and, in 2024, brought the first professional major league title to the city of Orlando, with the Club winning the NWSL Championship. The season saw the Pride complete the double, winning both the Championship and the NWSL Shield as the best team in the regular season, capping off a historic campaign that set numerous league records. Former Orlando City defender Seb Hines serves as the team’s head coach, not only the first Black head coach in the league, but also the first to win both the Championship and the NWSL Shield, and the 2024 NWSL Coach of the Year.

In 2017, both teams moved into its privately-owned, soccer-specific venue – Inter&Co Stadium – located in the heart of downtown Orlando.

In July 2021, the Club – which includes Orlando City SC, the Orlando Pride, Orlando City B (MLS NEXT Pro) and Inter&Co Stadium – was purchased by the Wilf Family, who also own the Minnesota Vikings of the National Football League.

For more information on Orlando City SC and Orlando, visit OrlandoCitySC.com or Orlando-Pride.com.

Center for Student Care and Advocacy:

The Center for Student Care & Advocacy (CSCA) serves as a centralized, student-centered resource dedicated to supporting the holistic well-being, basic needs, personal development, and academic success of University of Central Florida students. The Center provides an integrated approach to student support that recognizes the interconnectedness of students’ academic, personal, and basic-needs experiences.

 

The Opportunity:

UCF's Center for Student Care and Advocacy — a center committed to holistic student well-being — is seeking a skilled and professional Associate Director, Student Care Services to lead the daily review and prioritization of student-of-concern reports related to mental health, well-being, and basic needs support. This is a non-clinical student advocacy and support opportunity that does not require clinical licensure, diagnosis, or formal case management. The position is centered on proactive outreach, referral coordination, and direct partnership with students navigating mental health and wellness challenges — including those presenting moderate to high levels of distress. This work calls for professionalism and genuine commitment when engaging with students in crisis, as well as with the families, faculty, and staff who are concerned about a student's well-being. This role provides purposeful, person-centered leadership to advance student success, campus safety, and community well-being.

 

Responsibilities:

Daily Case Management & Triage

  • Review and prioritize student-of-concern referrals related to mental health, well-being, and basic needs support on a daily basis.

Student Support & Advocacy

  • Address the needs of students experiencing challenges related to mental health, physical health, psychosocial adjustment, personal and family emergencies, financial difficulties, or other circumstances requiring general assistance.
  • Provide guidance and advocacy to help students navigate the university environment and connect with the wide range of available campus and community resources, while prioritizing student well-being, academic persistence, and overall success.
  • Assist students in setting goals, developing customized action plans, and connecting them to appropriate academic, career, health, social, financial, and holistic care resources on campus.
  • Provide consultation to students and families on referrals to University and community resources, University policy interpretation, and family support.
  • Cross-train to support students with basic needs.

Crisis Response & Safety

  • Collaborate with the Assistant Dean, Dean of Students, or their designee when there are immediate concerns for student or community safety.
  • Assist with requesting wellness checks from UCFPD when needed.
  • Serve on the University Crisis Team as required.

Clinical Processes & Student Reentry

  • Assist with oversight of the Mandated Assessment process when students are returning from involuntary hospitalization, the medical leave process, and/or the involuntary withdrawal process.
  • Oversee students' reentry to UCF to ensure that the appropriate members of the UCF community are notified (Housing, UCFPD, Student Health Services, CAPS, etc.) and that a thorough review of each individual student has taken place prior to their return to campus.

Partnerships & Resource Management

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with Counseling and Psychological Services, Student Health Services, UCFPD, Housing and Residence Life, Victim Services, and both on- and off-campus partners.
  • Establish, oversee, and maintain effective communication and working relationships with campus and community resources (physicians, therapists, life coaches, and hospitals).
  • Work with on- and off-campus partners to develop intervention plans and facilitate the rapid resolution of issues to support student success.
  • Maintain a current directory of community resources available to students.

Leadership & Consultation

  • Provide leadership to the Dean of Students Office, the Center for Student Care and Advocacy, and other campus entities on mental health and well-being strategies.
  • Assist in leading the weekly cross-divisional Student of Concern team meetings and develop action plans as appropriate.
  • Facilitate and provide consultation on meetings with students, faculty, staff, and family members or guardians on matters such as concerning behavior, individual student support plans and resources, and University and community procedures, processes, and follow-up.

University Engagement & Committees

  • Serve on division and University committees as required.
  • Present at campus events, including open house, orientation, and others as needed.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's and 6+ years of relevant experience or Masters degree and 4+ years of relevant experience with at least 2+ year(s) of leadership experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., counseling, social work, higher education, public health, or related discipline) by time of hire.
  • Progressive leadership experience in student-facing roles within higher education or secondary education, including full-time experience directly related to the responsibilities of this position.
  • Demonstrated case management experience, including proficiency with case management systems, referral processes, documentation practices, and active follow-up.
  • Knowledge of mental health and wellness issues affecting college student populations, including familiarity with public assistance systems, equity and inclusion frameworks, and community resource mapping.
  • Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, with the ability to engage professionally and effectively with students, faculty, staff, families, and community partners across diverse teams and service environments.
  • Demonstrated crisis management, conflict resolution, and active listening skills, paired with the ability to think strategically and approach complex, sensitive challenges with creativity and sound judgment.
  • Proven track record of reliability, accountability, and goal achievement, with the ability to manage sensitive and confidential information with empathy and appropriate professional boundaries.

About this job

Full job description

Burnett Honors College:

The Burnett Honors College (BHC) provides UCF’s highly academically talented and motivated students with a challenging and unique scholarly experience, creating a strong foundation for future achievements. The BHC strives to create a learning community that fosters excellence, ethical, social and civic responsibility, personal growth, and a passion for lifelong learning. It also aims to provide a transformative, vibrant community that supports academic excellence, encourages interdisciplinary inquiry, and empowers creative problem-solvers to use their talent and passion to address dynamic challenges as future global leaders.

To learn more about the Burnett Honors College and its mission, visit our website honors.ucf.edu.

 

The Opportunity:

The Director of the Office of Prestigious Awards (OPA) provides leadership and strategic direction for the university's efforts to identify, recruit, advise, and support students pursuing nationally and internationally competitive scholarships and fellowships. The Director oversees all aspects of office operations, including student advising, scholarship application processes, institutional nominations and endorsements, faculty engagement, campus outreach, program assessment, and supervision of office personnel.

The Director works collaboratively with faculty, academic departments, university leadership, and external scholarship organizations to identify promising students, help them prepare for competitive scholarship opportunities, and guide them through the application process for nationally and internationally prestigious awards.

The Director also serves as a staff member of the Burnett Honors College and oversees the college's honors scholarship application process, including application coordination, review, and selection procedures.

 

Responsibilities:

Strategic Leadership, Office Administration, and Staff Supervision

  • Provides leadership and oversight of the Office of Prestigious Awards, including establishing program goals, developing policies and procedures, managing office operations, and implementing strategies to increase student participation and success in nationally and internationally competitive scholarship programs.
  • Supervises and provides direction to the program coordinator, graduate assistant, and student assistants, including assigning responsibilities, monitoring performance, and supporting their professional development.

Student Identification and Recruitment

  • Develops and implements strategies to identify and recruit highly qualified undergraduate and graduate students for prestigious scholarships and fellowships.
  • Collaborates with faculty, academic advisors, and university departments to identify promising candidates and encourage their participation in scholarship opportunities.

Individualized Student Advising and Development

  • Provides comprehensive, individualized advising and mentoring to students pursuing competitive scholarships and fellowships.
  • Assists students in evaluating scholarship opportunities, developing competitive academic and professional profiles, preparing application materials, and strengthening their candidacy through research, leadership, service, and other relevant experiences.

Scholarship Application and Institutional Endorsement Oversight

  • Directs and coordinates scholarship application processes, including institutional nomination and endorsement procedures.
  • Ensures compliance with scholarship requirements, institutional policies, and application deadlines.
  • Oversees the preparation, review, and submission of competitive applications and institutional endorsement materials.

Faculty Relations and Scholarship Selection Committees

  • Develops and maintains strong relationships with faculty and academic departments across the university to identify and recruit competitive scholarship candidates.
  •  Recruits faculty members to serve on institutional scholarship selection committees and chairs these committees, coordinating the review, evaluation, and selection of candidates for institutional nomination and endorsement.

Scholarship Writing and Application Development

  • Provides detailed guidance and feedback on personal statements, research proposals, statements of purpose, and other scholarship application materials.
  • Works closely with applicants to strengthen their written materials, articulate their academic and professional goals, and develop compelling applications that align with scholarship selection criteria.

Campus Outreach and Educational Programming

  • Develops and coordinates campus-wide outreach initiatives to increase awareness of prestigious scholarship opportunities.
  • Organizes and delivers informational sessions, workshops, classroom presentations, and other programming for students, faculty, and university departments.

University Partnerships and Collaboration

  • Establishes and maintains collaborative relationships with academic colleges, departments, faculty, administrators, and student support offices to promote scholarship opportunities and strengthen the university's scholarship recruitment and advising efforts.

External Scholarship and Fellowship Relations

  • Serves as the university's institutional representative and primary liaison to national and international scholarship foundations and organizations.
  • Maintains knowledge of scholarship requirements, policies, and selection processes and represents UCF in relevant professional networks and activities.

Program Assessment and Reporting

  • Oversees the collection, maintenance, and analysis of data related to student participation, scholarship applications, institutional nominations, and award outcomes.
  • Prepares annual reports, evaluates program effectiveness, and develops recommendations to strengthen recruitment, advising, and scholarship success.

Marketing, Communications, and Recognition

  • Oversees the development and maintenance of scholarship resources, informational materials, website content, and communications promoting prestigious award opportunities.
  • Collaborates with university partners to publicize student accomplishments and recognize scholarship recipients.

Burnett Honors College Scholarship Administration

  • Serves as a staff member of the Burnett Honors College and manages the college's honors scholarship application process, including coordinating application procedures, communicating with applicants, organizing application reviews, and facilitating scholarship selection processes.

Other Duties

University Operations:

The University Operations division at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.

 

The Opportunity:

Join our team as a Controls Specialist II where you will play a pivotal role in providing technical support, retro commissioning and first-analysis of HVAC performance investigations for coordinated operations and maintenance of HVAC systems to provide a safe, functional, clean, efficient and attractive learning environment. At this level, the employee is expected to have intermediate skills in HVAC and Controls Systems.

Responsibilities:

  • Perform preventative maintenance on HVAC building automation systems and related equipment in order to ensure continuous operation and prevent equipment interruptions through proactive analysis of the BAS front end and back end software platforms.

  • Proficient in the use of Building Management Systems software such as: Siemens Desigo, Trane, Tracer Ensemble, Tracer Summit, Enteliweb, and WebCTRL.
  • Knowledge of HVAC systems, boilers, chillers, air compressors, fans, and pumps.
  • Experience in repair and maintenance of digital building control systems.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office software (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, etc.) and other computer programs such as Visio is preferred.

  • Ability to read construction drawings and specifications.

Job.JobDescription:
Florida Center for Students with Unique Abilities:

Signed into law by Florida’s governor on January 21, 2016, the Florida Postsecondary Comprehensive Transition Program Act (the Act) (S 1004.6495, FS) established the Florida Center for Students with Unique Abilities at the University of Central Florida (the Center) and charged the Center with managing the Florida Postsecondary Comprehensive Transition Program (FPCTP) application and approval process. The Act also established criteria for FPCTP approval, scholarship awards for eligible students to attend approved programs, grant awards to promote new program development and existing program enhancements, and accountability requirements associated with these opportunities.

The Center works with higher education institutions across Florida to support implementation of the Act in three primary ways: (a) facilitate application and approval of their program that serves students with intellectual disabilities as a FPCTP, (b) provide scholarship awards to students attending an institution’s approved FPCTP, and (c) provide grant funding to foster starting up new and/or enhancing existing programs. These three components of the Center’s work aim directly at achieving the purpose of the Act.

 

The Opportunity:

The Florida Center for Students with Unique Abilities at the College of Community Innovation and Education invites applicants for the Program Assistant Director for Technical Assistance position.  The Program Assistant Director for Technical Assistance provides technical assistance to provide strategic planning to Florida Postsecondary Comprehensive Transition Programs (FPCTPs), support implementation and sustainability, monitor program and student reporting for FPCTPs at Florida state colleges, career technical centers/colleges, and universities as directed in legislation. The Program Assistant Director will lead professional development as well as present comprehensive transition and postsecondary (CTP) program effective practices.

 

Responsibilities:

Florida Center for Students with Unique Abilities:

Signed into law by Florida’s governor on January 21, 2016, the Florida Postsecondary Comprehensive Transition Program Act (the Act) (S 1004.6495, FS) established the Florida Center for Students with Unique Abilities at the University of Central Florida (the Center) and charged the Center with managing the Florida Postsecondary Comprehensive Transition Program (FPCTP) application and approval process. The Act also established criteria for FPCTP approval, scholarship awards for eligible students to attend approved programs, grant awards to promote new program development and existing program enhancements, and accountability requirements associated with these opportunities.

The Center works with higher education institutions across Florida to support implementation of the Act in three primary ways: (a) facilitate application and approval of their program that serves students with intellectual disabilities as a FPCTP, (b) provide scholarship awards to students attending an institution’s approved FPCTP, and (c) provide grant funding to foster starting up new and/or enhancing existing programs. These three components of the Center’s work aim directly at achieving the purpose of the Act.

 

The Opportunity:

The Florida Center for Students with Unique Abilities at the College of Community Innovation and Education invites applicants for the Web Applications Developer I position. The selected candidate will serve as the Florida Center for Students with Unique Abilities (FCSUA) Salesforce developer and administrator, responsible for the technical health of the Center's Salesforce organization and the integrations that connect it to the FCSUA website. The position implements web and data initiatives that are scoped and prioritized through FCSUA's web project intake process, building declarative and programmatic Salesforce solutions, maintaining the integrations and data model that supply the website's public content, and resolving platform, code, and data issues.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Design, build, test, and deploy Salesforce solutions, including Flows, Apex classes and triggers, Lightning Web Components, custom objects and fields, validation and duplicate rules, and other automation, to meet functional requirements for FPCTP program operations, case management, and reporting.
  • Administer the FCSUA Salesforce organization, including user access, profiles and permission sets, Experience Cloud site configuration, security settings, and platform health. Monitor Setup Audit Trail, debug and error logs, and automation outcomes to identify and resolve configuration defects, bugs, and data integrity issues.
  • Develop and maintain the integrations between Salesforce and the FCSUA website and other systems, including REST API connections, data synchronization jobs, authentication, and web-to-Salesforce forms. Diagnose sync failures and server or application errors and coordinate fixes with the infrastructure team.
  • Manage the release and environment lifecycle, including sandbox refreshes, version control, change sets or SFDX deployments, Apex test coverage, and readiness for Salesforce seasonal releases, deprecations, and security updates.
  • Design and maintain the Salesforce data model, report types, and data load and migration tooling that support FPCTP data collection and compliance reporting.
  • Build Experience Cloud pages and Lightning components to FCSUA's web governance and WCAG accessibility standards.
  • Provide technical assistance to FPCTPs and national clients on Salesforce-based tools and the Online Strategic Planning Tool, including access, permission, and impersonation issues escalated through coordinated support.
  • Produce and maintain technical documentation, including data model diagrams, deployment runbooks, code documentation, and release notes.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree and 2 years of relevant experience; or High School Diploma (or equivalent) and 6 years of relevant work experience in lieu of degree, or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Salesforce Administrator and/or Platform Developer experience.
  • Experience with Salesforce Experience Cloud site configuration and security settings.
  • Experience managing release lifecycles, including sandbox management, version control (Git), SFDX or change set deployments, and Apex test coverage.
  • Working knowledge of Salesforce declarative tools (Flows, validation rules, permission sets) and programmatic development (Apex, SOQL, and Lightning Web Components, JavaScript, HTML, CSS).
  • Experience building or maintaining system integrations using REST APIs.

College of Nursing Finance Business Center:

A leader in nursing education for more than 40 years, UCF College of Nursing is doing MORE to ensure a healthier future for all. With a new, permanent home at UCF’s Academic Health Sciences Center, we will have more space to prepare more Knight nurses with academic excellence and more opportunity to impact more lives with innovative, interdisciplinary research.

 

The Opportunity:

The Budget Analyst II is responsible for preparing financial reports, analyzing data, and reviewing, processing, and reconciling financial transactions. The position also supports financial administration of research activities, including budget and expenditure monitoring, financial reconciliation and reporting, and research-related purchasing activities.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Monitor budgetary variances and process budget amendments, as appropriate.
  • Review expenses and identify appropriate funding sources, including but not limited to E&G, Carryforward, Auxiliary, Concessions, C&G, Foundation, and Research Foundation funds.
  • Prepare and submit manual journals for departmental scholarships, Foundation scholarships, cash sales, and other transactions, as needed.
  • Reconcile financial transactions across funding sources to ensure accuracy and initiate worktag changes, as needed. Prepare and process Payroll Accounting Adjustments and Accounting Adjustments to correct payroll and other financial transactions, as appropriate.
  • Perform month-end activities to ensure financial transactions are fully processed and approved within the appropriate accounting period.
  • Prepare and compile routine financial reports for the CON Finance Business Center. Prepare and provide research financial reports to Principle Investigators (PIs).
  • Establish and monitor salary costing allocations for research activities, including initiating and maintaining personnel funding allocations for sponsored awards in accordance with approved budgets.
  • Facilitate periodic effort certification (ECC) activities.
  • Monitor and reconcile salary and non-salary expenditures for research activities to ensure costs are allowable, allocable, and reasonable.
  • Review expenditures and award activity to support compliance with university and sponsor requirements, under the direction of the Office of Research.
  • Coordinate procurement and purchasing activities for research, including establishing purchase orders for subawards, consultants, equipment, supplies, gift cards, and other research-related goods and services.
  • Review subaward invoices for required documentation and facilitate PI review and approval prior to payment processing.
  • Review and process invoices for research consultants and other research-related purchases.
  • Facilitate research award closeout meetings to support expenditure review, financial planning, and timely award closeout.
  • Participate in New Award Meetings and other meetings supporting CON research administration.
  • Monitor, track, and document cost-share commitments.

  • Experience with Workday Financial Management or a comparable enterprise financial system.
  • Experience processing or reviewing journal entries, accounting adjustments, payroll accounting adjustments, and/or salary costing allocations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft 365 applications.

Undergraduate Admissions:

The Office of Undergraduate Admissions coordinates the admission and enrollment of all undergraduate first-time-in-college, transfer, non-degree, dual enrollment, early admission, and non-Florida public institution transient students to the university. Our primary mission is to identify, attract, and enroll talented, and academically qualified students who will thrive at and contribute to the University of Central Florida.

 

The Opportunity:

UCF's Office of Undergraduate Admissions, within the Division of Student Success and Well-Being, is seeking a dynamic Assistant Director, Student Recruitment. In this role, you will supervise and lead a team of admissions counselors, serving as a key driver of student recruitment strategy and outreach. Reporting to the Associate Director, Undergraduate Admissions, you will also serve as the office's scholarship and recruitment travel coordinator — playing a central role in shaping how UCF connects with prospective students. This position/classification may be moved at management's discretion within the Division of Student Success and Well-Being to a commensurate level position as determined by the Vice President of Student Success and Well-Being or their designee.

RECRUITMENT & OUTREACH

ADMISSIONS & ENROLLMENT

  • Reviews and evaluates admission applications and academic credentials; computes high school and college GPAs in compliance with State of Florida and university admission standards; and renders admission decisions.

TEAM LEADERSHIP & SUPERVISION

OPERATIONS & COORDINATION

COLLABORATION & COMPLIANCE

  • Assists in implementing and monitoring university policies and procedures related to undergraduate student recruitment, admission, and enrollment.
  • Collaborates with campus offices and departments to align admission and enrollment processes, ensuring consistent communication and progress toward university enrollment goals.

In this role, you’ll be responsible for drafting, reviewing, and negotiating sponsored contracts, research-related agreements, and non-sponsored agreements for the UCF Research Foundation, while collaborating with faculty, research administrators, university partners, and external organizations.


In this highly collaborative setting, you’ll apply advanced knowledge of Research Foundation and University policies and procedures, along with applicable state and federal regulations and laws, to help navigate complex contracting matters. This opportunity is well suited for a detail-oriented professional who exercises sound judgment and can work independently, efficiently, and accurately while following assignments through to completion with minimal direction.


Responsibilities:

  • Draft or review modifications to sponsored and non-sponsored agreements.
  • Conduct negotiation with the other party. Route for internal reviews, approvals, and signature as needed.
  • Coordinate agreement reviews University units to ensure compliance units are notified, or have approved proposed contract activities, as required, for human subjects protections, animal welfare, bio-safety, environmental health and safety, export control, facility security, cybersecurity, data protection, conflict of interest, etc.
  • Incorporate edits as required to comply with applicable policies, laws and regulations.
  • Route revisions, as needed, for additional approvals. Route to obtain signatures of all parties.
  • Interpret and assess contractual language regarding issues such as intellectual property rights, confidentiality, liability, indemnification, risk, publishing rights, invoice and payment terms, governing law, and confirmation of sponsor's corporate registration, and negotiate terms compliant with University policies and state law.
  • Maintain proficiency in researching, reviewing, analyzing, and interpreting statutory and policy language, federal regulations such as FARs, DFARs, and CFRs, to ensure the application of appropriate terms for public educational institutions.
  • Determine appropriate flow-down provisions, as needed, from pass-through entities.
  • Advise faculty, administrators and staff in interpretation and clarification of contract terms, appropriate business unit, sponsor requirements, policies related to sponsored and non-sponsored Research Foundation activities, and applicable regulations and laws, including restrictions and other pertinent information.
  • Serve as primary contact for investigators and college and department research administrators in all matters related to the drafting, review, interpretation, analysis, negotiation and execution of assigned research contracts and other agreements in support of the Research Foundation activities.
  • Provide notice to Research Foundation award management team for the establishment of new projects; ensure all documents and information are filled for new project establishment or modifications to existing projects.
  • Assist with training and support of new staff members. Assist with special initiatives and projects.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 2+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • 2+ years of experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating contracts with various types of entities, such as corporate entities, non-profit organizations, and international organizations.
  • Proven ability to influence and persuade during contract negotiations.
  • Prior experience in research administration or related academic support roles.
  • Familiarity with contract management systems, including the Huron Grants Suite and third-party.
  • Knowledge of and experience with University of Central Florida (UCF) policies and procedures is highly desirable.

The most successful candidates may possess the following qualities:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across various disciplines.
  • Excellent critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.
  • Professional, positive, and customer-focused approach to work.

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $64,518 to $85,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • This is a Contract and Grant (C&G) funded position. Employment is subject to availability of funding and may cease at the time funding for this employment is depleted.

Full job description

Office of Research:

The University of Central Florida (UCF) Office of Research sets the standard for excellence in service to our stakeholders by supporting research, commercialization, and economic growth. Through strategic partnerships, collaboration, and integrity, we foster an environment where employees can pursue their personal and professional goals while contributing to organizational success. We serve as an essential resource for attracting and retaining premier talent and research funding through operational excellence, innovative technology, and cohesive teamwork.


The Opportunity:

Join UCF’s Office of Research as a Contracts Officer III and play an important role in advancing UCF's research mission. In this senior-level position, you'll independently negotiate complex sponsored research agreements, advise faculty and research administrators, navigate regulatory and institutional requirements, and work across the university to move research partnerships forward.


You'll also have the opportunity to serve as a resource and mentor to colleagues, contribute to quality review and training, and support strategic initiatives across the research enterprise.


Responsibilities:

Contract Drafting, Review & Negotiation

  • Serve as primary contact for investigators and college and department research administrators in assigned Colleges and Units in all matters related to the drafting, review, interpretation, analysis, negotiation and execution of research contracts and other agreements in support of Office of Research sponsored program activities.
  • Draft agreements, as needed, for external parties to use in contracting with the university, using agreement templates and contract terms from prior, approved agreements. For all research agreements, incorporate statements of work, budgeting information, payment terms, period of performance, deliverables, and other required components and terms consistent with university policies and principal investigator needs. Develop creative solutions to complex contract issues.
  • Interpret and assess contractual language regarding issues such as intellectual property rights, confidentiality, liability, indemnification, risk, publishing rights, invoice and payment terms, governing law, and confirmation of sponsor's corporate registration, and negotiate terms compliant with university policies and state law.
  • Draft or review research-related contracts, and other agreements, funded and unfunded, such as research and research services and consulting, memoranda of understanding, material transfer agreements, confidentiality agreements, master agreements, cooperative research and development agreements, data use, equipment loans, proprietary information, intergovernmental personnel assignments, and other agreements.
  • Draft, or review contract modifications received from sponsors; route for internal reviews, approvals, and signature, as needed.
  • Escalate non-standard contract terms, as needed, in accordance with approved escalation procedures.

Regulatory Compliance & Risk Management

  • Advises faculty, administrators and staff in interpretation and clarification of contract terms, appropriate business unit, sponsor requirements, and applicable regulations and laws, including restrictions and other pertinent information.
  • Research, review, analyze, and interpret statutory and policy language, federal regulations such as FARs, DFARs, and CFRs, to ensure the application of appropriate terms for public educational institutions. Determine appropriate flow-down provisions, as needed, from pass-through entities.
  • Ensure associated University compliance units are notified, or have approved proposed contract activities, as required, for human subjects protections, animal welfare, biosafety, environmental health and safety, export control, facility security, and conflict of interest.
  • Maintain proficiency interpreting and applying federal regulations governing sponsored programs including 2 CFR 200, Federal Acquisition Regulations, standard federal research terms and conditions, and agency-specific requirements.

Agreement Coordination & Sponsored Program Administration

  • Coordinate agreement reviews by other Office of Research components, other University units, and the Office of General Counsel. Incorporate edits as required to comply with applicable policies, regulations, and law. Conduct award negotiations with sponsoring agencies and serve as primary liaison for the University with sponsoring agencies, investigators, and other University offices. Route revisions for additional approvals, as needed; route for signatures to execute agreements.
  • Provide notice to Research Office award management team for the establishment of new projects; ensure all documents and information are filed for new project establishment or modifications to existing projects.
  • Collaborate in subaward process in accordance with internal office procedures.

Leadership, Training & Organizational Support

  • Assist with training and support of new staff members, including student workers. Serve as resource to Contract Officer II. Assist in quality reviews of other Contract Officers’ agreements.
  • Assist in the development & presentation of information sessions to investigators and college and department research administrators.
  • Remain current with developments in University sponsored contracting and research administration through participation in professional development activities such as attendance at professional meetings, and in-house webinars and other informational sessions.
  • Serve in the place of Manager, as needed. Assist with special initiatives and projects to include large-scale and strategic initiatives. Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience drafting, reviewing, and negotiating contracts with various types of entities, such as federal entities, corporate entities, non-profit organizations, and international organizations.
  • Proven ability to influence and persuade during contract negotiations.
  • Experience supporting sponsored research, research administration, or contracting within a higher education, governmental, healthcare, or research-intensive organization.
  • Experience using electronic research administration, contract lifecycle management, or grants management systems, such as Huron Research Suite or a comparable platform.
  • Knowledge of policies and contracting requirements applicable to public universities or governmental entities; experience with UCF policies and procedures is a plus.
  • Experience advising internal stakeholders on contract requirements and providing guidance, training, quality review, or mentorship to colleagues.
  • Experience providing leadership or guidance to colleagues through mentoring, training, quality review, serving as a subject matter resource, leading initiatives, or supervising others.

The most successful candidates may possess the following qualities:

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively across various disciplines.
  • Excellent critical thinking and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team.
  • Professional, positive, and customer-focused approach to work.

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $75,809 - $94,761. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • This is a Contract and Grant (C&G) funded position. Employment is subject to availability of funding and may cease at the time funding for this employment is depleted.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Full job description

Office of the President:

The President’s Office division is made up of bold, energetic and entrepreneurial leaders in policy and planning, strategic communications and marketing, and administrative and fiscal operations who advance UCF’s mission.

 

The Opportunity:

UCF's Office of the President seeks candidates for a Constituent Services Coordinator. The Coordinator serves as a welcoming face and first point of contact for the Office of the President. This is a pivotal position that shapes how the university engages with its most important audiences, including students, families, faculty, staff, and community members. This role is essential in managing sensitive inquiries, supporting office operations, and ensuring a seamless experience for all who engage with our office.

The primary responsibility of the Constituent Services Coordinator is to oversee and work alongside relevant leadership members across the University regarding any/all university constituent matters related to customer service needs and complaint handling, many times involving confidential and sensitive matters and complex problem-solving. In addition, the role will serve as the main contact for front desk operations and provide general administrative support. The role is designed to work independently, with limited supervision.

This is a highly visible, people-centered role, and requires the selected candidate to work on-site full time at UCF's Main Campus.

Classification Title: Administrative Coordinator III

 

Responsibilities:

  • Handles high-level and complex concerns or complaints from any/all university constituents. Provides strong customer service and problem-solving of such. Involves relevant leaders across the University, as applicable, and uses sensitivity and confidentiality protocols as relevant.
  • Manages front desk offices activities; serves as the first point of contact for entry into the President's Division; greets constituents and answers phones. Checks and triages all inbound emails. May schedule and supervise student workers.
  • Provides general administrative support as necessary, to include but not limited to items such as: providing reports, reviewing and analyzing data, preparing meeting rooms, managing files and records, handling office supplies and inventory, and serving as back-up to other area administrators as needed.
  • Provides dedicated administrative support to the Office of the President's operational team, to include but not limited to items such as: complex calendar management, travel coordination, expense reconciliation, meeting coordination, and miscellaneous project support as needed.

Minimum Qualifications: 

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 4+ years of experience in a customer service, administrative support, or office management role.
  • Experience supporting senior leadership and managing executive calendars.
  • Experience with project management and project management platforms (Asana or similar).
  • Familiarity with Customer Relationship Management software (CRM) such as Salesforce, Oracle, or similar.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite.

The ideal candidate will possess the following qualities:

  • Strong customer service mindset, with the ability to handle sensitive information with professionalism and discretion.
  • Exceptional organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Outstanding interpersonal skills with a proactive, helpful attitude.
  • Adaptable and able to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • Classification Title: Administrative Coordinator III

This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

University Operations:

The University Operations division at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.

 

The Opportunity:

University Operations is seeking to hire a Zone Manager, Floor Care & Projects. This role is responsible for coordinating and overseeing floor‑care operations and custodial project activities across assigned campus buildings. This position ensures that all services, staff, and processes align with university, state, and industry standards. Serving as the primary customer contact for service quality, communication, and project coordination, the Zone Manager plays a key role in maintaining a safe, clean, and welcoming campus environment. The ideal candidate is highly skilled in floor‑care techniques, equipment, and materials; experienced in leading teams and managing projects; and committed to delivering high‑quality, compliant, and customer‑focused service.

Responsibilities:

Operations & Supervision

  • Oversee all floor‑care services and custodial project activities within the assigned zone.
  • Supervise custodial, project, and lead staff, including staffing, scheduling, training, performance management, and corrective actions in accordance with departmental SOPs and guidelines.
  • Maintain internal controls to support efficient operations, asset protection, compliance requirements, and accurate financial tracking.
  • Conduct regular floor inspections and develop comprehensive maintenance plans for all flooring types.

Work Management & Planning

  • Review and manage zone work orders in the Integrated Work Management System (IWMS), ensuring accurate entry of work status, costs, dates, and corrective actions.
  • Develop coordinated schedules involving staff, trades, contractors, vendors, inspectors, and other stakeholders.
  • Align work with team‑cleaning frameworks and ensure the completion of preventive maintenance, including annual inventories of all floor‑care equipment.
  • Evaluate work schedules, forecast manpower needs, and prioritize backlog to ensure efficient work assignment and timely completion.
  • Generate weekly and monthly reports on planned and in‑progress work, including resource allocation and schedule performance.
  • Document schedule variances and adjust project timelines to meet quality, safety, and maintenance standards.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Review work packages—electronic or hard copy—for completeness and accuracy, ensuring specifications, manuals, and drawings meet university standards and regulatory requirements.
  • Inspect zone and contractor work to ensure scope fulfillment, workmanship quality, and process compliance.
  • Complete work order closure in accordance with work‑management processes, validating accuracy of all data, including labor, materials, dates, images, invoices, and corrective actions.
  • Ensure all activities comply with organizational policies, safety standards, codes, and regulations.

Customer Service & Communication

  • Serve as liaison between customers and service providers, facilitating timely resolution of requests and concerns.
  • Conduct customer work‑review meetings using planning documentation and progress reports.
  • Assess zone impacts to balance customer needs while meeting service standards.
  • Schedule periodic customer reviews to assess service quality and performance.
  • Maintain clear, consistent, and transparent communication with campus stakeholders and collaborate with other departments to coordinate services around operational schedules.

Safety, Training & Employee Development

  • Maintain a safe and healthy work environment in compliance with legal codes, regulations, and university standards.
  • Provide coaching and training on job duties, SOPs, and customer service expectations.
  • Ensure accurate documentation of employee performance, coaching, and compliance.
  • Ensure urgent and life‑safety work orders receive expedited response.
  • Perform quality checks to confirm that delivered services meet established standards and the university’s process guide.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of custodial management or floor-care leadership experience in a university, educational, healthcare, or large-scale commercial environment.
  • Advanced knowledge of floor‑care techniques, equipment, materials, and maintenance practices for a wide range of flooring types (e.g., terrazzo, VCT, carpet, hardwood, rubber, tile).
  • Experience managing custodial or facilities staff including training, performance evaluation, and corrective action within an SOP‑driven environment.
  • Strong project‑planning and scheduling skills, including the ability to forecast manpower requirements, prioritize backlogs, and coordinate multiple stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication and customer‑service skills, with experience serving as liaison between internal customers, contractors, and service providers.
  • Knowledge of OSHA regulations, safety practices, and applicable codes related to custodial operations and floor‑care activities.
  • Certifications in custodial management or floor‑care operations, such as ISSA, IICRC, or similar industry credentials.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $56,030 to $74,940. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • This position is eligible for 5% Shift Differential Pay of the pay range minimum.
  • Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.
  • If you are selected as the final candidate for an employment opportunity, both your position and salary will be significantly based upon the information that you have provided in your application for employment. We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.

Job.JobTitle: Manager, Recruitment Events and Visitor Experiences
Job.JobDescription:
Undergraduate Admissions:

The Office of Undergraduate Admissions supports the university in meeting its enrollment goals and fulfilling the UCF Strategic Plan. It is responsible for coordinating the identification, recruitment, admission and enrollment of all undergraduate first-time-in-college, transfer, non-degree, dual enrollment, early admission and non-Florida public institution transient students. The office leverages the UCF brand to market, communicate and engage with talented and academically qualified students who will enrich our community and achieve academic and personal excellence.

 

The Opportunity:

UCF's Undergraduate Admissions seeks a dynamic and innovative Manager, Recruitment Events and Visitor Experiences to join the Communications, Marketing and Visitor Experiences team. In this highly collaborative, student-centered role, you will lead the strategy, planning, and execution of signature recruitment events, campus tours, and operations in the Duke Energy UCF Welcome Center that showcases UCF and creates memorable experiences for prospective students and their families. You'll join a talented team of service-oriented professionals and student ambassadors dedicated to delivering engaging, welcoming, and seamless visitor experiences across every touchpoint. Leveraging technology, data, and student feedback, you'll continuously evaluate and enhance our programs, strengthen connections with future Knights, and help turn campus visits and recruitment events into meaningful steps toward enrollment. Working closely with campus partners, you'll play a key role in bringing UCF's story to life and advancing undergraduate recruitment and enrollment goals.

 

Responsibilities:

Lead Recruitment Events & Experiences

  • Plan and run on-campus and virtual events that create memorable experiences for students and families and support enrollment goals.
  • Manage open houses, admitted-student programs, and yield events from start to finish.
  • Design new event ideas with colleges and campus partners that showcase UCF's programs and community.
  • Handle scheduling, logistics, registration, staffing, and on-site operations, then evaluate results.
  • Promote events and keep attendees engaged to boost attendance and enrollment.

Direct Campus Tours & Visitor Programs

  • Lead the campus tour program, including daily tours, group visits, and information sessions.
  • Improve visit programs to show UCF's value and guide families' decisions.
  • Oversee tour scheduling, registration, staffing, and visitor communications.
  • Recruit, train, and manage the Admissions Ambassador team.
  • Use visitor feedback and attendance data to improve operations and enrollment impact.

Oversee Welcome Center Operations

Minimum Qualifications:

Preferred Qualifications:

Student Success and Well-Being/Housing and Residence Life:

The Division of Student Success and Well-Being (SSWB) is dedicated to creating an amazing UCF experience. From enrollment through graduation, and even as our Knights enter the global workforce, we walk beside students with wraparound programs and services.  The mission of the Department of Housing and Residence Life is to provide students living in university housing with safe, well-maintained facilities and programs that are conducive to student learning and success.

 

The Opportunity:

UCF's Student Success and Well-Being - Housing and Residence Life is seeking a strategic and service-oriented leader to join their team as Assistant Director, Housing Administration.  This role plays a critical part in shaping the residential experience for UCF students by overseeing housing assignment operations, ensuring policy compliance and fostering meaningful partnerships across the university community.

The ideal candidate brings a collaborative mindset, a commitment to customer service excellence, and the operational acumen to manage complex assignments processes in a dynamic, student-centered environment.   If you're passionate about supporting student success and thrive in a role where your work directly impacts where students call home, this opportunity is for you.

 

Responsibilities:

Leadership & Staff Supervision

  • Hire, train, supervise, and evaluate a team that handles housing assignments.
  • Work with residence hall staff to assign and oversee assignments-related tasks; provide training and support.
  • Fill in for the Associate Director on assignments and occupancy matters when needed.

Housing Assignments Operations

  • Plan and improve housing assignment procedures; manage daily tasks like vacancy checks and room changes.
  • Handle assignments for special groups (Living Learning programs, Greek housing, athletes, students with medical needs, etc.) and coordinate with Athletics to follow compliance rules.
  • Work with residence hall staff to assign and oversee assignments-related tasks; provide training and support.
  • Help set up, test, and troubleshoot the online housing application.

Policy and Procedure

  • Serve as the main contact for key procedures like enrollment checks, assistance animal applications, medical requests, and legal documents.
  • Use software (StarRez, PeopleSoft) to manage assignments and handle data requests; keep records following university and Florida state rules.
  • Develop and update policies for occupancy and assignments; track federal/state requirements that affect housing (e.g., emotional support animals).

Communication and Support

  • Communicate daily with students, parents, staff, and faculty by phone, email, and in person; oversee responses to housing inquiries.
  • Explain housing policies and contracts to students, parents, and staff; suggest policy changes to leadership.
  • Create reports, rosters, and data queries for occupancy management and campus partners; audit housing agreement data and fix errors.
  • Represent the department at university events (Open House, Orientation) and serve on committees.

Additional

  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's and 4+ years of relevant experience or Masters degree and 2+ years of relevant experience with at least 1+ year(s) of leadership experience, or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working in a dynamic higher education setting.
  • Proficiency with higher education housing software, such as StarRez, RMS/Mercury, PeopleSoft, eRezLife, etc. or comparable residence life environment.
  • Supervisory or leadership experience overseeing front line support staff.
  • Skilled at student/family interactions and support.
  • Well-developed written and verbal communication skills to convey information to multiple audiences in mass communication contexts.
  • Familiarity with developing or streamlining procedures for staff and student efficiency.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

About this job

Lead strategic partnerships and build national networks for the National Commercialization and Translation Institute, an NSF-funded initiative at UCF that connects deep-technology companies with mentors, investors, and commercialization resources. The role splits time between NCTI network development and university-wide partnership management across industry, research, and philanthropic sectors.

Good fit if you have 6+ years experience in technology commercialization, startup support, or strategic partnerships, with demonstrated success engaging investors, industry partners, and innovation ecosystems.

Full job description

College of Engineering and Computer Science

The National Commercialization and Translation Institute (NCTI) is a national initiative dedicated to helping innovative technology companies transform breakthrough ideas into commercial success. Supported through a National Science Foundation (NSF) initiative and led by the University of Central Florida, NCTI serves as a national hub connecting entrepreneurs, investors, industry leaders, government partners, and commercialization experts to accelerate innovation, business growth, and economic impact. NCTI is designed to help promising deep-technology companies navigate the journey from scientific discovery and technological advancement to sustainable market success.

 

As a new institute, NCTI offers a unique opportunity to shape the future of technology commercialization on a national scale. Through strategic partnerships, individualized commercialization support, and a collaborative innovation ecosystem, the institute is advancing solutions that help high-potential companies overcome commercialization barriers and bring transformative technologies to market. NCTI combines the agility and entrepreneurial spirit of a startup with the resources and credibility of a leading research university, creating an environment where innovation, partnership, and impact drive meaningful results.

 

The Opportunity

The Senior Director, NCTI and Strategic Partnerships builds and advances a portfolio of high-value external relationships that connect industry and organizational priorities with UCF’s strengths in research, talent, innovation, commercialization, and philanthropy. Working across UCF Advancement & Partnerships and the National Commercialization and Translation Institute (NCTI), the position leads complex, multi-channel partnerships from initial discovery and strategy development through implementation, evaluation, and long-term stewardship.

For the period of the NCTI grant, funded by the National Science Foundation (NSF), this position will operate through a coordinated dual-reporting structure to ensure alignment between university partnership priorities and NCTI program objectives. This position dedicates approximately 50% of its responsibilities to university-wide partnership development through UCF Advancement & Partnerships and 50% to developing and sustaining NCTI’s national network of mentors, investors, national laboratories, industry collaborators, entrepreneurial-support organizations, and commercialization resources. After the grant period, the role will transition fully to the Advancement & Partnerships team, reporting to the Executive Director of Partnerships.

 

Responsibilities

  • Builds and maintains NCTI’s national mentor and investor networks. Recruits and onboards mentors aligned with participating companies’ sectors and development stages and works with NCTI leadership to support appropriate mentor connections. Develops relationships with venture, angel, corporate, and mission-aligned investors and facilitates investor engagement based on company readiness.
  • Develops and stewards relationships with national laboratories, industry partners, entrepreneurial-support organizations, manufacturing resources, and founding collaborators. Creates pathways that connect participating companies with relevant technical expertise, commercialization resources, and customer, supply-chain, manufacturing, and strategic-partnership opportunities.
  • Monitors the effectiveness and coverage of NCTI’s partner network, identifies gaps, and develops additional relationships based on program needs. Maintains partner-engagement records and supports partner participation in NCTI councils, convenings, investor engagements, and other program activities.
  • Develops and manages a portfolio of corporate and organizational relationships on behalf of UCF, establishing engagement strategies and advancing opportunities across sponsored research, innovation and business collaboration, industry-sponsored student experiences, executive and continuing education, talent development and recruitment, philanthropic investment, and corporate co-location.
  • Serves as a primary liaison among external partners and UCF colleges, centers, institutes, and administrative units, helping partners navigate the university and experience UCF as a coordinated institution. Collaborates with deans, faculty members, researchers, and university leadership to identify institutional strengths, surface partnership opportunities, and present academic, research, workforce, and innovation capabilities in a compelling partner-facing manner.
  • Tracks portfolio activity, partnership pipeline, financial outcomes, engagement progress, and other established performance indicators. Prepares updates and reports for Advancement & Partnerships and NCTI leadership and maintains complete, accurate partnership records in designated university systems.
  • Contributes to the development of shared processes, tools, reporting practices, and service standards that create a consistent partner experience across UCF. Supports coordinated planning between Advancement & Partnerships and NCTI and communicates emerging opportunities, risks, resource needs, and areas requiring leadership direction.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 6+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience building and managing strategic partnerships within technology commercialization, innovation, entrepreneurship, startup, accelerator, or economic development environments.
  • Demonstrated success developing relationships with investors, industry leaders, government agencies, research organizations, or entrepreneurial support networks.
  • Experience supporting startup companies, technology ventures, or innovation-driven organizations through business growth, commercialization, fundraising, or market expansion efforts.
  • Familiarity with federal innovation and commercialization programs such as NSF SBIR/STTR, I-Corps, NSF Engines, ART, NIH, DoD, or similar initiatives.
  • Experience working with venture capital, angel investor, corporate innovation, or entrepreneurial ecosystems.
  • Prior experience in a startup, technology company, accelerator, incubator, or economic development organization.
  • Experience utilizing CRM systems to manage stakeholder relationships, engagement activities, and program outcomes.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants

  • The anticipated starting salary for this position is $105,000 annually. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • Regular domestic travel is required (partner and laboratory engagement, investor convenings, the in-person midpoint convening, annual showcase).
  • The selected candidate must comply with NCTI conflict-of-interest and nondisclosure protocols, including disclosure of any financial interest in applicant or cohort companies, given the position’s role in approving participant funding.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This is a Contracts & Grants (C&G) funded position. Employment is subject to availability of funding and may cease at the time funding for this employment is depleted. This position is approved for the first 18 months of the 24-month grant period.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
