Full job description

The Opportunity

UCF's University Brand & Marketing seeks a dynamic Senior Director of Brand Strategy to join their team. The Senior Director of Brand Strategy is a senior leader within UCF Brand & Marketing, responsible for advancing, protecting and strengthening the UCF brand through enterprise brand strategy, creative strategy and integrated brand marketing.

In partnership with the Chief Brand & Marketing Officer, the Senior Director will oversee the development and execution of brand strategy and stewardship, creative platforms and operations, and upper-funnel brand marketing initiatives designed to build awareness, strengthen reputation and increase affinity for UCF. The position will partner closely with the AVP of Performance Marketing & Digital Experiences, as well as colleges and units across the university, to ensure campaigns throughout the marketing funnel are grounded in a common brand strategy and reinforce a cohesive UCF story.

 

Responsibilities

Brand Strategy & Stewardship

  • Shape, strengthen and steward UCF’s enterprise brand strategy, ensuring a distinctive and consistent expression of the university while providing the frameworks that enable others to represent the brand effectively.

 

University Partnership & Brand Leadership

  • Partner with the AVP of Performance Marketing & Digital Experiences and marketing and communications leaders across UCF to provide brand governance and ensure brand strategy is carried consistently across the full marketing funnel.
  • Facilitate alignment among decentralized college and unit teams around shared brand priorities while supporting their distinct audiences and objectives.

Creative & Campaign Strategy

  • Lead and inspire creative teams to translate UCF’s brand strategy into Unmistakably UCF creative platforms and campaigns that build awareness, strengthen reputation and increase affinity while establishing a creative foundation that can extend across UCF marketing efforts.

Creative Leadership & Operations

  • Provide strategic oversight of University Brand & Marketing’s creative function and creative operations, partnering closely with the Creative Director, who directly leads the creative team.
  • Establish the vision, standards and systems that enable exceptional, Unmistakably UCF work across the university.
  • Develop leadership and talent, champion creative excellence and continuously optimize workflows, resources and operations to build a high-performing creative organization.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 8+ years of relevant experience, including 3+ years of leadership experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Significant progressive experience in brand strategy, integrated marketing, advertising, creative strategy or related disciplines, including leadership responsibility within a complex organization, agency or major consumer-facing brand.
  • Demonstrated experience developing, evolving and activating enterprise brand strategies, positioning and creative platforms.
  • Experience leading integrated, multichannel brand campaigns from strategy and concept development through creative execution.
  • Strong understanding of the relationship among brand strategy, creative strategy, audience strategy and marketing performance, with the ability to connect upper-funnel brand building to broader marketing objectives.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead and inspire creative professionals and provide strategic direction and constructive evaluation of creative work.
  • Experience developing audience-specific strategies and translating insights into relevant creative and marketing approaches.
  • Demonstrated success navigating complex, matrixed organizations and building alignment among stakeholders with differing priorities and objectives.
  • Ability to influence and provide leadership across decentralized teams and functions without relying on direct reporting relationships.
  • Strong executive presence and demonstrated ability to communicate strategy, present creative work and make recommendations to senior leaders and stakeholders.
  • Experience managing marketing or brand budgets, external agencies, production partners and other creative resources.
  • Demonstrated ability to improve creative operations, workflows, processes and systems while maintaining a high standard of creative quality.
  • Strong commitment to developing talent and building collaborative, accountable and high-performing teams.

The Opportunity:

The Utilities and Engineering Services unit within University Operations is seeking a strategic and collaborative leader to serve as Director and Building Code Official — the University's designated authority on building code compliance and the head of UCF's in-house Building Department. In this role, you'll lead a full-service department operating at the scale and complexity of a mid-sized municipality: overseeing plan reviews, permitting, inspections, code interpretation, staff development, and budget management across a broad portfolio of campus construction, renovation, and infrastructure projects, while partnering with architects, engineers, contractors, and university leadership to keep one of the nation's largest and most active campuses building safely and compliantly.

Responsibilities:

Department Leadership & Operations

  • Lead and oversee Building Department operations, programs, and staff.
  • Hire, develop, and ensure appropriate training and licensure of Building Department staff.
  • Oversee departmental budgeting, expenditures, and operational planning.

 

Code Administration & Compliance

  • Serve as the University's designated Building Code Official and code authority.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable building codes, regulations, and state requirements.
  • Direct plan reviews, building inspections, and code interpretation activities.
  • Manage permitting processes, inspection scheduling, fee administration, and recordkeeping.

 

Strategy & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Provide strategic leadership and guidance on construction compliance, facility safety, and code-related initiatives.
  • Develop and implement policies and procedures supporting construction and renovation projects.
  • Collaborate with architects, engineers, contractors, university stakeholders, and regulatory agencies.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 10+ years of relevant experience or a Bachelor's degree and 6+ years of relevant experience. Must have State of Florida certification as a Building Code Administrator. Must hold State of Florida certification and licensure as a Standard Plans Examiner in at least one (1) of the following disciplines: Building, Mechanical, Electrical, or Plumbing.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Public Administration, Building Construction, or a related field.
  • Florida Building Official certification.
  • Experience serving as a Building Official, Chief Building Official, or Building Department leader within a public-sector, municipal, higher education, or similarly complex organization.
  • Experience overseeing building permitting, inspections, plans review, and code compliance programs.
  • Experience leading and developing professional and technical staff, including licensed code professionals.
  • Experience managing departmental budgets, fee structures, and operational resources.
  • Experience interpreting and applying Florida Building Code and related state regulations.
  • Experience collaborating with architects, engineers, contractors, regulatory agencies, and executive leadership.
  • Experience supporting large-scale capital construction, renovation, and infrastructure projects.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop policies, improve processes, and lead strategic initiatives related to construction compliance and building safety.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

The anticipated salary range for this position is $104,664 - $156,996. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.


Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.

Job.JobTitle: Director, Learning Platforms and Service Operations
Job.JobDescription:
Center for Distributed Learning

For more than 30 years, the University of Central Florida (UCF) has been a national leader in online learning, advancing educational access, instructional innovation, and student success. Serving a university community of more than 70,000 students, UCF has developed one of the nation's most established and comprehensive digital learning environments, supported by decades of experience in online education, faculty development, and learning technologies.

 

The Center for Distributed Learning (CDL), within UCF's Division of Digital Learning (DDL), plays a central role in this success. As a nationally recognized leader in digital learning, CDL provides institutional leadership in the design, development, delivery, and continuous improvement of high-quality learning experiences. Working collaboratively with faculty, academic units, and university partners, CDL advances instructional excellence through innovative technologies, faculty development, research, data-informed practices, and strategic initiatives.

 

Building on UCF's history of innovation and commitment to access, CDL continues to shape the future of digital learning by exploring emerging technologies, strengthening institutional capabilities, and creating meaningful opportunities to improve teaching, learning, and student outcomes.

 

The Opportunity

UCF's Division of Digital Learning is seeking a Director, Learning Platform Services to provide strategic leadership for the people, platforms, and services that power teaching and learning across the university. This role offers the opportunity to shape the continued evolution of UCF's digital learning ecosystem while leading multidisciplinary teams responsible for learning management system administration, Webcourses@UCF support, learning data, and training and development. The Director will connect technology strategy with institutional priorities, helping ensure UCF's learning platforms and services remain reliable, responsive, and positioned to meet the evolving needs of faculty and students.

Operating at the intersection of technology, service delivery, and data, the Director will provide leadership across a complex environment of enterprise learning platforms, integrated technologies, technical support, and vendor partnerships. The role will help strengthen service management practices, including incident and change management, escalation processes, knowledge management, and continuous improvement, while guiding the university through platform enhancements, major changes, and critical service issues. As an important steward of learning data, the Director will also partner across UCF to support thoughtful data governance, appropriate access and use, privacy and security requirements, and data-informed decision-making.

UCF is looking for a collaborative, service-oriented leader who can develop high-performing teams, build trusted partnerships, and bring clarity to complex challenges. The ideal candidate will be comfortable communicating with audiences ranging from technical teams and technology vendors to faculty, academic leaders, and university executives, translating complex technology and operational issues into clear, actionable information. For a leader who enjoys bringing together people, processes, technology, and data to improve the digital learning experience, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact on how UCF supports teaching, learning, and student success.

 

Responsibilities

  • Provide strategic direction for UCF’s learning technology platforms and align platform services with institutional goals.
  • Lead and manage LMS Administrators, Webcourses@UCF Support staff, Learning Data Analyst, and Training and Development Manager to ensure effective operations.
  • Oversee diagnostics, resolve system and end-user issues, and escalate problems to vendors when necessary.
  • Plan, execute, monitor, and close LMS-related projects using project management best practices.
  • Coordinate communications on LMS policies and operational status and represent CDL and UCF in meetings and presentations.
  • Analyze learning data to inform decisions and recommend enhancements for improved user experience.
  • Perform additional responsibilities as needed to support CDL and institutional objectives.

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree and 8 years of relevant experience including 3+ years of leadership experience; or High School Diploma (or equivalent) and 12 years of relevant work experience in lieu of degree including 3+ years of leadership experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Progressive experience within higher education supporting or leading digital learning, learning technology, academic technology, or a related technology environment.
  • Experience administering or providing strategic oversight for enterprise learning management systems, preferably Canvas, including integrated third-party technologies and supporting services.
  • Experience leading service management and technical support operations, including incident management, change management, escalation processes, service delivery, and continuous service improvement.
  • Experience with enterprise technology integrations and architecture, including technologies or standards such as LTI, REST APIs, SAML/SSO, and third-party educational technology integrations.
  • Experience with data governance, data stewardship, and learning analytics in a higher education environment, including knowledge of FERPA, data privacy, security, and appropriate data-access practices.
  • Experience managing technology vendors, enterprise platform relationships, service-level expectations, and system implementation or enhancement projects.
  • Progressive supervisory or management experience leading technology, digital learning, technical support, or related teams, with demonstrated success developing employees and improving service operations.
  • Master's degree in higher education administration, educational or instructional technology, information technology, or a related field; or professional certification in service management or project management, such as ITIL, PMP, PMI-ACP, Agile, or Scrum.

The most successful candidates may possess the following qualities:

  • Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical, operational, and data-related information into clear and actionable communication for technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Collaborative and relationship-focused leadership, with the ability to build consensus and partnerships across teams and stakeholder groups with differing needs and priorities.
  • Strategic, service-oriented mindset, with sound judgment, adaptability, and the ability to balance long-term priorities with emerging operational needs while fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

 

Additional Application Materials Required

In addition to your application, please include a cover letter and resume.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants

  • Please note: UCF will observe its Thanksgiving closure from November 23 through November 27. Recruitment activities will pause during this time, with this search expected to resume the week of November 30.
  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $110,000-$120,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H 1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • Classification Title: Director, Learning Resources

School of Visual Arts and Design

At the UCF School of Visual Arts and Design we immerse our students in an environment that celebrates the fusion of traditional and contemporary art and design forms. Our mission is to harness the power of art to engage the senses, ignite the imagination, and inspire creativity across diverse mediums.

 

The Opportunity

UCF School of Visual Arts and Design seeks applications for multiple part-time openings for Figure Model positions to support the Studio Art and Emerging Media programs. Un-draped Figure Models (without clothing) serve as primary subjects for drawing and studio art courses at all levels within an academic setting, including foundations, intermediate, advanced, and graduate instruction. Models work under the direction of faculty to create poses appropriate for each class, ranging from quick poses for gesture drawings to long poses lasting for the duration of the class session.

Classes that require figure drawing rely heavily on the model; therefore, punctuality and preparedness are essential. Models are expected to hold a variety of poses, including standing, seated, and reclining, for reasonable periods of time to allow students to accurately observe and capture the figure.

Models must maintain professionalism in a classroom environment and follow faculty guidance regarding posing, breaks, and class needs. The role requires comfort working in an academic setting with students and faculty, and the ability to remain still during assigned pose durations. Reasonable breaks are provided.

 

Responsibilities

  • Pose for drawing and painting classes as directed by faculty.
  • Maintain stillness and composure during poses, including extended sessions.
  • Models will be scheduled in advance and expected to arrive promptly for scheduled sessions.
  • Collaborate respectfully with faculty and students in a classroom setting.
  • Enter hours in Workday on a daily basis and submit to model supervisor.
  • Complete periodic mandatory UCF Trainings.

Minimum Qualifications

High School Diploma or Equivalent and 0+ years of relevant experience.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience as a figure model for art classes or workshops; preferably in a higher education or academic studio environment.
  • Interest in the arts or humanities.
  • Punctuality, reliability, and a positive attitude.

 

Special Instructions to the Applicants

  • Position requires a valid Class E driver’s license. This position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.
  • UCF is seeking to fill multiple roles. Candidates for this job posting will be considered for additional vacancies in this department.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • Classification Title: Arts Technician I

Job.JobDescription:
University Operations:

University Operations at UCF is committed to creating a supportive and welcoming environment for our faculty, staff, students, and the broader community. We take pride in delivering exceptional service, sharing our expertise, and upholding the highest standards to ensure a world-class campus experience.

Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Instagram to learn more.

 

The Opportunity:

The Planning, Design and Construction Department within University Operations is seeking to hire a Construction Project Manager III. This position is responsible for the coordination and management of design and construction efforts to ensure the successful completion of both minor and major projects, in alignment with project schedules, budgets, and UCF's institutional strategy. The role involves planning, directing, and overseeing the design and construction of facilities, systems, and structures. The Construction Project Manager III leads the development of design and construction projects, manages their organization, scheduling, and implementation, and represents section leadership when needed.

Responsibilities:

Project Planning, Design & Compliance

  • Oversee all aspects of construction projects, including managing contractors, architects, engineers, and consultants, ensuring compliance with the Project Manager Manual.
  • Support sustainability goals and address design or implementation issues in collaboration with project teams.
  • Review project scopes and documents before bidding and permits.
  • Conduct inspections to ensure adherence to safety codes and regulations.
  • Ensure project documents meet UCF’s standards.

 

Budget, Contracts & Procurement

  • Develop and manage budgets and cost-tracking reports, identifying and resolving potential financial or quality issues.
  • Negotiate change orders and contract modifications with stakeholders.
  • Prepare estimates, bids, and Guaranteed Maximum Prices (GMP). Ensure timely payments for designers and contractors.
  • Develop purchasing strategies to address pre-construction challenges.

 

Project Execution & Stakeholder Management

  • Create and manage project schedules to meet deadlines.
  • Monitor contractor performance and track progress against the schedule.
  • Address delays and site emergencies as they arise.
  • Manage all phases of campus construction projects, collaborating with departments and facilities staff.
  • Maintain regular communication with stakeholders and involve them in decision-making.

 

Leadership & Departmental Support

  • Mentor and train junior project managers, improving departmental standards and efficiency.
  • Serve as signature authority in the absence of department managers.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience; or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Six or more years of experience managing complex construction or renovation projects through the full project lifecycle, from planning and design through construction and close-out.
  • Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously in the multimillion-dollar range, preferably within higher education, institutional, government, healthcare, or another similarly complex environment.
  • Experience developing and managing capital project budgets, schedules, procurement activities, change orders, project estimates, bids, and Guaranteed Maximum Price agreements.
  • Knowledge of applicable building codes, safety requirements, sustainability practices, and construction standards, with experience supporting project compliance and quality control.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP), Certified Construction Manager (CCM), LEED credential, or an advanced degree in construction management, architecture, engineering, or a related field.
  • Experience using project management information systems or construction-management platforms, such as Trimble Unity Construct, Microsoft Project, Procore, or comparable software, and providing formal or informal leadership through mentoring, training, or guiding project team members.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $89,076 - $111,345. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • This role requires the successful candidate to work on-site at UCF as their primary work location. On-site presence is an essential function of this role.
  • Position requires a valid class E driver’s license. The position may involve driving to various locations on and off campus to conduct University business.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.
  • If you are selected as the final candidate for an employment opportunity, both your position and salary will be significantly based upon the information that you have provided in your application for employment. We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.

The Opportunity (Job description):

The Department of Writing and Rhetoric (DWR) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) is accepting applications for part-time, adjunct faculty positions with an anticipated start date of January 11, 2027. This appointment is to teach in-person first-year composition courses on our main Orlando campus.

UCF’s First-Year Composition (FYC) Program serves more than 6,000 students annually and received the 2023 CCCC Writing Program Certificate of Excellence Award. FYC is driven by collaboratively-developed student learning outcomes and ePortfolios. The FYC curriculum is informed by guiding principles developed from rhetoric and composition praxis.

Part-time, adjunct faculty report to the Director of First-Year Composition and typically teach two courses.

As an independent writing department, DWR is the academic home to 11 tenure-earning faculty members, 35 full-time instructors and lecturers, and 15 graduate teaching assistants. DWR’s talented writing faculty have a range of expertise in rhetoric and composition and draw from various approaches to teach writing. The department offers a major and minor, graduate program, and certificate programs. The department houses the Center for Writing Excellence encompassing the University Writing Center and the Writing Across the Curriculum program.

UCF offers faculty members at all ranks opportunities for professional development and advancement through its Faculty Center for Teaching and Learning, Office of Faculty Excellence, and Center for Distributed Learning. One of the nation’s largest universities, UCF is a metropolitan, Hispanic serving institution (HSI) that promotes a diverse and inclusive environment. UCF holds the Carnegie Foundation's highest classifications for research activity and community engagement. Central Florida is one of the nation’s fastest-growing and diverse metropolitan areas and is home to a variety of cultural and natural attractions.

 

Responsibilities:

 

  • Teach first-year composition and support student writers
  • Establish strategies and practices that meet the program learning outcomes and ePortfolio
  • Utilize and develop curriculum informed by best practices in writing studies
  • Evaluate student writing in a timely manner   
  • Collaborate with students and colleagues in DWR

 

Minimum Qualifications:

 

  • Master’s degree from an accredited institution in Rhetoric and/or Composition or closely related field; degree must be conferred by August 1, 2026.
  • A minimum of two years teaching college-level composition courses.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Rhetoric and/or Composition from an accredited institution.
  • Graduate coursework in Composition Histories, Theories, and/or Pedagogy.
  • Demonstrated excellence in teaching college composition and experience working with a range of diverse writer populations, particularly multilingual writers.

Additional Application Materials Required:

 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/.  In addition to the online application, candidates should attach the following PDF documents:

  • curriculum vitae with contact information for three references,
  • teaching philosophy, and
  • unofficial transcript(s) of graduate-level coursework.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

 

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

Review of applications will begin immediately.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to Dr. Shane Wood at shane.wood@ucf.edu or for more information on DWR, visit http://writingandrhetoric.cah.ucf.edu.

About this job

Tenure-track assistant professor position in Clinical Psychology at UCF's Department of Psychology, one of the largest in the nation. Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in multiple modalities and conduct research in health services psychology within a department housing APA-accredited Ph.D. and master's programs.

Good fit if you have a Ph.D. in health services psychology, are eligible for Florida licensure, and have research interests complementing clinical psychology strengths.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The Department of Psychology in the College of Sciences (COS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for one full-time, 9-month, tenure track assistant professor position in Clinical Psychology, anticipated to begin in August 2027. We seek dedicated and collegial educators/scientists who can establish collaborative relationships within the department/college as well as with other colleges at the university and within the community. The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses in different modalities, including face-to-face and online. The instructional duties and services assignments are in accordance with the department’s current equitable workload policy.


Area of research specialization within health services psychology is open. We are interested in collaborative candidates with programs of research that can contribute to and complement program, department, and university strengths (see faculty areas of expertise here: https://sciences.ucf.edu/psychology/people/).


The Department of Psychology is one of the largest departments by enrollment at UCF, with more than 50 full-time faculty and approximately 4,000 undergraduate majors. The department has three broad areas of emphasis in clinical psychology, human factors and cognitive psychology, and industrial and organizational psychology. UCF’s online bachelor’s degree in Psychology is ranked #3 in the nation by U.S. News and World Report. All members of the department share a common goal of understanding behavior through empirical investigation, which is reflected in teaching and research. 


The department is home to two terminal master's programs in Clinical Psychology and I/O Psychology, and three Ph.D. programs in Clinical Psychology, I/O Psychology, and Human Factors and Cognitive Psychology.


The Clinical Psychology Ph.D. Program has maintained American Psychological Association (APA) accreditation since 2003, and in 2023 received the maximum re-accreditation period of ten years. The program houses a training clinic, which serves the UCF and surrounding communities.

To learn more about the Clinical Psychology program, please see our website at https://sciences.ucf.edu/psychology/graduate/ph-d-clinical/. For more information about the department visit https://sciences.ucf.edu/psychology/.


The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, physical, and social sciences and housing centers, institutes and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. With a mission to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers; a number of COS academic programs are among those nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others.


For more information, please visit https://sciences.ucf.edu.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in an area of health services psychology from an APA- or PCSAS-accredited program by the date of hire.
  • Eligible for licensure as a Psychologist in Florida, or able to obtain licensure as Psychologist in Florida within 2 years of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

Ideal candidates will have:

  • A research program with the potential for external funding.
  • Publications in peer-reviewed journals.
  • Evidence of, or potential for, teaching and/or mentoring effectiveness.
  • Demonstrated ability and/or potential to supervise Clinical Psychology Ph.D. students in evidence-based psychological services.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A cover letter of interest which includes statements of research (including future research plans), teaching interest (including evidence of teaching, if available, and clinical supervision interest), and eligibility for licensure as a Psychologist in the state of Florida  or plans for licensure.
  • A curriculum vitae (CV).

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalence evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials and names and contact information of three professional references.

Office of Research:

The University of Central Florida (UCF) Office of Research sets the standard for excellence in service to our stakeholders by supporting research, commercialization, and economic growth. Through strategic partnerships, collaboration, and integrity, we foster an environment where employees can pursue their personal and professional goals while contributing to organizational success. We serve as an essential resource for attracting and retaining premier talent and research funding through operational excellence, innovative technology, and cohesive teamwork.

  

The Opportunity:

The Finance/Budget Analyst will process financial transactions within university financial systems. They will also prepare statements and reports relating to an assigned area of responsibility, monitor records of past and present operations, and apply university accounting policies and procedures in working with accounting records and reports. The Analyst is tasked with assembling, analyzing, and reconciling data and transactions. They will monitor departmental accounts for compliance with applicable regulations and coordinate with the Budget/Finance Director and/or Manager on fiscal compliance.

 

Responsibilities:

  • Prepare budgets and forecast revenues and expenses and provide specialized financial reporting and analysis for Office of Research, including but not limited to the Institutes and Centers, Service Centers and Faculty Cluster Initiatives.
  • Develop and load budgets and associated adjustments into budget management systems and monitor budgetary variances and corrects as appropriate.
  • Correct unassigned budget transfers to appropriate revenue or spend categories and reconcile accounts to ensure accuracy of transactions.
  • Prepare costing allocations for payroll funding, corrections to payroll funding and review, reconcile, and validate Workday work tags, initiate work tag changes as needed.
  • Collaborate with HR on workforce funding planning and allocations and identify appropriate funding sources for various financial and HR transactions.
  • Prepare, review, or correct workforce funding changes and approve, deny, or return Workday spend transactions.
  • Work closely with other members of the business center and sponsored programs team to disseminate accounting information and ensure compliance.
  • Act as liaison between the PI, Office of Research and colleges/units. 
  • Perform all other duties as assigned.

 

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or combination of relevant comparable education and experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6). 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in financial forecasting, budget development, budget monitoring, and financial reconciliations, preferably within a higher education environment.
  • Proficiency in financial management systems, such as Workday or comparable ERP platforms.
  • Familiarity of financial regulations, policies, and accounting standards, particularly those applicable to higher education and research institutions.
  • Demonstrated experience in post award financial management, including the administration of sponsored projects, contract and grant accounts and coordination with principal investigators.

Resume and Cover Letter

About this job

Monitor compliance with institutional policies, sponsor agreements, and procedures at UCF's Pegasus Research Institute. Develop reporting tools, track corrective actions, and conduct reviews to ensure accuracy and integrity of programmatic, operational, and financial reporting.

Good fit if you have 5-8 years in compliance, audit, or sponsored research, with experience in evidence-quality testing and analytical review.

Full job description

Pegasus Research Institute:

Pegasus Research Institute (PRI) is the University of Central Florida’s applied research institute, bringing together expertise from across UCF to solve complex, real-world challenges. Through multidisciplinary collaboration among faculty, researchers, students, and industry and government partners, PRI helps move innovative ideas from research and prototyping to real-world validation and deployment. Its work spans space technologies, health and human performance, energy and sustainability, immersive experiences, and transformative technologies and national security, creating a dynamic environment where research, innovation, and operational impact intersect.


The Opportunity:

This position is responsible for monitoring adherence to institutional requirements, sponsor agreements, policies, and procedures while ensuring the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of programmatic, operational, and financial reporting. The analyst conducts reviews, maintains compliance documentation, tracks corrective actions, and develops reporting tools that support informed decision-making and continuous improvement.


Responsibilities:

  • Monitor compliance with institutional policies, sponsor requirements, agreements, and established procedures.
  • Maintain documentation, records, and evidence necessary to support audits, reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Perform evidence-quality testing and document-control activities to ensure reporting accuracy and audit readiness.
  • Develop and maintain reporting calendars, key performance indicators (KPIs), compliance checklists, and control schedules.
  • Track risks, exceptions, corrective actions, and compliance issues, ensuring appropriate follow-up and resolution.
  • Conduct analytical reviews and reconciliations across programmatic, project, operational, and financial reports.
  • Prepare recurring and ad hoc reports that communicate performance, compliance status, trends, and risks to leadership.
  • Identify reporting discrepancies, process gaps, and control weaknesses and recommend corrective actions.
  • Support internal and external audits by gathering documentation, coordinating responses, and tracking remediation efforts.
  • Assist with policy interpretation and provide guidance on compliance-related processes and requirements.
  • Collaborate with program, project, finance, and operational teams to improve reporting quality and process efficiency.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives that strengthen compliance controls and operational effectiveness.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with 5-8 years in compliance, audit, sponsored research, quality assurance, internal controls, or performance reporting.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Agreement, procedure, and institutional-requirement alignment.
  • Evidence-quality testing, audit readiness, and document control.
  • Reporting calendars, KPI definitions, control schedules, and review checklists.
  • Risk, corrective-action, exception, and issue tracking.
  • Analytical review and reconciliation across program, project, and financial reporting.
  • Policy interpretation and process improvement in regulated environments.

  • In addition to the online application, candidates should upload a cover letter and current curriculum vitae.
  • UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website.
  • The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

This position is responsible for planning, coordinating, and overseeing complex sponsored research activities, ensuring successful execution of program objectives, contractual requirements, budgets, schedules, and deliverables. The incumbent serves as a key liaison among principal investigators, research staff, institutional leadership, sponsors, and external partners, supporting the institute's research mission through effective program management, stakeholder engagement, and continuous process improvement.


Responsibilities:

  • Lead the planning, execution, monitoring, and closeout of complex research programs and projects.
  • Develop and maintain integrated program plans, work breakdown structures, schedules, budgets, milestones, and performance metrics.
  • Coordinate and lead cross-functional and multi-institutional teams to ensure alignment of program goals, deliverables, and timelines.
  • Monitor program performance and progress, proactively identifying and mitigating risks, issues, dependencies, and changes that may impact project outcomes.
  • Ensure timely and accurate sponsor reporting and facilitate deliverable reviews and acceptance processes.
  • Prepare executive-level briefings, program updates, and strategic reports for institute leadership and external stakeholders.
  • Support proposal development, project startup activities, and ongoing program administration for sponsored research awards.
  • Facilitate communication and collaboration among researchers, sponsors, partners, and administrative units.
  • Oversee program budgets and resource allocations to ensure effective stewardship of sponsored funds.
  • Promote consistent project and program management practices across the institute, including the development of tools, templates, and standard operating procedures.

Minimum Qualifications:

Master's degree from an accredited institution with 8-12 years of experience leading large, multidisciplinary research, engineering, or technology programs.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Integrated program plans, work breakdown structures, schedules, budgets, and milestones.
  • Sponsor reporting, deliverable acceptance, and executive briefings.
  • Leadership of cross-functional and multi-institution teams.
  • Risk, issue, dependency, and change management.
  • Mentoring program managers and promoting consistent execution practices.
  • Working knowledge of federal, state, industry, and sponsored-research award structures.

  • UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website.

About this job

Temporary position managing financial administration and sponsored research grants for UCF's Pegasus Research Institute. Oversee budgets, award management, compliance monitoring, and financial reporting for federal, state, and industry-funded research projects.

Good fit if you have a master's degree and 7-10 years of experience in financial management, grants administration, or research support.

Full job description

Pegasus Research Institute:

Pegasus Research Institute (PRI) is the University of Central Florida’s applied research institute, bringing together expertise from across UCF to solve complex, real-world challenges. Through multidisciplinary collaboration among faculty, researchers, students, and industry and government partners, PRI helps move innovative ideas from research and prototyping to real-world validation and deployment. Its work spans space technologies, health and human performance, energy and sustainability, immersive experiences, and transformative technologies and national security, creating a dynamic environment where research, innovation, and operational impact intersect.


The Opportunity:

This position provides strategic financial management and sponsored research administration support for the institute's research portfolio. The incumbent is responsible for overseeing budget development, financial forecasting, award management, compliance monitoring, financial reporting, and post-award administration for federal, state, industry, and other sponsored projects. This position serves as a key partner to institute leadership, principal investigators, and administrative offices to ensure sound financial stewardship, regulatory compliance, and effective management of research funding.


Responsibilities:

  • Manage the financial administration of sponsored research programs, grants, contracts, and institutional funding sources.
  • Develop and oversee operating budgets, multi-year financial plans, forecasts, and funding projections for research programs and institute operations.
  • Monitor expenditures and revenue activity to ensure appropriate use of funds and compliance with sponsor requirements and institutional policies.
  • Analyze funding availability and provide recommendations to institute leadership regarding budget planning, resource allocation, and financial strategy.
  • Prepare executive-level financial reports, budget summaries, projections, and ad hoc analyses to support decision-making.
  • Review and monitor cost allowability, cost allocation, cost sharing, and other financial compliance requirements.
  • Coordinate invoicing, account reconciliations, and financial transactions associated with sponsored awards and research activities.
  • Maintain accurate financial records and supporting documentation to facilitate audits, reviews, and sponsor reporting.
  • Manage award setup, modifications, amendments, subawards, and closeout activities in accordance with sponsor and institutional requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, sponsor, and institutional regulations governing sponsored research activities.

Minimum Qualifications:

Master's degree from an accredited institution with 7-10 years in strategic communications, public affairs, stakeholder engagement, research communications, or related program communications.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Communications strategy, message architecture, editorial planning, and brand governance.
  • Executive, public, sponsor, and multi-stakeholder communications.
  • Workshops, events, councils, industry outreach, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Website, content, publication, and technical-communications oversight.
  • Issues, approvals, sensitive-content, and crisis-communications management.
  • Team leadership and workload prioritization across communications deliverables.

Job.JobTitle: Visiting Instructor or Lecturer, School of Teacher Education
Job.CustomJobTypeName: K-12 Teacher, Education / Training, Adjunct / Professor
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity  

The School of Teacher Education (STE) in the College of Community Innovation and Education (CCIE) is dedicated to preparing and retaining exceptional student education teachers and professional educators who serve children and adults with special needs. In collaboration with Central Florida partners and CCIE's Toni Jennings Exceptional Education Institute (TJEEI), STE provides families of children with disabilities, UCF faculty and students, and educators with access to current information, resources and learning opportunities. Through teaching and research clinics, UCF faculty and students work to offer students with disabilities and their families services focused on assessment, behavior, reading, mathematics and community counseling. 


The School of Teacher Education is seeking applications for a 9-month, non-tenure earning, visiting instructor or lecturer. The successful candidate will teach four courses in the Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) and Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) program each semester, is expected to lead the ABA and BCBA programs, and provide administrative support for the current ABA accreditation, ABA attestations, and potentially support grant administration. The incumbent will also work with graduate affairs on behalf of STE with course substitutions.


This position is located on the Orlando campus and is anticipated to begin Spring 2027.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Instructor: A master’s degree in education, psychology, or a related field from an accredited institution; Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) credentials; and a minimum of five years of directly relevant professional experience in applied behavior analysis or a closely related area. All qualifications must be met by the time of hire.
  • Lecturer: A terminal degree (e.g., PhD, EdD) in education, psychology, or a related field from an accredited institution, and Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA) credentials. All qualifications must be met by the time of hire.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctoral-level Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA-D) credentials
  • PK-20 teaching experience
  • Experience with grant-related work (e.g., administration/writing, implementation, support)

Additional Application Materials Required: 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following: 

  • A curriculum vitae. 
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest. 

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later. 


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials. 

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Dan Ezell at Dan.Ezell@ucf.edu, Search Committee Chair.  

Special Instructions to the Applicants: 

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer. 


This is a visiting, 9-month, non-tenure track appointment with benefits, annually renewable for up to four academic years (maximum).

Note to applicants: Please keep in mind that a job posted without an end date may close at any time without notice. As such, we encourage you to submit your application and all required documentation as quickly as possible to ensure consideration for the posted position.

About this job

Senior Licensing Associate in UCF's Technology Transfer Office managing protection and licensing of physical science patents, trademarks, and copyrights. Responsibilities include drafting license agreements, assessing new technologies, promoting innovations at scientific conferences, and supervising IP specialists.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree with 4+ years of relevant experience, strong legal agreement drafting skills, and interest in technology commercialization.

Full job description

The Opportunity:

As part of UCF's Technology Transfer Office, the Senior Licensing Associate position manages the transfer of physical science technologies from university into commercial sectors. Manages technology review, intellectual property (IP) legal protection, IP license negotiations, and IP promotion in media and at scientific and technology related events.


Responsibilities:

  • Manages the protection and licensing of a portion of the UCF Research Foundation IP portfolio which includes patents, trademarks and copyrights in the areas of physical sciences. Drafts and negotiates license agreements and other types of agreements, including material transfer, inter-institutional, and nondisclosure agreements.
  • Assesses and evaluates new technologies disclosed to Technology Transfer. Identifies commercial uses and recommends appropriate legal protection and ensures adherence to IP laws and regulations.
  • Reviews and edits promotional materials to advertise new technologies to prospective industry partners. Leads outreach to commercialize technologies and promotes new technologies at scientific conferences and to business communities.
  • Reviews, edits, and negotiates IP terms and conditions for UCF sponsored research activities. Coordinates IP matters between contract manager, general counsel, principal investigator, and external sponsor/external counsel.
  • Attracts and cultivates relationships with university researchers, entrepreneurs and industry partners to drive licensing deal flow and potential sponsored research activity.
  • Supervises, trains, and instructs one or more intellectual property specialist, licensing assistant, students and/or interns.
  • Conducts workshops and delivers presentations to educate internal and external communities on Technology Transfer matters, best practices and IP policies.
  • Attends professional trade conferences.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications:

Bachelor's or Master's degree and 4+ years of relevant experience or an equivalent combination of education and experience pursuant to Fla. Stat. 112.219(6).


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in Engineering (e.g., Mechanical, Civil, Electrical) or a related physical science field.
  • 3+ years of demonstrated success in drafting, negotiating, and implementing legal agreements.
  • Strong customer service orientation with experience collaborating with faculty, legal teams, and external partners.
  • Proven business development and finance acumen.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with the ability to build and maintain strong relationships.
  • Ability to evaluate market potential and effectively communicate with different stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with patent assessment and market research methodologies.
  • Prior experience in technology transfer and outbound software licensing.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

  • The anticipated salary range for this position is $80,000 - $95,000. The final salary will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and internal equity considerations.
  • If you are selected as the final candidate for an employment opportunity here at UCF, both your position and salary will be significantly based upon the information that you have provided in your application for employment. We urge you to please take the time to complete the application in its entirety.
  • All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H‑1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer. 
  •  Classification Title: License & Patent Associate II

Job.JobTitle: Instructor or Lecturer, Film - Production Design
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Teach undergraduate and potentially graduate film production design courses at UCF's Nicholson School of Communication and Media. This is a 9-month, annually renewable instructor or lecturer position starting August 2027 with a clear promotion path based on years of service and performance.

Good fit if you have a master's degree in Film Production or related field, professional experience in production design, and proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud, Unreal, DaVinci Resolve, or similar software.

Full job description

The Opportunity 

The Nicholson School of Communication and Media (NSCM) in the College of Sciences (COS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for an instructor or lecturer position in the Film and Media Production and Management degree areas, anticipated to begin in August 2027. This job is a 9-month, non-tenure earning, annually renewable position that offers a clear career path with the possibility of promotion based on years of service and performance.   


The selected candidate will contribute to the mission of the Film and Mass Media program by teaching undergraduate courses and, depending on the highest degree attained, may teach at the graduate level and support the Film MFA degree by providing critiques, mentoring, and serving on graduate thesis committees. The successful candidate may be expected to teach in different modalities including face-to-face and online. The instructional duties and service assignments are in accordance with the department’s equitable workload policy. 


Other typical responsibilities include providing appropriate service in student advising (academic and career) and actively participating in the academic life of the school. This includes attending faculty meetings, graduations, assessing student learning, and engaging in committee work. These activities are integral to our commitment to student success and academic excellence.   


This position has no research expectation, but research and scholarly activities may be supported. 


Additionally, we are especially interested in a candidate who can contribute through their teaching and service to the excellence of our academic community and foster an environment in which faculty, staff, and students from a variety of backgrounds, cultures, and personal experiences are welcomed and can thrive. 


The UCF Nicholson School of Communication and Media (NSCM) is a student-centered experience at the exciting intersection of technology, media, film, advertising, communications and public relations. Our faculty and staff bring an impressive background of experience—from developing health communication to producing Super Bowl commercials—and connect our students to internship and career opportunities. As the premier academic program for communications and media in Central Florida with successful alumni around the globe, NSCM is known for excellence in research, teaching, and service to students and the community. The curriculum blends both the theoretical and applied aspects of the field, offering eight bachelor’s degree programs, four master’s degree programs, and a Ph.D. program in strategic communication. For more information about the school, visit https://communication.ucf.edu. 


The UCF College of Sciences (COS) is the largest college at the university and a powerhouse for the regional and national STEM workforce, spanning the natural, computational, physical, and social sciences and housing centers, institutes and initiatives that serve as hubs for research and innovation. Through sharing and applying knowledge, COS is cultivating pathways for students to solve our world’s most pressing and complex problems. With a mission to provide a world-class education in an environment where faculty, staff, and students thrive, research flourishes, and our community prospers; a number of COS academic programs are among those nationally ranked by U.S. News and World Report, Princeton Review, and others. For more information, please visit https://sciences.ucf.edu. 


UCF, named one of the most innovative public universities in the nation by U.S. News & World Report, is located in Orlando, Florida and is classified as a Very High Research Activity university by the Carnegie Foundation. With more than 70,000 students, UCF is one of the largest universities in the country, offering more than 240 degree programs. UCF is an economic engine, attracting and supporting industries vital to the region's future while providing students with real-world experiences that help them succeed after graduation. For more information, visit http://www.ucf.edu. 


Minimum Qualifications: 

  • A master’s degree (for an instructor) or a terminal degree (for a lecturer) in Film Production, or a related field (e.g., Production Design, Film Arts, Technical Arts, Digital Media, Mass Communication, etc.) from an accredited institution at the time of hire. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree as their highest degree will be considered an instructor applicant only if they can document a minimum of seven years of professional experience in production design in film and/or television production. 
  • Must have excellent communication and organizational skills and the ability to work effectively in a collaborative educational environment with faculty, students, and administrators.
  • Proficiency in production design software such as Abode Creative Cloud, Unreal, DaVinci Resolve, Toon Boom Story Board Pro or relevant software.  

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Professional Experience (five years or more) of production design, directing, cinematography, editing or relevant disciplines in film and/or television.
  • Professional experience in production design workflows and techniques.
  • At least one year of college-level teaching experience in a relevant discipline.
  • Experience working in virtual production and/or visual effects technologies.
  • Experience teaching in different modalities including face-to-face and online. 

Additional Application Materials Required: 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following: 

  • A letter of application (cover letter) indicating how you are prepared to join the faculty at UCF. 
  • A curriculum vitae (CV). 
  • A teaching statement of no more than 300 words that addresses the ability to teach using different delivery modes, including online or large classes. 
  • Links to preview work samples. 

Note: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later. 


The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials. 


Questions regarding this search should be directed to Rich Grula, Search Committee Chair, rgrula@ucf.edu.   


Special Instructions to Applicants: 

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.


Note to applicants: Please keep in mind that a job posted without an end date may close at any time without notice. As such, we encourage you to submit your application and all required documentation as quickly as possible to ensure consideration for the posted position.

The Opportunity:

The postdoctoral scholar with support a DARPA project focused on developing predictive pressure load models for external hypersonics aerodynamics. The postdoc will develop these data-informed models in collaboration with researchers at another university and an industry partner, and our own group at UCF. The postdoc will be responsible for rigorous model development, testing, and deployment to solve the demonstration problems. Postdoc will also write scientific journal articles, present novel research at technical conferences, attend collaborator meetings, and contribute to the quarterly project reports. To a lesser extent, the postdoc will help with mentoring of junior researchers in the group.

Minimum Qualifications: 

Must have a Ph.D. in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering with experience with machine learning tools, Python, and end-to-end training paradigms. Past experience in high-speed aerodynamics.

Preferred Qualifications: 

Multiphysics modeling experience focused on fluid-thermal-structural interactions. Prior work on developing generalizable and explainable ML models. Design of physics based loss functions in data-informed modeling frameworks. Direct experience with high-speed surface pressure models and panel methods.

Job.JobTitle: Professor and Director, School of Communication Sciences and Disorders
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The School of Communication Sciences and Disorders (CSD) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 12-month, tenured professor to serve as school director. The position is located at the UCF main campus with an anticipated start date in August 2027.


The successful candidate will assume leadership of a school with a growing team of internationally recognized faculty engaged in rigorous graduate and undergraduate education, expansive clinical service-delivery, cutting-edge research, and innovative partnerships. Opportunities for innovation and expansion abound in the interprofessional context of the College of Health Professions and Sciences within UCF’s Academic Health Sciences Center. The selected candidate will provide academic and administrative leadership (i.e., management of human resources, implementation of a new budget model, academic and clinical programming, student success and research excellence); facilitate intra- and inter- school collaborations to enhance the impact of scholarship, teaching, and service; support and mentor faculty to secure external funding; and advance impactful programming to fulfill the healthcare needs of the community.


The School of Communication Sciences and Disorders was founded in 1969 and was first accredited in 1987. It has a strong history of excellence in teaching, research, and community service. The school includes 34 full-time faculty members serving an average of 175 graduate and 500 undergraduate students. It offers bachelor’s, master’s, and Ph.D. degrees in communication sciences and disorders and ranks among the top 15% of speech-language pathology programs in the nation. The Master of Arts program boasts numerous internal and external affiliations, and the UCF Communication Disorders Clinic serves as the centerpiece for clinical education and applied research. This 15,000+ square foot state-of-the-art facility houses several research labs and specialty services, including audiology, the Aphasia House, the AAC Lab / Florida Alliance for Assistive Services and Technology (FAAST) Center, the Communication Technologies Research Collaborative, the Communication, Aphasia Recovery, and Emotion (CARE) Lab, Early Language & Literacy Intervention & Education Lab, Examining Patient-Provider Language and Interactions in Healthcare (EXPLAIN) Lab.  For more information about the school, visit our website at:  UCF School of Communication Sciences and Disorders - College of Health Professions and Sciences


Along with the School of Communication Sciences and Disorders, the College of Health Professions and Sciences at UCF is home to the School of Health Sciences, the School of Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Sciences, the School of Global Health Management and Informatics, and the School of Social Work. The college also houses several labs and research collaboratives, including the CHPS Rehabilitation Innovation Center – a state-of-the art interdisciplinary facility designed to become a destination center for solving complex healthcare problems through allied healthcare research, education, technology development/applications, and collaboration. UCF and its 12 colleges provide opportunities to more than 69,000 students offering 240+ bachelor's, master's, doctoral, and specialist degree programs.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • A research doctoral degree in communication sciences and disorders or a related discipline from an accredited institution;
  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a record of teaching, research/scholarly achievements, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of professor in the School of Communication Sciences and Disorders at UCF;
  • A record of administrative leadership and mentoring in a university setting.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Effective communication skills;
  • Experience overseeing complex budgets;
  • Experience with program accreditation;
  • Experience with student recruitment for undergraduate and graduate programs;
  • A record of federally funded research & mentoring faculty in securing external funding;
  • Experience with interprofessional education;
  • A record of facilitating successful collaborations within and outside the university setting;
  • Experience with alumni engagement; and
  • Experience with curriculum revisions and launching new educational programs.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.


Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Shawn Lawrence at Shawn.Lawrence@ucf.edu.

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Job.JobTitle: Psychiatrist (Assistant, Associate, or Professor of Medicine)
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Physician / Medical Director, Healthcare, Adjunct / Professor
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

UCF College of Medicine seeks a psychiatrist to teach medical students and residents in psychiatry, psychopharmacology, and medical interviewing while providing outpatient psychiatric care at UCF Health Faculty Practice. This non-tenure track role emphasizes undergraduate and graduate medical education with significant clinical responsibilities.

Good fit if you have an M.D./D.O., are board certified or eligible in psychiatry and neurology, and have experience teaching medical students or residents.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida College of Medicine (UCF COM) is seeking an experienced psychiatrist at the rank of assistant, associate, or professor of medicine to have a significant teaching role in undergraduate medical education (UME), graduate medical education (GME), and provide direct, outpatient psychiatric care at UCF Health Faculty Practice. This position is a non-tenure track appointment.


College of Medicine Educational Programs (60-70%)

The successful applicant will teach psychopathology, psychopharmacology, and fundamentals of medical interviewing in an integrated format to first- and second-year medical students and participate in case directed learning sessions. This position will serve as the discipline lead for the Integrated Sciences 4 module, which focuses on pre-clinical psychiatry and neurology. Additionally, teaching psychiatry didactics in the 3rd year clerkship, assisting with mid-clerkship evaluations, and teaching and mentorship in the psychiatry residency program will be required.  Collaborations with both basic science and clinical faculty to integrate and reinforce psychiatry concepts throughout the M.D. program curriculum is an essential element of this role.  All faculty are expected to pursue scholarly activities to fulfill the criteria for academic advancement. General and specialty-trained psychiatrists with an interest in medical education are encouraged to apply.

The College of Medicine aspires to become an extraordinary research-based institution training physicians of the future who will become exemplary clinicians, leaders in medicine, scholars in science, innovators in medical technology and compassionate providers of health care. 


Clinical Responsibilities (30-40%)

Psychiatric medical care will be provided at UCF Health Faculty Practice, an expanding adult outpatient multi-specialty clinic.  The successful candidate will provide care in a team that embraces other health care disciplines and involves collaborating with physicians and advanced practice practitioners from a variety of specialties including Primary Care, Rheumatology, Endocrinology, Dermatology, Cardiology, and Ophthalmology.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Candidates must hold an M.D./D.O. from an accredited institution. Candidates must be eligible for licensure or licensed to practice in the state of Florida. Must be board certified or board eligible by the American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology upon completion of training. Board certification would be expected within two (2) years of completion of training.
  • The candidate’s scholarly background and experience must be commensurate with the faculty rank for which the application is submitted.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience teaching medical students and/or residents in an LCME/ACGME accredited program.
  • Commitment to student-centered, active learning in a multidisciplinary environment that integrates basic sciences with clinical application.
  • Proficiency with instructional technology and digital platforms.
  • Track record of scholarly activity.

Additional Application Materials Required: 

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following: 

  • A curriculum vitae. 
  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest. 

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later. 

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.
