Job.JobTitle: Professor and Miller Technology Endowed Chair in Intelligent Work Systems, The Barry S. Miller College of Business
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The Barry S. Miller College of Business at the University of Central Florida invites applications for the Miller Technology Endowed Chair in Intelligent Work Systems, a 9-month tenured position at the rank of professor. This position is located on the UCF Main Campus with an anticipated start date in Fall 2027.

The central question addressed by this chair is: How should organizations design work and allocate responsibilities between humans and intelligent technologies to maximize organizational performance? Advances in artificial intelligence, robotics, automation, and digital platforms are fundamentally reshaping the nature of work. We seek a scholar whose work advances understanding of organizational design, the future of work, human-AI collaboration, leadership, workforce systems, organizational behavior, decision-making, or related areas.

This endowed chair is part of a broader investment, five endowed chairs in all, each committed to advancing scholarship and education at the intersection of technology and business transformation. The Miller Chairs are not organized around traditional academic disciplines, but around consequential problems emerging from the intersection of technology, organizations, and markets.

Miller Chairs are intended for scholars whose work has shaped—or has the clear potential to shape—how organizations function in a technology-driven economy. The successful candidate will play a central role in shaping the intellectual direction of the College’s technology-focused initiatives and will contribute to the School of Technology Leadership and Innovation (STLI), a university-wide initiative focused on translating advances in technology into organizational capability, market innovation, and executive practice.

The UCF College of Business is one of the largest business schools in the United States and is located in Orlando, one of the nation’s fastest growing and most dynamic economic regions. UCF is a Carnegie R1 institution and is recognized for its leadership in innovation, partnerships, and its identity as Florida’s Technology University.

The college is actively investing in initiatives that position it at the forefront of technology-enabled business education, including interdisciplinary programs, applied research collaborations, and new models of engagement with industry.

Responsibilities include:

  • Serve as an intellectual architect for the college’s Intelligent Work Systems initiative by building collaborations among faculty, industry, and government that establish UCF as a national leader in the field.
  • Demonstrate ability to translate scholarly expertise into organizational practice through industry partnerships, executive education, public engagement, policy influence, or other mechanisms that create measurable impact.
  • Conduct high-impact research on how organizations design and manage the interaction between people, technology, and decision systems.
  • Contribute to the development of new academic programs and executive offerings aligned with the College’s technology focus.

  

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in business, economics, information systems, engineering, computer science, psychology, or a closely related field from an AACSB-accredited (or equivalent) institution at time of application.
  • A record of scholarly achievement sufficient to qualify for appointment with tenure at the rank of Full Professor in the College of Business.
  • Demonstrated impact in research related to organizational design, leadership, decision-making, or technology-enabled work systems.
  • Evidence of an active and sustained research agenda with publications in leading peer-reviewed journals.
  • Experience teaching at the undergraduate and/or graduate level.

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Candidates should demonstrate a history of engaging with organizations in ways that shape practice, including through applied research, advisory roles, or collaborative initiatives.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead interdisciplinary collaborations that produce new research, educational programs or industry partnerships.
  • Commitment to translating scholarship into executive education and organizational capability.
  • A record of leadership in shaping academic programs, research centers, or major initiatives.

 

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • Cover letter
  • Curriculum vitae
  • Research statement
  • Teaching statement
  • Contact information for three professional references will be required prior to extending an offer

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Dr. Pradeep Bhardwaj at Pradeep.bhardwaj@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

The Opportunity


The Singla Lab at the University of Central Florida College of Medicine in Orlando seeks a highly motivated, creative, and ambitious postdoctoral fellow to study treatment resistance and tumor-microenvironment interactions in various cancer models and associated toxicological studies.


This part of the project focuses on developing cancer models; therefore, we are looking for a postdoctoral fellow who will conduct innovative cancer research using functional studies with 3D culture models and organoids. Identify the underlying mechanisms using cell biology and molecular biology techniques. They will also be expected to perform research, write manuscripts, assist in grant proposals, and present their findings at local and national meetings. The fellow should work independently, lead project(s), troubleshoot issues, present their work, and train other lab members as part of their postdoctoral training. 


Prof. Singla’s lab is a friendly and welcoming place with great excitement for cancer and cardiovascular research.


Minimum Qualifications


The ideal candidate should have a Ph.D. in cancer biology/immunology/molecular biology with a strong background in cancer cell culture models (2D, 3D, and organoids), cancer mouse models such as xenotransplantation models, and basic and advanced molecular biology techniques. Candidates should possess a track record of scientific productivity, as well as excellent oral, written, and interpersonal communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications


Experience in testing preclinical animal models, including PDX using humanized mice, syngeneic mouse models, and xenografts, is highly desired.


Additional Application Materials Required


A cover letter, CV, names and contact information of three professional references, and date of availability will be required to be considered.

Post Doctoral Scholar

 

The Opportunity:

The Department of Civil, Environmental and Construction Engineering at the University of Central Florida is inviting a motivated Postdoctoral Associate to join the DISCOVER (Digital-Twin Infrastructure Science for Operations and Visualization in Engineering Resilience) Laboratory and become part of an interdisciplinary research team conducting research at the convergence of multiscale computational mechanics, civil infrastructure resilience and digital twin modeling. However, other more-experienced candidates will also be given consideration.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Full-time, tenure-earning or tenured faculty position in Transportation Engineering Systems within Civil Engineering. UCF's Transportation Science program ranks first in the U.S. and will house the newly established Florida Transportation Research Institute.

Good fit if you have a doctorate in Engineering or related field, expertise in transportation (vehicles, logistics, data analytics, traffic operations, or related areas), and research experience.

Full job description

The Opportunity   

 The University of Central Florida (UCF) is dedicated to increasing the prominence of its Civil, Environmental, and Construction Engineering (CECE) Department. UCF offers B.S., M.S., and Ph.D. degrees in Civil Engineering and the undergraduate degree is ABET-accredited.  

The CECE department houses several high-impact labs. Transportation Science and Technology at UCF is ranked the top program in the U.S. and 19th globally in the 2025 Shanghai Ranking. Learn more about the Transportation Science program at UCF here: https://www.ucf.edu/transportation-science/. The CECE department faculty maintain diverse, active, and successful research programs. Learn more about the CECE department at https://www.cece.ucf.edu/. UCF is a leader in Transportation in Florida and will house the newly established multimillion-dollar Florida Transportation Research Institute (FTRI) mandated by the Florida legislature and Florida Secretary of Transportation in 2024. 

To strengthen these efforts, we invite applications for a full-time, 9-month, tenure-earning assistant professor or tenured associate professor, or professor position in Transportation Engineering Systems within the Civil Engineering program, with an anticipated start date of August 8, 2027.  

The selected candidate hired for this position is expected to have either demonstrated (tenured) or shown a clear potential (tenure-earning) for creative and independent research that has led (tenured) or would potentially lead (tenure-earning) to strong extramurally funded research and national/international recognition. The selected candidate is also expected to train postdoctoral scholars, serve as the primary advisor for graduate students, and teach graduate and undergraduate courses in Civil Engineering.  

Minimum Qualifications:  

  • A doctorate from an accredited institution in Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field at the time of the appointment.  

  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured associate professor or professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a demonstrated record of teaching, research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of associate professor or professor in the applicable tenure home.  

  • Candidates must have expertise in one or more aspects of transportation, including but not limited to the following: connected vehicles/automated vehicles’ applications; transportation technologies; traveler behavior and demand modeling; freight and transportation logistics; applications of econometrics and data analytics to transportation planning; traffic signals’ control and technologies; traffic operations; smart mobility; big data and internet of things; air mobility; transportation economics and policies; etc.  

  • Successful applicants will have either demonstrated or shown a clear potential for creative and independent research that has led or would lead to strong extramurally funded research. 

  

Preferred Qualifications:  

  • Preference will be given to those with a few years of experience in academia or industry with a proven ability to publish in top transportation and transportation technology journals. 

Additional Application Materials Required:  

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:  

  • A curriculum vitae, 

  • A signed cover letter, 

  • A two-page maximum statement outlining research vision and teaching interests,

  • A list of at least three professional references complete with address, phone number, and email address. 

   

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.  

  

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.  

  

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: CECESearch@ucf.edu or Dr. Mohamed Abdel-Aty at m.aty@ucf.edu

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Full-time, 9-month lecturer position teaching nursing leadership and management courses primarily in online MSN and DNP-Executive programs at UCF's College of Nursing. Rank (lecturer, associate lecturer, or senior lecturer) determined by credentials and experience; start date Fall 2027.

Good fit if you have a doctorate in nursing or health-related field, current RN license, and documented teaching experience in academic settings.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The College of Nursing at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for multiple full-time, 9-month, non-tenure earning faculty positions as Lecturer in the Department of Nursing Systems. The selected candidates will teach nursing leadership and management courses, primarily in the online MSN-Leadership and Management program, the DNP-Executive programs, and other programs as assigned. The positions will be located on the UCF Academic Health Sciences Campus at Lake Nona and are expected to start Fall 2027. The appropriate rank (lecturer, associate lecturer, or senior lecturer) will be determined based upon the selected candidates’ credentials and prior experience.

The selected candidates will work collaboratively with colleagues, remain actively involved in professional organizations, and actively participate in College of Nursing faculty governance.

Responsibilities include:

  • Teach online courses in the MSN -Leadership and Management Program, DNP -Executive Program, and other graduate or undergraduate courses as assigned and qualified.

  • Plan, organize, and deliver instruction that supports student learning and success.

  • Support the College of Nursing mission and departmental efforts to advance excellence in teaching and learning.

  • Collaborate with the department chair and faculty colleagues to plan, develop, and improve courses and curricula.

  • Advise and mentor students and, as appropriate to rank, support adjunct faculty and early-career faculty.

  • Participate in department, college, and university service, including committee leadership as appropriate to rank.

Minimum Qualifications for a Lecturer:

  • Earned doctorate in nursing or a health-related field from an accredited institution at he time of application.

  • Graduate degree in nursing (master’s degree in nursing if doctoral degree is not in nursing).

  • Unencumbered RN license. Florida licensure expected by date of hire; with multi-state endorsement expected by date of hire.

  • Documented teaching experience (online, hybrid, and/or classroom) in an academic setting.

Minimum Qualifications for an Associate Lecturer:

  • Earned doctorate in nursing or a health-related field from an accredited institution at the time of application.

  • Graduate degree in nursing (master’s degree in nursing if doctoral degree is not in nursing).

  • Unencumbered RN license. Florida licensure expected by date of hire; with multi-state endorsement expected by date of hire.

  • Five or more years of full-time academic teaching experience (online, hybrid, and/or classroom) at the baccalaureate level or above as demonstrated on CV.

  • A consistent record of excellence in teaching and service to colleges and universities as demonstrated by teaching/course evaluations and CV.

Minimum Qualifications for a Senior Lecturer:

  • Earned doctorate in nursing or a health-related field from an accredited institution at the time of application.

  • Graduate degree in nursing (master’s degree in nursing if doctoral degree is not in nursing).

  • Unencumbered RN license. Florida licensure expected by date of hire; with multi-state endorsement expected by date of hire.

  • Five or more years of full-time academic teaching experience (online, hybrid, and/or classroom) at the baccalaureate level or above.

  • A consistent record of excellence in teaching and service to colleges and universities as demonstrated by teaching/course evaluations, and CV.

  • Demonstrated leadership in student advising, professional development, and/or mentoring.

  • Demonstrated leadership in peer mentoring including orientation of new or adjunct faculty.

  • Demonstrated leadership in curriculum or course development, enhancement, and/or revision.

  • Demonstrated leadership in departmental, college, university, and professional service, through leadership roles or contributing leadership to specific work of the committees.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Expertise in nursing leadership, including healthcare finance, quality improvement, patient safety, and systems leadership.

  • Demonstrated experience designing courses and curricula.

  • Certification or formal preparation in online education quality standards, such as Quality Matters or the Online Learning Consortium.

  • Experience using virtual simulation applications in teaching or learning.

  • Experience teaching online courses in leadership, informatics or AI, population health management, financial management, ethics and professional behavior, or organizational dynamics.

  • Certification in nursing leadership, such as NE-BC, NEA-BC, CNML, or CENP.

  • Demonstrated scholarship, such as publications or national presentations.

  • Active participation in professional organizations related to nursing leadership, nursing management, or executive health leadership.

  • Formal training or experience in leadership coaching, executive coaching, or mentorship programs that support leadership development in healthcare settings.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.

  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as teaching experience/interest.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

UCF College of Medicine seeks three full-time primary care physicians (Internal Medicine or Family Medicine) for outpatient practice in Orlando. Faculty positions include patient care, teaching medical learners, and potential clinical research involvement.

Good fit if you have an M.D. or D.O., Florida licensure or eligibility, board certification or eligibility, and prefer outpatient settings.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida (UCF), College of Medicine Faculty Practice at UCF Health in Orlando, FL is seeking three (3) full-time primary care physicians in Internal Medicine or Family Medicine to join an expanding multi-specialty academic practice. Applicants should be exceptional clinicians who have demonstrated a value-based philosophy of patient care and are seeking an exclusively outpatient care environment. The majority of the assignments for the selected candidates will be to provide direct patient care while building their outpatient practice in collaboration with multiple specialties. Being faculty in the College of Medicine, they may have small roles for teaching or precepting medical learners and other health-related trainees (e.g., for medical students and interprofessional education), as well as participating in clinical research (e.g., sponsored pharmaceutical trials). In that the UCF Health practice is growing in size and scope, the faculty assignment is likely to include a role in Federally Qualified Health Clinics (FQHCs) which would involve providing care in a team that embraces other health care disciplines and involves advanced practice practitioners. The positions are non-tenure track clinical appointments at the rank of assistant, associate or professor of medicine. These are full-time positions at five days a week, with protected non-face-to-face patient care and administrative time.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Candidates must have an M.D. or D.O. degree from an accredited medical or osteopathic school.

  • Candidates must be eligible for licensure or actively licensed to practice in the state of Florida.

  • Must be boarded or board eligible in their specialty upon completion of training. Board certification would be expected within two (2) years of completion of training.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • It is preferred that the candidate have at least three years of experience in a busy high-volume outpatient clinic practice as well as prior experience in rendering care that involves physician extenders.

  • Previous experience working with medical as well as interprofessional health care learners in a clinical outpatient setting is desired.

  • Candidates with publications or other scholarly output are encouraged to apply.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload a curriculum vitae and cover letter.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Job Posting Title: 

Post Doctoral Scholar

The Opportunity:

University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for one two-year Postdoctoral Research Scholar position at the HARP Lab (Human Factors, AI, Risk, and Privacy Lab). The candidate will work with Dr. Grace Fox and members of her interdisciplinary team at UCF and collaborate with academic partners within UCF and internationally. The candidate will work on several collaborative projects and funding proposals related to the research areas of focus at the HARP lab including cybersecurity, privacy, artificial intelligence, risk, trust, and human behavior. The successful candidate will collaborate with faculty, graduate students, and external partners.

Responsibilities:

Responsibilities include designing and conducting empirical behavioral research using mixed methods, qualitative and quantitative research designs including interviews, focus groups, surveys, and experiments, analyzing quantitative and qualitative data, publishing in leading conferences and journals across various disciplines, contributing to grant proposal development; mentoring graduate and undergraduate researchers.

The candidate will work with Dr. Fox and her team to manage project milestones, participate in team meetings, lead and contribute to the dissemination of findings across several projects in collaboration with graduate students, and faculty collaborators in UCF and internationally. The candidate must have excellent interpersonal, writing, and research skills, initiative, strong time management and organizational skills, and the ability to prioritize and meet deadlines and work independently and as a research team member. 

Minimum Qualifications: 

  •  A Ph.D. degree from an accredited educational institution in Cybersecurity, Computer Science, Management Information Systems, Psychology, Human Factors, Human-Computer Interaction, Statistics Data Science, or a related discipline is required.
  • The candidate must have experience conducting and publishing research in one or more areas related to privacy and cybersecurity from a behavioral perspective.
  • Experience designing and leading quantitative human factors studies.
  • Record of publishing in well regarded journals/conferences within their field of study.
  • Strong experience in various advanced statistical methods (e.g., HLM, SEM, non-linear dynamical systems).
  • Experience working in multidisciplinary teams.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • The candidates should have future research publication goals and plans.
  • Prior experience in designing and conducting research experiments is highly desired.
  • Experience working on funded projects and proposals.
  • Strong Programming skills (e.g., R, Python, MATLAB) are a plus.

  • A curriculum vitae.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Job.JobTitle: Research Assistant Professor of Medicine, Biomedical Optics and Photonics
Job.CustomJobTypeName: Adjunct / Professor, Education / Training, Biomedical Scientist
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Research-focused assistant professor position at UCF College of Medicine applying optics and photonics to biomedical health challenges. Role includes developing a funded research program and training graduate students, with access to state-of-the-art facilities and collaboration opportunities with the CREOL College of Optics and Photonics.

Good fit if you hold a Ph.D. in science, have postdoctoral experience, a record of research productivity, and experience bridging biomedical science with optics or photonics

Full job description

The Opportunity

The Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences (BSBS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF), College of Medicine (COM), seeks outstanding applicants for a 12-month, non-tenure-earning, research-focused COM faculty position at the rank of assistant professor of medicine.  The research focus should be on the use of optics and/or photonics to address research topics related to human health. Applicants with a biomedical research program that can establish collaborations with the UCF CREOL College of Optics and Photonics (https://creol.ucf.edu) are encouraged to apply.

The successful applicant must hold a science Ph.D. from an accredited institution, have postdoctoral experience, a record of research productivity, and relevant experience with potential for collaboration across biomedical science with optics and/or photonics. Preference will be given to candidates who have already demonstrated experience in bridging both fields. In addition to developing or maintaining a well-funded research program, hired faculty will be expected to actively participate in the training of graduate students. The UCF College of Medicine provides faculty with highly competitive state-supported salaries, generous startup packages and laboratory space. The research facilities are state-of-the-art and include BSL3 laboratory space, transgenic animal facilities and excellent core equipment.

The UCF College of Medicine is a research-based medical school with a culture based on partnerships and collaboration. As part of the UCF College of Medicine, BSBS has 59 full-time faculty, more than 2,000 undergraduate majors and 150 graduate students in M.S., Ph.D., and M.D./Ph.D. programs located on two campuses. The new hire will have a lab located at the health sciences campus at Lake Nona. BSBS at Lake Nona is a critical part of the biomedical cluster at “Medical City” that includes the new UCF Lake Nona Medical Center Hospital, the UCF Lake Nona Cancer Center, the Orlando VA Medical Center, and the Nemours Children’s Hospital. Further information on the BSBS and its research divisions can be found at http://med.ucf.edu/biomed. 

The UCF CREOL College of Optics and Photonics (https://creol.ucf.edu) is one the world’s foremost institutions for research and education in optics and photonic science and engineering. The college offers Ph.D. and M.S. degrees in optics and photonics, and a B.S. degree in photonic science and engineering. The faculty engage in fundamental and applied research and education in lasers, optical fibers, semiconductor and integrated photonic devices, nonlinear and quantum optics, imaging, sensing and displays.

UCF is one of the nation's largest universities with over 60,000 students enrolled in bachelor's and master's degrees, doctoral programs, and a fully accredited M.D. program. UCF is located in Orlando, a progressive metropolitan area and a major player in high-tech industry with a top ranked Research Park.

Minimum Qualifications

Candidates must have a science Ph.D. from an accredited institution, have postdoctoral experience, a record of research productivity, and relevant experience with potential for collaboration across biomedical science with optics and/or photonics.

Preferred Qualifications

Demonstrated experience in bridging both fields of biomedical science with optics and/or photonics.

Additional Application Materials Required

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. 

In addition to the online application, interested candidates must upload a cover letter, a curriculum vitae, and a three-page summary of current and future research plans.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

Review of applications will begin in October 2026 and continue until the position is filled.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Justine Tigno-Aranjuez, Associate Professor of Medicine at Justine.Tigno-Aranjuez@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants

All applicants must be authorized to work for any U.S. employer. H-1B visa sponsorship is not available for this position, and the university cannot accommodate H-1B transfers or employment-based visa processing for individuals currently sponsored by another employer. 

This position is funded by contracts and grants and is contingent upon available funding.

Job.JobTitle: Visiting Instructor or Lecturer, Economist in Residence
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Nine-month visiting instructor or lecturer position teaching economics undergraduates at UCF's College of Business. Role includes serving as Economist-in-Residence to establish a new Economic Decision Systems Initiative focused on how organizations design decisions in data and technology-rich environments.

Good fit if you have a master's or terminal degree in economics, applied economic reasoning to organizational decision-making, and interest in building new programs and partnerships.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The Barry S. Miller College of Business at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 9-month, non-tenure earning, visiting instructor or lecturer to teach and mentor undergraduate students in the Department of Economics. The selected candidate will also have responsibilities as Economist-in-Residence to help lead a new Initiative on Economic Decision Systems with an anticipated start date as early as Spring 2027. This appointment is renewable for up to 4 years and is located on the UCF main campus.

The Economic Decision Systems Initiative is focused on how organizations design and operate decision systems in environments where data, technology, and human judgment increasingly interact. Through the Economic Decision Systems Lab, organizations will bring real decision problems into a working environment where faculty, students, and organizational partners examine how decisions are structured, how incentives are aligned, and how organizational capability develops over time.

The Economist-in-Residence will play a foundational role in helping establish the operating model for the Initiative. This role is intended for an economist with a dynamic, entrepreneurial interest in building new programs, creating applied partnerships, and translating economic reasoning into organizational practice.

The successful candidate will lead applied projects and will mentor students participating in structured project experiences. The projects will be tied to real organizational decision environments involving issues such as organizational design, decision rights, pricing systems, automation, risk and resilience, and human-machine decision integration.

This institution-building role focuses on establishing the Initiative during its formative phase. Continued appointment may be considered based on the success of the Initiative, the evolution of organizational partnerships, and the strategic direction of the college. Success will be defined primarily by the establishment of a functioning and sustainable Economic Decision Systems Lab through the development of a distinctive student experience, meaningful industry engagement, and successful applied projects.

Over the initial period, the Economist-in-Residence will be expected to help establish:

  • a distinctive student experience tied to real organizational decision environment

  • sustained engagement with external organizational partners

  • a repeatable pipeline of applied decision-system projects

  • operating processes and practices that allow the Initiative to function as a durable platform for applied engagement

  • visible integration of economic reasoning into organizational decision-making challenges involving technology, data systems, and human judgment

About the College of Business

Consistent with UCF’s identity as Florida’s technological university, the College of Business is expanding its focus on technology-enabled business transformation, industry engagement, and applied research while remaining deeply committed to student success and academic excellence.

The College is entering a period of significant strategic investment and institutional momentum following a transformative $50 million philanthropic commitment from entrepreneur and investor Barry S. Miller. At the heart of this commitment is the focus on the intersection of business, technology, markets, organizations, and decision-making.

Economic Decision Systems represents one component of the college’s broader effort to help organizations navigate environments increasingly shaped by data systems, artificial intelligence, and technological change.


Minimum Qualifications:

  • A master's degree (for an instructor) or a terminal degree (for a lecturer) in economics or a related discipline from an accredited institution at the time of application.

  • Demonstrated experience applying economic reasoning and data analysis to support organizational decision-making in data-rich environments.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience applying economics to improve decisions in industry, consulting, government, financial services, technology, or other organizations.

  • Experience leading applied projects at the intersection of economic reasoning, analytics, technology, and organizational design.

  • Experience mentoring students or early-career professionals, or leading collaborative teams.

  • Experience integrating human and artificial intelligence for organizational decision-making.

  • A dynamic, entrepreneurial interest in developing partnerships and new programs.

  • Ability and willingness to engage external organizations and help shape the direction of the Initiative.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.

  • A letter of interest describing qualifications and how their experience aligns with the goals of the Initiative and the qualifications listed above.

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search should be directed to: Uluc Aysun at uluc.aysun@ucf.edu.

Special Instructions to the Applicants:

On March 10, 2026, UCF received clarification that the current State moratorium on H‑1B visas applies not only to new sponsorships but also to H‑1B transfers into the institution. This means we are unable to process transfers for individuals currently holding H‑1B status with other employers. UCF will share updates as soon as State guidance changes or additional details become available.

Job.JobTitle: Instructor or Lecturer, Health Sciences – Nutrition & Dietetics
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity:  

The Department of Health Sciences in the College of Health Professions and Sciences (CHPS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 9-month, non-tenure earning, instructor or lecturer position. The position is open to master’s and doctoral level Registered Dietitian Nutritionists who hold valid credentials through the commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR). The preferred start date is as early as January 2027, but no later than August 2027. 

We are seeking a dynamic and collaborative faculty member to support undergraduate education and the development, implementation and ongoing operation of a newly approved Master of Science in Nutrition Science and Dietetics, with the goal of achieving ACEND candidacy as a Nutrition and Dietetics Coordinated Program (CP).

The successful candidate will be expected to: 

  • Teach undergraduate and/or graduate courses in nutrition and related areas using evidence based, student centered instructional approaches.

  • Develop graduate courses with content specific to program needs using evidence-based, student-centered teaching approaches.

  • Supervise and evaluate students during supervised experiential learning (SEL) across diverse practice settings.

  • Foster and maintain partnerships with healthcare systems, community organizations, food and nutrition service providers, preceptors and other stakeholders to support high-quality experiential learning opportunities.

  • Contribute to student recruitment and mentoring.

  • Pursue ongoing professional development to maintain currency in nutrition and dietetics practice, education, and competency-based learning models.

  • Contribute to a collaborative, student focused academic environment.

  • Engage in scholarly activities, service, and professional development.

    Minimum Qualifications: 

    • Master’s degree (for an instructor) or doctorate, Ph.D. or equivalent (for a lecturer) in human nutrition/dietetics or a closely related discipline from an accredited academic institution at the time of application.  

    • Credentialed as a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist (RDN) by the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR). 

    • Minimum 4 years full-time professional practice post-CDR credentialing with experience providing patient care in hospital, rehabilitation, or long-term care facilities or managing food service operations. 

    Preferred Qualifications: 

    • Experience applying advanced clinical nutrition skills as a member of an interdisciplinary team caring for medically complex patients in a hospital, rehabilitation, or long-term care facility or directing food service operations in these facilities. 

    • Teaching, preferably in an academic setting or mentoring students in professional practice.  

    • Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills. 

    • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders. 

    Additional Application Materials Required: 
    UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, candidates will be required to upload the following documents: 

    • Cover letter outlining your qualifications and how they align with and support success in this position’s roles and responsibilities.

    • Curriculum vitae 

    • Teaching philosophy

Job.JobTitle: Lecturer, Health Sciences – Nutrition and Dietetics
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Experience: 5+ years
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Develop and teach graduate and undergraduate courses for a newly approved Master of Science in Nutrition Science and Dietetics program at UCF. Serve as program coordinator working toward ACEND accreditation while supervising student experiential learning and maintaining partnerships with healthcare systems.

Good fit if you hold a doctoral degree in nutrition or related field, are a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist, and have at least 5 years of dietetics practice or education experience.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The Department of Health Sciences in the College of Health Professions and Sciences (CHPS) at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for a 12-month, non-tenure earning, lecturer position. The position is open to doctoral level Registered Dietitian Nutritionists who hold valid credentials through the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR). The preferred start date is as early as January 2027, but no later than August 2027.

The Department of Health Sciences is home to 19 full-time faculty and approximately 3000 undergraduate students in the major and about 500 students in the minor. We offer an undergraduate degree in Health Sciences with two tracks – Pre-Clinical and Health Promotion and a Master of Science degree in Health Promotion and Behavioral Science. Development of a Master of Science in Nutrition Science and Dietetics is a future goal pending university approval. The Department of Health Sciences is recognized for its high-quality educational offerings and growing research impact. For more information about the Department of Health Sciences, visit our website at: UCF Department of Health Sciences - College of Health Professions and Sciences.

We are seeking a dynamic and collaborative faculty member to support the development, implementation and ongoing operation of a newly approved Master of Science in Nutrition Science and Dietetics, with the goal of achieving ACEND candidacy as a Nutrition and Dietetics Coordinated Program (CP). This position plays a pivotal role as a coordinator working in tandem with the program director in shaping an innovative, competency-based graduate program designed to prepare future Registered Dietitian Nutritionists through integrated coursework and supervised experiential learning.

The successful candidate will be expected to:

  • Develop graduate level courses and learning activities aligned with the competencies and performance indicators outlined in the 2027 ACEND Accreditation Standards for Nutrition and Dietetics CP.

  • Teach graduate courses that require instruction in specific advanced content areas, including nutrition assessment, medical nutrition therapy, nutrition and metabolism, or food science and food service management using evidence‑based, student‑centered teaching approaches.

  • Teach undergraduate courses in nutrition and related areas.

  • Serve as a program coordinator assisting the program director with program development, including curriculum/course development, site development for supervised experiential learning (SEL), student placement coordination, assessment of student competence, program compliance, reporting, and continuous quality improvement.

  • Foster and maintain partnerships with healthcare systems, community organizations, food and nutrition service providers, preceptors and other stakeholders to support high-quality supervised experiential learning opportunities.

  • Supervise and evaluate graduate students during supervised experiential learning across diverse practice settings.

  • Contribute to program accreditation activities, including documentation, data collection, assessment, management, and preparation of materials for ACEND review.

  • Contribute to student recruitment, advising, mentoring, and retention efforts.

  • Pursue ongoing professional development to maintain currency in nutrition and dietetics practice, education, and competency-based learning models.

  • Contribute to a collaborative, student focused academic environment.

  • Engage in scholarly activities, service, and professional development.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Doctoral degree (i.e., PhD, DCN, DrPH) in Nutrition, Dietetics, or a closely related field by the start of the appointment.

  • Credentialed as a Registered Dietitian Nutritionist by the Commission on Dietetic Registration (CDR).

  • Minimum 5 years of professional experience in dietetics practice and/or education.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong practice-based experience providing inpatient hospital-based clinical care and/or food service management.

  • Familiarity with ACEND accreditation standards and processes, particularly those relevant to the 2027 ACEND Accreditation Standards for Nutrition and Dietetics CP.

  • Strong record of at least one of the following: teaching, mentorship, scholarship, or leadership.

  • Excellent communication, organizational, and interpersonal skills.

  • Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with diverse stakeholders.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, candidates will be required to upload:

  • Cover letter addressing qualifications and how these will contribute to the successful launch and evolution of the Nutrition Science and Dietetics CP

  • Curriculum vitae

  • Teaching philosophy

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Only applications that contain all required materials will be considered. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit a list of references and official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

The University of Central Florida Recreation and Wellness Center employs PRN (as needed) Athletic Trainers to serve in the supervision and coordination of the Recreation and Wellness Center’s overall sports medicine program, including, but not limited to: injury prevention, evaluation, management, and treatment of athletic injuries, short-term and long-term rehabilitation of athletic injuries, education and counseling of student-athletes, and athletics related health care administration in consultation with and under the supervision of the Athletic Training Coordinator and Physician(s).

Job.JobTitle: Professor and Chair, Department of Marketing
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Tenured professor and chair position in the Department of Marketing at the University of Central Florida's College of Business Administration, starting Fall 2027. The role leads the department during a period of institutional investment, including a $50 million philanthropic commitment, with focus on technology-informed marketing research and education.

Good fit if you have a Ph.D. in marketing, proven academic administrative leadership experience, and a record of research and teaching at the professor level.

Full job description

The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida’s (UCF) College of Business Administration invites applications for a 9-month, tenured professor and chair in the Department of Marketing. This position is located on the UCF main campus with an anticipated start date in Fall 2027.

The chair of the Department of Marketing will serve as a central leader in advancing the department’s academic, research, and external engagement missions during a period of significant institutional momentum and investment.

Consistent with UCF’s identity as Florida’s technological university, the College of Business is expanding its focus on technology-enabled business transformation, industry engagement, and applied research while remaining deeply committed to student success and academic excellence. The college is entering a period of significant strategic investment and institutional momentum following a transformative $50 million philanthropic commitment from entrepreneur and investor Barry S. Miller. This investment includes the creation of five $2 million endowed chairs intended to attract nationally recognized scholars working at the intersection of business, technology, markets, and organizational transformation. Together, these investments signal a long-term institutional commitment to building nationally prominent programs, expanding research capacity, strengthening industry partnerships, and positioning the college as a leader in preparing students and organizations to thrive in an economy increasingly shaped by data, automation, artificial intelligence, and technological change.

As a member of the college leadership team, the chair will work collaboratively with faculty, college leadership, alumni, and industry partners to guide the department’s strategic direction, strengthen its national visibility, and expand its impact in research, education, and industry engagement.

The chair is expected to support and elevate the department’s full range of scholarly strengths while helping position the department at the forefront of understanding how technology is transforming markets, organizations, and consumer experiences. The successful candidate will foster a collaborative and research-active environment that supports faculty development, intellectual diversity, and innovation across teaching, scholarship, and external engagement. The chair will also play a key role in strengthening relationships with industry and integrating those relationships into both the student experience and faculty research activity in ways that enhance career readiness, organizational relevance, and scholarly impact.

The chair will work closely with an associate chair who supports academic programs and departmental operations, enabling shared leadership and effective management of the department’s activities.

Chair Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Provide strategic leadership aligned with the department’s mission and priorities.

  • Support faculty research productivity across diverse methodological traditions.

  • Oversee academic programs and curriculum innovation.

  • Support and strengthen the department’s doctoral program and contribute to the continued development of graduate and executive education offerings, including MBA programs.

  • Lead faculty hiring, mentoring, and evaluation processes.

  • Build and sustain relationships with industry, alumni, and external stakeholders.

  • Promote student success and career readiness.

  • Engage in fundraising and development activities in collaboration with the college.

  • Represent the department within the college, university, and broader academic and professional communities.

The department has articulated a clear strategic direction centered on understanding how emerging technologies are reshaping markets, consumer behavior, business strategy, and societal outcomes. Building on existing strengths across consumer behavior, quantitative modeling, marketing strategy, and professional selling, the department seeks to become a recognized leader in technology-informed marketing research and education.

To support this direction, the department is actively pursuing several strategic initiatives, including:

  • Development of a Technology and Markets Living Lab integrating research, teaching, and industry collaboration.

  • Creation of a Marketing Insights Collaborative to enhance research productivity and visibility.

  • Establishment of a Sales Center supporting the department’s nationally ranked Professional Selling Program.

  • Launch of Professional MBA concentrations in Supply Chain and Digital Marketing.

  • Expansion of corporate partnerships, speaker series, and conference initiatives.

  • Progress toward becoming a named and endowed Department of Marketing.

The department values methodological and theoretical diversity and seeks to support excellence across behavioral, quantitative, and strategy-oriented scholarships. Faculty members are encouraged to engage collaboratively across disciplinary perspectives while contributing to the department’s growing focus on technology-enabled market transformation.

The department offers undergraduate, master’s, and doctoral programs, including a Ph.D. in marketing, and plays an active role in the college’s professional and executive MBA programs. These programs provide opportunities for engagement in doctoral education, executive development, and industry-facing teaching while contributing to the department’s visibility and impact.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. in Marketing or a closely related field from an AACSB-accredited institution at the time of application.

  • To be eligible for appointment as a tenured professor upon hire, the selected candidate must have a demonstrated record teaching, research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of professor.

  • Demonstrated academic administrative leadership experience (e.g., department chair, associate chair, program director, center director, or comparable role).

  • Evidence of scholarly contributions in marketing or related fields.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated ability to lead and support a research-active, multidisciplinary environment.

  • Demonstrated ability to support and respect diverse research traditions, including behavioral, quantitative, and strategy-oriented scholarship.

  • Record of effective leadership in complex academic environments, including faculty development, program oversight, and external engagement.

  • Interest in or engagement with research related to technology-driven marketing contexts.

  • Experience fostering collaboration across faculty with varied methodological approaches.

  • Demonstrated success in faculty development and mentoring.

  • Experience building partnerships with industry and external stakeholders.

  • Evidence of involvement in program development or innovation.

  • Experience with fundraising, corporate engagement, or development initiatives.

  • Leadership roles in academic or professional organizations.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • Letter of interest

  • Curriculum vitae

  • Leadership statement (optional but encouraged)

  • List of references

  • Selected publications or working papers

  • Evidence of teaching effectiveness

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Job.JobTitle: Medical Dermatology (Assistant, Associate or Professor of Medicine - Clinical Track)
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

The University of Central Florida College of Medicine (UCF-COM) Department of Medicine is seeking a full-time medical Dermatology physician and a full-time procedural Mohs dermatology physician to join our outpatient UCF Health academic practice. These are non-tenure track clinical positions at the assistant, associate or professor of medicine level.

Medical Dermatologist:

We are seeking a medical dermatologist with strong skills in general and procedural dermatology (non-Mohs) to complement the expertise of our current dermatology faculty.  The selected candidate will participate in or help to develop cross-specialty clinics (e.g., for dermato-rheumatology, dermato-oncology or occupational dermatology). Applicants need to have demonstrated outstanding clinical practice delivering high quality, value-based, team-based care.

Collaboration with other care providers is an essential component of this position. Examples include working with rheumatology faculty, fellows and internal medicine residents.  On occasion there will be medical students, residents and fellows from our Internal Medicine residency and fellowship programs rotating through our clinics. There will also be a small component of undergraduate and graduate medical education instruction.

Mohs Dermatologist:

This position is for a procedural Mohs dermatologist to complement the expertise of our current dermatology faculty and practice in a state-of-the-art Mohs surgery facility. Applicants need to have demonstrated outstanding clinical practice delivering high quality, value-based, team-based care.  On occasion medical students, residents and fellows from our Internal Medicine residency and fellowship programs will be rotating through our clinics. There will also be a small component of undergraduate and graduate medical education instruction.

The success of the university faculty practice, UCF Health, has led to continuing growth and expansion that includes modern state-of-the-art dermatology clinic facilities, and expansion of multiple specialties across our academic departments and participating hospitals. Candidates interested in developing and growing dermatology services at UCF are desired.

These are  UCF Health clinical positions with opportunities to: collaborate with other dermatologists at nearby partner institutions (e.g., at the VA Medical Center, the Nemours Children’s Hospital and the UCF Lake Nona Medical Center); pursue interprofessional education with other members of our multi-disciplinary Academic Health Sciences Center; conduct clinical or translational research with the support of our extensive human research team;  pursue educational scholarship in collaboration with other COM faculty members; and serve as a formal medical student advisor or mentor. The chosen applicants will also be expected to provide service to the educational programs and other missions of the college and university.

The UCF College of Medicine educates and inspires individuals to be exemplary physicians and scientists, leaders in medicine, scholars in discovery, and adopters of innovative technology to improve the health and well-being of all. The College of Medicine is an LCME-accredited medical college with an annual matriculation of 120 medical students and is part of a new Academic Health Sciences Center which includes multiple health affairs disciplines.

The College of Medicine campus is part of a growing biomedical cluster known as “Medical City” at Lake Nona, which is dedicated to innovation in health and wellness and continues development east of the Orlando International Airport. The College of Medicine is located in a well-equipped medical education building with modern Anatomy, Histology and simulation laboratories, as well as a state-of-the-art library.  In addition to the medical school, the Lake Nona campus includes our recently opened university teaching hospital (UCF Lake Nona Hospital), a state-of-the-art research center at the Burnett School of Biomedical Sciences, multi-college graduate education programs, UCF outpatient clinics, the Orlando Veterans Affairs Medical Center, the Nemours Children’s Hospital, the new UCF Lake Nona Cancer Center, and the Guidewell Innovation research incubator. The nearby Osceola Regional Medical Center is another primary site of UME and GME instruction.

Minimum Qualifications:

Job.JobTitle: Dermatology Division Chief (Associate or Professor of Medicine)
Job.JobDescription:
The Opportunity

With the rapid successful growth of the University of Central Florida’s (UCF) Department of Medicine, Dermatology will now become its own Division to further our academic missions of education, research and high quality state-of-the-art clinical care. We seek an accomplished dermatologist with a strong vision for dermatology excellence to serve as the founding Division Chief with major leadership roles in the College of Medicine (COM) and the UCF Faculty Practice. The successful candidate will be at, or eligible for hire at, the associate professor or professor rank in the clinical or tenure tracks. The Chief will be charged with the goals to:

  • Grow the dermatology clinical service lines by the recruitment of multiple general dermatology and Mohs micrographic surgery faculty for our UCF Health Faculty Practice. The clinics are state-of-the-art facilities that include advanced Mohs technical and laboratory resources. The goal is to collaborate with faculty in other COM specialties to establish clinical programs of excellence that have impact for, and well-beyond, our local communities. The Chief will also work with clinic leadership to optimize the day-to-day operational performance of the Division’s faculty in delivering superior medical care with the highest quality, safety, ethical standards and financial practices.
  • Expand clinical and translational research with a focus on hypothesis-driven investigator-initiated externally funded studies, in addition to sponsored trials. This will be facilitated by a robust human research team which has offices in each of our primary clinic sites and extensive logistic administrative support. A goal is to further research pursuits aligned with our other COM disciplines, specifically with a focus on oncology and immunology research; the latter will be facilitated by clinical and laboratory resources at our UCF Cancer Center. Another aim is collaborative research and technology development with our faculty colleagues in the College of Optics and Photonics (e.g., for high-resolution imaging, laser therapeutics) and the College of Engineering and Computer Science.
  • Start a Dermatology Residency Program, which will be facilitated by planning that has already been underway including multiple training sites (e.g., the local VA Medical Center, private practitioners), dermatopathology and pediatrics.
  • Enrich our current medical school dermatology curriculum with new faculty for didactics and clinical rotations. The successful candidate will also arrange for the Division to participate in the current advising program for students seeking dermatology residencies.
  • Work with the Internal Medicine Residency and Fellowship Program Directors to incorporate dermatology rotations into the clinic schedule.
  • Establish co-specialty clinics such as dermatology-rheumatology for the purposes of patient care, learner education, and clinical or translational research.
  • Provide mentorship and other career guidance for COM’s trainees and faculty.
  • Provide leadership, personal and Divisional service to the Department, College and University by such activities as committee participation and a commitment to supporting our community.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • All candidates must have an M.D. or D.O. degree from an accredited university and be board certified in dermatology.
  • Three years of postgraduate clinical practice in an academic institution.
  • Previous experience building, leading or expanding a program, division, institute, other clinical service group or equivalent responsibility within an academic or academically affiliated organization.
  • Experience participating as faculty in a Dermatology Residency Program and/or Mohs Micrographic Surgery Fellowship Program.
  • Experience in clinical practice administration, management, or related academic leadership with demonstrable strong organization and process management skills.
  • Outstanding written and oral communication skills.
  • The candidate’s scholarly background and experience must be commensurate with the faculty rank for which the application is submitted.
  • To be eligible to be hired as a tenured associate professor or professor of medicine upon hire, the selected candidate must have a demonstrated record teaching, research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of associate professor or professor of medicine. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience as Program Director for a Dermatology Residency Program.
  • Experience as Program Director for a Mohs Microsurgery Fellowship Program.
  • Experience in dermatology didactic or clinical instruction at the medical school level.
  • Experience at the leadership level for the medical school dermatology curriculum.
  • Leadership experience as a director for a busy general dermatology practice.
  • Consistent track record of research and peer-reviewed publications in dermatology.
  • Demonstrable experience or specific interest in collaborations for the development of dermatology technology and research in the fields of optics and photonics for both diagnostics and therapeutics, such as:  high-resolution in vivo skin microscopy, Mohs tissue imaging and analytics, photoacoustic imaging, photobiomodulation, photodynamic therapy, and laser treatments.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.

  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.
     

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The selected candidate will be required to submit official transcripts (and, as applicable, U.S. degree equivalency evaluations) documenting the conferral of their qualifying academic credentials.

Questions regarding this search may be directed to:  Brittany Hofmann at Brittany.hofmann@ucf.edu.

This means we are unable to process transfers for individuals currently holding H‑1B status with other employers. UCF will share updates as soon as State guidance changes or additional details become available.

This postdoctoral research position is housed in a laboratory focused on clean energy and carbon neutrality, with an emphasis on high‑impact research in electrochemical energy conversion. The successful candidate will conduct advanced experimental research, contribute to scholarly publications in top-tier journals, and support the development of competitive research proposals for federal funding agencies.

Experimental Research
Design, synthesize, and evaluate advanced electrocatalysts (e.g., NiFeMo systems, spinel oxides) and integrate them into seawater electrolyzers, fuel cells, and battery platforms.

Data Analysis and Publication
Analyze complex electrochemical performance data, conduct comprehensive materials characterization, and prepare high‑quality manuscripts for submission to leading peer‑reviewed journals (e.g., Nature Communications).

Project Management
Support the Principal Investigator in the preparation of research proposals (e.g., NSF DMR) and assist with the management of technical reports for ongoing clean energy research projects.

Mentorship and Training
Provide technical guidance and hands‑on training to graduate and undergraduate students, with particular emphasis on electrochemical reactor operation and laboratory safety protocols.

Laboratory Operations and Maintenance
Ensure the proper operation and maintenance of electrochemical workstations and oversee the procurement of specialized membranes, chemicals, and laboratory supplies.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Orlando, FL
  • Benefits: Health insurance, paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Full-time faculty position in optics and photonics at CREOL, one of the world's leading research institutions in the field. Candidates will establish a research program, teach graduate and undergraduate students, and contribute to service, with research areas including space photonics, quantum photonics, lasers, directed energy, and advanced imaging.

Good fit if you have a Ph.D. in optics or related discipline, strong research publications, and experience or interest in photonics research and education.

Full job description

The Opportunity

CREOL, The College of Optics and Photonics at the University of Central Florida (UCF) invites applications for multiple full-time, 9-month faculty positions at the rank of Assistant Professor (tenure-earning), Associate Professor or Professor (tenured) in the area of optics and photonics. Topics of interest include but are not limited to: Space Photonics, Quantum Photonics, Lasers, Directed Energy, Advanced Imaging and Optical Materials. This search is tied to a major strategic investment by the University of Central Florida in Science, Engineering, and Technology.

Successful candidates will be expected to establish a top-quality, vigorous, highly visible research program, teach and mentor graduate and undergraduate students, and contribute to service in the institution and profession. CREOL is one the world’s foremost institutions for research and education in optics and photonic science and engineering. The college offers Ph.D. and M.S. degrees in optics and photonics, and a B.S. degree in photonic science and engineering. The faculty engage in fundamental and applied research and education in lasers, optical fibers, semiconductor and integrated photonic devices, nonlinear and quantum optics, imaging, sensing and displays. In addition, the College of Engineering and Computer Science and the College of Sciences provide rich opportunities for collaboration. For more information visit www.creol.ucf.edu.

UCF has been consistently ranked highly among Best Global Universities for Optics by various agencies such as U.S. News & World Report. Located in Orlando, Florida, UCF is classified as a Very High Research Activity (R1) university by the Carnegie Foundation. With a diverse student body of more than 70,000 students, UCF is one of the largest universities in the country. The university offers more than 240 degree programs. UCF is committed to diversity and was designated a Hispanic Serving Institution in 2019. For the fifth consecutive year, UCF has been recognized among the nation’s most innovative universities according to U.S. News & World Report while Kiplinger’s and The Princeton Review have ranked UCF as one of the nation’s best values for a college education. For more information, visit https://www.ucf.edu.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Ph.D. from an accredited institution in optics or a closely related discipline at the time of appointment.

  • Applicants must demonstrate strong research experience with a high record of scholarly publications.

To obtain tenure upon hire, the selected candidate(s) must have a demonstrated record of teaching, research, and service commensurate with a tenured faculty appointment at the rank of associate professor or professor.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Demonstrated experience in photonics research and education.

  • A successful record of submitting proposals for research funding.

Additional Application Materials Required:

UCF requires all applications and supporting documents to be submitted electronically through the Human Resources employment opportunities website, https://www.ucf.edu/jobs/. In addition to the online application, interested candidates should upload the following:

  • A curriculum vitae.

  • A letter of interest describing qualifications for the position, such as research agenda and teaching experience/interest.

  • Statement of research and teaching plans

NOTE: Please have all documents ready when applying so they can be simultaneously uploaded. Once the online submission process is finalized, the system does not allow applicants to submit additional documents later.

The Opportunity

The Petelski Lab in the Department of Materials Science & Engineering is seeking applicants for a Postdoctoral Scholar who will help with lab set-up, drive scientific projects, and mentor junior researchers. Ideally, the applicant has experience in mass spectrometry proteomics. As a member of the Petelski Lab, the scholar will be active in pursuing relevant research questions in proteomics while developing expertise for independent work. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Conduct research aimed at profiling proteome changes in cancerous environments, during process of regeneration and/or in response to biomaterials.
  • Prepare and analyze samples using single-cell and bulk proteomics methodologies. 
  • Write and publish high-impact scientific manuscripts. 
  • Build clinical collaborations with hospitals and research institutes. 
  • Supervise and train graduate and undergraduate students. 

Minimum Qualifications:

  • PhD in Biomedical Sciences, Bioengineering, or any related field. 

Preferred Qualifications:

Working knowledge of mass spectrometry proteomics, including instrument set-up, sample preparation, data acquisition, and data analysis. 

  • Experience in preparing human tissues for downstream protein analyses, especially for single-cell.  
  • Biological handling experience in musculoskeletal disease (such as osteoarthritis) or cancer. 
  • Additional experience in materials characterization is of interest. 
  • Familiarity with R or similar computational language. 
  • Strong writing and oral communication skills. 
     
  • Ability to engage in creative troubleshooting.

Additional Application Materials Required:

  • Materials required: updated CV, cover letter, and contact information of 3-4 references. In the cover letter, please describe your hands-on experience, what makes you interested in the Petelski lab, and a summary of at least 1 scientific project you would like to pursue.

The Ph.D. must be conferred before the commencement of employment in the Postdoctoral Scholar position at the University of Central Florida.
