Job.JobTitle: School Psychologist at The Autism Center
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: The Villages, FL
  • Physical: Lifting up to 10 lbs

About this job

School psychologist for a PreK-8th autism center using Applied Behavior Analysis. Provides assessment, intervention, and mental health services to support students' academic, social, and emotional development.

Good fit if you have a specialist's degree or master's in school psychology, a Florida teaching certificate, and prefer experience as a school psychologist.

Full job description

The Villages Charter School Autism Center is dedicated to meeting the educational needs of students on the autism spectrum. The center supports students’ academic, social, and emotional development through a combination of individualized instruction, specialized programs, and targeted therapies provided by our highly trained staff. Through incorporating principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), students will receive the support they need in a nurturing educational environment focused on individualized learning and growth.

The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) is a subsidiary of The Villages Charter School, Inc., which operates by a charter agreement approved by the Sumter County Board of Education and the Florida State Department of Education. Both The Villages Charter School (“VCS”) and The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) are Charter in the Workplace schools (see also School of Choice) founded primarily for the benefit of the children of employees of The Villages of Lake-Sumter, Inc. and those Business Partners who have in the past and continue to participate in the development of The Villages. Unlike traditional county schools, our enrollment criteria is based upon the place of employment of one of the parents/guardians rather than the geographic address of their home.

The Autism Center is located on the Buffalo Ridge campus, serving PreK-8th-grade students, offering a comprehensive support system tailored to each child’s unique needs through a collaborative approach involving passionate educators, therapists, behavioral specialists, and families. 

 DESCRIPTION:

The Villages Charter School Autism Center is accepting applications for a School Psychologist for the 2026-2027 School year. Applicants must have a current Florida Teaching Certificate in the appropriate area and at the appropriate instructional level.

Applicants must complete The Villages Charter School Autism Center online application. In order for the application to be complete, you must also include copies of all transcripts, a copy of the Florida Professional Certificate or “Statement of Eligibility” from the Florida Department of Education, resume and letters of recommendation.

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

The School Psychologist collaborates with staff, families, and community agencies to enhance students' academic achievement, behavioral/social skills, and emotional well-being through direct support, individualized testing, and consultations. They apply expertise in mental health, pedagogy, and behavior to provide assessment, support, and intervention services. Responsibilities include partnering with stakeholders to foster safe, healthy learning environments, improving school-wide policies, and coordinating community services.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The expectations include the following and other duties as assigned:

  • Select, administer, score and interpret individual tests of intelligence, academic achievement, psychological processing, and personality and attitudes of referred students.
  • Analyze evaluation data and formulate hypotheses and conclusions relating to learning and behavioral issues.
  • Develop appropriate interventions and strategies to assist individual students in academic growth and school adjustment.
  • Conduct informal and formal observations of students as part of the evaluation process.
  • Participate in school educational planning and staffing teams to develop assistance plans for at-risk students.
  • Review student records and analyze information pertinent to student learning and school adjustment needs.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and comply with all relevant state regulations and confidentiality standards.
  • Communicate evaluation findings to parents, teachers and others through written reports and oral presentations.
  • Assist in the development of meaningful, objective, and measurable Individualized Education Program (IEP) goals and support personnel in the progress monitoring of these goals.
  • Participate in IEP meetings and contribute psychological expertise.
  • Participate in the periodic re-evaluation of students with disabilities.
  • Actively support school teams in conducting, implementing, and data collection for Functional Behavioral Assessments (FBA) and implementing Behavioral Intervention Plans (BIP). 
  • Provide staff development for school personnel on various topics pertinent to meeting the instructional needs of all students, including, but not limited to, academic assessment and intervention, progress monitoring, behavioral assessment, classroom management, positive behavioral support, data collection, graphing, and data analysis. 
  • Participate in student manifestation of disability meetings.
  • Serve as expert witness in due process hearings related to students with disabilities.
  • Interpret state and federal rules, laws and policies as they relate to identification, placement and service provisions for students with disabilities or gifted ability and maintain current knowledge of same.
  • Provide mental health and counseling services to students in one-to-one and small group settings.
  • Counsel individual students with acute emotional distress as referred by school personnel.
  • Engage in risk/threat assessment screenings
  • Utilize technology as an organization tool to keep track of, but not limited to student consents, testing dates, timelines.
  • Perform other tasks as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Specialist’s or higher degree with a major in school psychology; or
  • Master’s Degree in Psychology or School Psychology with sixty (60) semester hours of graduate credit in school psychology.
  • Certification as School Psychologist or eligible for certification.
  • Successful experience as a school psychologist preferred. 
  • Such additional or alternative qualifications to the above as the Board may find appropriate and acceptable.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to manipulate objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms, and talk and hear. The employee may be required to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Noise level in the work environment is usually quiet.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT:

221 days – Exempt. Salary is based on experience. Benefits shall be paid consistent with the TVCS AC policy.  Length of the work year and hours of employment are those established by the Board.

All prospective employees will be required to be fingerprinted through the Clearinghouse, instructions provided when hired.  If you have questions regarding the Clearinghouse, please see https://info.flclearinghouse.com/. 

 EVALUATION: 

Performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with the provisions of the TVCS AC policy on evaluations of personnel.

Job.JobTitle: Full-Time Aftercare Coordinator at The Autism Center
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: The Villages, FL
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Physical: Lifting up to 10 lbs

About this job

Coordinate and supervise the aftercare program at The Villages Charter School Autism Center for K-5 students after the 3:00 pm school day ends and during break camps. Manage program activities, staff, records, billing, and parent communication while maintaining student safety and confidentiality.

Good fit if you have a high school diploma or GED and experience in program coordination, childcare, or autism support services.

Full job description

The Villages Charter School Autism Center is dedicated to meeting the educational needs of students on the autism spectrum. The center supports students’ academic, social, and emotional development through a combination of individualized instruction, specialized programs, and targeted therapies provided by our highly trained staff. Through incorporating principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), students receive the support they need in a nurturing educational environment focused on individualized learning and growth.

The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) is a subsidiary of The Villages Charter School, Inc. which operates by a charter agreement approved by the Sumter County Board of Education and the Florida State Department of Education. Both The Villages Charter School (“VCS”) and The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) are Charter in the Workplace schools (see also School of Choice) founded primarily for the benefit of the children of employees of The Villages of Lake-Sumter, Inc. and those Business Partners who have in the past and continue to participate in the development of The Villages. Unlike traditional county schools, our enrollment criteria is based upon the place of employment of one of the parents/guardians rather than the geographic address of their home.

The Autism Center is located on the Buffalo Ridge campus serving K-5 elementary students, offering a comprehensive support system tailored to each child’s unique needs through a collaborative approach involving passionate educators, therapists, behavioral specialists, and families. 

 DESCRIPTION:

The Villages Charter School Autism Center is accepting applications for an Aftercare Coordinator. 

 SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

 The management of The Villages Charter School Autism Center After Care Program will provide leadership, guidance, and staff training to ensure a safe and rewarding experience for the students to remain at the Autism Center after the school day has ended at 3:00 pm and during break camps.

 ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The expectations include the following and other duties as assigned:

  • Upholds The Villages Charter School Autism Center core values.
  • Develops, coordinates, executes, and supervises the aftercare, seasonal camps and activities of the Autism Center, providing a challenging and rewarding experience, while maintaining the safety and welfare of the students.
  • Maintains the accuracy of various program records, monies collected, reports and databases including but not limited to student information, attendance, billing, discipline records, behavior logs, transportation requests, data entry, spreadsheets, word documents and record retrieval.
  • Utilizes current telecommunications, as appropriate, to perform job functions and participates in training programs offered to increase telecommunication skill level, job proficiency, current trends and best practices relevant to the area of responsibility.
  • Maintain student confidentiality.
  • Organize seasonal camp planning and assists with transportation for field trips, as necessary.
  • Serve as a liaison between the parents and program staff.
  • Inventory, select and order all supplies and equipment for Aftercare program.
  • Inform administrative personnel about program activities through regular meetings.
  • Collect data and submit accurate reports, when requested.
  • Facilitate regular meetings with program staff to assess progress and to allocate program tasks.
  • Keep professional skills and knowledge updated.
  • Contact parents to review accounts and payments. 
  • Work as a team with other staff.
  • Work with computer applications to create and maintain records on individual student accounts.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.

  QUALIFICATIONS

Applicants must have a high school diploma or general education degree (GED); or one to three months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.  Additional or alternative qualifications to the above as the Board may find appropriate and acceptable.

 ADA AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS:

 Positions in this class require: stooping, crouching, reaching, standing, walking, fingering, grasping, feeling, talking, hearing, seeing and repetitive motions.

 PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to manipulate objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms, and talk and hear. The employee may be required to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds with assistance.  Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Noise level in the work environment is moderate.

 TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT:  

 261 days – Exempt. Length of the work year and hours of employment are those established by the Board.

 All prospective employees will be required to be fingerprinted through the Clearinghouse, instructions provided when hired.  If you have questions regarding the Clearinghouse, please see https://info.flclearinghouse.com/

 EVALUATION: 

 Performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with provisions of TVCS AC policy on evaluations of personnel.

Job.CustomJobTypeName: Social Media Manager, Marketing / Communications / PR
Job.JobDescription:
Within the spirit of “Making People’s Dreams Come True”, this is responsible for helping to drive and reinforce The Villages brand across various social media platforms and capture/create compelling posts, recommend original content, suggest creative ways to attract more prospective residents, grow followers, increase engagement, implement, and maintain social media initiatives, all while supporting the greater marketing goals and objectives of The Villages as a whole. This role collaborates closely with other members of the marketing team to promote The Villages brand and plays a vital role within the department. These duties are accomplished while delivering Raving Fans customer service to both internal and external customers.

Full Time, Onsite Position

Benefits for full-time eligible positions:
Medical (HSA/FSA), Dental, and Vision | 401K and/or ROTH | PTO & Paid Holidays | Basic Life & AD&D | The Villages Charter School eligibility | and much more!

Responsibilities

  • Work with the Social Media Manager(s) and Senior Manager(s) to launch resident engagement campaigns.
  • Suggest new ways to attract additional followers and prospective residents.
  • Provide suggestions to monthly editorial calendar(s).
  • Use Social Media platforms to schedule editorial calendar and posts.
  • Capture and edit authentic content in The Villages community to develop social media posts.
  • Partner with and mentor Social Media Coordinator(s).
  • Work with other members of the Social Media Team on projects to ensure success.
  • Collaborate with the Creative and Photo/Video Teams to develop compelling text, image, and video content in alignment with The Villages voice and brand to inspire, inform and/or entertain.
  • Develop original and creative copies for social media posts.
  • Design posts to sustain viewers’ curiosity and inspire action around new and existing initiatives and programming.
  • Use project management software to create and track social media initiatives.
  • Moderate and facilitate online conversations with customers and respond to queries in a friendly and timely manner.
  • Measure the success of social media campaigns and influence future recommendations based on findings/results.
  • Monitor performance for continuous improvement and/or adjustments to our active social strategies.
  • Understand resident audiences and current social trends.
  • Follow other brands on social media to be aware of industry trends and best practices.
  • Share social media trends and best practices for developing content specifically for social media in a collaborative manner with the Creative and Social Media Teams.
  • Utilize office computer and office equipment (copier, scanner, etc.) along with a host of other software applications, including Microsoft Office Suite, social Media applications (ex: Hootsuite/Sprout Social), Workfront and subsequent project management tools.
  • Drive to various locations for social media assignments and events; using one’s own vehicle or company golf car.
  • Attend special meetings, educational sessions and assist leadership in ongoing training of team members as asked.
  • All other duties as assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities

No supervisory responsibilities in this position.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree (B.A.) in Marketing, Communications or related field and a minimum of two (2) years direct experience in social media on behalf of a brand or a combination of six (6) years education and experience.
  • Strong knowledge of social media content development and copywriting, with great attention to detail required.
  • Ability to utilize iPhone to capture quality photo and video content for social media use.
  • Ability to comfortably work in the field and interact with Residents and Guests to capture social media content.
  • Solid understanding of web and social media analytics to include proficiency in Google Analytics and related social media tools (ex: Hootsuite, SproutSocial, etc.) required.
  • Excellent written and oral communications skills required.
  • Basic math skills required.
  • Time management skills and ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • This position is subjected to The Villages Vehicle Safety Program and its policies as it requires the use of personal vehicles for company business. Please refer to the Vehicle Safety Program for the policies and procedures that this position is required to follow.
  • A Valid Driver’s License with a record acceptable to company standards is required for this position.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: The Villages, FL

About this job

Answer customer service calls, create and manage service tickets in ConnectWise software, and route issues to appropriate departments. Maintain customer accounts in ConnectWise and IBM I systems while ensuring timely ticket closure and customer satisfaction.

Good fit if you have a high school diploma or GED, can use ticketing software, and communicate clearly with customers and internal teams.

Full job description

Within the spirit of "Making People's Dreams Come True", this position provides initial service to TSG's customer base.  Customer Service Assistant will initiate problem resolution by routing concerns, questions, and problems to the appropriate department via the ticketing system dispatch function.  Customer Service Assistant will generate "service ticket" for calls, fix ticket inaccuracies, and will close service tickets upon completion.  Customer Service Assistant will maintain customer and vendor accounts in ConnectWise and provide account maintenance in the IBM I system.  These duties are accomplished while delivering Raving Fans customer service to both internal and external customers.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as a liaison to TVHS IT Rep.
  • Answer customer service line in a friendly, prompt, knowledgeable, and timely manner.
  • Ask a pre-determined set of questions and input client answers into ConnectWise ticketing software.
  • Make basic decisions on call routing, and dispatches to the most appropriate service board or team member for resolution.
  • Bundles tickets upon request.
  • Make follow up calls when clarification is needed or to verify resolution is complete to ensure customer satisfaction.
  • Close completed service tickets within 48 hours of completion, in ConnectWise, while ensuring company and billing information are accurate.
  • Become familiar with TSG accounting procedures, TSG Customer SLA's, and contracts.
  • Grant access to client portal and send welcome letter.
  • In the IBM I system, maintain user accounts, basic printer management, and Special Authorization request such as granting access to specific screens for users.
  • Run regular ConnectWise reports on defined intervals for different groups such as our Charter School team, Sales, and Marketing.
  • Confirm accuracy of tickets on Aging Reports and make changes where necessary based on pre-determined guidelines.
  • Provide training to take calls and use ConnectWise as backups.
  • Provide backup assistance to front desk.
  • Provide assistance to other members of the Program Management Team whenever and wherever possible.
  • Performs other duties as assigned by the Executive Director of Program Management.
  • All other duties as assigned.

Education & Experience Requirements:

  • High School Diploma or General Education Degree (GED); or one (1) to three (3) months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Ability to read/write and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
  • Ability to write routine reports and correspondence.
  • Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, and other employees of the organization.
  • Ability to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals.
  • Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percentage and to draw and interpret bar graphs.

Job.JobTitle: Part-Time Traffic Attendant at Buffalo Ridge
Job.JobDescription:
The Villages Charter School (VCS) opened in August 2000 and is one of the most successful public charter schools in Florida. In fact, VCS has been a "High Performing Charter School", earned a "School of Excellence" and has received 23 straight "A" ratings from the Florida Department of Education! This year, VCS earned the “Cognia School and Systems of Distinction” from the international accreditation group Cognia.

The Villages Charter School spans two campuses. Our Buffalo Ridge campus has three elementary attendance centers and one middle school building. Our newest campus, “Middleton”, opened in August 2023 with a K-8 center and a state-of-the-art high school complex.

VCS currently serves over 4100 students, kindergarten through 12th grades with an overall capacity of 6500 (500 students per grade level) across both campuses.

The Villages Charter School offers a world-class comprehensive K-12 curriculum and state-of-the-art facilities taught by an instructional staff second to none. 

We invite you to look over our school website (www.tvcs.org) to learn more and we welcome you to apply to join our incredible team.

DESCRIPTION:

The Villages Charter School is accepting applications for school Traffic Attendants for our Buffalo Ridge Campus. This is a part time position, assisting with directing school traffic at various positions & intersections located on the Buffalo Ridge Campus. The Traffic Attendants will be responsible for the smooth, transitional, and safe movement of traffic on our campus during carline which occurs at the beginning and end of our school day. 

Applicants must complete The Villages Charter School online application. In order for the application to be complete, you must also include copies of all transcripts and resume.

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

To contribute to the safety of the students by directing traffic at designated intersections to assure the safe flow of motor vehicle travel.

​ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The expectations include the following and other duties as assigned:

  • Supervise the safe movement of motor vehicle traffic on select roadways and/or intersections at assigned posts before and after school hours.
  • Assist motor vehicles in entering and leaving school property or crossing other intersections by safely directing the flow of traffic. Allow school motor vehicle traffic to navigate through our school zone safely while dropping off and picking up students in carline. 
  • Report to supervisor safety violations at assigned intersections.
  • Attend preliminary and refresher training sessions on traffic control hand signals and proper methods for interrupting traffic flow, as assigned by The Villages Charter School safety specialist.
  • Perform any additional related duties required by the charter school or through necessity of situations.
  • Perform other duties that may be assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • High School Diploma or GED.
  • Must be 18 years of age or older.
  • Possess normal visual perception in both eyes.
  • Possess normal hearing range.
  • Be free of infirmities that would prevent standing or walking at least two hours per day.
  • Demonstrate freedom of motion of upper extremities to execute arm and hand traffic signals.
  • Will be required to attend and successfully complete a Florida School Crossing guard certification course as soon as possible after assignment and maintain certification.
  • Additional or alternate qualifications to the above as the Board may find as appropriate and acceptable.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand; use hands to manipulate objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms, and talk and hear. The employee may be required to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and frequently lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds with assistance. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. The noise level in the work environment is moderate to loud.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT:

The length of the work year and hours of employment shall be part-time for 183 days. Hours of work will be split, requiring both early morning and afternoon shifts. 

All prospective employees will be required to be fingerprinted through the Clearinghouse, instructions provided when hired. If you have questions regarding the Clearinghouse, please see https://info.flclearinghouse.com/. 

EVALUATION:

The performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with provisions of TVCS policy on evaluations of personnel.

Applicants must complete The Villages Charter School online application.  In order for the application to be complete, you must also include copies of all transcripts, copy of resume and letters of recommendation.

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

To safely and efficiently transport students to and from their school site and/or special event.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The expectations include the following and other duties as assigned:

  • Comply with all state and local traffic laws and School Board policies and procedures relative to the safe operation of a school bus.
  • Inspect the bus to ensure the bus is in safe operating condition before leaving on a route or trip.
  • Assume responsibility for the safety of his/her passengers including loading and unloading.
  • Instruct students in safety precautions and practices.
  • Maintain appropriate student discipline and report unruly behavior to the School Principal/Principal’s designee.
  • Sweep and keep the bus clean at all times.
  • Prepare FEFP and other required operational reports accurately and submit in a timely manner.
  • Make recommendations to improve school bus routes, stops and loading/unloading zones at school.
  • Use effective, positive interpersonal communication skills.
  • Report to the Service Manager or appropriate administrator, any defects in the bus or repairs needed for safe operation of the bus.
  • Complete required in-service and training programs.
  • When not assigned a bus route to run, will assist the Transportation Supervisor at whatever duties may be assigned.  Reporting time will be established but the Transportation Supervisor when this occurs.
  • Report all accidents and complete all required reports.
  • Transport only authorized students.
  • Keep to assigned route schedule.
  • Perform other transportation duties that may be assigned from time to time from the Supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Must possess a valid CDL Class B License with passenger and air brakes endorsements.

Full Time, On Site Position

About this job

Full-time Benefits Clerk position at The Villages Charter School's Middleton-Central Office. Administers employee benefits programs including Open Enrollment, benefits tracking, compliance monitoring, and 401(k) administration for a school serving over 4,100 students.

Good fit if you have two years of Benefits Administration experience, know FMLA and workers' compensation, and have ADP Workforce Now experience.

Full job description

The Villages Charter School (VCS) opened in August 2000 and is one of the most successful public charter schools in Florida. In fact, VCS has been a "High Performing Charter School", earned a "School of Excellence" and has received 23 straight "A" ratings from the Florida Department of Education! This year, VCS earned the “Cognia School and Systems of Distinction” from the international accreditation group Cognia.

The Villages Charter School spans two campuses.  Our Buffalo Ridge campus has three elementary attendance centers and one middle school building. Our newest campus, “Middleton”, opened in August 2023 with a K-8 center and a state-of-the-art high school complex.

VCS currently serves over 4100 students, kindergarten through 12th grades with an overall capacity of 6500 (500 students per grade level) across both campuses.

The Villages Charter School offers a world-class comprehensive K-12 curriculum and state-of-the-art facilities taught by an instructional staff second to none. 

We invite you to look over our school website (www.tvcs.org) to learn more and we welcome you to apply to join our incredible team.

DESCRIPTION:

Applicants must complete The Villages Charter School online application.  In order for the application to be complete, you must also include a resume.

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

To accurately administer, track, and support employee benefits programs.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The expectations include the following and other duties as assigned:

  • Assist in monitoring organizational compliance with Equity, EEOC/OCR regulations, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA), and the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA).

  • Demonstrate effective, positive interpersonal communication skills.

Job.JobTitle: ESE Elementary Teacher at The Autism Center
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Benefits: Health insurance, 401(k)

About this job

Full-time ESE Elementary Teacher for a charter school autism center serving K-8th grade students. Position uses Applied Behavior Analysis principles and focuses on individualized instruction, academic progress, and social-emotional development in a structured classroom model.

Good fit if you hold Florida certification in ESE and Elementary Education, have experience managing behavior in autism or special needs settings, and can work with a classroom team.

Full job description

The Villages Charter School Autism Center is dedicated to meeting the educational needs of students on the autism spectrum. The center supports students’ academic, social, and emotional development through a combination of individualized instruction, specialized programs, and targeted therapies provided by our highly trained staff. Through incorporating principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), students will receive the support they need in a nurturing educational environment focused on individualized learning and growth.

The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) is a subsidiary of The Villages Charter School, Inc. which operates by a charter agreement approved by the Sumter County Board of Education and the Florida State Department of Education. Both The Villages Charter School (“VCS”) and The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) are Charter in the Workplace schools (see also School of Choice). Unlike traditional county schools, our enrollment criteria are based upon the place of employment of one of the parents/guardians rather than the geographic address of their home. It was founded and is provided funding by The Villages of Lake-Sumter, Inc. as a business partnership charter school primarily for the benefit of the children of employees of The Villages of Lake-Sumter, Inc. and those Business Partners who have in the past and continue to participate in the development of The Villages.The Autism Center is located on the Buffalo Ridge campus, serving K-8th-grade students, offering a comprehensive support system tailored to each child’s unique needs through a collaborative approach involving special educators, therapists, behavioral specialists, and families.

DESCRIPTION:

We are seeking a full-time Exceptional Student Education (ESE) Elementary Teacher for the remainder of the 2026-2027 school year. In order for the application to be complete, you must also include copies of all transcripts, a copy of the Florida Professional Certificate or “Statement of Eligibility” from the Florida Department of Education, a copy of your resume, and letters of recommendation.

Anticipated start date for this position is January 4, 2026.

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

Under the supervision of the Principal, the ESE Elementary Teacher will assist with designing and implementing The Villages Charter School Autism Center’s adopted curriculum and students’ IEP goals within the TVCS AC structured classroom model and be able to model these activities for other staff in the classroom to ensure fidelity and compliance.

The expectations include the following and other duties as assigned:

● Promote the intellectual, emotional, physical, and psychological growth of our learners

● Uphold and model TVCS Autism Center Core Values

● Serve as teacher and point person in a classroom of 6-12 students

● Meet with and instruct assigned classes in the locations at the times designated.

● Provide a safe, nurturing environment that stimulates academic, moral, and social growth.

● Work with a classroom team with the support and oversight of one - two support staff, if applicable.

● Assist students in learning to accept responsibility, demonstrate respect for people and property, and demonstrate self-discipline.

● Implement a variety of instructional techniques to meet the varying learning styles of students.

● Plan and effectively implement instructional activities designed to achieve the goals and objectives of the curriculum.

● Take all necessary and reasonable precautions to protect students, equipment, materials, and facilities.

● Evaluate student progress on a regular basis, including academic and social growth of the students.

● Maintain accurate, complete, and correct records and inventories as required by law, district policy, and administrative regulations.

● Assist in the enforcement of school rules, administrative regulations, and Board policy.

● Ensure that classroom support staff are implementing instructional strategies and lessons as set forth by the principal, if applicable

● Weekly lesson planning for instruction of state standards with other classroom teachers and support staff

● Provide daily feedback to support staff, if applicable

● Collect and report data with high fidelity and analyze data bi-weekly to make instructional decisions

● Communicate clearly and effectively in both written and oral form with students, parents, and others, following TVCS AC guidelines

● Adapt materials to meet student needs and IEP requirements

● Maintain substitute plans in case of absence

● Participate in all duties and responsibilities as appropriate for a TVCS AC faculty member

● Contribute to IEPs as appropriate

● Other duties as assigned by the administration

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

● Must hold or be eligible for certification by the State of Florida in Exceptional Student Education (ESE)

● Must hold or be eligible for certification by the State of Florida in Elementary Education (K-6)

● Ability to train, coach, and motivate support staff.

● Mastery and enthusiasm for best practices in autism education

● Track record of success in behavior management with students with autism or other special needs

● Ability to approach situations with optimism and perseverance

● Ability to communicate with parents, co-workers, and professional contacts in a courteous and professional manner, and following TVCS AC guidelines

● Ability to work independently and coordinate multiple tasks simultaneously

● Ability to exercise reasonable judgment and maintain confidentiality

● Experience in structured teaching, center-based model preferred

● Such additional or alternative qualifications to the above as the Board may find appropriate and acceptable

PREFERRED:

● Florida Department of Education Reading Endorsement

● Florida Department of Education ESOL Endorsement

● At least 3 years of experience in classroom teaching

● At least 3 years of experience working with students with moderate to severe disabilities

● Experience and training in Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)

● Florida Department of Education Autism Endorsement

BENEFITS:

● School located in a new state-of-the-art Autism Center

● Competitive pay based on experience

● Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance

● PDO (Paid Day Off) time provided

● 401K

● Great professional development and advancement opportunities.

SUPERVISORY REQUIREMENTS:

● Set up lessons and instructional activities for classroom teaching staff. Coaches, monitors, and mentors classroom support staff working with students with disabilities.

ADA AND OTHER REQUIREMENTS:

Positions in this class require: stooping, crouching, reaching, standing, walking, fingering, grasping, feeling, talking, hearing, seeing, and repetitive motions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to manipulate objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms, and talk and hear. The employee may be required to lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds, and occasionally lift and/or move up to 100 pounds with assistance. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. Noise level in the work environment is moderate.

TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT:

98 days – Exempt. Length of the work year and hours of employment are those established by the Board.

All prospective employees will be required to be fingerprinted through the Clearinghouse, instructions provided when hired.  If you have questions regarding the Clearinghouse, please see https://info.flclearinghouse.com/. 

EVALUATION:

Performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with the provisions of TVCS AC policy on evaluations of personnel.

About this job

Senior Cyber Security Engineer responsible for security operations, threat monitoring, vulnerability assessments, and incident response. Full-time, on-site position in The Villages, Florida requiring 24x7 availability for incident response and SOC tool management.

Good fit if you have an Associate degree plus five years related experience, hold required Microsoft and security certifications, and can demonstrate expertise in SIEM, IDS/IPS, firewalls, and network analysis.

Full job description

Within the spirit of “Making People’s Dreams Come True”, this position is responsible for focusing on all aspects of security, regulations, and compliance related to our business and our clients. These duties are accomplished while delivering Raving Fans customer service to both internal and external customers.

Full Time, On Site Position

Benefits for full-time eligible positions:
Medical (HSA/FSA), Dental, and Vision | 401K and/or ROTH | PTO & Paid Holidays | Basic Life & AD&D | The Villages Charter School eligibility| and much more!

Responsibilities:

Cyber Security Operations

  • Proactively monitor and respond to threat indicators or incidents with Security Operations Center (SOC) software and tools including but not limited to:  Anti-virus, Vulnerability management, Intrusion Detection and Prevention System (IDS, IPS), Security Incident and Event Monitoring (SIEM), Data loss prevention (DLP), Intrusion Detection/Prevention Systems (IDS/IPS) and Threat intelligence systems
  • Perform threat and vulnerability assessments (Physical and Virtual) to ensure that systems are protected from known and potential threats (datacenter, cloud, network, server/desktop, BYOD, IOT, etc.).
  • Research detected threats and evaluated additional IOCs via malware analysis, sandboxing, VirusTotal, etc. to further investigation and mitigation.
  • Create Documentation of new and existing system designs for compliance with security standards and best practices.
  • Research, recommend, evaluate, document, and implement cyber security solutions that identifies and/or protects against potential threats and responds to security incidents.
  • Stay informed about current and emerging threats to general technology and to specific threats to The Villages or its customers through research and testing.
  • Develop and document methods of proactively detecting/mitigating threats using threat intelligence, honeypots/traps, IDS, etc.
  • Continually evaluate, test, and recommend new tools and security products to protect systems in the ever-changing threat landscape.
  • Review, recommend, document, and implement Active Directory Group Policy Security Best Practices.
  • Work closely with the Network division to monitor and investigate security related issues originating from Network division tools or reviews.
  • Work closely with Security and Compliance Administrator to achieve cohesive forensic analysis and incident reporting.

Incident Response

  • Provide 24x7 access for incident response, including log review, data collection, SOC tool research, and forensic capture of system information.
  • Work with law enforcement, as required, to meet submission or reporting requirements.
  • Communicate with legal representatives of customers when required.
  • Provide post incident security reports detailing available information concerning attack, possible avenues of compromise, remediation actions, and any recommendations for preventing future attacks of a similar nature.
  • Provide Tier II support to our Server Operations Engineers and Field Engineers
  • Require use of our current ticketing system to keep track of work items, SLA, priorities, documentation of work performed and follow-up to our customers.
  • Communicate with appropriate people using the most effective medium whenever there is an issue or possible outage of service. This includes notification when an issue or outage has been resolved.
  • Advise Director of Cyber Security of any issues that affect our delivery of services to our customers promptly.
  • All other duties as assigned.

Education & Experience Requirements:

  • Associate degree (A.A.) or equivalent; and/or five (5) years of related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • At least one of the following Microsoft Certifications or current equivalents required: MTA, MCSE, MCSA or MCITP.
  • At least one of the following or equivalent required: CompTIA Security+, GIAC Security Essentials, CEH, CISSP, CISM.
  • Ability to demonstrate and apply understanding of the following: web content filters/proxies, email security capabilities, IDS, IPS, SIEM, DNS security practices, advanced log analysis, network monitoring, network flow analysis, packet capture analysis, network proxies, firewalls, anti-virus capabilities, Linux/UNIX command line, and access control lists.

Through incorporating principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), students will receive the support they need in a nurturing educational environment focused on individualized learning and growth.

DESCRIPTION:

The Villages Charter School Autism Center is seeking multiple ESE Paraprofessional candidates to support the ESE teacher in creating an enriching learning environment for our students with Autism Spectrum Disorder.

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

The ESE paraprofessional is responsible for assisting the teacher(s) and/or other school personnel by performing assigned tasks in the classroom and during wrap-around services. The goal is to provide a quality educational program for students within a specialized school setting.

The expectations include the following and other duties as assigned

  • Uphold and model TVCS Autism Center Core Values
  • Assist the special education teacher in implementing IEPs and plans tailored to meet the individual needs of students with autism and monitor their progress.
  • Assisting in the educational and social development of students under the direction and guidance of classroom teachers.
  • Providing support for individual students inside and outside the classroom to enable them to fully participate in activities.
  • Providing support and supervision within the classroom and during wrap-around services to our students. 
  • Working in a team environment that includes other professionals such as behavioral therapists, teachers, and resource staff.
  • Assisting classroom teachers with maintaining student records and data collection.
  • Supporting students with emotional or behavioral concerns and assisting them in developing appropriate social skills.
  • Assisting students with self-care including toileting, dressing, and hygiene.
  • Assist the classroom teacher(s) in supervising classroom learning activities and preparation of instructional materials and equipment.
  • Use effective, positive interpersonal skills
  • Maintain a clean and orderly environment for students.
  • Maintain confidentiality regarding student information.
  • Assist in maintaining positive relationships between the school and the parents.
  • Assist teacher in correcting student classwork and homework.
  • Reading to students in small groups.
  • Supervising students when the teacher must leave the room for a short period of time.
  • Ability to administer basic first aid using universal precautions.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

  • Minimum of 60 college hours (equivalent to an Associate Degree) or pass the ParaPro test.
  • Experience working with children with autism in an educational or therapeutic setting.
  • Knowledge of behavior management techniques and intervention strategies.
  • Ability to work collaboratively as a part of a team and adapt to changing situations.
  • Patience, empathy, and a genuine passion for working with autistic children.
  • The ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information appropriately.
  • Familiarity with Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA) is a plus, but not a requirement. 
  • Such additional or alternative qualifications to the above as the Board may find appropriate and acceptable.

197 days – Non-Exempt. Length of the work year and hours of employment are those established by the Board. Additional days may be available for work during Fall, Winter, Spring, and Summer camps. 

All prospective employees will be required to be fingerprinted through the Clearinghouse, instructions provided when hired.  If you have questions regarding the Clearinghouse, please see https://info.flclearinghouse.com/. 

EVALUATION: 

Performance of this job will be evaluated in accordance with provisions of TVCS AC policy on evaluations of personnel.

Quick facts

  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: The Villages, FL
  • Benefits: 401(k), paid time off, paid holidays

About this job

Create photo and video content for multiple digital channels at The Villages, working with marketing and leadership teams. Role includes recording, editing, photography, voice-overs, and supervising two or more full-time employees.

Good fit if you have a bachelor's degree in a related field or four years of experience, proficiency in Final Cut Pro X and Adobe Creative Cloud, and a valid driver's license.

Full job description

Within the spirit of “Making People’s Dreams Come True”, this position is responsible for creating distinct and engaging photo and video content that is used across multiple digital channels. With the master-level photo-video production and editing skills, this role works closely with the Marketing Department and executive leadership team to produce eye-catching ‘on-brand’ content. Daily duties include but are not limited to recording and editing video projects, shooting photography, assisting with cataloging photo/video assets, maintaining editing tools and hardware, collaborating and coaching teammates on photo/video project scope, vision, and technique, uploading content, conducting voice-overs, creating concept boards and/or articulating proposed edits in addition to various related photo/video duties, tasks, and material. Video material may include the manipulation of camera footage, dialogue, sound effects, graphics, transitions, music, and special effects. Photography material may include photo rendering, photo shop, color and light correction and other photo enhancing techniques. These duties are accomplished while delivering Raving Fans customer service to both internal and external customers.

Full Time, Onsite Position

Benefits for full-time eligible positions:
Medical (HSA/FSA), Dental, and Vision Insurance | 401k and/or ROTH | PTO & Paid Holidays | Basic Life & AD&D | The Villages® Charter School eligibility | and much more!

Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with the Marketing team and executive leadership team to establish the desired look and feel for all video content and creation.
  • Manage technical aspects of video recording and editing.
  • Establish a clear understanding of the storyline and purpose of a video's creation from marketing leadership; bringing to life concept boards and/or articulate proposed edits based on that understanding.
  • Coordinate with the Photo/Video team regarding digital productions, schedule coordination and talent.
  • Determine filming locations and lead all logistics for travel and logging equipment.
  • Record and edit video and sound projects, including but not limited to selecting program format for final output, capturing/importing media, editing footage, and audio files, creating/inserting static and motion graphics, and media/file management.
  • Improve video and sound quality using various video software, tools, and techniques.
  • Edit video to include preselected music, interviews, sound clips and other important aspects of the project and video completion.
  • Assist with voice-over recordings when requested.
  • Gather and transfer all forms of media into editing software and ensure all materials are uploaded and formatted correctly.
  • Operate computer editing systems and equipment used for video media and effects, troubleshooting when necessary.
  • Ensure the correct formatting and presentation for finalized videos match team specifications and vision.
  • Use expertise and skill to capture professional, high-quality images; assignments may include candid photos, portraits, architectural structures, abstract compositions, etc.
  • Select and use appropriate photographic and video equipment to record events and subjects.
  • Enhance the appearance of subjects with natural or artificial light.
  • Use photo editing software and applications to edit, crop, and enhance photographs.
  • Produce images that accompany written content, coordinating with marketing team members to ensure photographs present a unified message matching the publication's purpose, tone, and audience.
  • Ensure all photo/video equipment is charged, in proper working order and logged.
  • Assist with cataloging inventory and video assets in addition to maintaining editing tools and hardware.
  • Review artistic content and provide feedback.
  • Adhere to the company's brand guidelines, ensuring alignment with The Villages’ brand and voice.
  • Drive company vehicle(s) and safely transport shoot materials to and from events and various destinations; at times using own transportation when necessary.
  • Utilize office computer and office equipment (copier, scanner, etc.) along with a host of other software applications, including Microsoft Office Suite, MAC applications and subsequent editing management tools (ex: Final Cut Pro X, Adobe Premier and other Creative Cloud applications, After Effects, etc.).
  • Attend special meetings, educational sessions and assist leadership in ongoing training of team members as asked.
  • Assist the Marketing Team in their overall initiatives as requested.
  • All other duties as assigned.

Supervisory Responsibilities:
Customarily and regularly directs the work of two or more full-time employees or the equivalent and has the authority to make decisions regarding the hiring, firing, and promotion of these reports.

Education & Experience Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s Degree (B.A.) in a related field; or four (4) years of related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Must be proficient in Final Cut Pro X, Adobe Premier and other Creative Cloud Applications, After Effects and/or similar editing software, tools, and platforms.
  • Strong interpersonal skills, enthusiasm for The Villages and all it has to offer, robust photo and video production experience with the ability to problem solve using ‘out of the box’ creative thinking to handle a variety of variables required.
  • Must be able to communicate confidently and effectively with customers, guests and team members, always.
  • Must have strong leadership skills to instruct and direct subjects, coach teammates, and interact with all levels of leadership.
  • This position is subjected to The Villages Vehicle Safety Program and its policies as it requires the use of personal vehicles for company business. 
  • A Valid Driver’s License with a record acceptable to company standards is required for this position.

Job.JobTitle: Part-Time Buffalo Adventure Guide at The Autism Center
Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Schedule: Part-time
  • Location: The Villages, FL
  • Education: High school diploma or GED
  • Physical: Lifting up to 25 lbs

About this job

Part-time after-school program guide for PreK-7th grade students at The Villages Charter School Autism Center. Provides supervision, activities, and support using positive interpersonal skills and behavioral guidelines in a structured environment.

Good fit if you have a high school diploma or GED, can work flexible hours during school days, and are comfortable supervising small groups of students.

Full job description

The Villages Charter School Autism Center is dedicated to meeting the educational needs of students on the autism spectrum. The center supports students’ academic, social, and emotional development through a combination of individualized instruction, specialized programs, and targeted therapies provided by our highly trained staff. Through incorporating principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), students will receive the support they need in a nurturing educational environment focused on individualized learning and growth.

The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) is a subsidiary of The Villages Charter School, Inc. which operates by a charter agreement approved by the Sumter County Board of Education and the Florida State Department of Education. Both The Villages Charter School (“VCS”) and The Villages Charter School Autism Center, LLC (TVCS AC) are Charter in the Workplace schools (see also School of Choice). Unlike traditional county schools, our enrollment criteria are based upon the place of employment of one of the parents/guardians rather than the geographic address of their home. It was founded and is provided funding by The Villages of Lake-Sumter, Inc. as a business partnership charter school primarily for the benefit of the children of employees of The Villages of Lake-Sumter, Inc. and those Business Partners who have in the past and continue to participate in the development of The Villages.

The Autism Center is located on the Buffalo Ridge campus serving K-7 students, offering a comprehensive support system tailored to each child’s unique needs through a collaborative approach involving special educators, therapists, behavioral specialists, and families.

DESCRIPTION:

The Villages Charter School is accepting applications for a Buffalo Adventure Guide.  Buffalo Adventures is the after-school program for students at The Villages Charter School Autism Center grades PreK through 7th. 

SCOPE OF RESPONSIBILITIES:

To provide support for a safe, nurturing, fun and rewarding experience for PreK-7th ESE students in accordance with the mission and goals of The Villages Charter School.

 ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

The list of essential functions as outlined herein, is intended to be representative of the tasks performed within this position and not necessarily descriptive of any one position.  The omission of an essential function does not preclude management from assigning duties not listed herein if such functions are a logical assignment to the position.

  • Use effective, positive interpersonal skills.
  • Provide direct, active supervision in a 1:5 ratio, as directed.
  • Prepare and distribute daily snacks for participating students.
  • Assist in the storage, disbursement and inventory of materials and supplies.
  • Lead student activities using the set guidelines while maintaining the safety and welfare of students in White Buffalo Adventures.
  • Safely transition students on the Autism Center campus between activities
  • Follow behavioral guidelines as set forth by The Autism Center’s BCBA, including de-escalation tactics as training through the use of CPI (Crisis Prevention)
  • Communicating with admin to ensure students meet after care guidelines
  • Work flexible hours necessary for the efficient operation of the program.
  • Utilize current telecommunications, as appropriate, to perform job functions and participate in training programs offered to increase telecommunication skill level, job proficiency, current trends and best practices relevant to the area of responsibility.
  • Communicate effectively through handheld devices.
  • Maintain a clean and orderly environment for students in all areas of use during White Buffalo Adventures.
  • Maintain confidentiality regarding student information.
  • Ability to recognize emergency situations i.e. injury and follow school protocol as described in the training guide.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned by the White Buffalo Adventures Coordinator
  • Exhibit The Villages Charter School core values.


QUALIFICATIONS

Applicant must have a high school diploma or general education degree (GED); or one to three months related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.  Additional or alternative qualifications to the above as the Board may find appropriate and acceptable.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

The physical requirements described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of the job. Tasks require the ability to exert somewhat strenuous effort in work involving moderate physical activity involving some combination of standing; walking; reaching with hands and arms; kneeling; crawling; climbing; balancing; bending; crouching or twisting.  While performing the duties of this job, the employee must occasionally lift and/or carry, push and/or pull up to 25 pounds.  Manual dexterity is required.  Noise level can be moderate to loud at times.

SENSORY REQUIREMENTS:

While performing the duties of this job, tasks require oral communication ability; the ability to perceive and discriminate sounds; visual perception and discrimination; and the ability to distinguish color.

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

While performing the duties of this job, tasks are regularly performed with exposure to adverse environmental conditions, such as outdoor weather conditions and noise.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally exposed to moving mechanical parts and risk of electrical shock while working with or near office equipment.

LANGUAGE SKILLS:

Ability to read and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence and memos.   Ability to write simple correspondence.   Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to students, colleagues, and other employees of the organization.

 TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT:  

Part-time 183 days while school is in session.  There will be other opportunities during school breaks to provide care for students.  Length of the work year and hours of employment are those established by the Board.

All prospective employees will be required to be fingerprinted through the Clearinghouse, instructions provided when hired.  If you have questions regarding the Clearinghouse, please see https://info.flclearinghouse.com/

Position Summary

Our Deloitte Finance Transformation team practices to help chief financial officers, controllers, and finance teams define and execute their finance and global business services agendas and strategies. You will work with leading-class teams and solutions, helping clients navigate challenging environments, market uncertainty, technology development, and regulatory considerations to unlock value. Your work may span strategy, operations, process design, and technology as we partner with clients to transform finance.

Recruiting for this role ends on 12/3/2026.

Work You’ll Do

As a Project - Manager, Controllership on the Specialized Finance Solutions team, you will be responsible for:

  • Support accounting operations for the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI), including property, plant, and equipment (PP&E); leases; accounts payable; accounts receivable; reimbursable agreements; and Intragovernmental Payment and Collection (IPAC) transactions.
  • Prepare and support monthly financial reporting deliverables.
  • Support charge card management and compliance activities.
  • Reconcile accounting data and maintain documentation that supports reporting and operational processes.
  • Coordinate assigned tasks, monitor deadlines, and communicate status, issues, and deliverables with engagement and client stakeholders.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
 

The Team

Deloitte’s Government & Public Services (GPS) practice – our people, ideas, technology and outcomes – is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Our Controllership and Treasury Transformation offering modernizes the finance function to support the evolving business objectives of the organization. We work with the CFO, CAO, controller, and treasurer to develop an efficient, high quality, data-driven, tech-enabled controllership and treasury function that empowers our clients to drive more value to their business partners and to their investors.

The Project Delivery Talent Model is designed for professionals with specialized skills that align to a current client need. Team members focus on delivering services to clients, without additional expectations related to business development or promotion. Their employment is tied to their role on a project, and they are eligible for a benefits package that is competitive for project delivery-focused professionals.

 

Qualifications

Required: 

  • Bachelor’s degree 
  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future 
  • Must be able to obtain and maintain the required clearance for this role
  • 3+ years of experience supporting accounting operations involving property, plant, and equipment; leases; accounts payable; accounts receivable; reimbursable agreements; or Intragovernmental Payment and Collection (IPAC) transactions.
  • 3+ years of experience preparing monthly financial reports.
  • 3+ years of experience supporting charge card management and compliance activities.
  • You must reside within a commutable distance of your assigned office with the ability to commute daily, if required, without the need for overnight accommodations.
  • Ability to travel 0-25%, on average, based on the work you do and the clients and industries/sectors you serve.

Preferred:

  • Experience working in SAP (Systems, Applications, and Products in Data Processing).

Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

Deloitte Global is the engine of the Deloitte network. Our professionals reach across disciplines and borders to develop and lead global initiatives. We deliver strategic programs and services that unite our organization.

Work you'll do

This position represents a unique opportunity for a professional to support the continued development of the Deloitte Global Boardroom Program through eminence-building and knowledge-sharing activities.

The candidate will take an active role positioning Deloitte Global and its member firms as leaders in the governance arena and in building and deepening relationships with the most influential non-executive board members of our largest clients around the world.

Want to make an impact that matters? Consider Deloitte Global.

  • Work closely with the Global Boardroom Program Leadership to implement the annual priorities and supporting governance structures.
  • Prepare fluent and executive-ready presentations and speeches, communications, and reporting metrics for Global Leadership, senior executives, and client audiences.
  • Plan agendas, create materials, and manage technical hosting of periodic Boardroom community meetings.
  • Support the development, delivery, and activation of key deliverables and offerings, including but not limited to webinars, events, eminence, and newsletters.
  • Develop internal and external messaging in collaboration with the Global Program leaders, appropriate national and global office groups, and subject matter experts, related to the Program's key role-based programs, including the Chair Program, Audit Committee Program, and others, as appropriate.
  • Review, synthesize, and summarize external reports and studies on corporate governance topics for educating specific audiences, such as Deloitte partners, principals, and directors. 
  • Contribute to Program eminence activities to include supporting research and analysis, creating toolkits materials for Global Growth stakeholders, and creating and executing activation plans.
  • Assist in project management tasks to build project plans and calendars, and track and communicate progress towards completion with Global Program leadership.
  • Help the Global Program leaders coordinate the work of offshore team members.
  • Establish and maintain contacts with third parties, and help ensure that a consistent boardroom and governance message is delivered to all constituencies, applying strong interpersonal, writing, and organizational skills.


The team

Global Growth creates an opportunity for you to build a new perspective and see both Deloitte and our priority clients through a global lens. While collaborating with some of our most experienced leaders and talent across the organization, your voice will influence Deloitte’s strategic direction, growth, brand, and impact in the market. Your network will rapidly expand, and you will create meaningful connections and relationships globally. You will build deep institutional knowledge and gain an understanding of clients’ heart-of-business issues, and Deloitte’s offerings and solutions. Global Growth’s diverse, inclusive, and flexible culture is an opportunity for you to become a role model for agile working.



Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in commerce, marketing, accounting, finance, international relations, communications, area studies, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 3 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 2 years within professional services.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, and deadlines simultaneously. Agile experience is an asset.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience developing executive-level communications and deliverables.
  • Confident and professional communicator with the ability to engage effectively with senior internal and external stakeholders across cultures and geographies.
  • Strong understanding of Deloitte’s functional capabilities, service offerings, tools, and methodologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to navigate complex organizational structures, ambiguity, and competing priorities with a consultative mindset.
  • Strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to balance detailed execution with broader strategic objectives.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, with experience producing high-quality, executive-ready deliverables.
  • Ability to remain productive and responsive in a fast-paced environment and deliver high-quality work under tight deadlines.
  • Experience supporting Member Firm leadership and senior stakeholders.
  • Experience working with boards, committees, or similar governance structures is an asset.
  • Strong interest in international affairs and global business, with curiosity and awareness of different cultures and perspectives.

Job.JobDescription:
Position Summary

The Prime Contracts team is responsible for the reviewing and processing of all fully executed net new awards, option periods, and contract modifications as well as coordination for at risk items for the Deloitte GPS Practice. This position requires a strong working knowledge of Federal Acquisition Regulations, and commercial contracting principles. Supports the execution of all facets of the contract life cycle. Performs contract administration duties for federal contracts and ensures the accuracy of the contracts and financial systems. Exercises increased independence and judgment in reviewing and analyzing moderately complex contracts actions. Maintains a keen awareness of requirements and status associated with assigned contracts. Effectively, manages personal portfolio and advises account teams on contracts administration matters. Compiles and analyzes contract related data; and maintains historical information and documentation.

Work you'll do

As a Specialist Manager, Government Client Contracts Management on the Prime Contracts team, you will be responsible for...

  • Proactively provides support to the development, review, and negotiation of contracts, modifications, prime contractor NDA and teaming agreements and subcontracts consistent with company policies.
  • Ensure contract data is entered into appropriate forms and databases. Checks existence, accuracy, and completeness of electronic documents and contract systems related data.
  • Reviews Federal solicitations, requests for information, quotes, proposals, and identifies business risks, documents the findings, and provides recommendations.
  • Has a keen understanding and knowledge of key terms and conditions of assigned contracts that would affect performance or compliance with the ability to convey salient information to the appropriate stakeholders.
  • Prepares standard contract language (e.g., technical/price assumptions, certifications & representations, proposal questions, organizational conflict of interest certificates, etc.) for inclusion into proposals.

  • Develop relationships with external client stakeholders and attend industry and government events.
  • Collaborate and coordinate across GPS teams to provide comprehensive solutions and insights to internal and external clients related to contracts portfolio.
  • Reviews for compliance with federal contract regulations and various reporting requirements.
  • Performs other job-related duties as assigned.

  • Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for employer sponsorship, now or at any time in the future.

Preferred:

  • Experience supporting contracts within the Federal environment

  • Experience using Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint

Position Summary

Our Deloitte AI & Engineering team works to transform technology platforms, drive innovation, and help make a significant impact on our clients’ success. You’ll work alongside talented professionals reimagining and reengineering operations and processes that are critical to businesses. Your contributions can help clients improve financial performance, accelerate new digital ventures, and fuel growth through innovation.

Work you'll do

As a Data Engineer III on the AI & Data team, you will be responsible for…

  • Design enterprise cloud data architectures that support transformation initiatives using modern cloud architecture principles.
  • Develop data pipelines, data models, and advanced analytics products using Databricks and/or Snowflake.
  • Apply DevOps practices and data and statistical programming tools to build, deploy, and improve cloud-based data solutions.
  • Conduct business-process assessments and prepare strategic deliverables, including strategic plans and visioning-session materials.
  • Facilitate client sessions and collaborate with executive-level stakeholders to translate business needs into technical delivery priorities.
  • Support State and Local Government client relationships and high-priority business-development activities.

A successful candidate would possess these skills:

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate as part of a team
  • Effective written and verbal communication skills
  • Meticulous attention to detail and quality of work product
  • Ability to build and sustain professional relationships
  • Ability to lead projects or workstreams
  • Ability to manage and prioritize multiple tasks in a fast-paced and dynamic environment
  • Strong interpersonal skills and professional demeanor
  • Ability to meet deadlines
  • Ability to provide clear guidance to others

The team

Deloitte’s Government & Public Services (GPS) practice – our people, ideas, technology and outcomes – is designed for impact. Serving federal, state, & local government clients as well as public higher education institutions, our team of professionals brings fresh perspective to help clients anticipate disruption, reimagine the possible, and fulfill their mission promise.

Lead complex resilience initiatives as a Senior Manager, Technical Resilience, helping clients prepare for, respond to, and recover from disruption. In this role, you will drive the design and delivery of resilience strategies across business, technology, and operational environments while guiding teams and advising senior stakeholders on continuity, recovery, and risk priorities. • Advise senior client stakeholders on recovery strategies, continuity plans, playbooks, and governance for critical business and technology functions

• Lead executive and stakeholder working sessions, exercises, and testing activities to evaluate readiness and strengthen response capabilities

The work is collaborative, fast-paced, and focused on delivering practical outcomes across industries.

• Experience designing, implementing, or managing on-premise and cloud solutions across at least one major public cloud provider

• Experience designing and implementing large-scale solutions or leading infrastructure/datacenter migrations
