POSITION OBJECTIVE:   The Diversion Specialist will be responsible for managing a caseload of families served via Family Support Services (FSS) cases. Services to be provided In Home to children and families who are safe but could benefit from services provided via providers in their communities to inhibit them from moving further into the system of care. Diversion Specialist are to oversee the delivery and care coordination of services, make referrals, provide community linkages This position will conduct child safety assessments, complete family assessments and 30- day home visits minimally (or more frequent visits as identified as needed depending on the dynamic of the family) for families served in Orange County. The Diversion Specialist will coordinate and facilitate Family Team Conferences in a flexible, responsive, culturally competent service delivery system. This position will provide family stabilization support to children and families and coordinate with all members of the Family Team including caregivers, providers, DCF and informal and natural supports.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

·       Provide specialized assistance to Child Welfare teams and the children and families in care.

·       Coordinate planning strategies and maintain positive relationships with agencies and         community members as applicable.

·       Conduct home visits.

·       Assist in the assessment of client’s behaviors and emotional needs to determine the best possible community services to be implemented with/ for youth/ family.

·       Act as a liaison with DCF/case management and the community

·       Conduct home visits at a minimum every 30 days or weekly visits as needed or identified, depending on the family’s need and dynamic that is presented at the Diversion staffing.

·       Attending staffing’s (lockout staffing’s, MDT, LRT other community meetings as needed or identified).

·       Maintain positive relationships with other agencies and community members as applicable.

·       Complete any necessary file documentation and process data through FSFN and other required data systems.

·       Prepare documentation to identify prevention efforts.

·       Attends and participates in monthly diversion meetings.

·       Coordinates and attend Diversion MDT staffing.

·       Diverts families from the dependency system.

·       Act as a support for the CPI regarding providing/ offering a service that will keep children in their homes/ communities safely and not have to enter out of home care or foster care, as well as service delivery with providers and community resources.

·       Maintains monthly diversion logs and diversion tracking mechanisms for diversion/prevention purposes.

·       Enters information into FSFN and ensures family support pages are created and maintained regarding reason for diversion/prevention involvement and funding etc. Ensure that family support pages are closed in a timely manner as well.

·       Staff cases for diversion/prevention involvement and or to implement a safety service as needed.

·       Expected to be a part of the CPI initial consultations and 2nd  tier staffing’s. Also available to be included in impromptu staffing regarding present and impending danger plans. Be a critical part in the decision of what services are available and can be implemented to ensure a child/ children is able to be kept in their home safely.

·       Attach themselves to a CPI case that has been identified as needing prevention services and assist CPI with gathering information from parents/ other providers that the family may have been involved with or is currently with to move case forward and keeping the children safe without “ongoing” case management.

·       Act as the conduit between providers and families. They are the linkage of services and ensure that contact between the provider and family has occurred and they are engaged. Also obtain all monthly documentation from providers and scan into the FSFN file cabinet and or update notes in FSFN timely and continuously.

·       Ensure that parents sign the FSS Acknowledgement forms upon initial contact.

·       Completes funding authorization form/ Diversion Supervisor signs the funding authorization and Diversion Manager approves and signs off for final approval.

·       Screens all referrals to community providers and programs in the community.

·       Maintain and complete ongoing Diversion tracking logs (weekly and as needed)

·       Participates in the agency strategic plan & quality improvement processes.

·       Ability to safely & successfully perform essential job functions consistent with the ADA, FMLA, & other federal, state, & local standards, including meeting qualitative & quantitative productivity standards.

·       Ability to maintain reasonably regular, punctual attendance consistent with ADA, FMLA & other federal, state, & local standards

·       Ability to comply with all personnel policies & procedures

We understand the importance that every provider, parent and employee plays in the success of our mission to protect and inspire every child, every day.  An essential function of all employees is to provide excellent customer service by being professional and respectful in all interactions each and every day.  It is also expected that all employees are timely and responsive in their communication with others.

NON-ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:

·         Duties in other counties as assigned.

 

This list of functions is not intended to be exhaustive.  The agency reserves the right to revise this job description as needed to comply with actual job requirements.

 

QUALIFICATIONS:

REQUIRED:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social work or related area of study

o   Related degrees include:  human services, criminology, juvenile justice, psychology, sociology, counseling, special education, education, human development, child development, family development, marriage and family therapy, and nursing

  • 2 years’ experience in child welfare services.
  • State of Florida Child Welfare Certification (CWCM)

PREFERRED:

  • Master’s Degree from an accredited college or university.

SKILLS:

 

REQUIRED:

·         Must be proficient in Microsoft Office Suite

·         Conducts self in a professional manner with colleagues, peers, and clients. Demonstrates professional behavior toward clients consistent to the enhancement of the client’s dignity and well-being. Upholds established policies and professional standards of conduct.

·         Effective leadership and planning skills

·         Excellent interpersonal and communication skills

·         Must be capable of completing assignments with minimum guidance and supervision.

·         Ability to objectively coach & mentor staff through complex & difficult issues

·         Demonstrated ability to identify, prioritize, and execute tasks to meet deadlines.

·         Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions

·         Ability to analyze, integrate and report data

·         Ability to maintain a high level of confidentiality

·         Ability to represent and promote positive and solution-oriented behaviors within their team and the organization.

·         Demonstrate cultural and linguistic competence & sensitivity to population served

·      Ability to travel

 

SPECIAL CONDITIONS:

 

·         Thorough Background Screening upon hire including FBI, FDLE, Local Law check, Employment Reference check, DMV check, Criminal Records check, Social Security Trace & Drug Screening.  FDLE check will be run at least every 5 years.

·         Travel- local: 10% per week, long-distance: 1% per month

·         Attend at least 15 hours of in-service training annually

Analyzing (N), Bending-neck (P), Bending-waist (P), Calculations (P),

Carrying/Lifting (P), Climbing (P), Crawling/Crouching (P), Finger Movements (N), Handling Objects (N), Kneeling (P), Pushing/Pulling (P), Reaching (P), Reading & Comprehending (N), Reasoning (N), Sitting (P), Squatting (P), Standing (P), Twisting-neck (P), Twisting-waist (P), Walking (P), Writing (N)

About this job

Care Coordinator for youth and young adults in or previously in foster care. Coordinates Family Team Conferences and wraparound services to support permanency and individualized service delivery.

Good fit if you have 2+ years child welfare experience, valid driver's license, and social work or human services background.

Full job description

Salary: $49,700/year

Position Summary: The Care Coordinator is responsible for facilitating the Wraparound process for youth and young adults in or previously in foster care that are eligible to receive services and support through the youth services department. The Care Coordinator coordinates and schedules Family Team Conferences to promote permanency and prioritizes urgent requests. The Care Coordinator maintains information regarding the environment of current services to ensure a flexible, responsive, culturally competent service delivery system. This position is a 2-year Federal grant funded position.

Technical/Functional Expectations:

1.   Family Team Conferences - Essential Function: Coordinate and facilitate Family Team Conferences in order to achieve consensus among family and other participants in developing an appropriate plan based on the needs of the families and to ensure compliance with FPOCF procedures, values, and standards.

2.   Service and Treatment Delivery - Essential Function: Ensure services and treatment are delivered from a

strength based framework and customized in order to meet individualized needs of consumers and are

culturally competent.

3.   Utilization Management--Essential Function: Authorization and monitoring of resources, including agency

and community, to meet client’s needs.

4.   Relationship Maintenance--Essential Function:  Foster and maintain ongoing relationships with family

members, care managers, providers, and identified resources in order to call on others to implement

client plans.

5.  Adhere to SOC Values and Principles-Essential Function:  This is required in order to embrace and promulgate the values and principles of the System of Care on a consistent basis with each family and

interaction.

6.  Planning/Scheduling/Meeting multiple deadlines: Plan and schedule meetings, conferences, and travel schedules in order to maintain staff schedules.

7.   Other duties as required: Job performance requires fulfilling other incidental or related duties as assigned,

assisting and training others, and performing duties of higher rated positions from time to time for

developmental purposes.

Behavioral Competencies:

1.   Innovation: Able to generate new or different products, processes, or solutions; create unique solutions to problems; express fresh insights or innovations regularly; think outside of existing paradigms.

2.   Facilitation: Able to use judgment and provide a process to ease group resolution of issues; clarify

points of view and terminology to gain group acceptance; facilitate the actions, decisions, or opinions of

others in a positive direction.

3.   Develop Relationships: Able to relate with others while building credibility and rapport; give personal

support and reassurance; put others at ease; build cooperative relationships.

4.   Customer Service: Able to anticipate and respond to consumer's needs, concerns, or questions in order to

meet or exceed their expectations; help evaluate needs and options; show care and concern to

demonstrate consumer importance and value.

5.   Influence:  Able to positively change opinions and actions of others in a desired direction; present

information in a persuasive manner; clarify information in order to gain understanding and buy-in.

6.   Problem Solving: Able to exercise judgment in building realistic solutions to problems; understand the real

issues behind problems; use common sense and take practical action to solve problems.

7.   Sensitivity: Work effectively with and show sensitivity to cultural differences and various socio-economic

backgrounds of others.

8.   Ethics: Adhere to and model principles and values of Agency and System of Care by being strength-based, solution-focused, maintains highest level of integrity and ethical standards and work collaboratively with

employees, partners, stakeholders and clients in all interactions.

Business Experience:

1.   Minimum of 2 years knowledge of child welfare systems: This is required in order to understand and successfully function within our system of care and to adhere to Florida statute and code.

2.   Strong computer/data entry skills: This experience is required in order to maintain our utilization

management system.

3.   3+ years’ Experience working with families and children: This experience is essential in order to

effectively work with children and families within our system of care.

4.   Collaboration, negotiation and problem-solving skills: This experience is essential in order to effectively

facilitate the Wraparound Family Team conferencing process.

5.   Valid Driver's License & Appropriate Insurance - Essential: This position requires a valid driver’s license in

order to travel throughout the County and requires $100,000/$300,000 bodily injury insurance coverage

(per FL Statute) in order to transport clients.

Educational and Experience Requirements:

1.       A high school diploma or GED equivalent (official transcripts required) AND four or more years of full-time social work or human services experience.

  1. An associate degree from an accredited college or 60+ college credits from an accredited college AND two years of full-time social work or human services experience or two years of professional work experience.  Examples of work experience could be, but are not limited to:
    • Guardian Ad Litem or similar child advocate role
    • Family Support Worker
    • Group Home Staff
    • Teacher’s assistant/aide
    • Childcare provider/staff
    • Therapeutic Assistant
    • Behavioral health technician
    • Family intervention specialist
    • Home health aide
    • Nurse (LPN or RN) or similar profession
    • Nursing facility assistance
    • Emergency Medical Services (EMS
    • Other professional jobs that require an assessment of factors that can contribute to trauma or protective capacities with children and families.
  2. Bachelor’s Degree, Human Services or Social Work preferred. (Related degrees are Criminology, Psychology, Sociology, Counselling, Special Education, Education, Human Development, Child Development, Family Development, Marriage and Family Therapy although other degrees may apply.)
  3. 1 to 2 years related experience required.
  4. 2 to 5 years Wraparound and related experience required.
  5. You must obtain a Child Welfare Case Manager Certification within 12 months of completion of paid pre-service training.

Position Summary:

This position will be based at the Rockledge care center. The Family Allies Family Support Worker position serves as a paraprofessional support to Dependency Care Managers, with primary focus on coordinating and supervising Family Time with families involved with the Dependency Child Welfare System of Care. Family Support Workers will be responsible for maintaining records, program referrals, accompanying/transporting children and parents to therapeutic services, other providers, and supervising Family Time. The Family Support Worker will develop and maintain client records and program documentation based on first hand observations and assessments.

Technical/Functional Expectations:

  1. Complete required training - Essential Function – Comply with training requirements, to include completion of required in-service training hours, to include Wrap-Around Training.
  2. Safety - Essential Function – Facilitate and provide Supervision for families during Family Time activities.  Must act decisively, when necessary, to protect clients and model appropriate boundaries for parents and children during supervised Family Time.
  3. Permanency - Essential Function– Adhere to and monitor Family Time Guidelines to successfully achieve permanency for children placed in out-of-home care.
  4. Reports - Essential Function –Prepare   all   required   documentation   and   submit   within   the   required   timeframes;   make recommendations; testify at court hearings regarding observations and interactions during supervised Family Time, reunification, permanent guardianship, termination of parental rights, or other case management activities.
  5. Documentation - Essential Function – Ensure documentation occurs within the SACWIS system and other related systems within required timeframes. Complete professional, timely program case documentation and reporting, including the tracking and monitoring of client progress and outcomes.
  6. Engagement - Essential Function – Adhere to the local System of Care values, goals and priorities for Brevard’s children, youth and families; Utilize a family centered strength based approach to care; Monitor quality of care by ensuring appropriate visitation plans are in place to correlate to the needs of the family.
  7. Support - Essential Function - Provide support to staff, children, caregivers and family members to ensure timely achievement of permanency; Coordinate cases with team members, providers, DCF and attorneys as needed.
  8. Court Appearance and Preparation - Essential Function- At times this position may require a court appearance.  Case information must be reviewed prior to every hearing in order to be prepared to answer any questions from the Court regarding the status of the case, services, and progress towards permanency; Dress appropriately for Court appearances and ensure all court hearings are attended timely.
  9. Other duties as required: Job performance requires fulfilling other incidental or related duties as assigned, assisting and training others, and performing duties of higher rated positions from time to time for developmental purposes.

Behavioral Competencies:

  1. Trust and Respect: Able to demonstrate and treat others in an honest and straightforward manner; keep dealings with others confidential; keep word and follow through on commitments.
  2. Sensitivity: Work effectively with and show sensitivity to cultural differences and various socio-economic backgrounds of others.
  3. Ethics: Adhere to and model principles and values of Agency and System of Care by being strength- based and solution-focused; maintains highest level of integrity and ethical standards and work; ability to handle confidential information appropriately.
  4. Partnership: Work collaboratively with employees, partners, stakeholders and clients in all interactions.
  5. Communication: Able to confidently present information to children, parents, partners, court, etc. and speak to individuals and co-workers in an effective and persuasive manner.
  6. Flexibility - Able to perform job duties at a high level of autonomy or with minimal supervision; able to set appropriate limits and boundaries with children and families; able to travel and make home visits; able to work flexible hours including afternoons, evenings and weekends and on call as required.

Business Experience:

  1. Valid Driver's License - Essential: A valid driver's license is required in order to transports clients around the community; attend trainings and other activities throughout the County and State.
  2. Strong written and verbal communication skills: Strong communication skills are essential in order to clearly and concisely coach parents if needed during Family Time sessions. Strong written skills are required as observations of client contacts will be documented in SACWIS system and emails and other requests require a professional and courteous response.
  3. Collaborative, solution-focused approach: A collaborative, solution-focused approach is essential in order to foster and develop relationships with clients, peers, and providers in the community; and to build consensus among parties with conflicting positions and opinions.
  4. Computer literacy: Intermediate skill in Microsoft Suites and SACWIS system are required.

Educational and Experience Requirements:

  1. High school diploma or equivalent required.
  2. Associates degree or higher level of educational attainment preferred
  3. At least 2 years’ experience in child welfare or human services.
  4. Strong knowledge about dependency case management, supervised family time and child welfare system of care.

Position Summary: The Licensing Specialist serves as the primary point of contact for prospective foster parents and is responsible for the timely and thorough completion of foster home studies in accordance with Florida Administrative Code. This role evaluates applications and provides recommendations for the approval or denial of licenses. The specialist also assesses incident reports and licensing concerns related to potential foster homes, offering recommendations for appropriate resolution. Under the guidance of the Licensing Supervisor, the Licensing Specialist is responsible for collecting, organizing, monitoring, and distributing documentation to ensure licensing standards are met. This position supports the successful progression through the various levels of initial or re-licensure for foster care applicants, ensuring compliance with all regulatory requirements.

Technical/Functional Expectations

1.       Complete Licensing Home Studies-Essential Function: The position completes initial and/or re-licensure home studies inclusive of the assessment and evaluation of all household members and babysitters, to include background screening and abuse report history.

2.       Background Checks – Essential Function: Review and evaluate criminal history reports, fingerprint results, child abuse and neglect registry checks, sex offender registry searches, and other required clearances. Ensures continuous compliance with Title IV-E requirements by monitoring and tracking background check renewals, preventing lapses in required screenings and clearances for foster parents and household members.

3.       Home Visits to Family Foster Homes-Essential Function: This position will provide regular and ongoing home visits to family foster homes throughout the licensure process.

4.       Conduct Ongoing Assessments-Essential Function: This position will conduct ongoing assessments to determine capacity as indicated based on family skills, training, household composition, physical space and other determining factors.

5.       Liaison between Foster Parents and Case Managers – Essential Function: This position will serve as a Liaison between foster parents and case managers ensuring open communication and timely resolution of any identified concerns when applicable.

6.       Foster Care Referrals-Essential Function: This position will comply with Administrative Code requirements for any foster care referral on a licensed foster home. The licensing specialist will make recommendations for resolution of

all incident reports, foster care referrals and licensing concerns related to existing foster homes. This includes any joint visits for DCF institutional reports on assigned foster homes.

7.       Confidentiality – Essential Function: Maintain strict confidentiality and security of sensitive personal information in compliance with applicable privacy laws and regulations.

8.       Licensing Packets – Essential Function: Ensure licensing packets for caregivers meet code requirements, licensing expiration and DCF submission requirements.

9.       Foster Care Regulations – Essential Function: Stay current on changes to foster care licensing regulations, background screening requirements, and agency procedures.

10.    Knowledge of Microsoft Office Applications – Essential Function: Utilize Microsoft Office applications and agency databases to manage workflow, analyze information, and produce reports.

11.    Attention to Detail and Judgement – Essential Function: Demonstrate strong attention to detail, critical thinking, and sound judgment when reviewing eligibility-related information. Effectively prioritize workload and manage multiple cases while meeting established deadlines.

12. On Call Rotation – Essential Function: Participate in first tier on call rotation.

13. Other duties as required: Job performance requires fulfilling other incidental or related duties as assigned, assisting, and training others, and performing duties of higher rated positions from time to time for developmental purposes.

 

Behavioral Competencies:

1.           Attention to Detail: Able to be thorough and complete when working with assembling, processing, or providing detailed information; track details when under pressure.

2.           Customer Service: Able to anticipate and respond to customer's needs, concerns, or questions to meet or exceed their expectations; help evaluate needs and options; show care and concern to demonstrate customer importance and value.

3.           Integrity: Able to demonstrate consistency of words and actions; protect confidential information; do what is right even when no one is watching; demonstrate sound business ethics; consistently comply with organizational values.

4.           Verbal Communication: Able to clearly express ideas, information, or concerns; presents verbal information in a straightforward manner; ask questions to open channels of communication; listen to understand perspective of others.

5.           Self-Control: Able to maintain a composed problem-solving approach when faced with unrealistic expectations, pressing time demands, frustration, or interpersonal conflict.

6.           Trust and Respect: Able to demonstrate respect and treat others in an honest and straightforward manner; follows through on commitments.

7.           Sensitivity: Work effectively with and show sensitivity to cultural differences and various socio-economic backgrounds of others.

 

Business Experience:

1.       Valid Driver License - Essential: This is required to travel throughout the County and other locations for client and other meetings.

2.       Effective verbal and written communication skills: This is required to develop effective and collaborative communications with children and families, the community and service providers.

3.       Advanced computer and data entry skills: This is required to maintain spreadsheets and data in Level 1 licensing.

4.       Collaboration, negotiation, and problem-solving skills: This skill and experience is required to ensure successful integration into our system of care.

Educational and Experience Requirements:

1.           An associate degree from an accredited college or 60+ college credits from an accredited college AND two years of full-time social work or human services experience or two years of professional work experience. OR a high school diploma or GED equivalent (official transcripts required) AND four or more years of full-time social work or human services experience.

2.           BA/BS - Bachelor’s Degree or equivalent preferred.

3.           2+ years licensing experience preferred.

4.           Florida Child Welfare Certification required (training provided)

Physical Requirements:

1.           Lifting 20 pounds

2.           Carrying 20 pounds

3.           Sitting

4.           Standing

5.           Stooping / Crouching

6.           Bending

7.           Reading

8.           Speaking

9.           Listening

10.        Typing

11.        Writing

12.        Noise Condition

About this job

Care Coordinator facilitates Wraparound services for families in the child welfare system, coordinating Family Team Conferences and managing service delivery. This is a 4-year federally grant-funded position in Rockledge.

Good fit if you have 2+ years child welfare experience, valid driver's license with required insurance, and an associate degree or 60+ college credits plus 2 years social work experience.

Full job description

Salary: $49,700/year

Position Summary: The Care Coordinator is responsible for facilitating the Wraparound process for families served in the child welfare system in a timely and responsive manner. The Care Coordinator coordinates and schedules Family Team Conferences to promote permanency and prioritizes urgent request. The Care Coordinator maintains information regarding the environment of current services to ensure a flexible, responsive, culturally competent service delivery system. This position is a 4-year Federal grant funded position.

Technical/Functional Expectations:

1.   Family Team Conferences - Essential Function: Coordinate and facilitate Family Team Conferences in order to achieve consensus among family and other participants in developing an appropriate plan based on the needs of the families and to ensure compliance with FPOCF procedures, values, and standards.

2.   Service and Treatment Delivery - Essential Function: Ensure services and treatment are delivered from a

strength based framework and customized in order to meet individualized needs of consumers and are

culturally competent.

3.   Utilization Management--Essential Function: Authorization and monitoring of resources, including agency

and community, to meet client’s needs.

4.   Relationship Maintenance--Essential Function:  Foster and maintain ongoing relationships with family

members, care managers, providers, and identified resources in order to call on others to implement

client plans.

5.  Adhere to SOC Values and Principles-Essential Function:  This is required in order to embrace and promulgate the values and principles of the System of Care on a consistent basis with each family and

interaction.

6.   Planning/Scheduling/Meeting multiple deadlines: Plan and schedule meetings, conferences, and travel schedules in order to maintain staff schedules.

7.   Other duties as required: Job performance requires fulfilling other incidental or related duties as assigned,

assisting and training others, and performing duties of higher rated positions from time to time for

developmental purposes.

Behavioral Competencies:

1.   Innovation: Able to generate new or different products, processes, or solutions; create unique solutions to problems; express fresh insights or innovations regularly; think outside of existing paradigms.

2.   Facilitation: Able to use judgment and provide a process to ease group resolution of issues; clarify

points of view and terminology to gain group acceptance; facilitate the actions, decisions, or opinions of

others in a positive direction.

3.   Develop Relationships: Able to relate with others while building credibility and rapport; give personal

support and reassurance; put others at ease; build cooperative relationships.

4.   Customer Service: Able to anticipate and respond to consumer's needs, concerns, or questions in order to

meet or exceed their expectations; help evaluate needs and options; show care and concern to

demonstrate consumer importance and value.

5.   Influence:  Able to positively change opinions and actions of others in a desired direction; present

information in a persuasive manner; clarify information in order to gain understanding and buy-in.

6.   Problem Solving: Able to exercise judgment in building realistic solutions to problems; understand the real

issues behind problems; use common sense and take practical action to solve problems.

7.   Sensitivity: Work effectively with and show sensitivity to cultural differences and various socio-economic

backgrounds of others.

8.   Ethics: Adhere to and model principles and values of Agency and System of Care by being strength-based, solution-focused, maintains highest level of integrity and ethical standards and work collaboratively with

employees, partners, stakeholders and clients in all interactions.


Business Experience:

1.   Minimum of 2 years knowledge of child welfare systems: This is required in order to understand and successfully function within our system of care and to adhere to Florida statute and code.

2.   Strong computer/data entry skills:  This experience is required in order to maintain our utilization

management system.

3.   3+ years’ Experience working with families and children:  This experience is essential in order to

effectively work with children and families within our system of care.

4.   Collaboration, negotiation and problem-solving skills: This experience is essential in order to effectively

facilitate the Wraparound Family Team conferencing process.

5.   Valid Driver's License & Appropriate Insurance - Essential: This position requires a valid driver’s license in

order to travel throughout the County and requires $100,000/$300,000 bodily injury insurance coverage

(per FL Statute) in order to transport clients.

Educational and Experience Requirements:

1.          An associate degree from an accredited college or 60+ college credits from an accredited college AND two years of full-time social work or human services experience or two years of professional work experience.  Examples of work experience could be, but are not limited to:

a.       Guardian Ad Litem or similar child advocate role

b.       Family Support Worker

c.        Group Home Staff

d.       Teacher’s assistant/aide

e.       Childcare provider/staff

f.         Therapeutic Assistant

g.       Behavioral health technician

h.       Family intervention specialist

i.         Home health aide

j.         Nurse (LPN or RN) or similar profession

k.        Nursing facility assistance

l.         Emergency Medical Services (EMS

m.     Other professional jobs that require an assessment of factors that can contribute to trauma or protective capacities with children and families.

n.       A high school diploma or GED equivalent (official transcripts required) AND four or more years of full time social work or human services experience.

2.           Bachelor’s degree, preferably in a social work or related area of study from an accredited college or university. (Related degrees are Criminology, Psychology, Sociology, Counselling, Special Education, Education, Human Development, Child Development, Family Development, Marriage and Family Therapy although other degrees can apply)

3.           Two years’ experience working with at risk children and families preferred.

4.           2 to 5 years Wraparound and related experience required.

Job.JobDescription:
Quick facts

  • Pay: $48,200 a year
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Location: Rockledge, FL

  • License: Valid driver's license
  • Physical: Lifting up to 20 lbs

About this job

Care Manager Trainee for Family Partnerships of Central Florida in Rockledge. The role involves child and family assessments, safety planning, permanency coordination, and court involvement, with training provided to achieve certification.

Good fit if you have a valid driver's license and personal vehicle, strong communication skills, and experience working collaboratively with families and professionals.

Full job description

Starting Salary: $48,200/yr ($23.17/hr), Increase to $49,700/year ($23.89/hour) once full certification is achieved.

Position Summary: The Family Allies Care Manager adheres to the FPOCF System of Care principles of practice and provides family cantered strength-based assessment, planning, linkage, coordination, and advocacy for children and families. The Care Manager works as a team member with key partners including parents, family members, foster parents, caregivers, guardian ad litem, DCF Protective Investigators, CLS attorneys, therapists, providers, and other appropriate professionals. The Care Manager will train and become proficient in identifying and assessing child and family needs with the ultimate goal of achieving permanency.

Must successfully complete Child Protection Certification training and examination, then a considerable period of monitored field practice under close supervision and the associated field case assessment process.

Technical/Functional Expectations:

  1. Complete required certification - essential function: Attend Child Protection Certification training (pre-service) and successfully attain a passing score on the required examination.
  2. Safety - essential function: Conduct family function and child safety assessments; develop, monitor, and manage required safety plans.
  3. Permanency - essential function: Identify and develop plan to successfully achieve permanency for children placed in out -of-home care.
  4. Service Delivery - essential function: Assess child and family needs; develop service plans; coordinate the delivery of services; ensure all referrals and linkages to children/parents/caregivers are completed.
  5. Reports -essential function: Prepare all required court reports and submit within the required timeframes; make recommendations; testify at court hearings regarding reunification, permanent guardianship, termination of parental rights, or other case management activities; ensure court orders are completed within required timeframes.
  6. Documentation –essential function: Develop and maintain case and program documentation according to contract; ensure documentation occurs within the SACWIS system and other related systems within required timeframes.
  7. Engagement -essential function: Adherence to the local SOC values, goals and priorities for Brevard’s children, youth and families; Utilize a family centered strength based approach to care; Monitor quality of care by conducting face-to-face home visits with children minimally every 30 days, or with increased frequency as determined by case situations and supervisory direction; facilitate, monitor, and assess visitation between children, parents, and siblings to ensure safety and observe interactions.
  8. Support - essential function: Provide support to children, caregivers and family members to assure stable placement and timely achievement of permanency; Coordinate cases with supervisor, team members, providers, DCF and attorneys as needed.
  9. Court Appearance and Preparation - essential function: Review case information prior to every hearing in order to be prepared to answer any questions from the Court regarding the status of the case, services, and progress towards permanency; Dress appropriately for Court appearances and ensure all court hearings are attended timely.
  10. Initiatives - essential function: Embraces and participates in initiatives and programs designed to enhance the System of Care. 
  11. On Call - essential function: This position is required to participate in the on-call function on nights and weekends once provisional certification has been achieved.
  12. Other duties as required: Job performance requires fulfilling other incidental or related duties as assigned, assisting and training others, and performing duties of higher rated positions from time to time for developmental purposes.

Behavioral Competencies:

  1. Trust and Respect: Able to demonstrate and treat others in an honest and straightforward manner; keep dealings with others confidential; keep word and follow through on commitments.
  2. Prioritizing: Able to quickly focus on what is important; establish a sequence of tasks and completion dates; set priorities and allocate time and resources when faced with competing demands.
  3. Sensitivity: Work effectively with and show sensitivity to cultural differences and various socio- economic backgrounds of others.
  4. Ethics: Adhere to and model principles and values of Agency and System of Care by being strength- based and solution-focused; maintains highest level of integrity and ethical standards and work; ability to handle confidential information appropriately.
  5. Partnership: collaboratively with employees, partners, stakeholders and clients in all interactions.
  6. Communication: Able to confidently present information to children, parents, partners, court, etc. and speak to individuals and co-workers in an effective and persuasive manner.
  7. Flexibility - Able to perform job duties at a high level of autonomy or with minimal supervision; able to set appropriate limits and boundaries with children and families; able to travel and make home visits; able to work flexible hours as required.

Business Experience: 

  1. Valid Driver's License - Essential: A valid driver's license is required in order to attend meetings and other activities throughout the County and State.
  2. Possess an operational private vehicle for the use of daily work activities.  Proof of registration and insurance coverage is required.
  3. Strong written and verbal communication skills: Strong communication skills are essential in order to clearly and concisely articulate programs, proposals, write policies and respond to program inquiries in a professional manner.
  4. Collaborative, solution-focused approach: A collaborative, solution-focused approach is essential in order to foster and develop relationships and to build consensus among parties with conflicting positions and opinions.
  5. Computer literacy: Intermediate skill in Word, Excel, SACWIS system are required

Educational and Experience Requirements:

  1. A high school diploma or GED equivalent (official transcripts required) AND four or more years of full time social work or human services experience.
  2. An associate degree from an accredited college or 60+ college credits from an accredited college AND two years of full-time social work or human services experience or two years of professional work experience.  Examples of work experience could be, but are not limited to:
    • Guardian Ad Litem or similar child advocate role
    • Family Support Worker
    • Group Home Staff
    • Teacher’s assistant/aide
    • Childcare provider/staff
    • Therapeutic Assistant
    • Behavioral health technician
    • Family intervention specialist
    • Home health aide
    • Nurse (LPN or RN) or similar profession
    • Nursing facility assistance
    • Emergency Medical Services (EMS
    • Other professional jobs that require an assessment of factors that can contribute to trauma or protective capacities with children and families.
  3. Bachelor’s degree, preferably in a social work or related area of study from an accredited college or university. (Related degrees are Criminology, Psychology, Sociology, Counselling, Special Education, Education, Human Development, Child Development, Family Development, Marriage and Family Therapy although other degrees may apply.
  4. Two years’ experience working with at risk children and families preferred.
  5. You must obtain a Child Welfare Case Manager Certification within 12 months of completion of paid pre-service training.

Physical Requirements: 

  1. Lifting 20 pounds
  2. Carrying 20 pounds
  3. Reaching
  4. Sitting
  5. Standing
  6. Bending
  7. Near Acuity
  8. Reading
  9. Speaking
  10. Listening
  11. Typing
  12. Writing

About this job

Install, maintain, and repair electrical systems at water and wastewater treatment facilities. Chinchor Electric is a 40-year family-owned commercial and industrial contractor with paid training in apprenticeships and certifications, medical benefits with employer-paid options, and a 20% night shift differential.

Good fit if you have 3+ years electrical experience, preferably in water or wastewater treatment, and can work nights and out of town occasionally.

Full job description

Chinchor Electric, Inc. is family owned and operated and has been in business for 40 years. We are celebrating being one of the Nation’s Top Workplaces after receiving the honor of being granted the Orlando Sentinel's Top Workplace award in both 2024 and 2025! We are a Commercial and Industrial Electrical contractor, performing Heavy Industrial Electrical, Highway Lighting, Traffic Signalization projects, and much more. We work with both corporate clients and government entities and maintain yearly contracts with Orange, Seminole, Osceola, and Volusia counties, as well as the Florida Department of Transportation. We are proud to share that we have opened a second location in St. Augustine, Florida to serve Jacksonville and the surrounding areas and are expanding to open a third location in Summerfield to serve Ocala and the surrounding areas. We have opportunities for advancement in both career and education.
 
Chinchor Electric, Inc. is seeking highly motivated and hardworking experienced Industrial Electrician. Join our team, apply today!
 
Educational Opportunities and Benefits:
  • Medical (100% Employer-Paid Plan Options)
  • Dental
  • Vision
  • Life Insurance
  • 401K + Match
  • Christmas Bonus
  • Paid Time Off
  • 20% Night Shift Differential
  • Employee Referral Program
  • Advancement Opportunities
  • Paid apprenticeship and training opportunities through the 4-year Florida Electrical Apprenticeship & Training (FEAT) and Northeast Florida Builders Association (NEFBA) apprenticeship programs.
  • Paid certifications including:
    • CDL-A
    • Crane Certification (rigging, signaling, operating)
    • IMSA
    • Maintenance of Traffic
    • Traffic Signal Technician Levels I, II, and III
 
Job Type: Full Time, Hourly, Non-Exempt
Pay: $25+ Hourly, Based on Experience
Travel & night work may be required. MUST be able to work out of town and nights, on occasion.
 
Industrial Electrician Responsibilities:
  • Install, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair electrical systems associated with water and wastewater treatment facilities, including pumps, motors, MCCs, control panels, instrumentation, SCADA systems, underground conduit, and duct bank systems.
  • Install and terminate conduit, wiring, feeders, and electrical equipment for treatment processes, lift stations, and facility infrastructure.
  • Diagnose electrical and control system issues using testing equipment and hand tools to safely restore system operation.
  • Inspect electrical systems and equipment for hazards, defects, and code compliance.
  • Perform testing of electrical systems, controls, instrumentation, and power distribution equipment to ensure safe and reliable operation.
  • Coordinate with supervisors, operators, engineers, and other trades to support plant operations and project activities.
  • Follow all company safety procedures, lockout/tagout requirements, and site-specific safety standards.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.
Requirements – Water & Wastewater Treatment Electrician:
  • Minimum of 3 years of electrical experience preferred, with experience in water or wastewater treatment facilities strongly preferred.
  • Working knowledge of electrical systems including motors, pumps, MCCs, VFDs, control panels, instrumentation, and SCADA systems.
  • Experience installing and maintaining conduit systems, underground conduit, duct banks, feeders, and power distribution equipment.
  • Ability to read and interpret blueprints, one-line diagrams, control schematics, and electrical specifications.
  • Proficient in troubleshooting electrical and control systems using standard testing equipment and hand tools.
  • Knowledge of NEC requirements, electrical safety standards, and lockout/tagout procedures.
  • Ability to work safely in active industrial, water treatment, and wastewater treatment environments.
  • Capable of lifting materials, working outdoors in varying weather conditions, climbing ladders, and working in confined spaces when required.
  • Strong communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.
  • Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation required.
  • Class A CDL *Preferred*.
 
Physical Demands
Must be able to perform multiple tasks and can handle the physical demands of the job, including but not limited to, digging using a shovel, standing, walking, kneeling, bending, crouching, pulling, pushing, climbing, and lifting at least 50lbs.

Drug Free Workplace
To help ensure a safe, healthy, and productive work environment for our employees and others, to protect Chinchor Electric, Inc. property, and to ensure efficient operations, Chinchor Electric, Inc. has adopted a policy of maintaining a workplace free of drugs and alcohol. This policy applies to all employees and other individuals who perform work for Chinchor Electric, Inc.

Your Opportunity

The Sales Learning & Coaching team is responsible for empowering our Schwab Retail professionals to build trusted relationships and deliver modern wealth management to our clients through world-class learning and coaching experiences. Our goal is to enable increased engagement and retention of clients, enhance confidence in the professionals we support, and improve overall sales professional performance.

This role will report to the Director of Sales Learning and Coaching Strategy and will play a critical part in shaping how strategy is enabled through technology, insights, platforms, and AI. The role will help translate business priorities into scalable solutions that improve leader decision-making, modernize learning and coaching experiences, deepen client relationships, and drive meaningful outcomes across Schwab Retail.

What You Will Do

  • Shape strategy and executive narratives: Translate business priorities, insights, and tradeoffs into clear strategies, roadmaps, and executive communications that drive alignment and action.
  • Advance technology-enabled solutions: Use data, platforms, automation, and AI to simplify work, personalize experiences, improve adoption, and scale learning and coaching impact.
  • Lead complex initiatives: Structure and manage cross-functional workstreams, priorities, timelines, risks, stakeholder feedback, adoption plans, and performance measures.
  • Turn ambiguity into action: Apply structured problem solving, data, leader feedback, and business context to assess impacts, clarify tradeoffs, and recommend practical next steps.
  • Build partnerships and adapt quickly: Influence across business, technology, risk, and analytics teams while navigating changing priorities and balancing speed, governance, adoption, and scalability.

What Success Looks Like

  • Learning and coaching strategies are supported by clear technology roadmaps, scalable tools, and practical execution plans.
  • Leaders have easier access to insights, dashboards, and platform experiences that help them prioritize, coach, and make decisions with confidence.
  • Technology, data, and AI are used to simplify manual work, personalize learning and coaching moments, and improve adoption across the field.
  • Cross-functional teams are aligned on priorities, success measures, risks, and tradeoffs before solutions are launched.
  • The work creates measurable business impact through stronger leader routines, improved sales professional readiness, deeper client relationships, and better performance outcomes.

 

Technology Fluency

  • Microsoft 365 suite, including PowerPoint, Excel, Word, Outlook, Teams, SharePoint, and Loop.
  • Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Power BI.
  • SQL and Tableau for data analysis, reporting, dashboarding, and insight generation.
  • GitHub and Visual Studio Code for solution documentation, technical collaboration, version control awareness, and partnership with technology teams.
  • Microsoft Copilot and AI-enabled productivity tools to support research, content creation, automation, process improvement, and scalable learning experiences.

  • Bachelor’s degree

Job.JobTitle: Offer Strategy and Management, Senior Manager
Job.JobDescription:
Your opportunity


The Offer Strategy & Management, Senior Manager is a senior individual contributor responsible for shaping DAFgiving360’s portfolio of client offers, specifically the development, evolution, and ongoing management of those offers. The role translates business strategy, client needs, market opportunities, competitive insights, and performance signals into a cohesive portfolio of differentiated offers that create value for clients and advance the business’s strategic objectives.

Working across Strategy, Client Experience & Research, Product, Marketing, Sales/Distribution, Operations, Technology, Finance, Risk, and other business functions, this individual develops recommendations, structures complex offers, and drives cross-functional work from opportunity framing through execution. The role succeeds through subject-matter expertise, influence, facilitation, and disciplined execution. This role will report to the Offer Strategy and Management team leader within DAFgiving360's Strategy organization.

Offer Strategy

  • Define the offer architecture, including how individual products, services, capabilities, experiences, and benefits come together into cohesive client offers
  • Establish clear offer positioning and value propositions, articulating the client problem being solved, target audience, differentiated value, and intended business outcome
  • Translate client research, market trends, competitive intelligence, business performance, and strategic priorities into offer opportunities and implications
  • Identify areas of unmet client need and market opportunity that could warrant a new offer, an enhancement to an existing offer, or investment in a new capability
  • Develop a multi-year offer roadmap identifying the capabilities and investments required to move from the current offer toward the desired future state
  • Produce clear, evidence-based recommendations and executive-ready materials that enable timely offer and investment decisions

Offer Development

  • Apply a structured offer discovery and development process to convert strategic opportunities and client needs into tangible offer concepts
  • Frame opportunities by defining the client problem, target audience, desired experience, value proposition, business value, strategic fit, and measures of success
  • Bring together products, services, experiences, pricing or economics, servicing models, capabilities, and other components into an integrated offer
  • Define the current-state and target-state offer, identifying gaps between existing capabilities and what is required to deliver the desired proposition
  • Evaluate alternatives and trade-offs and recommend how an offer should be designed, packaged, positioned, and delivered
  • Facilitate cross-functional working sessions and leadership decisions at critical points in development, including whether opportunities should advance, change, pause, or stop
  • Partner with accountable business and delivery teams to translate approved offer concepts into clear requirements, roadmaps, ownership, and implementation plans

Offer Management

  • Support offer governance, including decision rights, forums, approval processes, standards, and escalation mechanisms.
  • Establish measures of effectiveness for individual offers
  • Monitor available signals such as client adoption, utilization, client feedback, economics, competitive position, operational performance, and strategic alignment to assess whether offers are delivering their intended value
  • Conduct periodic reviews to identify opportunities to strengthen, simplify, consolidate, reposition, or retire offers
  • Maintain core offer artifacts, decision records, portfolio views, and roadmaps so stakeholders have a shared understanding of offer direction and status

What you have


Required Qualifications

  • 6–10 years of experience in strategy, offer management, product management, management consulting, financial services, or a related field
  • Demonstrated ability to bring together products, experiences, services, and capabilities into a holistic offer strategy
  • Proven ability to influence business leaders and partners and drive outcomes
  • Strong strategic thinking paired with the ability to translate strategy into practical recommendations, roadmaps, and actions
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to synthesize complexity into clear recommendations for executive audiences
  • Strong facilitation, structured problem-solving, and decision-support skills
  • Comfort working through ambiguity, competing priorities, and evolving business needs
  • Experience partnering with data analytics teams or using data and research insights to inform offer or product strategy
  • Experience incorporating client sentiment, preferences, and needs into offer or product development and design

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree; MBA or equivalent advanced degree preferred
  • Experience applying structured problem-solving, opportunity assessment, portfolio management, and decision-making frameworks in complex environments
  • Experience in nonprofit organizations, donor-advised funds, philanthropy, or charitable giving
  • Understanding of investor and advisor needs and behaviors related to charitable giving

Your opportunity


The Business Acceleration Team (BAT) at DAFgiving360 was established to accelerate large, cross-enterprise initiatives across the company. This organization partners closely with teams across DAFgiving360 and Schwab to support all facets of transformation, from identifying, scoping and designing opportunities to implementing and executing strategic initiatives.

BAT is seeking a Sr Manager (PL), Business Acceleration to lead a team of 2-3 professionals and help shape the direction, charter, and operating model of the team. This leader will provide strategic direction on large-scale projects, establish clear expectations for how the team engages with partners, and create the conditions for team members to successfully fulfill the charter. The Sr Manager will have broad influence across DAFgiving360, partnering with the Project Management Office (PMO), Business Sponsors, the Senior Management Team (SMT), and leaders across the organization to activate and advance complex strategic initiatives. The role will balance people leadership, team development, strategic problem solving, and hands-on support for high-priority work that drives greater scale and efficiency, improves the client experience, and modernizes how DAFgiving360 operates.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Provide strategic oversight across multiple initiatives while selectively serving as the Business Lead on large, complex, or highly visible efforts
  • Partner with the Strategy leadership team and key stakeholders to shape and advance strategic initiatives
  • Lead, coach, and develop a team of 2-3 professionals, setting clear priorities, providing timely feedback, and creating meaningful development opportunities aligned with the team charter and individual career goals
  • Create the structure, standards, tools, and team norms needed to deliver high-quality, consistent work across initiatives
  • Collaborate closely with the PMO, Business Sponsors, SMT, and cross-functional partners to define strategy, design plans, manage execution, and facilitate effective handoffs
  • Build trusted relationships across DAFgiving360 and Schwab and use influence, sound judgment, and enterprise perspective to align stakeholders and move work forward
  • Anticipate portfolio-level risks, capacity constraints, dependencies, and organizational impacts; elevate issues and adapt plans as needed
  • Communicate priorities, progress, decisions, and outcomes clearly to senior leaders and stakeholders, ensuring alignment and sustained engagement throughout the life cycle of initiatives
  • Promote learning across the portfolio by capturing and applying best practices, insights, and reusable approaches that strengthen DAFgiving360’s transformation capabilities
  • Contribute actively to the culture of Strategy and the broader organization by modeling collaboration, accountability, inclusion, adaptability, and a growth mindset

Ideal Candidate Profile:

  • People leader - Develops strong, capable teams through clear expectations, coaching, feedback, delegation, and differentiated development; creates an environment where people can do their best work
  • Team builder and charter shaper - Can turn a broad mandate into a clear team charter, operating model, priorities, roles, and ways of working

About this job

Senior Banker role serving Schwab Wealth Advisory clients with lending, deposit, and trust solutions. Responsibilities include advising on mortgages, home equity lines of credit, securities-based lending, and coordinating with internal teams to develop customized solutions for high net worth clients.

Good fit if you have banking or lending experience and can build relationships with wealth advisory partners and high net worth clients.

Full job description

Your opportunity


We believe that, when done right, investing liberates people to create their own destiny. We are driven by our purpose to champion every client’s goals with passion and integrity. We respect and appreciate the diversity of our employees, our clients, and the communities we serve. We challenge conventions strategically to create value for our clients, our firm and the world. We live and bring to life the concept of ‘own your tomorrow’ every day. We champion our employee strengths, guide their development, and invest in their long-term success. We hire optimistic, results-oriented, curious, innovative, and adaptable people with the desire to help our clients and one another succeed.

As a company, we were established by Chuck over 40 years ago to champion Main Street over Wall Street, and to help Americans transform themselves from earners to owners. Through advocacy and innovation, we work to make investing more affordable, accessible and understandable for all. As we enter our fifth decade, we are looking for talented, innovative and driven people who believe they can help themselves, and our clients, create a better future.

Charles Schwab Bank (CSB) has proven successful in serving the lending needs of Schwab’s core Retail consumer clients which is an important business line that we will continue to grow.  We now have a unique opportunity to expand our lending capabilities by targeting Schwab’s high net worth (HNW) clients and registered investment advisory (RIA) firms.  To seize this growth opportunity, we will build a separate, parallel lending business model leveraging Charles Schwab Premier Bank (CSPB).  HNW clients and RIA firms have complex credit profiles and higher service level expectations requiring a different approach with specialized expertise to serve their needs. 

Our Opportunity:

The Senior Banking team is seeking a high potential candidate to partner with Schwab Wealth Advisory partners and their end clients by providing Banking and Credit solutions. Bank lending products include residential mortgages, home equity lines of credit, and securities-based lending. Schwab Bank also offers trust services and deposit products including checking and savings accounts. The Senior Banker will be responsible for serving Schwab Wealth Advisory clients and will work closely with partners across the Bank including the Bank Sales Team, Bank Credit Team, Bank Operations, Trust and Deposit service teams to develop solutions and recommendations meeting the unique needs of Schwab Wealth Advisory clients. This role encompasses internal marketing such as meetings with various Schwab Partners and client meetings as may be requested. The Senior Banker will also coordinate with Schwab Wealth Advisory clients’ accountants, attorneys or other professionals as needed. Additionally, the Senior Banker acts as the primary contact for assisting loan inquiries, loans in process and problem resolution that may need to be completed for both origination and servicing requests.

What you’ll do: 

  • Advise Schwab Wealth Advisory clients on appropriate Bank lending, deposit and trust solutions including products, pricing and recommended deal structures. Gather information from clients using internal and external resources for the completion of the application process.
  • Partner with Schwab teammates in assigned geographies to discuss Schwab Wealth Advisory client base and identify lending, deposit and trust opportunities and recommend opportunity action plans.
  • Establish a reputation of execution and excellence. Gain confidence of Schwab Partners to fully develop lending, deposit and trust opportunities with their Schwab Wealth Advisory clients.
  • Develop and present creative and intelligent lending, deposit and trust solutions; consult partners, such as credit specialists, as needed.
  • Take ownership of banking client experience from initial contact to loan funding or account establishment, working closely with partners and third-party providers to ensure a smooth process for Schwab Wealth Advisory clients.
  • Work with and communicate effectively with Schwab partners.
  • Responsible for the early identification of complex transaction structures, such as: entity, trust, guarantor, co-op, unique property requirements, condensed timeframes, properties under construction, and need for multiple co-borrowers.
  • Maintain full awareness of status for all Schwab Wealth Advisory banking applications in pipeline and function as primary Schwab Bank liaison for all parties involved in bank account opening process, including service, credit, risk and third-party vendors.
  • Address all issues surfaced during loan process and assist with underwriting requests for additional information as needed.

Why You're Set Up for Success

You will join a highly collaborative environment focused on delivering exceptional client outcomes through relationship-based advice and comprehensive wealth management strategies. You'll partner closely with specialists across investment management, banking, lending, trust, insurance, and planning disciplines to develop tailored solutions for complex client needs.

Success in this role comes from combining deep financial expertise with an entrepreneurial mindset, strategic perspective, and the ability to influence decisions and manage conflict constructively. Your ability to anticipate client needs, uncover growth opportunities, coordinate resources, and sustain trusted relationships will enable you to deliver meaningful outcomes for clients and their families.

Schwab Training and Development

  • Ongoing professional development focused on wealth management, investment strategy, retirement income planning, and client relationship management.
  • Access to specialized training, coaching, and development opportunities designed to strengthen advisory skills, deepen technical expertise, and support career growth.
  • Opportunities to collaborate with experienced wealth specialists and subject matter experts across Schwab's wealth management organization.

The Senior Banker role provides opportunities for continued growth across the banking organization. As expertise and influence expand, career opportunities may include leadership pathways, advanced advisory roles, private client segments, and specialized wealth management functions.

Schwab also supports a 'choose your own adventure' approach to career development, allowing employees to pursue opportunities aligned with their strengths, interests, and long-term goals.

What you have


What you have:

  • Minimum of 5 years of successful lending consultation and business development experience in Financial Services or working closely with HNW/UHNW clients.
  • Expert knowledge of credit products including residential mortgage products, home equity lines of credit, and securities-based loans. Familiarity with bank deposit and cash management products and brokerage margin product as well as business banking requirements and structures.
  • Proven ability to analyze cash flow and balance sheet of HNW/UHNW retail brokerage clients and develop client’s personal financial statement. General understanding of estate planning techniques, entity structuring, and tax strategies.
  • Strong skills in diplomacy, discretion, and professionalism; ability to efficiently, tactfully & professionally screen, manage and/or decline transactions while maintaining partner and HNW/UHNW client relationships.
  • Possess excellent oral and written communication skills. Exceptional presentation skills.
  • Strong relationship building capabilities with Schwab teammates, HNW/UHNW clients, and matrix partners (e.g., service, credit, risk and third-party vendors).
  • Strong collaboration skills in a team-oriented environment.
  • Attention to detail and the ability to multi-task and work efficiently, independently and with teams, to meet tight deadlines with minimal supervision.
  • Strong command of mortgage underwriting guidelines. Completion of formal credit training strongly preferred.
  • Banking background with experience working with HNW/UHNW brokerage clients strongly preferred.
  • Undergraduate or advanced degree preferred.
  • NMLS license required or to be obtained within 90 days of employment.
  • Series 7 and 63/65 or 66 licenses required.

You demonstrate these behaviors:

  • Building Collaborative Relationships:  The ability to develop, maintain, and strengthen partnerships with others inside or outside of the organization who can provide information, assistance, and support.
  • Customer Orientation: Demonstrated concern for satisfying one’s external and/or internal customers.
  • Diagnostic Information Gathering: Identifying the information needed to clarify a situation, seeking that information from appropriate sources, and using skillful questioning to draw out the information when others are reluctant to disclose it.
  • Fostering Teamwork: As a team member, the ability and desire to work cooperatively with others on a team; as a team leader, interest, skill, and success in getting groups to learn to work together cooperatively.
  • Results Orientation: Focusing on the desired result of one’s own or one’s units work; setting challenging goals, focusing effort on the goals, and meeting or exceeding them.

 What you’ll get:

  • Comprehensive Compensation and Benefits package
  • Financial Health: 401k Match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan, Employee Discounts, Personalized advice, Brokerage discounts
  • Work/Life Balance: Sabbatical, Paid Parental Leave, New Mothers returning to work Program, Tuition Reimbursement Programs, Time off to volunteer, Employee Matching Gifts Program
  • Everyday Wellness: Health and Lifestyle Wellness Rewards, Onsite Fitness Classes, Healthy Food Choices, Wellness Champions
  • Inclusion: Employee Resource Groups, Commitment to diversity, Strategic partnerships
  • Not just a job, but a career, with an opportunity to do the best work of your life

About this job

Lead strategy and execution for transforming Advisor Services knowledge into a structured, reusable asset for people, systems, and AI capabilities. Modernize content operations and build a semantic knowledge foundation to support workflows, platforms, and future innovation.

Good fit if you have 10+ years in product management or platform transformation in financial services, direct people leadership experience, and knowledge of knowledge management and AI-ready content structures.

Full job description

Your opportunity


At Schwab, you’re empowered to make an impact on your career. Here, innovative thinking meets disciplined execution to challenge the status quo and transform the finance industry together.

We believe in the importance of in-office collaboration and fully intend for the selected candidate for this role to work on site in the specified location(s).

The Director, Advisor Services Knowledge Solutions will lead the strategy, product direction, and execution model for turning Advisor Services knowledge into a strategic asset that can be used by people, systems, automation, internal and client-facing AI capabilities, and external 3rd party APIs. This role will strengthen the human-readable knowledge advisors and service professionals rely on today while making priority knowledge structured, consistent, governed, reusable, and ready to support workflows, internal platforms, digital experiences, APIs, and emerging AI-enabled capabilities.

This is a foundational opportunity to modernize the Advisor Services content operations cycle so knowledge is easier for SMEs to update, closer to real time, and more accurate at the source. By building a semantic, intelligent knowledge foundation, this leader will help reduce friction, improve execution quality, and strengthen Schwab Advisor Services’ ability to scale knowledge across people, platforms, and future innovation.

This role will be responsible for:

Product, Technology & Semantic Knowledge Strategy

  • Lead the Advisor Services Knowledge Solutions strategy, roadmap, capability model, and success measures that connect knowledge transformation to business outcomes.
  • Build the semantic knowledge foundation needed to make priority knowledge structured, reusable, system-interpretable, and ready for platform, workflow, API, search, and AI-enabled use cases.
  • Translate business priorities, servicing workflows, operational needs, and advisor pain points into product requirements, roadmap inputs, and execution plans.
  • Advance Advisor Services-specific knowledge transformation while coordinating with enterprise data, search, knowledge, technology, risk, compliance, and operations teams.

Content Operations Transformation & Knowledge Governance

  • Modernize how Advisor Services knowledge is created, structured, governed, updated, measured, and activated across the business leveraging modern technology automation and AI capabilities. .
  • Streamline and automate the content update process so SMEs can maintain accurate knowledge more easily, more frequently, and closer to real time.
  • Establish standards for content structure, metadata, ownership, update models, quality controls, and governance so knowledge can be refreshed, validated, and applied consistently.

People Leadership, Partnership & Execution

  • Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team responsible for knowledge product strategy, content operations transformation, governance, requirements, and execution.
  • Lead through influence across a matrixed environment, aligning partners around shared priorities, clear ownership, and measurable outcomes.
  • Create executive-ready recommendations, roadmap updates, and business cases that show how knowledge transformation improves execution and creates strategic leverage for Advisor Services allowing it to differentiate the client experience

What Success Looks Like

  • Delivered a clear Advisor Services Knowledge Solutions strategy with defined outcomes, governance, roadmap, ownership, prioritization, and measurable business value.
  • Modernized the content operations cycle so high-value knowledge is easier for SMEs to maintain, more accurate, and closer to real time.
  • Established a semantic knowledge foundation that makes priority knowledge structured, governed, reusable, workflow-ready, and easier for systems to consume.
  • Reduced operational friction by addressing fragmented content, manual interpretation, stale guidance, downstream validation, NIGO, and rework.
  • Unlocked knowledge as a strategic asset that improves today’s execution while preparing Advisor Services for platform integration, search, APIs, workflow automation, and future AI-enabled capabilities.

What you have


Required Qualifications

  • Experience in financial services, custody, brokerage, advisor platforms, or internal servicing operations.
  • Background in knowledge management modernization, content operations transformation, or AI readiness.
  • Familiarity with Knowledge as a Product, RAG, context engineering, agent-ready content, metadata and taxonomy, knowledge graphs, and semantic models.
  • 10+ years of experience across product management, technology strategy, platform transformation, knowledge solutions, content operations, or related roles in complex, regulated environments.
  • Must have direct people leadership experience, directly leading individuals, not just cross functional
