Job.JobTitle: Senior Subrogation Attorney, Remote (Los Angeles, CA)
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. 

Job Description

Join Allstate's legal frontline and play a critical role in recovering losses and advancing strategic litigation outcomes. As a Senior Subrogation Attorney, you will lead complex auto and property subrogation matters from investigation through resolution, while providing legal guidance to claims partners and business stakeholders.   

This role offers the opportunity to independently manage sophisticated litigation, develop recovery strategies, conduct negotiations, and represent Allstate in court, arbitration, mediation, and trial proceedings. You will collaborate closely with legal and claims teams, provide thought leadership on subrogation matters, and contribute to meaningful financial and operational impact through successful recovery efforts. 

Applicants must be licensed to practice in the state of California 

Applicants must reside in the following states: CA, WA, AZ, NV, OR 

 

This position is eligible for a $10,000 sign-on bonus, subject to applicable terms and conditions. 

Key Responsibilities  


  • Manage all aspects of complex auto and property subrogation litigation from investigation through resolution, including discovery, depositions, motion practice, negotiations, arbitrations, trials, and post-trial motions.  
  • Investigate and evaluate subrogation opportunities, determine liability and damages, and develop recovery strategies to maximize results.  
  • Lead negotiations with carriers, attorneys, and third parties to achieve favorable recovery outcomes and efficient dispute resolution.  
  • Review new file assignments, develop litigation strategies, and provide legal guidance aligned with business objectives.  
  • Partner with claims professionals and business stakeholders to provide legal counsel on litigation risks, recovery opportunities, and case strategy.  
  • Prepare and present witnesses, conduct depositions, and represent the Company in hearings, mediations, arbitrations, and trials.  
  • Analyze claims files, expert reports, legal authorities, and other case materials to support litigation strategy and recovery recommendations.  
  • Prepare and argue pre-trial and post-trial motions, settlement proceedings, and other complex legal matters.  
  • Monitor developments in applicable laws, regulations, and case law, providing proactive guidance on potential impacts to subrogation recoveries and litigation strategy.  
  • Manage a high-volume caseload and legal projects effectively while collaborating with attorneys, claims teams, and support staff to drive successful outcomes  

Education  


  • Juris Doctorate required.  
  • Active membership in good standing with the California State Bar required.  

Minimum Requirements  


  • 4+ years of litigation experience, including insurance defense, subrogation, personal injury, property damage litigation, or related practice areas.  
  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage a substantial litigation caseload from inception through resolution.  
  • Experience conducting depositions, mediations, arbitrations, hearings, and other litigation proceedings.  
  • Strong knowledge of civil litigation procedures, legal strategy development, negotiation, and dispute resolution.  
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office, LexisNexis (preferred), and legal research platforms.  
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with attorneys, paralegals, claims professionals, and support staff.  
  • Comfortable working in a remote environment and willing to travel throughout California for trials & court appearances on an as needed basis. 

Skills

Arbitration, Case Management, Court Appearances, Depositions, Litigation, Trial Practice

Compensation

Compensation for this role ranges from $150,000 to $170,800 annually, based on experience and qualifications, with an additional annual bonus opportunity.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. 

Job Description

We are seeking a Lead Threat Hunter to lead hypothesis-driven, intelligence-led hunts across enterprise, cloud, and OT/IoT environments. This role proactively identifies adversary tradecraft that evades existing detections, operationalizes findings into durable detection logic, and partners with Threat Intelligence, Detection Engineering, IR, Exposure Management, and REM to reduce dwell time and shrink the enterprise exposure plane. The hunter will leverage MITRE ATT&CK, the Pyramid of Pain, and the Diamond Model to drive measurable risk reduction.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead hypothesis-driven, intelligence-led hunt campaigns from formulation through reporting, mapped to MITRE ATT&CK
  • Design and execute custom analytics against large-scale security telemetry (SIEM, EDR/XDR, identity, cloud, network) to uncover adversary tradecraft that evades existing detections
  • Perform identity-centric hunting across Entra ID, Active Directory, and SaaS platforms - token theft, session hijacking, MFA bypass, OAuth abuse, and conditional access circumvention.
  • Conduct cloud-native hunting across AWS, Azure, M365, and SaaS control planes, including audit logs, identity events, and workload telemetry.
  • Convert hunt findings into durable detections, signatures, and SOAR playbooks in partnership with Detection Engineering, closing the hunt-to-detect loop
  • Perform Deception Operations by defining adversary-aligned use cases, authoring detection requirements for deception-generated activity, and tuning signal vs. noise thresholds
  • Leverage AI and LLM-assisted tooling to accelerate hunting - including query generation, log summarization, entity pivoting, anomaly clustering, and large-scale pattern discovery across disparate telemetry sources
  • Hunt within AI and LLM environments - including enterprise copilots, internal/external LLM deployments, AI agents, RAG pipelines, model endpoints, and AI/ML infrastructure - for threats such as prompt injection, model abuse, data exfiltration via AI channels, agent hijacking, supply-chain compromise of models, and unauthorized model access
  • Produce post-hunt reports with explicit evidence and measurable outcomes tied to exposure reduction
  • Partner with Threat Intelligence to operationalize finished intel into targeted hunt missions and feed collection requirements upstream
  • Support purple team exercises and validate detection efficacy against adversary emulation campaigns (Atomic Red Team, CALDERA, Stratus Red Team)
  • Develop and maintain custom tooling and automation to support hunting, investigation, and analyst efficiency
  • Mentor junior hunters; contribute to internal knowledge bases, hunt libraries, and team training
  • Support Incident Response, Forensics, and Insider Threat/Fraud investigations as a senior technical resource when adversary expertise is needed
  • Serve as a liaison for Threat Services across Cyber Operations, communicating findings clearly to technical peers and executive leadership
  • Identify needs, drive solutions, and operate autonomously within strategic priorities
  • Identify visibility and telemetry gaps discovered during hunts and partner with engineering teams to improve enterprise collection coverage
  • Develop behavioral, anomaly-based, and baseline-deviation hunt methodologies beyond known ATT&CK tradecraft


Required Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience in security operations with 4+ of those years dedicated to threat hunting
  • Deep experience hunting in large, complex enterprise environments
  • Demonstrable experience executing MITRE ATT&CK-aligned hunts with documented outcomes and detection handoffs
  • Hands-on experience with modern SIEM (Splunk, Sentinel, Elastic) and EDR/XDR (CrowdStrike, Defender, SentinelOne, Tanium)
  • Demonstrated experience using AI/LLM-assisted tooling (e.g., Security Copilot, custom GPTs, agentic workflows, embeddings-based analytics) to accelerate hunting, triage, and analytic development.
  • Working knowledge of hunting in AI/LLM environments - familiarity with the MITRE ATLAS framework, OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, and common AI-specific threats (prompt injection, model theft, training data poisoning, agent abuse, sensitive data leakage through AI channels)
  • Working knowledge of threat intelligence frameworks: Diamond Model, Kill Chain, and the Pyramid of Pain
  • Strong scripting and automation skills in Python, PowerShell, GO, and/or Bash
  • Deep understanding of common network and application stack protocols: TCP/IP, DNS, TLS, HTTP, SMTP, etc.
  • Experience with signature and analytic development: CQL/KQL/SPL analytics, Sigma, YARA, Snort/Suricata
  • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with a research mindset and a passion for puzzles
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to produce executive-ready summaries of technical findings
  • Demonstrated leadership and mentorship capability
  • Strong motivation to understand and train in new technologies, techniques, and a self-starter
  • Demonstrated ownership of end-to-end hunting programs, including hypothesis generation, data source evaluation, hunt execution, findings analysis, stakeholder communication, and measurement of outcomes


Desirable Criteria

  • Proficiency in KQL/CQL/SPL; comfortable building complex queries and analytics across large datasets
  • Experience hunting in cloud environments (AWS, Azure, M365) using native telemetry such as CloudTrail, Azure Activity, M365 Unified Audit Log, and identity provider logs
  • Adversary emulation experience using Atomic Red Team, CALDERA, Stratus Red Team, or equivalent
  • Recent experience with malware analysis and reverse engineering
  • Hands-on experience securing or hunting within AI/ML pipelines, model registries, vector databases, and agentic systems
  • Hands-on experience with vulnerability research, penetration testing, or exploit development (offensive mindset)
  • Experience with container and Kubernetes security telemetry (Falco, runtime security, cloud workload protection)
  • Experience consuming deception technology outputs as a hunting data source
  • Familiarity with threat hunting maturity models (e.g., Hunting Maturity Model - HMM) and capability of advancing program maturity
  • Experience with insider threat or fraud-adjacent hunting use cases
  • Published research, conference talks, CTF participation, or contributions to open-source detection content (Sigma rules, Atomic Red Team, hunt libraries)
  • Familiarity with OT/ICS or IoT environments
  • Relevant certifications such as:
    • GIAC: GCTD, GCTI, GCFA, GCFE, GNFA, GREM, GDAT, GCIA
    • Offensive: OSCP, OSCE, CRTO
    • Cloud: AWS Security Specialty, AZ-500, SC-200
    • AI Security: AI/ML security certifications, MITRE ATLAS training, AI red-team credentials
    • Foundational: CISSP, CEH
  • Tool-specific certifications in Splunk, Sentinel, CrowdStrike, or similar platforms

Skills

Analytical Research, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Cybersecurity Operations, Cyber Threat Hunting, Cyber Threat Intelligence, Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), IT Automation, Large Language Models (LLMs), Mentorship, MITRE ATT&CK Framework, Project Leadership, Scripting, Security Incident Response, Security Information and Event Management (SIEM)

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. 

Job Description

Technology Operations, Risk & Compliance (TORC) is ACC’s first-line operating system for controls, risk management and remediation, compliance, and resilience. TORC operates at the intersection of cybersecurity, technology operations, risk, controls, compliance, resilience, and enterprise transformation, turning ACC priorities and enterprise obligations into measurable controls, actionable intelligence, accountability, and sustained risk reduction.

TORC is entering the next phase of that evolution: engineering risk and control capabilities that operate at enterprise scale. A cornerstone of this work is the Unified System of Controls (USC), a strategic ACC product intended to provide a sustainable command-and-control capability for controls, bringing together control expectations, procedures, measurement, evidence, reporting, exceptions, ownership, and accountability.

The Principal Engineer will help build the engineering function required to make that ambition real.

Job Summary

The role will also establish close engineering partnerships with Product Security (ProdSec) and Security Operations (SecOps) across ACC, leveraging and integrating their capabilities into TORC products where appropriate and avoiding creation of parallel security engineering capabilities.


Key Responsibilities

Build and Lead the TORC Engineering Function

  • Build and mature TORC's engineering capability, including the talent, engineering practices, operating model, delivery discipline, and technical competencies necessary to deliver enterprise-scale products.
  • Establish an engineering culture centered on quality, automation, reliability, security, reuse, observability, and measurable outcomes.
  • Build and develop a high-performing engineering organization capable of solving complex technology, risk, and control problems.
  • Establish clear engineering accountability and decision rights while developing future technical leaders and strengthening engineering capability across the organization.
  • Create reusable engineering patterns and capabilities that enable TORC to scale beyond individual solutions.


Deliver the Unified System of Controls (USC)

  • Provide senior engineering leadership for the Unified System of Controls, translating its product direction and requirements into scalable, production-grade technology.
  • Lead engineering delivery of capabilities supporting control measurement, evidence, reporting, exceptions, workflow, integration, accountability, and decision-grade insight.
  • Enable the movement from point-in-time and manually intensive control processes toward sustainable capabilities supported by automation and continuous telemetry.
  • Ensure USC engineering is designed for enterprise scale, sustainability, interoperability, security, reliability, and reuse.
  • Establish an extensible engineering foundation that can support additional TORC and ACC strategic products over time.


Translate Strategy and Product Direction into Engineering Execution

  • Partner with Digital Product leadership to convert product vision, priorities, and outcomes into executable engineering roadmaps and delivery.
  • Apply sound engineering judgment to determine how capabilities should be implemented within established enterprise technology and architecture direction.
  • Bring an engineering perspective into product discovery, helping teams understand technical feasibility, complexity, dependencies, scalability, and implementation tradeoffs.
  • Maintain strong discipline between strategy ownership, product ownership, architecture accountability, and engineering execution.


What Success Looks Like

Success is not simply delivering a technology solution. It is establishing engineering as a durable capability within TORC.


The Principal Engineer will have:

  • Built a mature, high-performing TORC engineering function with clear accountability, strong talent, disciplined engineering practices, and an outcome-oriented culture.
  • Delivered significant engineering capabilities supporting the Unified System of Controls and demonstrated that USC can operate as a sustainable enterprise product.
  • Created strong working relationships across Platform Consulting, Digital Product, Architecture, Product Security, Security Operations, and other ACC engineering functions.
  • Established reusable engineering capabilities that can scale additional TORC and ACC strategic products.
  • Increased the use of automation, integration, telemetry, and continuous measurement within TORC products.
  • Demonstrated that complex risk and control challenges can increasingly be addressed through sustainable engineering rather than additional manual process.
  • Established TORC Engineering as a trusted, high-impact technology partner within ACC.


Education

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related technical field required.
  • Master's degree or equivalent advanced technical experience preferred.


Experience

  • 12+ years of progressive technology and engineering experience preferred.
  • Significant experience leading enterprise-scale software, platform, or engineering capability.
  • Demonstrated experience building or materially transforming engineering teams and engineering practices.
  • Experience delivering secure, enterprise-scale applications or platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead highly complex initiatives spanning multiple organizations and technology domains.
  • Experience translating strategy, product direction, and business requirements into engineering execution.
  • Demonstrated success operating with senior executives and influencing across organizational boundaries.


Leadership & Functional Capabilities

  • Exceptional engineering depth, with significant experience delivering secure, reliable, and scalable enterprise technology.
  • Strong knowledge of modern software engineering, APIs, data integration, automation, cloud, telemetry, observability, reliability, and secure engineering practices.
  • Ability to assess highly complex technical and business challenges, evaluate implementation options and tradeoffs, and make sound decisions in high-pressure or time-sensitive environments.
  • Strong product and business orientation, with the ability to translate strategy and desired outcomes into executable engineering roadmaps, standards, reusable patterns, and delivery disciplines.
  • Ability to communicate complex engineering concepts in clear business language and influence senior executives, engineering leaders, peers, and cross-functional partners without relying solely on positional authority.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead across highly matrixed and distributed environments, building alignment among product, platform, architecture, cybersecurity, risk, and engineering stakeholders.
  • Experience leading significant technology, engineering, or operating-model transformation and establishing the practices required to sustain change.
  • Strong talent and capability-building skills, including coaching, role clarity, accountability, upskilling, and development of future technical leaders.
  • Sound judgment regarding the application of modern technology, AI, and automation, including the ability to balance innovation, business value, security, and risk.
  • Ability to connect engineering decisions to measurable business outcomes through analytical rigor, technology fluency, and disciplined execution.


Why This Role Matters

TORC's next evolution depends on our ability to engineer solutions to risk and control problems that historically relieve process, manual intervention, and point-in-time visibility.


The Principal Engineer will be the senior engineering leader responsible for helping make that transition real.


This leader will build the engineering capability behind TORC, deliver foundational products such as the Unified System of Controls, and connect Product, Platform, Architecture, ProdSec, SecOps, and engineering execution to create sustainable technology solutions that improve how Allstate understands and manages control and technology risk.

Skills

Automation, Data Integration, Enterprise Architecture (EA), Executive Leadership, People Leadership, Software Engineering

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 199,000.00 - 274,000.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. 

Job Description

Exposure Response team and overall work scope

 

  • The team operates within a newly established Exposure Management function in the broader cybersecurity organization, focused on modernizing how the enterprise identifies, prioritizes, and mitigates security vulnerabilities shifting from traditional patch approaches to a more strategic focus on true business risk and exploitability
  • Exposure Response aligns more closely with security operations than traditional vulnerability scanning. The team evaluates newly disclosed CVEs, zero-days, KEVs, and critical exposures; determines enterprise impact; continuously refines scope; coordinates remediation; and drives events toward risk reduction.
  • The role: Senior hands-on technical operator responsible for protecting the enterprise from critical vulnerability and exposure risk. This role combines advanced technical investigation, threat-hunting and incident-response techniques, Incident Command, cross-functional coordination, and analyst development. When investigation identifies potential or active compromise, the Lead engages the appropriate SOC and Incident Response teams and provides the technical context needed to support their response

This isn't a traditional vulnerability scanning role. You'll work in situations where the answer may not yet be known, the scope may change as evidence emerges, and timely technical judgment matters.


Coverage & Working Model

 

  • We're hiring three Security Exposure Response Leads aligned to U.S. operating-day coverage: East, Central, and  West
  • Each Lead will generally work 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. in their respective time zone, allowing active exposure events to transition from East to West as the operating day progresses.
  • Exposure Response operates as one team. Active investigations may be handed over from one coverage period to another so investigation, decision-making and remediation can continue without losing momentum.
  • The broader operation supports a 24/7/365 response model. The positions will participate in an on-call rotation, and critical events may occasionally require work beyond normal hours.

Key Accountabilities

 

  • Hands-On Exposure Investigation : Investigate newly disclosed CVEs, zero-days with unknown scope or impact, KEVs, actively exploited vulnerabilities, and critical exposures. Correlate security and technology data, test hypotheses, identify affected assets, and continuously refine scope and impact as new information becomes available.
  • Incident Command: Lead fast-moving exposure events and serve as Incident Commander when appropriate. Make timely decisions with incomplete information, establish priorities, coordinate parallel workstreams, continuously track actions and decisions, and refine scope, impact, and response as the event evolves.
  • Response Coordination and Escalation: Coordinate across technology and security teams to establish ownership, drive remediation, resolve blockers, maintain momentum, and escalate conditions that threaten timely risk reduction. Engage SOC and Incident Response when findings indicate potential or active compromise.
  • Technical Leadership and Development: Provide hands-on coaching and training to develop analysts, strengthening capabilities in exposure investigation, threat hunting, investigative analysis, scope development, case management, escalation, and operational decision-making.
  • Operational Continuity: Maintain clear operational awareness and documentation of active events, including scope, findings, decisions, ownership, remediation status, blockers, and unresolved questions. Provide structured handoffs across coverage periods to maintain continuity and momentum.

Qualifications

 

Required

  • 5+ years of cybersecurity or technology operations experience involving technical investigation, coordination, escalation, and resolution.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead or coordinate high-priority, fast-moving operational events and make sound decisions with incomplete or changing information.
  • Strong hands-on technical and investigative skills, with the ability to correlate multiple data sources, test assumptions, establish scope and impact, and determine required actions.
  • Ability to coordinate across technical teams without direct authority and drive issues toward resolution.
  • Experience mentoring, training, or providing technical guidance to developing analysts.

 

Preferred

  • Experience in Security Operations, Incident Response, Threat Hunting, network operations, infrastructure operations, or another high-tempo technical operations environment.
  • Experience applying threat-hunting or incident-response investigative techniques to events where scope and impact evolved during the investigation.
  • Experience leading significant security or technical events, including Incident Command.
  • Familiarity with enterprise vulnerability, endpoint, cloud, asset, network, or exposure-management technologies.

 

You don't need experience with a specific security product or platform to be successful in this role. We're more interested in how you investigate, connect technical evidence, make decisions, and drive complex issues toward resolution.

What Makes This Opportunity Different

This is a role for someone who enjoys operating between vulnerability management, threat hunting, security operations and incident response.

Rather than simply identifying vulnerabilities and handing them off, you'll stay close to the problem: investigating what an emerging exposure means to the enterprise, developing the scope, coordinating the response, and helping drive it toward measurable risk reduction.

If you enjoy technically ambiguous problems, can move comfortably from deep investigation to coordinating multiple teams, and are energized by helping others become stronger security practitioners, this is an opportunity to have meaningful influence on how critical cyber exposures are handled

Skills

Cyber Incident Response, Cyber Threat Analysis, Cyber Threat Hunting, Endpoint Security, Exposure Assessment, Exposure Management, Exposure Monitoring, Incident Response, Incident Response Operations, IT Security Operations, Security Incident Response, SOC Operations, Threat and Vulnerability Management, Threat Assessment, Threat Detection, Vulnerability Management

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 100,000.00 - 170,500.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The candidate(s) offered this position will be required to submit to a background investigation.

Job Description

We are seeking an experienced Senior PostgreSQL Database Administrator to join the Database Engineering team and help build, operate, and modernize our enterprise PostgreSQL platform. This role will be responsible for the design, implementation, automation, security, performance, high availability, backup and recovery, and operational support of PostgreSQL environments across on-premises and cloud platforms.

The ideal candidate will have deep PostgreSQL expertise, strong Linux administration skills, hands-on experience with high availability and disaster recovery technologies, and the ability to partner effectively with application, infrastructure, security, SRE, and cloud engineering teams.

Lead to Expert level is considered, Expert level is desired.

Key Responsibilities 

PostgreSQL Platform Engineering 

  • Design, build, deploy, administer, and support enterprise PostgreSQL environments across production and non-production landscapes.
  • Lead PostgreSQL installation, configuration, patching, upgrades, migrations, and lifecycle management activities.
  • Define and maintain PostgreSQL engineering standards, reference architectures, build procedures, operational controls, and best practices.
  • Participate in architecture reviews and advise application teams on database design, scalability, resilience, and operational readiness.

High Availability and Disaster Recovery 

  • Design and support PostgreSQL high-availability solutions using technologies such as Patroni, etcd, HAProxy, Keepalived, and streaming replication.
  • Implement and maintain disaster-recovery strategies across multiple sites or regions.
  • Plan and execute failover, switchover, recovery, and resiliency tests.
  • Work with stakeholders to define, validate, and maintain recovery time and recovery point objectives.

Backup and Recovery 

  • Design, implement, and operate enterprise PostgreSQL backup and recovery solutions.
  • Administer pgBackRest, WAL archiving, point-in-time recovery, retention, and recovery validation processes.
  • Conduct regular restore testing and support disaster-recovery exercises to verify recoverability.

Performance and Reliability 

  • Monitor database availability, capacity, health, and performance.
  • Analyze and optimize SQL queries, indexes, execution plans, database configurations, and workloads.
  • Troubleshoot complex production incidents, lead root-cause analysis, and implement preventive actions.
  • Drive database reliability, observability, capacity planning, and operational excellence initiatives.

Security and Compliance 

  • Implement database security controls, access-management standards, and least-privilege practices.
  • Manage roles, privileges, authentication, encryption, auditing, and credential-management integrations.
  • Support compliance reviews, vulnerability remediation, security assessments, and evidence requests.

Automation and DevOps 

  • Develop automation for database provisioning, configuration, deployment, patching, validation, and routine operations.
  • Use Infrastructure as Code, configuration management, source control, and CI/CD practices to improve consistency and repeatability.
  • Partner with engineering teams to expand safe self-service capabilities and reduce manual operational effort.

Platform Operations and Technical Leadership

  • Provide support for mission-critical production and non-production PostgreSQL environments. 
  • Participate in on-call rotations, major incident response, change management, and problem management.
  • Create and maintain runbooks, troubleshooting guides, standards, and operational documentation.
  • Mentor engineers, review technical solutions, and provide technical leadership for PostgreSQL initiatives.

Required Qualifications

Lead Level

  • 7+ years of database administration experience. (preferred)
  • 7+ years of hands-on PostgreSQL administration experience supporting mission-critical production environments. (highly desired)
  • Plus the Technical Skills listed below.

Expert Level

  • 10+ years of database administration experience.
  • 8+ years of hands-on PostgreSQL administration experience supporting mission-critical production environments.
  • Plus the below Technical skills listed below

Technical Skills

  • Strong Linux administration experience; RHEL or a comparable enterprise Linux distribution is preferred.
  • Deep understanding of PostgreSQL architecture, internals, configuration, security, maintenance, and performance tuning.
  • Hands-on experience with PostgreSQL streaming replication, high availability, disaster recovery, backup and recovery, point-in-time recovery, WAL management, and capacity planning.
  • Strong SQL, execution-plan analysis, indexing, and query-optimization skills.
  • Proven ability to troubleshoot complex database, operating system, storage, and connectivity issues in production environments.
  • Experience planning and executing database upgrades, migrations, patching, and production changes.
  • Ability to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders and work effectively across organizational boundaries.

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Experience with Percona Distribution for PostgreSQL or Percona-supported PostgreSQL environments.
  • Hands-on experience with Patroni, etcd, HAProxy, Keepalived, pgBackRest, and PostgreSQL-native monitoring and diagnostic tools.
  • Experience with cloud database and infrastructure platforms such as Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services, or Google Cloud Platform.
  • Experience with observability platforms such as Datadog, Prometheus, Grafana, or Percona Monitoring and Management.
  • Experience with automation and delivery tools such as Ansible, Terraform, GitHub, GitLab, or CI/CD pipelines.
  • Exposure to other database technologies such as Oracle, SQL Server, MySQL, MongoDB, or Neo4j.
  • Experience leading technical initiatives, mentoring team members, and influencing platform standards.

Desired Attributes 

  • Strong ownership, accountability, and customer focus.
  • Excellent analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and drive technical initiatives to completion.
  • Strong collaboration, documentation, and communication skills.
  • Experience working in large-scale, highly available, and regulated enterprise environments.


Supervisory Responsibilities

  • This job does not have supervisory duties.

Skills

Access Management, Access Management, Accountability, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Authentication, Backup and Recovery, Cloud Computing, Cloud Engineering, Cloud Platform, Collaboration, Communication, Compliance, Computer Science, Continuous Integration Software, Credential Management, Database Administration, Database Design, Database Engineering, Database Management Systems (DBMS), Database Performance, Database Security, Database Technologies, Datadog, Data Modeling, DevOps {+ 48 more}

Compensation

Compensation offered for this role is 110,000.00 - 181,025.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

The Direct Sales Agent Specialist is responsible for driving profitable growth by generating new business, cross-selling existing customers, and building lasting relationships. This role focuses on understanding customer needs, delivering tailored solutions, and maintaining a strong book of business.

This role sells to local customers both in person and over the phone, while driving growth through community involvement, relationship building, and outside marketing efforts.

If you are ready to start working in a fun & exciting environment  while making a difference, then apply to join our team today! 

As a Direct Sales Agent Specialist, you will:

  • Achieve sales goals through new business, cross-sell, and retention
  • Build and maintain a consistent pipeline, including local lead generation and referrals
  • Develop relationships within the community (e.g., dealerships, events, local partners) to support business growth
  • Conduct outbound prospecting and follow-ups to convert opportunities into sales
  • Partner with leadership to support sales and local marketing initiatives
  • Stay informed on products, underwriting guidelines, and market competition
  • Deliver results aligned with performance standards, compliance requirements, and customer experience expectations

What makes Direct Auto Insurance unique?

  • Medical, Dental, Vision, Tuition Reimbursement, Pension & so much more
  • 20 PTO Days per year & 6 Paid Holidays
  • Ability to sell a multitude of industry-leading products through retail stores and phone
  • Entrepreneurial, performance-based, and results-focused culture
  • Multi-tiered and comprehensive paid training program
  • Base hourly rate plus uncapped monthly incentive

Job Description

The Lead Digital Product Manager(Sr Manager) will lead product strategy and delivery across Allstate’s Workday ecosystem. This individual will manage a team of product managers responsible for capabilities spanning Core HR, compensation, time and attendance, talent management, recruiting, and onboarding. The role will partner closely with HR, technology, engineering, and other product teams to build and execute an outcome-based roadmap that improves employee experience and advances enterprise priorities.

This leader will bring strong Workday platform knowledge and product management experience within an internal, end-user environment. They will evaluate competing business needs, determine how Workday capabilities fit together, and make thoughtful build, buy, or partner recommendations. Success requires balancing immediate stakeholder requests with broader platform implications, long-term product strategy, and the needs of Allstate employees.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the product strategy, vision, roadmap, and lifecycle management for Allstate’s Workday product portfolio.
  • Manage, coach, and develop a team of product managers supporting Workday products and capabilities across Core HR, compensation, time and attendance, talent management, recruiting, and onboarding.
  • Translate HR and business outcomes into clear product strategies, roadmaps, capabilities, and prioritized backlogs.
  • Balance the needs of HR Centers of Excellence and other business stakeholders with the broader experience of Allstate employees as the primary end users.
  • Evaluate incoming requests based on employee impact, business value, effort, risk, dependencies, and alignment with long-term product priorities.
  • Make and communicate build, buy, and partner recommendations that advance product strategy and maximize the value of Allstate’s existing technology investments.
  • Determine when to use existing Workday capabilities, develop internal solutions, or consider additional vendor offerings.
  • Partner with engineering and technology teams to evaluate opportunities to build internal capabilities, including AI-enabled and agentic solutions that improve employee experience and business processes.
  • Develop clear product roadmaps that help stakeholders understand how and when their desired outcomes will be addressed, including situations where the solution or sequencing differs from a vendor recommendation.
  • Lead discovery, testing, and learning activities to validate product concepts and inform investment decisions.
  • Define and monitor product KPIs to measure employee adoption, business outcomes, operational effectiveness, and overall product value.
  • Work across Workday and internally developed products to coordinate shared features, integrations, dependencies, and backlogs.
  • Communicate product decisions, tradeoffs, and priorities to senior leaders, HR stakeholders, technical teams, and vendor partners.
  • Serve as a trusted Workday product expert while maintaining an enterprise-first perspective rather than focusing solely on vendor adoption.
  • Challenge assumptions and make informed decisions that move work forward without requiring business stakeholders to resolve every individual product or implementation detail.
  • Monitor product investments and operational effectiveness and recommend adjustments based on performance, changing priorities, and emerging employee needs.
  • Lead the development and adoption of product management practices, techniques, and processes that support innovative and scalable solutions.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Strong knowledge of the Workday platform, including an understanding of how products, modules, features, and dependencies work together.
  • Experience leading product strategy and roadmap development for Workday or another large-scale, enterprise SaaS platform in an internal, end-user environment.
  • Workday experience across multiple functional areas. Experience with Core HR, compensation, and time and attendance is strongly preferred. Experience with talent management, recruiting, or onboarding is also valuable.
  • Demonstrated experience evaluating and communicating build-versus-buy decisions.
  • Experience developing outcome-based product roadmaps and prioritizing competing requests across multiple stakeholder groups. 
  • Strong judgment regarding when a technically simple request should be deferred because of broader priorities, testing needs, downstream implications, or limited enterprise value.
  • Experience partnering with engineering teams and evaluating opportunities to use internal technology or AI-enabled capabilities alongside a vendor platform.
  • Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills.
  • Ability to explain complex product decisions and tradeoffs clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
  • Experience leading, coaching, and developing product managers.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a complex, cross-functional environment spanning HR, technology, engineering, operations, and vendor partners.
  • Engineering experience is not required, but the candidate should be comfortable discussing technical dependencies, integrations, implementation considerations, and platform capabilities.

Experience

  • Ten or more years of relevant product management, enterprise platform, HR technology, or related experience preferred.
  • Prior experience managing product teams and leading products across multiple business or functional areas preferred.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position has supervisory responsibilities.


Work Arrangement

This is a remote position. Candidates should be able to travel for periodic in-person meetings, potentially up to once per quarter.

Job.JobTitle: Bodily Injury Adjuster - Represented, Moderate/Complex (EST/CST) Remote
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. 

Job Description

A day in the life of a Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster Moderate/Complex, and what it takes to do the job! 


As a Represented Bodily Injury Adjuster, your main focus will be investigating automobile accidents involving single or multiple vehicles, which result in property damage and/or bodily injury with attorney/litigation involved. You will have the convenience of working remotely from your home while efficiently handling your responsibilities. You will assess coverage, liability, and damages while providing exceptional customer service throughout your day. Customer and attorney communication will take place through different channels, including voice calls, email, and text messages. Through the utilization of innovative platforms and tools, you will engage in negotiation processes to reach fair and timely injury settlements with all parties involved.


***The ideal candidate will be able to handle a high-volume of pending cases and have experience with not only third-party casualty adjusting, but also first-party collision and third-party property damage claims.***


Candidates for this role must reside in the Eastern or Central Time Zones.


Claims experience in Rhode Island, Massachusetts, Maine, New Hampshire, or Vermont highly preferred


Qualifications

  • Prior represented third-party casualty claim handling experience is required
  • Florida, Georgia, Nevada, Texas, California claims experience also preferred
  • 2-5 years of moderate/complex Bodily Injury claim handling experience is preferred
  • Prior litigation claims experience a plus
  • Proficient communication skills, especially over the phone, to establish rapport and assess claims accurately.
  • Ability to work independently and remotely, while managing time efficiently.
  • Proficient knowledge of insurance policies, coverage, and liability determination and state regulations.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to evaluate and negotiate injury claims successfully.
  • Knowledge of innovative tools and platforms for effective claims evaluation.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite a plus


You’ll wear a few hats to fill a few roles throughout your day that all require a level of experience:

  • The Customer Service Expert –you’ll live into Allstate’s Claims Culture by caring, empowering, and restoring, and you will accomplish that by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each casualty claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator – you’ll confidently and independently investigate casualty claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.
  • The Effective Communicator – you’ll use phone, emails and sometimes even video chat with customers to help them through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. You’ll also incorporate a specific approach to claim handling to offer the customer their preference of communication to efficiently discuss their claim needs and keep them updated on the claim progress.
  • The Negotiator – You will evaluate and negotiate claims settlements with customers, vendors, third party carriers and claimants, in accordance with all legal and business standard methodologies. With negotiations, you will incorporate tactics in handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solver –you’ll utilize multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimate tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, all while using your sharp critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorder –you’ll protect the company financially by executing policies along policy agreements, and you keep a clear record of your work in a claims system that you will be trained on. You’ll accomplish this by ensuring timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim. 

Notice of Licensing Requirement

  • As a condition of employment, your office/area may require you to obtain an adjuster and/or an appraiser license which includes passing an additional background check with the Department of Labor.  If applicable, you will be required to secure license(s) within 60 days of hire.
  • If required, the Hiring Manager will work with you along with the Centralized Licensing team to ensure that you are properly licensed.

Sign On Bonus:

You may be eligible for a $1000 Licensing Sign on Bonus if you have the applicable active licenses needed for this role.  This could include Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License.*


**Candidates who have previously worked for and are seeking to be rehired at Allstate and its family of companies are not eligible for this sign-on bonus.


This position is not available to residents of California, Washington, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico.


The first approximately 6-9 weeks of employment are dedicated to onboarding, licensing (if applicable), and role-specific training designed to prepare you for success in the role. Successful candidates must be able to attend required training sessions, actively participate in virtual learning activities, and successfully complete the training program.


Allstate Benefits

  • Being a part of Allstate means you receive a benefits package from Day 1 of employment.  This includes time off, healthcare, retirement, and more.  That is why as an Allstater, you’ll enjoy a Total Rewards package that includes:
  • Competitive pay with needed support for continuous development and career advancement.
  • Flexibility in scheduling and a time off policy that helps support your work/life balance.
  • Initial and ongoing training to get you proficient in your new role
  • Comprehensive benefits like a 401K/pension, education reimbursement, and programs to help you balance work with the rest of your life. Visit https://www.allstate.jobs/benefits/ to learn more.

Skills

Business Communications, Critical Thinking, Fraud Investigations, Information Collection, Time Management

Compensation offered for this role is 56,000.00 - 92,000.00 annually and is based on experience and qualifications.

  • Deploy and manage Kong in Kubernetes-based environments.
  • Monitor, troubleshoot, and optimize gateway performance and availability.
  • Automate deployments and operational processes using DevOps tools.

Experience

  • Minimum 3 to 5 years of hands-on experience with Kong Gateway Administration.

Job Description

The Cybersecurity Strategy Manager helps Allstate Cybersecurity & Controls (ACC) leaders turn complex cybersecurity risks, strategies, performance information, and technical initiatives into clear decisions, aligned action, and measurable outcomes. As part of the ACC Strategy team, this role develops compelling narratives and executive-ready communications for the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), ACC leadership, senior executives, the Board, and the Audit Committee. Operating as a trusted advisor in an evolving and often ambiguous environment, the role brings structure to complex questions, synthesizes technical and business perspectives, and frames priorities, trade-offs, risks, and recommendations in concise, non-technical language. Success is reflected in stronger executive decision-making, consistent strategic narratives, greater visibility into cybersecurity posture and outcomes, clear accountability, and coordinated progress on the highest-priority risks.

Key Responsibilities  


  • Develop clear, compelling cybersecurity narratives for the CISO, senior executives, Board, and Audit Committee. 
  • Translate complex cybersecurity risks, strategies, metrics, and technical initiatives into concise, non-technical, decision-ready communications. 
  • Create executive-level presentations and communications, including briefings, talking points, strategic reports, leadership updates, and Board materials. 
  • Support the development and governance of the Allstate Cybersecurity & Controls (ACC) strategy, ensuring alignment with enterprise priorities, business strategy, and the evolving cybersecurity risk environment. 
  • Monitor cybersecurity threats, regulatory developments, technology trends, and business changes to identify strategic implications and emerging priorities. 
  • Coordinate cross-functional strategic governance, including key commitments, portfolio outcomes, dependencies, risks, metrics, and leadership decisions. 
  • Measure and communicate strategic progress and cybersecurity outcomes through meaningful metrics, trends, gaps, and indicators of risk reduction. 
  • Analyze complex and ambiguous business and cybersecurity challenges, combining quantitative and qualitative information to develop practical recommendations. 
  • Frame strategic options, trade-offs, and recommendations and facilitate leadership discussions around prioritization, sequencing, and risk-informed decision-making. 
  • Build alignment across cybersecurity and enterprise partners, including Technology, Enterprise Risk, Legal, Compliance, Internal Audit, and Communications, while strengthening governance practices and team standards. 

Required Education and Experience 

  • 4+ years of experience in strategy, executive communications, strategic planning, management consulting, business analysis, portfolio governance, risk, technology, financial services, or related roles. 
  • Demonstrated experience developing executive presentations, strategic narratives, briefing materials, or Board-facing content and synthesizing complex technical and business information into clear insights and recommendations. 
  • Experience supporting strategy development, governance, metrics, portfolio reporting, facilitation, cross-functional decision-making, or senior executive communications. 
  • Experience in cybersecurity, technology, risk, consulting, financial services, insurance, or another complex regulated environment preferred. 
  • Must be willing and able to travel into our Chicago, Illinois office on an as needed basis.

Job Description

Design, build, and own scalable data products and pipelines using Microsoft Fabric and modern data engineering practices, ensuring reliability, performance, governance, and effective delivery of trusted data for digital products and analytics.

As a Senior Data Engineer, you will design, build, and support high-quality data solutions and pipelines using modern engineering practices and tools. In this role, you will partner closely with product managers, software engineers, and data analysts to deliver scalable, reliable data capabilities that power digital products and business insights. You will be accountable for the end‑to‑end lifecycle of your data products, from design and implementation through production support, data quality, and performance against key metrics. 

 

Key Responsibilities:


Design, Build & Manage Data Solutions 

  • Design, develop, and enhance scalable data pipelines and data processing systems. 
  • Build reusable ingestion, transformation, and storage patterns to support product and analytical needs. 
  • Integrate data from diverse sources including APIs, databases, event streams, and third‑party systems. 
  • Implement data models and schemas that create unified, consistent views of business operations. 

Engineering Excellence 

  • Apply modern engineering practices, including version control, testing, CI/CD, and automated deployments. 
  • Ensure data quality, integrity, and reliability through validation, monitoring, and observability tools. 
  • Optimize data workflows for performance, cost efficiency, and operational resilience. 
  • Document data flows, lineage, and technical components in support of transparency and maintainability. 

Product Collaboration & Delivery 

  • Collaborate closely with product managers, engineers, and analysts to understand data requirements. 
  • Participate in iteration planning, ensuring shared understanding of backlog items and technical needs. 
  • Engage in daily standups, retrospectives, and product ceremonies as an active member of the team. 

Governance, Standards & Continuous Improvement 

  • Contribute to data governance practices such as metadata management and data lineage. 
  • Ensure compliance with data privacy, security, and regulatory requirements. 
  • Evaluate new technologies, frameworks, and patterns to improve data infrastructure and engineering capabilities. 
  • Share knowledge and mentor less experienced engineers, contributing to team growth and best practices. 

 

Core Skills

  • Strong proficiency in developing scalable data pipelines using PySpark and Python.
  • Hands-on experience with modern data engineering frameworks and tools, including Apache Spark, Kafka, Flink, dbt, or equivalent technologies.
  • Strong knowledge of SQL, NoSQL databases, data modeling, and data architecture principles.
  • Demonstrated ability to optimize SQL queries, data pipelines, and storage for performance, scalability, and cost efficiency.
  • Experience designing and developing batch and/or real-time streaming data solutions.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Fabric Notebooks for developing, debugging, testing, and operationalizing data engineering workflows.
  • Experience with containerization and orchestration technologies, such as Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Experience implementing monitoring and observability solutions, with Datadog experience preferred.
  • Ability to work effectively in collaborative, iterative, and product-centric engineering environments.
  • Strong communication, analytical, troubleshooting, and problem-solving skills

 

Preferred Skills 

  • Experience with cloud data services (Azure, AWS). 
  • Hands‑on experience with Microsoft Fabric components, including Lakehouse, Warehouse, Data Pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, and Semantic Models. 
  • Familiarity with CI/CD pipelines (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, etc.). 
  • Performance tuning for data pipelines, databases, and queries. 
  • Familiarity with generative and agentic AI tools to improve engineering productivity.

Job Description

The Data Expert provides technical leadership in designing and delivering scalable, reliable, and well-governed enterprise data solutions. This role defines data architecture and engineering standards, solves complex data challenges, and drives modernization and engineering excellence across teams.

As a Data Expert, you will provide technical leadership in the design, engineering, governance, and evolution of enterprise data solutions. This role serves as a senior technical authority for complex data initiatives, translating business and analytical needs into scalable, secure, reliable, and well-governed data products.


You will lead the design of modern data architectures and engineering patterns, establish technical standards and best practices, and solve highly complex data problems spanning multiple systems and business domains. You will partner with product managers, architects, engineers, analytics teams, and business stakeholders to modernize data platforms and create trusted, reusable data capabilities.


You are expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy, influence technical direction across teams, mentor engineers, and drive continuous improvement in data architecture, engineering, governance, quality, observability, and operational excellence.


Key Responsibilities:


Data Architecture & Technical Leadership

  • Lead the architecture and design of complex, enterprise-scale data solutions across cloud, lakehouse, warehouse, streaming, and analytical platforms.
  • Define scalable architectural patterns for data ingestion, transformation, storage, integration, consumption, and lifecycle management.
  • Provide technical direction for complex initiatives involving multiple applications, data domains, platforms, and engineering teams.
  • Establish standards for data modeling, interoperability, metadata, lineage, security, performance, and platform integration.
  • Lead technical design reviews and evaluate architectural trade-offs involving scalability, reliability, maintainability, performance, security, and cost.
  • Serve as a technical escalation point for complex data architecture, engineering, integration, and production challenges.
  • Guide modernization of legacy data platforms and workloads using modern cloud and distributed data technologies.

Advanced Data Engineering

  • Design and lead implementation of highly scalable batch, streaming, and event-driven data processing solutions.

At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. 

Job Description

As a Claims Resolution Adjuster, your focus will be investigating automobile accidents involving bodily injury. In this role, you will assess coverage, liability, and damages while providing exceptional customer service. You will communicate with customers through voice calls, email, and text messages, and use innovative platforms and tools to negotiate fair injury settlements with all parties involved.

Candidates for this role must reside in the Pacific or Mountain time zones. This position is not available to residents of California, Washington, Alaska, Hawaii and Puerto Rico.


At Allstate, responsibilities may vary from day to day. We are looking for adaptable professionals who thrive in a dynamic environment, bring care and sound judgment to each claim, and are excited to make an impact.


  • The Customer Service Expert – You’ll support customers by caring, empowering, and restoring throughout the claims process. You will do this by being compassionate, clear, and a committed partner in each Casualty claim. You lead with empathy, always.
  • The Investigator – You’ll confidently and independently investigate casualty claims by performing detailed reviews of damage and interpreting policies to determine coverage.
  • The Effective Communicator – You’ll use phone, email, and sometimes video chat to help customers through a fast, fair, and easy claims process. You’ll also tailor your approach to claim handling by honoring the customer’s communication preferences and keeping them updated on claim progress.
  • The Negotiator – You will evaluate and negotiate claim settlements with customers, vendors, third-party carriers, and claimants in accordance with legal and business standards. You will incorporate tactics for handling challenging and complex situations.
  • The Problem Solver – You’ll use multiple tools to get the job done in a fast-paced environment, including estimating tools, job aids, and additional settlement platforms, while applying strong critical thinking skills.
  • The Recorder – You’ll help protect the company financially by following applicable policies and keeping a clear record of your work in the claims system. You’ll ensure timely and accurate documentation is completed as you work on each claim.

Preferred Qualifications 

  • 2+ years of claims experience, specifically with casualty bodily injury claims.
  • Claims investigation and negotiation experience preferred.
  • Experience with liability investigations, coverage investigations, property damage coverage, method of inspection, rental, and liability resolution preferred.
  • Strong phone communication skills, with the ability to build rapport and assess claims accurately.
  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate and negotiate injury claims successfully.

Work Location


This position is a remote home-based role. Your home office does not need to be near an Allstate office, but it does need to be in the United States within one of the listed time zones above.


When you work from home full time, you’ll need:

  • A dedicated workspace in your residence that is private and free from distractions.
  • A minimum internet bandwidth of 50 MB down/5 MB up.
  • Appropriate work surface and seating.


What will Allstate provide?

  • A technology bundle that includes all equipment needed to perform your work from home (laptop, monitors, headset, keyboard, mouse).
  • Connectivity reimbursement of $80 per month to offset some of the cost of internet.

Work Schedule 

  • 8-hour shift Mon-Fri | 8:00am - 4:30pm with potential Saturday duty rotation. 

Licensing Requirements 

  • You may be required to obtain an adjuster and/or appraiser license as a condition of employment. 
  • If required, licensing may include an additional Department of Insurance background check and must be completed within 60 days of hire. 
  • If you currently hold an active insurance license, you must terminate all existing appointments before onboarding and must not hold any outside appointments during employment. 
  • If you are seeking an adjuster role and hold a resident producer license, you must formally surrender that license when instructed by the licensing team. 
  • The Hiring Manager and Centralized Licensing team will provide support if licensing is required. By proceeding with the application process, applicants acknowledge and agree to comply with these licensing requirements. 

Sign-On Bonus Information

  • Candidates with the active license(s) required for this role may be eligible for a $1,000 Licensing Sign-On Bonus. 
  • Eligible licenses may include a Home Resident Property & Casualty License, Designated Home State (DHS) Florida or Texas License, and/or applicable Appraiser License. 
  • Current employees and candidates previously employed by Allstate or its family of companies are not eligible for this sign-on bonus. 

Allstate Benefits 

  • Day 1 benefits, including time off, healthcare, retirement, and more. 
  • Competitive pay, plus support for ongoing development and career advancement. 
  • Time off programs and resources that support work/life balance. 
  • Initial and ongoing training to help you succeed in the role. 
  • Additional benefits may include 401(k)/pension, education reimbursement, and programs that support life outside of work. Visit www.allstategoodlife.com to learn more. 

Please Note: 

  • In our virtual environment, employees are expected to be on camera and actively participate during online meetings and training sessions. 
  • This job description is not intended to include a complete list of all duties and responsibilities. Employees may be asked to perform other related duties as assigned. 
  • Regular, predictable attendance is an essential function of this role.

The first approximately 8-12 of employment are dedicated to onboarding, licensing (if applicable), and role-specific training designed to prepare you for success in the role. Successful candidates must be able to attend required training sessions, actively participate in virtual learning activities, and successfully complete the training program.

Job.JobTitle: Digital Product Manager - Control Integration Engineering
Job.JobDescription:
At Allstate, great things happen when our people work together to protect families and their belongings from life’s uncertainties. And for more than 90 years, our innovative drive has kept us a step ahead of our customers’ evolving needs. From advocating for seat belts, air bags and graduated driving laws, to being an industry leader in pricing sophistication, telematics, and, more recently, device and identity protection. 

Job Description

The Control Integration Engineering (CIE) organization accelerates consistent adoption, integration and measurement of enterprise security capabilities across Allstate and its subsidiary Market Facing Businesses (MFBs). We are seeking an experienced Digital Product Manager specializing in Integration Product Management to own the security-control integration and adoption journey for an assigned MFB portfolio.

The DPM understands each MFB's technology landscape, security posture, priorities and constraints, and works with MFB teams, control owners, Product Security, CIE engineering, architecture, risk and governance to turn them into a prioritized integration roadmap, reusable patterns and measurable adoption outcomes.

Rather than managing a traditional security product, this role productizes the integration experience, making enterprise security capabilities easier, faster and more consistent to consume. It owns the product strategy, roadmap, prioritization and outcomes for integrating these capabilities into the assigned MFB portfolio.

Integration Strategy, Roadmap & Prioritization 

  • Own the integration product strategy and multi-quarter adoption roadmap for assigned MFBs, aligned to enterprise security priorities and MFB needs. Prioritize CIE investment by security value, adoption impact, effort, dependencies and reuse potential, sequencing adoption where capabilities add the most value. 
  • Define outcomes, milestones and acceptance criteria with CIE engineering, reassessing priorities as needs, capacity and results change.
  • Manage competing demand and make transparent recommendations when demand exceeds CIE capacity.

Customer Discovery & MFB Partnership

  • Treat MFBs as CIE's internal customers; run structured discovery with their security, engineering, cloud, infrastructure and architecture leaders.
  • Understand their capabilities, patterns and constraints; identify adoption friction and separate legitimate requirements from unnecessary divergence.
  • Represent MFB needs within CIE and enterprise security, influencing capabilities before designs become difficult to change.

Productize Integration

  • Spot recurring requirements across MFBs so CIE solves each integration problem once, turning successful implementations into reusable patterns, playbooks, blueprints and automation with Managing and Product Engineers.
  • Feed recurring needs back to product and control owners, and ensure clear transitions to sustainable operational ownership.

Adoption & Outcome Management

  • Define adoption measures and track posture, gaps, blockers and divergence across assigned MFBs, using evidence to shape roadmap priorities.
  • Support enterprise reporting with control, measurement and governance teams, and communicate outcomes, trends, risks and opportunities to CIE and security leadership.

The DPM is accountable for whether adoption actually happened, measured by adoption velocity, coverage, time-to-integrate, reduced friction and variation, pattern reuse and sustainable operational transition, not stories completed, meetings held or projects closed.


Cross-Functional Leadership & Delivery

  • Lead initiatives spanning MFBs, Product Security, control owners, CIE engineering, architecture, risk and enterprise technology, influencing without direct authority.
  • Communicate trade-offs to senior leadership in business terms, surface unresolved dependencies and keep control, MFB risk and operational ownership with the appropriate organization.
  • Translate priorities into epics and requirements with Managing Engineers, keeping a backlog with outcome-based acceptance criteria; treat Agile as a means, not the purpose of the role.

Essential Skills

Integration Product Management

Demonstrated ability to develop product strategy and roadmaps through customer and technical discovery, prioritize across competing needs and dependencies, translate complex requirements into outcomes, define product and adoption measures, manage complex internal portfolios and influence direction without authority.


Technical & Security Acumen

Enough technical depth to work credibly with security architects and engineers. The DPM need not be the solution architect, but must question assumptions, recognize integration complexity and translate constraints into product decisions. Experience in several of these areas is preferred: cybersecurity controls; cloud security (AWS/Azure/GCP); identity and privileged access; application and API security; DevSecOps; vulnerability management; endpoint and network security; data protection; security architecture, platforms and tooling; and enterprise infrastructure. 


Enterprise Integration Leadership

Experience leading platform adoption, integration, modernization or transformation across federated enterprises, working with engineering and architecture teams, managing senior stakeholders and competing priorities, and translating between business, security, product and engineering audiences. Subsidiary, acquisition or independent business-unit experience is highly desirable.


Qualifications

Essential

  • 5+ years in Product, Technical Product, Security Product or Platform Product Management, or comparable technology leadership roles.
  • Experience owning complex technology products, platforms, integrations or adoption initiatives, including strategies and roadmaps.
  • Strong analytical, prioritization, problem-solving and communication skills, with proven ability to lead through influence.

Desirable

  • Cybersecurity experience, including control frameworks and integrating cloud and security platforms across heterogeneous environments.
  • M&A technology integration or subsidiary/business-unit experience.
  • Relevant security, product or cloud certifications.

Supervisory Responsibilities

This position does not have direct supervisory responsibilities.











#LI-JB2

Skills

Business, Business Case Analyses, Cross-Functional Teamwork, Cybersecurity, Enterprise Technologies, Product Knowledge, Product Management, Product Roadmapping, Product Strategies, Strategic Roadmaps, Systems Thinking, Waterfall Model
