Job Summary

IAM Information Security Lead Specialist provides technical and strategic leadership for identity governance, access management, authentication, and IAM modernization initiatives. Collaborates with program sponsors, cross-functional teams, and assigned project managers to plan and develop scope, deliverables, required resources, work plan, budget, and timing for new security initiatives. 

Essential Tasks & Leadership Philosophy

  • Lead the deployment, integration, and optimization of enterprise Identity and Access Management (IAM) solutions, ensuring alignment with business, security, and regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as a strategic IAM subject matter expert, identifying opportunities to enhance identity governance, access management, authentication, and authorization capabilities across the organization.
  • Drive the adoption of modern identity security practices, including Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), Privileged Access Management (PAM), and identity lifecycle management.
  • Develops expertise in insurance business operations in order to drive security innovations for a financial services organization.
  • Evaluate emerging IAM technologies and industry best practices to improve security, operational efficiency, and user experience.
  • Develops and implements innovative IAM programs, automation capabilities, and minimum viable products (MVPs) that support the organization's strategic security roadmap.
  • Partner with business leaders, technology teams, and security stakeholders to define IAM requirements, establish priorities, and deliver enterprise-wide identity initiatives.
  • Lead complex IAM projects and programs with broad scope, significant business impact, and cross-functional dependencies.
  • Coordinate activities across multiple IAM, cybersecurity, and technology initiatives to ensure alignment with organizational goals and security objectives.
  • Resolve complex identity, access, and authentication challenges by developing practical solutions that balance risk reduction with business enablement.
  • Develop metrics, dashboards, and executive reporting to communicate IAM program effectiveness, operational performance, compliance posture, and risk trends.
  • Builds and owns relationships that positively influence business outcomes.
  • Influence enterprise adoption of identity governance and access management best practices through effective communication, education, and stakeholder engagement.
  • Partners with business leaders to ensure information security risk findings are reviewed and solutions are implemented.
  • Effectively mentors, coaches and influences peers.

First Year Success Factors

  • Develop and Execute an Enterprise IAM Roadmap: Assess the current IAM, IGA, PAM, SSO, and MFA environment. Identify security gaps, compliance risks, and improvement opportunities. Create a prioritized roadmap aligned to business and security objectives.
  • Strengthen Identity Governance and Access Controls: Improve joiner, mover, and leaver processes. Enhance role-based access controls (RBAC).Implement or mature access certification and periodic access reviews. Reduce inappropriate or excessive access privileges.
  • Advance Identity Security Capabilities: Increase adoption of: Single Sign-On (SSO); Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA); Privileged Access Management (PAM); Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) and Improve authentication security while maintaining a positive user experience.
  • Deliver Major IAM Initiatives Successfully: Lead large-scale IAM projects across business and technology teams. Ensure implementations are delivered on time and within scope. Minimize disruption to business operations.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree required.
  • Relevant Information Security certification (CISSP, SCC, ISSAP and/or ISACA, etc.) required.
  • 7-10 years related experience in IT Security or identity access management, and Project Management, or comparable base of knowledge/expertise in the field.
  • Strong knowledge of Identity and Access Management principles, including authentication, authorization, identity governance, and access lifecycle management.
  • Deep expertise in Identity and Access Management, Identity Governance and Administration (IGA), authentication, authorization, and access lifecycle management.

Physical Actions

Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. Occasionally moves, lifts, carries, and places objects and supplies weighing 0-10 pounds without assistance. Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (e.g. others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Visually verifies and reads information. Visually locates material, resources and other objects. Ability to operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.

Physical Environment

This position operates in an open office working environment which will include normal and customary distractions, noise, and interruptions.

A Day in the Life of a Field Adjuster

  • Conduct both virtual and on-site investigations by visiting policyholders’ residences to assess propertydamage, determine liability, evaluate the extent of loss, and negotiate fair settlements.
  • Use claims handling software, a company car, and a laptop to determine claims-related damage and write estimates in a paperless environment.
  • Evaluate and report on potential subrogation opportunities.
  • Reports incidents involving theft, fraud, or arson to appropriate state and industry agencies.
  • Perform duties independently, with work directly impacting management outcomes.
  • Acts as a company representative in public interactions, maintaining a professional demeanor consistentwith management standards.
  • Engages regularly with a variety of stakeholders, including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses,contractors, law enforcement, fraud and arson investigators, attorneys, medical professionals, and otherrelevant parties.
  • Use strong customer service skills to negotiate with policyholders to settle the claim.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.
  • Promotes safety at all times and complies with safety/ergonomicstandards as outlined in relevant company published manuals.

Employees assigned to the Catastrophe team will be required to travel away from their residence for a specified period of time, usually consisting of 23 days. 

  • Although this is not a CAT-specific role, hires will be expected to commit to 1–3 CAT deployments per year.
  • Earn additional hourly pay and overtime during deployment assignments.

If you have the following:

  • High School diploma or equivalent required. 
  • Excellent Customer service experience, preferably in a retail environment
  • Construction or Insurance experience is highly desirable and preferred.
  • Excellent communication skills – both oral and written.
  • Computer Literate: MS Word, Excel, Outlook.
  • Proficiency with smartphones and applications.
  • Eagerness to learn about insurance policies and property damage from the inside out to identify how coverage applies to a particular loss.
  • Outgoing personality that would enjoy interacting with a wide variety of people including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses, and fraud investigators.
  • Valid driver's license and Bondable.  Final candidates will also be subject to a Motor Vehicle Record background check as this position may include a company vehicle.
  • Previous property damage claims experience preferred but we are willing to train the right candidate!

... then this could be a great career opportunity for you!

Final candidate qualifications may be reviewed against the requirements for the associated level of this role.

Candidates must be willing and able to:

  • Climb Ladders to inspect roofs, and be comfortable working on rooftops, multiple times per day, 
  • Work in small, confined spaces that have been damaged; such as attics and crawlspaces.
  • Achieve a minimum passing score on all claims training exams.

Job Summary

This position provides advanced technical underwriting expertise and authority, directly supporting underwriting centers through complex risk assessment, referral decisions, and consultation. The role serves as a primary escalation point for high-exposure accounts, ensuring sound risk selection and alignment with underwriting strategy and appetite.

Essential Job Functions

  • Evaluate and approve complex and high-exposure risks beyond standard underwriting authority levels.
  • Serve as a key referral and escalation point for underwriting teams, exercising judgment on large or non-standard accounts.
  • Provide guidance to underwriting centers, field underwriters, and leadership on risk selection, coverage, pricing considerations, and account management for complex or atypical risks.
  • Review and assess large or complex submissions, providing recommendations and decisions that support profitability and adherence to underwriting standards.
  • Monitor loss trends, large losses, and portfolio performance indicators to inform underwriting decisions and provide guidance that supports profitability, growth, and retention objectives. Lead the underwriting partnership with claims in the loss reformation investigation process.
  • Conduct targeted underwriting reviews focused on technical decision-making and risk selection.
  • Identify trends and provide feedback to improve underwriting quality and consistency.
  • Partner with internal teams to support underwriting decisions, address complex risks, and ensure alignment with business objectives and regulatory requirements, including coordination and portfolio management of individual account reinsurance placements and collaboration with the reinsurance team on annual facility placements.
  • Support development of underwriting capabilities by providing technical guidance, mentorship, and input into training initiatives for underwriting staff.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Education Requirements

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Bachelors degree preferred.
  • CPCU, CIC, or equivalent designation preferred.

Experience Requirements

  • 8+ years experience in commercial lines underwriting with demonstrated technical experience.
  • Experience in underwriting areas of Liability, Work Comp & Business Auto preferred.
  • Guidewire experience preferred.

Additional Qualification

Experience providing technical consultation and referral support, including applying underwriting guidelines, authority levels, and risk selection practices in a high-volume environment. Possesses strong technical aptitude. Strong technical underwriting judgment and ability to make consistent decisions aligned to appetite, profitability, and compliance requirements. Ability to influence internal and/or external constituents. Ability to communicate clearly and confidently with UW Centers and cross-functional partners; strong consultation and influence skills. Demonstrated analytical skills. Demonstrated problem solving skills. Ability to drive multiple projects to successful completion. Demonstrated ability to drive execution and adoption of underwriting changes. Excellent organizational skills.

This role partners with internal stakeholders to support regulatory compliance, operational efficiency, and customer outcomes.

If you are looking for the following in your next career ...

  • Paid training through the award-winning and industry-leading University of Farmers.
  • Flexibility and independence to work outside the confines of a desk job.
  • Total Rewards Benefits Package: 401K and a competitive starting salary.
  • Rapid growth potential and management opportunities for success-oriented people through education,mentorship programs, and inspirational leadership at a company you can be proud of.


… then Farmers Insurance is the place for you!

A Day in the Life of a Field Property Adjuster:

  • Conduct both virtual and on-site investigations by visiting policyholders’ residences to assess propertydamage, determine liability, evaluate the extent of loss, and negotiate fair settlements.
  • Use claims handling software, a company car, and a laptop to determine claims-related damage and write estimates in a paperless environment.
  • Evaluate and report on potential subrogation opportunities.
  • Reports incidents involving theft, fraud, or arson to appropriate state and industry agencies.
  • Perform duties independently, with work directly impacting management outcomes.
  • Acts as a company representative in public interactions, maintaining a professional demeanor consistentwith management standards.
  • Engages regularly with a variety of stakeholders, including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses,contractors, law enforcement, fraud and arson investigators, attorneys, medical professionals, and otherrelevant parties.
  • Use strong customer service skills to negotiate with policyholders to settle the claim.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.
  • Promotes safety at all times and complies with safety/ergonomicstandards as outlined in relevant company published manuals.

Employees assigned to the Catastrophe team will be required to travel away from their residence for a specified period of time, usually consisting of 23 days. 

  • Although this is not a CAT-specific role, hires will be expected to commit to 1–3 CAT deployments per year.

If You Have the Following:

  • High School diploma or equivalent required. 
  • Excellent Customer service experience, preferably in a retail environment
  • Construction or Insurance experience is highly desirable and preferred.
  • Excellent communication skills – both oral and written.
  • Computer Literate: MS Word, Excel, Outlook.
  • Proficiency with smartphones and applications.
  • Eagerness to learn about insurance policies and property damage from the inside out to identify how coverage applies to a particular loss.
  • Outgoing personality that would enjoy interacting with a wide variety of people including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses, and fraud investigators.
  • Valid driver's license and Bondable.  Final candidates will also be subject to a Motor Vehicle Record background check as this position may include a company vehicle.

... then this could be a great career opportunity for you!

Final candidate qualifications may be reviewed against the requirements for the associated level of this role.

Candidates Must be Willing & Able to:

  • Climb Ladders to inspect roofs, and be comfortable working on rooftops, multiple times per day, 
  • Work in small, confined spaces that have been damaged; such as attics and crawlspaces.
  • Achieve a minimum passing score on all claims training exams.

Physical Actions & Environment:

  • Bending, Kneeling, Pulling, Pushing, Sorting, Carrying up to 50 lbs., Climbing, Reaching, Standing, Walking, Seeing
  • Speaking (English), Reading (English), Writing (English), & Key Entering

Required job duties are performed in the field and an in-home office environment. Job Summary

The Sr. Manager, Product Marketing will lead the digital customer experience strategy for Farmers' product solutions. This role will partner with enterprise stakeholders to define product strategies, enhance customer experiences, and drive digital innovation across the organization.This individual will serve as a bridge between business, marketing, product, and technology teams, identifying opportunities to improve customer engagement, optimize digital experiences, and bring innovative solutions to market. The role requires a strategic thinker who can navigate ambiguity, influence cross-functional stakeholders, build business cases, and lead initiatives from concept through execution.

A key focus of the position will be evaluating emerging technologies and digital capabilities that can enable customer experience transformation while supporting both short- and long-term business objectives. The successful candidate will combine strategic vision with strong execution skills, helping shape the future of Farmers' digital customer journey and product experience ecosystem.

Essential Tasks & Leadership Philosophy

  • Lead the vision, strategy, and application of digital product solutions, leveraging emerging technologies such as Artificial Intelligence (AI), Augmented Reality/Virtual Reality (AR/VR), Connected Devices, and evolving product development methodologies.
  • Identify, evaluate, and scope enterprise opportunities, including the development and delivery of prototypes, proofs of concept (POCs), and minimum viable products (MVPs).
  • Drive key customer experience transformation initiatives by leading cross-functional teams, prioritizing work across product backlogs, and delivering solutions that align with Farmers' customer experience standards and business objectives.
  • Foster a culture of innovation by promoting a test-and-learn mindset and enabling new capabilities through experimentation and continuous improvement.
  • Effectively engage and influence executive leadership by presenting strategic recommendations, facilitating decision-making, and driving alignment across stakeholder groups.
  • Partner with enterprise stakeholders to gather business requirements and develop detailed use cases, customer journeys, and user stories that support strategic objectives.
  • Collaborate closely with Technology, Operations, and business partners to develop, manage, and execute product roadmaps that address customer needs and deliver measurable business value.
  • Serve as the bridge between business objectives and technology solutions, ensuring tools, processes, and methodologies align with Marketing and Customer Strategy goals.
  • Lead all aspects of product development and implementation, including strategy, requirements definition, prototyping, testing, training, communications, support planning, and deployment.
  • Monitor innovation trends within the insurance industry and adjacent sectors to identify opportunities that can enhance digital experiences and drive competitive advantage.
  • Develop competitive analyses and benchmarks to evaluate potential enhancements, quantify benefits, and support investment decisions.
  • Assess emerging technologies and leverage customer, market, and performance data to identify opportunities for innovation and customer experience optimization.
  • Recommend and prioritize short- and long-term product investments and roadmap initiatives that align with Customer Strategy, Marketing objectives, and enterprise priorities.
  • Conduct competitive landscape assessments to inform product strategy, customer experience enhancements, and go-to-market planning.
  • Establish measurement frameworks, success metrics, and reporting requirements to evaluate program effectiveness and ensure successful delivery and ongoing performance management.
  • Analyze and report on digital experience, product, and marketing performance metrics, providing actionable insights and recommendations to business leaders and key stakeholders.

First Year Success Factors

  • Establish yourself as the trusted leader for digital customer experience initiatives by building strong partnerships across Marketing, Product, Technology, Underwriting, Operations, and Sales.
  • Lead the optimization of Farmers' digital quote-and-buy experience, driving enhancements that improve customer outcomes, increase digital production, and create a more seamless end-to-end customer journey.
  • Develop and execute a prioritized product roadmap that delivers measurable improvements in customer engagement, conversion, customer satisfaction, and business performance.
  • Identify, evaluate, and implement innovative solutions and emerging technologies that enhance the customer experience and support enterprise growth objectives.
  • Drive complex cross-functional initiatives from concept through implementation, aligning stakeholders, influencing decisions, and delivering measurable business value.

Leadership Competencies

  • Strong executive presence with the ability to communicate effectively at all levels of the organization.
  • Proven ability to navigate ambiguity, establish priorities, and drive initiatives from concept through implementation.
  • Demonstrated strength in stakeholder management, organizational influence, and building alignment across diverse teams.
  • Strategic thinker with a customer-centric mindset and a passion for innovation, continuous improvement, and measurable business impact.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Communications, Information Systems, Product Management, Digital Strategy, or a related field required.
  • Master's degree (MBA or related discipline) preferred.
  • Equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience will be considered.
  • Minimum of 5 years of progressive experience in Product Marketing, Product Management, Digital Strategy, Customer Experience, Marketing Technology, or related disciplines.
  • Demonstrated experience leading digital customer experience initiatives and partnering across business and technology organizations to deliver customer-centric solutions.
  • Proven success developing product strategies, business cases, roadmaps, and requirements that drive measurable business outcomes.
  • Experience leading complex cross-functional programs and influencing stakeholders across matrixed organizations without direct authority.
  • Strong background translating customer insights, business needs, and market opportunities into actionable product enhancements and customer experience improvements.
  • Experience evaluating, implementing, or supporting emerging technology solutions, including AI, automation, personalization, digital platforms, or other customer experience enabling capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to define success metrics, analyze performance data, and leverage insights to optimize customer engagement, digital adoption, and business performance.
  • Experience working within insurance, financial services, banking, or other highly regulated industries preferred.
  • Experience supporting digital quote, purchase, enrollment, self-service, or customer acquisition platforms strongly preferred.
  • Knowledge of Agile methodologies, user story development, backlog prioritization, and digital product delivery practices preferred.

… then Farmers Insurance is the place for you!

A Day in the Life of a Field Property Adjuster:

  • Conduct both virtual and on-site investigations by visiting policyholders’ residences to assess propertydamage, determine liability, evaluate the extent of loss, and negotiate fair settlements.
  • Use claims handling software, a company car, and a laptop to determine claims-related damage and write estimates in a paperless environment.
  • Evaluate and report on potential subrogation opportunities.
  • Reports incidents involving theft, fraud, or arson to appropriate state and industry agencies.
  • Perform duties independently, with work directly impacting management outcomes.
  • Acts as a company representative in public interactions, maintaining a professional demeanor consistentwith management standards.
  • Engages regularly with a variety of stakeholders, including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses,contractors, law enforcement, fraud and arson investigators, attorneys, medical professionals, and otherrelevant parties.
  • Use strong customer service skills to negotiate with policyholders to settle the claim.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.
  • Promotes safety at all times and complies with safety/ergonomicstandards as outlined in relevant company published manuals.

Employees assigned to the Catastrophe team will be required to travel away from their residence for a specified period of time, usually consisting of 23 days. 

  • Although this is not a CAT-specific role, hires will be expected to commit to 1–3 CAT deployments per year.

If You Have the Following:

  • High School diploma or equivalent required. 
  • Excellent Customer service experience, preferably in a retail environment
  • Construction or Insurance experience is highly desirable and preferred.
  • Excellent communication skills – both oral and written.
  • Computer Literate: MS Word, Excel, Outlook.
  • Proficiency with smartphones and applications.
  • Eagerness to learn about insurance policies and property damage from the inside out to identify how coverage applies to a particular loss.
  • Outgoing personality that would enjoy interacting with a wide variety of people including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses, and fraud investigators.
  • Valid driver's license and Bondable.  Final candidates will also be subject to a Motor Vehicle Record background check as this position may include a company vehicle.

... then this could be a great career opportunity for you!

Final candidate qualifications may be reviewed against the requirements for the associated level of this role.

Candidates Must be Willing & Able to:

  • Climb Ladders to inspect roofs, and be comfortable working on rooftops, multiple times per day, 
  • Work in small, confined spaces that have been damaged; such as attics and crawlspaces.
  • Achieve a minimum passing score on all claims training exams.

Physical Actions & Environment:

  • Bending, Kneeling, Pulling, Pushing, Sorting, Carrying up to 50 lbs., Climbing, Reaching, Standing, Walking, Seeing
  • Speaking (English), Reading (English), Writing (English), & Key Entering

Required job duties are performed in the field and an in-home office environment. Exposure to some or all of the following environments when in the field: Uncontrolled outside environmental conditions, Excessive noise levels, Chemicals Chemical/Biological conditions, Moving mechanical parts, Areas considered dangerous, Conditions which could affect the respiratory system or skin such as fumes, odors, dust, mists, gases, oils, smoke, soot, or poor ventilation.

Job Summary

At Farmers, data powers better decisions. As a Sr. Associate Decision Scientist, you'll help transform complex business questions into actionable analytical solutions that shape strategy across our Direct & Strategic Partnerships organization.

In this role, you'll leverage advanced analytics, statistical modeling, and data visualization to uncover insights, identify opportunities, and influence critical business decisions. Working closely with business leaders and cross-functional partners, you'll apply tools such as Python, SQL, Excel, and Power BI to analyze large datasets, develop predictive models, and deliver recommendations that drive growth, improve customer outcomes, and optimize business performance.

Success in this role requires a blend of technical expertise, intellectual curiosity, and business acumen. The ideal candidate thrives in solving ambiguous problems, translating data into compelling stories, and turning analytical insights into measurable business impact.

Essential Tasks & Leadership Philosophy

  • Apply moderately advanced statistical, mathematical, and analytical techniques to solve medium-to-large-scale business problems impacting current and future business strategies.
  • Build descriptive and explanatory models or leverage outputs from predictive and machine learning models developed by others.
  • Analyze large and complex datasets to identify trends, patterns, risks, and business opportunities.
  • Utilize data visualization tools and advanced analytical methods, including: Distribution analysis, Correlation analysis, Outlier detection, Multivariate analysis, Time-series analysis, Machine learning techniques.
  • Conduct exploratory data analysis (EDA), test hypotheses, and validate findings with business stakeholders.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to understand business objectives and develop data-driven solutions.
  • Collect, integrate, and transform data from multiple sources into cohesive datasets for analysis.
  • Evaluate data quality and apply data governance and hygiene practices to ensure reliability and accuracy.
  • Perform quality-control checks, document processes, and collaborate with peers on data validation efforts.
  • Work closely with IT, Data Engineering, Data Science, and other technical teams to optimize data pipelines and resolve data quality issues.
  • Support the deployment, monitoring, and maintenance of predictive models within business workflows.
  • Translate complex analyses into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for business leaders.
  • Utilize effective storytelling and visualization techniques to make analytical findings accessible and impactful.
  • Stay current on emerging data science methodologies, technologies, and industry best practices.
  • Contribute to a culture of continuous learning and knowledge sharing.
  • Provide informal coaching or mentorship to less experienced team members as needed.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

First Year Success Factors

Within the first 12 months, a successful candidate can expect to have achieved the following:

  • Establish strong partnerships with business leaders and become a trusted advisor for data-driven decision-making across Direct & Strategic Partnerships.
  • Deliver actionable insights through advanced analytics, statistical modeling, and predictive techniques that solve complex business challenges and influence strategic outcomes.
  • Lead high-impact analytical projects from problem definition through implementation, driving measurable improvements in growth, customer experience, operational performance, and profitability.
  • Develop, validate, and deploy analytical models that identify key business drivers, improve forecasting capabilities, and support informed decision-making.
  • Leverage Python, SQL, Power BI, and other analytical tools to transform complex datasets into scalable analytical solutions and executive-ready insights.
  • Translate complex analytical findings into clear, actionable recommendations that influence leadership decisions and advance business objectives.

Education & Career Experience Requirements

Candidates would ideally reflect the following professional qualifications and experiences:

  • Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Economics, Business Analytics, Computer Science, or a related quantitative discipline. Equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
  • Three or more years of experience applying advanced analytics, statistical modeling, predictive analytics, or quantitative problem-solving to support business decision-making. Experience in insurance, financial services, or other data-driven industries is preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex or ambiguous business questions into analytical approaches, actionable insights, and measurable business outcomes.
  • Strong technical proficiency with Python, SQL, Excel, Power BI, and other analytical tools used for data exploration, statistical analysis, modeling, and visualization.
  • Experience developing, validating, and deploying analytical models, including forecasting, segmentation, driver analysis, optimization, predictive modeling, and performance measurement.
  • Solid foundation in statistical methods and analytical techniques, including hypothesis testing, regression analysis, experimental design, forecasting, and trend analysis.
  • Proven ability to communicate complex analytical findings to both technical and non-technical audiences, translating data into clear recommendations that influence business strategy and decision-making.

Benefits

Job.JobDescription:

At Farmers, helping others is at the heart of what we do.

Ready to make your mark? Discover our vibrant culture and explore career opportunities at www.Farmers.com/careers/corporate. Connect with us on Instagram, LinkedIn and TikTok, and let’s build something incredible together!

Workplace: Remote ( #LI-Remote )

Farmers believes in a culture of collaboration, creativity, and innovation, which thrives when we have the ability to work flexibly in a virtual setting as well as the opportunity to be together in person. Our hybrid work environment combines the best of both worlds with at least three (3) days in office and up to two (2) days virtual for employees who live within fifty (50) miles of a Farmers corporate office. Applicants beyond fifty (50) miles may still be considered.

Job Summary

This position supports the growth of life insurance sales by leveraging data to make recommendations to agents that drive premium and profit objectives for an assigned territory. The role takes ownership of sales outcomes through proactive engagement and solution-driven approaches. The position develops and implements business plans to enhance agency productivity and profitability, deepen relationships, and promote life insurance products and the companys value proposition. The position collaborates with internal teams, field leadership, and agency stakeholders to address complex or high-value challenges, implement life insurance sales initiatives, and achieve sales objectives. This position is an individual contributor and performs work independently while receiving minimal guidance and direction.

Essential Job Functions

Drives life insurance sales by consulting with agency owners to meet sales objectives across multiple product lines and on high-value and complex cases. Takes ownership of sales outcomes by managing both assisted and unassisted sales activities. Focuses on point-of-sale interactions to drive successful transactions and meet sales targets. Promotes life insurance products and company value proposition. Achieves activity targets and production goals by proactively engaging with district managers and agency owners to identify needs or opportunities and deliver tailored solutions, and continuously monitor outcomes. Follows up on implemented strategies to assess effectiveness and pivots as needed when results do not meet expectations. Develops and implements customized sales plans for assigned agency to drive sales growth and meet sales objectives, including quarterly and annual sales targets. Aligns agency-specific sales plans with broader business objectives and leverages adjacent revenue stream opportunities to drive life sales. Demonstrates strong knowledge of life insurance products and services to effectively compete in the marketplace. Independently provides recommendations on product illustrations, case designs, and sales focus. Acts as a liaison between internal teams, field leadership, and agency stakeholders on complex underwriting, commissions, customer service, licensing, and other issues. Builds and maintains relationships with elite agents through targeted consultation, training, and education on products, services, marketing campaigns, technology, and advanced sales strategies. Supports agency growth by assisting with producer recruitment and development, optimizing performance and profitability, and delivering guidance virtually or in-person. Monitors agency performance through CRM systems and other tools. Tracks sales activities, analyzes data and identifies trends or patterns, and provides actionable insights to help agencies address performance gaps and improve sales results. Measures changes in agency performance resulting from the deployment of various tailored solutions. Mentors, trains, and coaches less experienced team members or lower level life sales consultants to develop their skills and improve performance. Provides ongoing support and feedback to support professional development and enhance team capabilities. Performs other duties as assigned.

Education Requirements

High School Diploma or equivalent required. Bachelors degree preferred. Valid life insurance and FINRA 6, 63 licenses required. Other preferred designations include Financial Services Certified Professional (FSCP), Chartered Life Underwriter (CLU), Chartered Financial Consultant (ChFC).

Experience Requirements

Minimum seven years of experience in sales, account management, or agency operations, preferably within the insurance industry. Experience required in direct point of sale, life insurance wholesale, and sales leadership.

Additional Qualification

Strong verbal communication and listening skills. Demonstrated written communication skills. Ability to influence internal and/or external constituents. Demonstrated analytical skills. Possesses strong product knowledge. In-depth knowledge of life insurance products and services and in-depth understanding of company product offerings. Possesses strong technical aptitude. Proficient in Microsoft Office suite. Strong proficiency in CRM and similar systems. Able to adapt quickly to new technology. Develops and delivers effective presentations. Possesses a high degree of initiative. Instills commitment to organizational goals. Effectively coaches and delivers constructive feedback.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Benefits

The starting wage for this position is $29.61/hr. or higher. Additional compensation may be offered based on relevant experience and transferable skills.  

If you are looking for the following in your next career ...

  • Paid training through the award-winning and industry-leading University of Farmers.
  • Flexibility and independence to work outside the confines of a desk job.
  • Total Rewards Benefits Package: 401K and a competitive starting salary.
  • Rapid growth potential and management opportunities for success-oriented people through education,mentorship programs, and inspirational leadership at a company you can be proud of.


… Then Farmers Insurance is the place for you!

A Day in the Life of a Field Property Adjuster:

  • Conduct both virtual and on-site investigations by visiting policyholders’ residences to assess propertydamage, determine liability, evaluate the extent of loss, and negotiate fair settlements.
  • Use claims handling software, a company car, and a laptop to determine claims-related damage and write estimates in a paperless environment.
  • Evaluate and report on potential subrogation opportunities.
  • Reports incidents involving theft, fraud, or arson to appropriate state and industry agencies.
  • Perform duties independently, with work directly impacting management outcomes.
  • Acts as a company representative in public interactions, maintaining a professional demeanor consistentwith management standards.
  • Engages regularly with a variety of stakeholders, including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses,contractors, law enforcement, fraud and arson investigators, attorneys, medical professionals, and otherrelevant parties.
  • Use strong customer service skills to negotiate with policyholders to settle the claim.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.
  • Promotes safety at all times and complies with safety/ergonomicstandards as outlined in relevant company published manuals.

Employees assigned to the Catastrophe team will be required to travel away from their residence for a specified period of time, usually consisting of 23 days. 

  • Although this is not a CAT-specific role, hires will be expected to commit to 1–3 CAT deployments per year.

If You Have the Following:

  • High School diploma or equivalent required. 
  • Excellent Customer service experience, preferably in a retail environment
  • Construction or Insurance experience is highly desirable and preferred.
  • Excellent communication skills – both oral and written.
  • Computer Literate: MS Word, Excel, Outlook.
  • Proficiency with smartphones and applications.
  • Eagerness to learn about insurance policies and property damage from the inside out to identify how coverage applies to a particular loss.
  • Outgoing personality that would enjoy interacting with a wide variety of people including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses, and fraud investigators.
  • Valid driver's license and Bondable.  Final candidates will also be subject to a Motor Vehicle Record background check as this position may include a company vehicle.

... then this could be a great career opportunity for you!

Final candidate qualifications may be reviewed against the requirements for the associated level of this role.

Candidates Must be Willing & Able to:

  • Climb Ladders to inspect roofs, and be comfortable working on rooftops, multiple times per day, 
  • Work in small, confined spaces that have been damaged; such as attics and crawlspaces.
  • Achieve a minimum passing score on all claims training exams.

Physical Actions & Environment:

  • Bending, Kneeling, Pulling, Pushing, Sorting, Carrying up to 50 lbs., Climbing, Reaching, Standing, Walking, Seeing
  • Speaking (English), Reading (English), Writing (English), & Key Entering

Required job duties are performed in the field and an in-home office environment. Job Summary

Farmers Insurance is seeking a Technology Auditor to support high‑quality technology audits as part of our transformation to a modern, risk‑focused Internal Audit function. This role is hands‑on and execution‑focused, with primary responsibility for technology control testing, evidence evaluation, and audit documentation across IT and cyber risk areas.

What You'll Do

  • Lead discussions with technology and business stakeholders to understand the objectives, processes, systems, data flows, key risks, and control environment associated with the area under review, and challenge assumptions where necessary.
  • Independently identify and assess technology risks, evaluate key controls, and help shape audit scope, testing strategies, and evidence requirements using a risk-based approach.
  • Execute technology audits across cybersecurity, identity and access management, applications, cloud, infrastructure, data, and emerging technology domains.
  • Perform stakeholder discussions, evaluate process and control design, and identify gaps, inconsistencies, or emerging risks by asking effective "why" and "how" questions.
  • Gather, evaluate, and challenge the completeness, reliability, and relevance of evidence obtained through interviews, system reports, configurations, logs, tickets, analytics, and other audit procedures.
  • Apply professional judgment and skepticism throughout the audit by assessing whether evidence supports management's assertions and investigating anomalies, exceptions, and conflicting information.
  • Own assigned audit areas from planning through reporting, proactively managing activities, stakeholder requests, dependencies, and timelines while escalating risks and blockers promptly.
  • Work in iterative audit cycles, continuously reassessing risks, adjusting testing approaches, and incorporating feedback as new information emerges.
  • Prepare high-quality workpapers that clearly document procedures performed, evidence reviewed, judgments applied, and conclusions reached in accordance with Internal Audit methodology and quality standards.
  • Identify, evaluate, and develop audit issues by determining root causes, assessing business and technology impacts, validating facts with stakeholders, and recommending practical corrective actions.
  • Clearly communicate risks, observations, and audit conclusions to stakeholders at various levels, translating technical issues into business-relevant risk implications.
  • Participate actively in audit team reviews, challenge sessions, showcases, and quality discussions, providing constructive challenge to strengthen audit outcomes.
  • Leverage approved analytics, automation, and AI-enabled tools responsibly to improve audit effectiveness, insight generation, and efficiency while maintaining accountability for audit conclusions.
  • Assess the design and effectiveness of remediation activities and validate that corrective actions appropriately address underlying risks and root causes.
  • Continuously expand expertise in technology, cybersecurity, emerging technologies, audit methodology, risk management, and industry practices through ongoing learning and professional development.

Essential Job Functions

  • Leads audit engagements with minimal supervision - on time and in a quality manner.
  • Preparation of reports and communication with the business.
  • Administrative duties supporting departmental activities, individual development plan, training, performance management, and general administration.
  • Participates in departmental special projects.

Physical Actions

This role, whether performed virtually or in an office setting, will include normal and customary distractions, noise, and interruptions. Sits or stands for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Occasionally reaches overhead and below the knees, including bending, twisting, pulling, and stooping. Occasionally moves, lifts, carries, and places objects and supplies weighing 0-10 pounds without assistance. Listens to, interprets, and differentiates auditory information (example others speaking) at normal speaking levels with or without correction. Visually verifies and reads information. Visually locates material, resources and other objects. Ability to continuously operate a computer for extended periods of time, up to a full work shift. Physical dexterity sufficient to use hands, arms, and shoulders repetitively to operate keyboard and other office equipment up to a full work shift.

Education Requirements

High School Diploma or equivalent required. Bachelors degree preferred. Certified Internal Auditor (CIA), Certified Public Accountant (CPA), CISA, or other comparable designation preferred.

Experience Requirements

Five or more years experience in Auditing at an external firm or financial services firm, or seven years experience with Farmers Insurance and/or one year as a Farmers Insurance Auditor. Detailed subject matter expertise of at least one area of the business or industry.

Special Skill Requirement

Strong analytical skills. Strong oral and written communication skills. Strong project management skills. Ability to effectively communicate with individuals in the business.

We are seeking an experienced trial attorney to join our Washington staff counsel team! Our attorneys work from home and handle in-person appearances and trials as required so we are open to candidates throughout Washington. We offer developmental opportunities, and a comprehensive benefits package including annual bonus potential up to 20% of the salary, generous 401k, auto allowance, PTO, medical/dental/vision, paid parental leave, and much more all without the stress of billable hours!   

Job Summary

This position is responsible for representing clients in all areas of insurance defense practice, handling cases that are primarily moderate to high complexity and exposure and/or involve unique insurance defense issues. Manages all phases of cases from intake to resolution.

Essential Job Functions

  • Litigates moderate to high complexity and exposure cases and/or cases involving unique legal or procedural issues and performs duties necessary from intake to trial and/or settlement. This includes but is not limited to preparation of pleadings, motions, discovery, and briefs.
  • Acts as the lead attorney at hearings, conferences, interviews, mediations, arbitrations, and/or trials.
  • Develops strategies and arguments to thoroughly prepare for trial. Utilizes knowledge of legal precedents to analyze the probable outcomes of a case.
  • Identifies the strengths and weaknesses of approaches to a case. Performs or ensures completion of any other tasks or duties necessary for the proper representation of clients.
  • Consults with Claims Executive team and renders legal strategy recommendations regarding the legal aspects of the handling of personal injury claims.
  • Provides guidance to ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards. Interprets applicable industry laws, rulings and regulations.
  • Functionally supervises attorneys who are assisting in the handling of cases as development opportunities.
  • Provides guidance and mentorship with the autonomy to learn.

Physical Actions

Job is performed in-person at a Farmers office or virtually at an approved alternative work location. Job may include work performed at field locations. The physical work environment is indoors and climate-controlled with adequate lighting and ventilation. Normal and customary distractions include background noise produced by office equipment and chatter among people, as well as interruptions. Field work performed outdoors may include exposure to weather elements. Frequently sits or stands for prolonged periods of time, up to a full shift. Occasionally moves about the workplace including navigating stairs, ramps, and level or uneven surfaces. Occasionally moves, pushes, pulls, lifts, carries, and places objects or materials weighing up to 50 pounds without assistance. Frequently uses shoulders, arms, hands, and fingers to manipulate equipment, tools, and objects necessary to perform job duties. Frequently performs fine motor tasks such as typing, mousing, or writing, up to a full shift. Occasionally performs movements such as bending, stooping, crouching, kneeling, twisting, and reaching overhead or below the knees. Possesses clear vision, with or without correction, to visually read and verify information. Relies on depth perception and peripheral vision to navigate the work environment visually by identifying barriers, changes in terrain and locating objects. Possesses adequate hearing, with or without correction, to communicate with co-workers, respond promptly to auditory signals or alarms, and discern sounds essential for maintaining safety and productivity in the workplace. Jobs in this category may require regular travel between Farmers offices, alternative work locations, and/or field locations.

Physical Environment

Required job duties are normally performed in a climate- controlled office environment, with some exposure to uncontrollable outside environmental conditions and travel via automobile and/or commercial transportation.

Education Requirements

Bachelors degree preferred. Licensed to practice Law in applicable states required upon hire.

Experience Requirements

Seven years of litigation experience required. Insurance defense, personal injury, and/or jury trial experience required. First and second chair trial experience in bodily injury litigation strongly preferred. Multistate jurisdictional practice preferred.

Special Skill Requirement

Public speaking, ability to function and handle high case loads in adversarial or confrontational situations, driving.

Additional Qualification

Effective leadership skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to command the attention of an audience. Demonstrated problem solving skills. Possesses a genuine interest in the defense of Insurance regulations. Ability to represent the company with external constituents. Handles conflict effectively with the ability to quickly interpret and respond to new information. Demonstrates excellent judgment and decision making skills. Ability to work within tight timeframes and meet strict deadlines. Excellent time management and priority setting skills. Articulate and responsive to colleagues. Possesses strong technical aptitude. Adept and proficient at using technology to maximize efficiency in virtual, paperless environment.

A Day in the Life of a Field Property Adjuster:

  • Conduct both virtual and on-site investigations by visiting policyholders’ residences to assess propertydamage, determine liability, evaluate the extent of loss, and negotiate fair settlements.
  • Use claims handling software, a company car, and a laptop to determine claims-related damage and write estimates in a paperless environment.
  • Evaluate and report on potential subrogation opportunities.
  • Reports incidents involving theft, fraud, or arson to appropriate state and industry agencies.
  • Perform duties independently, with work directly impacting management outcomes.
  • Acts as a company representative in public interactions, maintaining a professional demeanor consistentwith management standards.
  • Engages regularly with a variety of stakeholders, including policyholders, claimants, agents, witnesses,contractors, law enforcement, fraud and arson investigators, attorneys, medical professionals, and otherrelevant parties.
  • Use strong customer service skills to negotiate with policyholders to settle the claim.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.

Employees assigned to the Catastrophe team will be required to travel away from their residence for a specified period of time, usually consisting of 23 days. 

  • Although this is not a CAT-specific role, hires will be expected to commit to 1–3 CAT deployments per year.

  • Construction or Insurance experience is highly desirable and preferred.

  • Valid driver's license and Bondable.  Final candidates will also be subject to a Motor Vehicle Record background check as this position may include a company vehicle.

The Role at a Glance

As Retirement Sales Director, you will be responsible for driving growth through new retirement plan sponsor acquisition, with a primary focus on mid to large market plans ($50M+ in assets). In this role, you will develop and execute a territory business plan designed to achieve ambitious sales, AUM, and market share goals across your assigned geography. You will serve as a key external representative, building and expanding relationships with retirement plan consultants, advisors, brokers, and plan sponsors. This is a highly consultative, relationship driven sales role that requires deep retirement industry knowledge, disciplined pipeline management, and close collaboration with internal partners to deliver comprehensive retirement solutions and exceptional client outcomes.

What you'll be doing

Drive Growth & New Business Acquisition
•    Lead new retirement plan sponsor acquisition with a focus on plans with $50M+ in assets
•    Develop and execute a territory and prospecting strategy to meet or exceed annual sales and AUM targets
•    Identify, qualify, and cultivate prospective plan sponsors through proactive outreach, referrals, networking, and consultant relationships
•    Manage the full sales cycle, from initial engagement through finalist presentations, pricing, contract negotiation, and close.
Build and Deepen Influencer Relationships
•    Build, maintain, and grow strong relationships with retirement plan consultants, advisors, brokers, and other centers of influence impacting mid to large market plan decisions
•    Increase territory penetration by strengthening partnerships with influential specialists and consulting firms
•    Position the organization as a preferred retirement provider through consistent engagement, education, and thought leadership
Deliver Consultative Retirement Solutions
•    Conduct needs based discovery with plan sponsors to understand fiduciary objectives, plan design, investments, participant outcomes, and service expectations
•    Present tailored retirement solutions, including recordkeeping, investments, managed accounts, and financial wellness offerings
•    Clearly articulate value propositions around fiduciary governance, plan outcomes, fee reasonableness, and participant engagement
Territory & Sales Execution Excellence
•    Manage a large geographic territory, executing external wholesale sales programs that drive revenue and market share growth
•    Conduct in person and virtual meetings such as due diligence sessions, consultant updates, one on one meetings, and industry sponsorships
•    Represent the organization at industry conferences, client events, and networking functions
•    Maintain accurate pipeline, activity tracking, and forecasting in CRM and sales reporting systems
•    Forecast sales activity and revenue with discipline, transparency, and accountability
•    Effectively manage expense budgets to maximize territory coverage and sales impact
Collaboration & Operational Discipline
•    Partner closely with internal stakeholders including operations, product, client service, core market counterparts, and consultant relations teams to support opportunities and ensure seamless onboarding and issuance
•    Ensure sold business is properly processed from point of sale through implementation
•    Uphold the highest standards of professionalism, ethics, and compliance, adhering to all policies, procedures, and cultural expectations

What we’re looking for

Must-Haves:
•    Minimum of 5+ years of experience in Defined Contribution retirement plan sales and/or relationship management, with direct alignment to the responsibilities of this role
•    Bachelor’s degree required, or equivalent professional experience (4 additional years of relevant experience in lieu of a degree)
•    Ability to obtain FINRA Series 6, Series 63, and Life & Health licenses within 120 days of hire
•    Confident and effective communicator with strong written and verbal communication skills
•    Demonstrated ability to communicate credibly and knowledgeably with senior leaders, both internally and externally
•    Strong presentation capabilities with a proven track record of influencing stakeholders at all levels through clear, logical, and well informed discussions
•    Advanced relationship management skills, including the ability to partner collaboratively with internal teams and build trusted relationships with external clients
•    Willingness and ability to travel up to 50%
 
Nice-to-Have:
•    Strong working knowledge of ERISA rules and regulatory requirements governing retirement plans

The Role at a Glance

We are seeking an experienced Director of Customer Experience to lead and scale Customer Experience capabilities across Workplace Solutions. This leader will bring deep, hands-on CX expertise and a demonstrated track record of building mature, repeatable practices that embed customer-centered decision-making across an organization. In this role, you will set the CX strategy and operating model, strengthen governance and measurement, and create the tools, standards, and ways of working that enable teams across Product, Operations, Technology, Digital, Marketing, and Distribution to consistently improve the experience. You will champion the voice of the customer while connecting customer insights and experience improvements to measurable business outcomes, including growth, retention, efficiency, and differentiation.

This is not a role focused solely on journey mapping or Voice of Customer programs. We are looking for a proven CX leader who has helped an organization move from individual projects to an integrated, enterprise-scale CX capability. You will influence senior leaders, develop talent, build cross-functional commitment, and translate customer needs into clear priorities, investment decisions, and sustained change.

What you'll be doing

•    Lead, coach, and develop a team of Customer Experience professionals, setting clear expectations and building the strategic, analytical, and influencing capabilities needed to deliver meaningful impact.
•    Define and execute a scalable CX strategy and operating model, including governance, standards, roles, decision rights, prioritization, and cross-functional ways of working.
•    Build and mature the organization's CX capabilities by establishing repeatable methods, tools, training, and frameworks that enable teams to apply customer-centered practices consistently and independently.
•    Partner with senior leaders across Product, Operations, Technology, Digital, Marketing, and Distribution to embed customer needs into business strategy, transformation roadmaps, investment decisions, and solution design.
•    Establish an enterprise approach to journey management that identifies priority journeys, clarifies ownership, connects insights across touchpoints, and drives coordinated improvement over time.
•    Integrate Voice of Customer, research, behavioral and operational data, market intelligence, and employee insights to identify root causes, size opportunities, and inform strategic recommendations.
•    Translate complex customer and business challenges into actionable strategies, business cases, executive-level recommendations, and sequenced roadmaps.
•    Define and monitor a CX measurement framework that connects experience outcomes to business results such as growth, retention, utilization, digital adoption, cost, and operational performance.
•    Drive adoption and accountability through change leadership, stakeholder engagement, communication, and capability-building across the organization.
•    Champion the thoughtful use of AI and emerging technologies to improve customer outcomes, increase efficiency, and create competitive advantage.

What we’re looking for

Must-haves:
•    5+ years of progressive CX experience, including CX strategy, journey management, customer insights, experience measurement, service design, or related disciplines
•    Demonstrated experience building, scaling, or maturing a CX practice across a complex organization, including establishing operating models, governance, standards, tools, measurement, and cross-functional adoption
•    3+ years of people leadership experience, with a track record of developing high-performing teams and leading through influence in a matrixed environment
•    Experience translating customer insights and journey opportunities into enterprise priorities, funded roadmaps, measurable improvements, and business outcomes
•    Strong executive presence and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to influence senior leaders and gain alignment across functions with competing priorities
•    Strong business acumen and the ability to connect CX investments to growth, retention, efficiency, risk reduction, and market differentiation
•    Demonstrated change leadership experience, including building organizational commitment, establishing accountability, and driving sustained adoption of new CX practices
•    Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience (4 years of experience in lieu of a Bachelor's degree)

Nice-to-haves:
•    Recognized Customer Experience certification, such as CCXP, or comparable certification in human-centered design, service design, design thinking, or change management
•    Experience leading CX in financial services, insurance, employee benefits, retirement, or another regulated and complex service environment
•    Working knowledge of Group Benefits and/or Retirement Plans
•    Experience applying AI, analytics, and emerging technologies to improve customer experiences and operational outcomes

The pay range for this position is $106,875 - $171,000 with anticipated pay for new hires between the minimum and midpoint of the range and could vary above and below the listed range as permitted by applicable law. Pay is based on non-discriminatory factors including but not limited to work experience, education, location, licensure requirements, proficiency and qualifications required for the role. The base pay is just one component of Lincoln’s total rewards package for employees.  In addition, the role may be eligible for the Annual Incentive Program, which is discretionary and based on the performance of the company, business unit and individual.  Other rewards may include long-term incentives, sales incentives and Lincoln’s standard benefits package.

About The Company

Lincoln Financial (NYSE: LNC) helps people to confidently plan for their version of a successful future. We focus on identifying a clear path to financial security, with products including annuities, life insurance, group protection, and retirement plan services. 

With our 120-year track record of expertise and integrity, millions of customers trust our solutions and service to help put their goals in reach. 

Lincoln Financial Distributors, a broker-dealer, is the wholesale distribution organization of Lincoln Financial. Lincoln Financial is the marketing name for Lincoln Financial Corporation and its affiliates including The Lincoln National Life Insurance Company, Fort Wayne, IN, and Lincoln Life & Annuity Company of New York, Syracuse, NY. Lincoln Financial affiliates, their distributors, and their respective employees, representatives and/or insurance agents do not provide tax, accounting or legal advice. 

Lincoln is committed to creating an inclusive environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status. 

Follow us on Facebook, X, LinkedIn, Instagram, and YouTube. For the latest company news, visit our newsroom. 

Be Aware of Fraudulent Recruiting Activities

If you are interested in a career at Lincoln, we encourage you to review our current openings and apply on our website. Lincoln values the privacy and security of every applicant and urges all applicants to diligently protect their sensitive personal information from scams targeting job seekers. These scams can take many forms including fake employment applications, bogus interviews and falsified offer letters.

Lincoln will not ask applicants to provide their social security numbers, date of birth, bank account information or other sensitive information in job applications. Additionally, our recruiters do not communicate with applicants through free e-mail accounts (Gmail, Yahoo, Hotmail) or conduct interviews utilizing video chat rooms. We will never ask applicants to provide payment during the hiring process or extend an offer without conducting a phone, live video or in-person interview.  Please contact Lincoln's fraud team at fraudhotline@lfg.com if you encounter a recruiter or see a job opportunity that seems suspicious.

Benefits That Go Beyond The Basics

We strive to be Above all in Service® to our customers—and to our employees. That’s why Erie Insurance offers you an exceptional benefits package, including:

  • Premier health, prescription, dental, and vision benefits for you and your dependents. Coverage begins your first day of work.

Additional benefits that include company-paid basic life insurance; short-and long-term disability insurance; orthodontic coverage for children and adults; adoption assistance; fertility and infertility coverage; well-being programs; paid volunteer hours for service to your community; and dollar-for-dollar matching of your charitable gifts each year.

Position Summary

Exercises independent discretion and judgment in handling or directing litigated claims.


  • This is a remote position that requires the ability to travel and service Illinois.  

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conducts investigations, evaluates and makes recommendations regarding coverage, liability, and resolution strategies.
  • Selects, engages, and collaborates with defense counsel in the handling of lawsuits.
  • Manages litigation expenses and ensures that defense counsel adheres to ERIE's billing guidelines.
  • Complies with and directs defense counsels' utilization of Outside Counsel Guidelines. 
  • Trains and mentors.
  • Documents claim files.


The first four duties listed are the functions identified as essential to the job. Essential functions are those job duties that must be performed in order for the job to be accomplished.

Regular and predictable attendance is an essential job function. For certain positions at ERIE, including leadership roles, regular and predictable onsite presence may also be an essential job function based on business and operational needs.


This position description in no way states or implies that these are the only duties to be performed by the incumbent. Employees are required to follow any other job-related instruction and to perform any other duties as requested by their supervisor, or as become evident.

Additional Experience

Position Summary

Exercises independent discretion or judgment in handling all types of property claims. Also assists or acts on behalf of the claims supervisor when required.

Exercises independent discretion or judgment in handling property claims within designated level of authority. Also responsible for servicing assigned territory and may handle litigated claims.

• The selected candidate will ideally live in La Crosse, WI or surrounding area. 
• The hiring manager will consider candidates for Property Adjuster Trainee (F08), Property Adjuster I (F09) or Property Adjuster II (F10).   
• Level of position offered will be based upon the depth and breadth of selected candidate's experience and qualifications. 
• A company car and equipment to work from home will be provided.
• Ability to drive/travel regularly within the assigned territory.
 
How the Property Adjuster Trainee program works:   


Tentative Program Start Date: 1/4/2027 
• The 15-week training program will require multiple weeks of training in Erie, PA, which will prepare you for immediate success as a Property Adjuster.   
• The Smart Start class of Property Adjuster Trainees will consist of both classroom and hands-on training activities in the ERIE Technical Learning Center (in Erie, PA), where individuals will learn ERIE's property estimating platform.   
• Trainees will be provided with field experiences and opportunities to learn about workflows within their branch office and apply what they have learned to claims that they handle alongside their mentors and supervisors.   
• This program gives interested individuals comprehensive training to successfully prepare them for the Property Adjuster role.  Additional program details, expectations, and timing will be discussed during the interview process.    


Class Dates at the Technical Learning Center in Erie, Pa:
• 1/4/27- 1/15
• 2/8- 2/19
• 3/22- 3/26
  
Check out this video that showcases ERIE’s corporate offices: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GQBh-yvmqQ0

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Conducts investigations, interviews, and inspects damage, driving to site of damage within assigned territory or other if required. Prepares estimates, makes recommendation, and handles coverage questions, and litigation.
  • Sets and maintains reserves, reviews reports and related materials, directs experts, determines coverage and claim value, issues or declines payment, and negotiates claims with plaintiff attorneys when necessary.
  • Documents claim files and submits report for closure.
  • Recognizes subrogation situations and initiates appropriate action.
  • Services assigned territory and brings assigned claims to conclusion.
  • Interacts with Agents and district sales managers on matters of mutual concern.
  • Assists claims supervisor or acts on his/her behalf, including representing the company at legal proceedings, as required.
  • Completes industry-related training programs and continues to attend training programs to remain informed on policy changes, interpretation or new legislation.
  • Assists in training of new claims adjusters.
  • Participates on Catastrophe Team when required.

Join Aon’s Digital Finance transformation as a Senior Manager, Finance Systems, where you’ll play a key role in shaping the future of finance. In this highly visible position, you’ll work at the intersection of finance, data, and technology — leading the modernization of financial systems and leveraging platforms like Databricks, Workday, TM1 and Power BI to deliver scalable solutions, real-time insights, and advanced analytics. This is a unique opportunity to drive innovation, enable AI-powered decision-making, and partner across the business to transform planning, forecasting, and reporting at scale. Aon is in the business of better decisions At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world. As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed. What the day will look like Lead digital transformation efforts across financial systems, driving automation and scalable architecture. Partner with Finance, IT, and Business stakeholders to define requirements, deliver solutions, and ensure alignment with enterprise goals. Architect and maintain complex, multi-dimensional financial data models that support dynamic planning, forecasting, and scenario analysis Leverage Databricks, Snowflake and other AI platforms to manage large-scale financial data and enable predictive analytics and machine learning. Develop and maintain interactive dashboards using Power BI or similar tools to deliver real-time insights. Conduct systems analysis to identify inefficiencies and implement process improvements. Manage reconciliation processes between Workday, IBM Planning Analytics (TM1), and other financial subsystems, ensuring data accuracy and consistency. Maintain documentation and enforce data governance and internal control standards. How this opportunity is different Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, or related field; Master’s or CPA preferred. Expertise in financial systems, including Workday and IBM Planning Analytics (TM1). Strong proficiency in data modeling and dashboarding tools (e.g., SQL, Python, Power BI, Anaplan, Tableau). Proven experience with Databricks, Snowflake, or similar AI/data platforms. Excellent analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills. Understanding of financial processes (e.g., budgeting, forecasting, general ledger).
